Description:
It is the intent of these specifications, terms, and conditions to describe fine art handling, framing and fabrication services being requested by the County. Services are defined as follows:
Fine Art Handling Services:
 Museum-quality fine art handling services to transport and install artwork in the County’s art collection as well as temporary art exhibitions in County buildings, and provide other related fine art fabrication and technical services,
Fine Art Framing Services:
 Museum-quality fine art archival, custom framing services for the County’s art collection, and
Fine Art Fabrication Services:
 Museum-quality fine art fabrication in multiple two-dimensional formats for the County’s art collection and provide other related technical services.
The County intends to award a three-year contract (with the option to renew for two years) to a pool of up to four (4) Bidders for Fine Art Handling Services, a pool of up to three (3) Bidders for Fine Art Framing Services, and a pool of up to four (4) Bidders for Fine Art Fabrication Services. Award(s) will be made to the most responsive and responsible Bidder(s) whose response(s) conform to the RFP and meet(s) the County’s requirements. Bidders responding to this RFP may submit a proposal for one or multiple services, but must clearly indicate which service(s) their proposal addresses.
The County will engage the awarded pool of contractors for projects on an as-needed basis. The Contractors will then provide their proposal for each project, including turnaround time and the number of billable hours. Total cost, turnaround time, the specific expertise, and performance of the particular contractor(s) who provide estimates will be the determining factors in which contractor is selected for a particular project. The County has sole discretion regarding which contractor(s) will be utilized for each particular project.

The Alameda County Arts Commission (ACAC) is building a collection of public artwork created by Alameda County and Bay Area artists that will be installed at County buildings for the benefit and enjoyment of the general public. Through this RFP, the County seeks to engage the following museum-quality fine art service professionals to assist ACAC in building and maintaining its public art collection.
 
Fine Art Handling Services
Fine art handlers with museum-quality fine art handling, transportation, and installation experience who are interested in submitting a response to this solicitation must provide an hourly rate for transportation and installation services and technical consultation services. Fine art handlers will be responsible for the safe handling, transportation, and installation of artwork in the County’s art collection as well as temporary art exhibitions in County buildings, and provide other related fine art fabrication and technical services. The majority of the artwork which will be installed through this contract is framed two-dimensional artwork and will be wall-hung using security hangers, or for temporary exhibitions on a picture railing or other wall surfaces. A limited number of permanent, site-specific artworks may also be installed through this contract and may require additional license(s), fine art fabrication, technical services, supplies, and site-preparation. The fine art handlers must be able to provide expertise regarding appropriate mounting hardware and installation systems for a variety of circumstances. Bidders must demonstrate their specialized capabilities and experience using past projects as examples in the relevant experience section of Exhibit A – Bid Response Packet.
Fine Art Framing Services
Fine art picture framers, with extensive experience with museum-quality picture framing who are interested in submitting a response to this solicitation must provide a price quote for three sample frame styles in specified finished sizes. The specified styles are representative of framing styles and materials for newly acquired artworks. Each framing project will be for a unique artwork, and the Contractor must demonstrate the experience and capability to collaborate with ACAC to address project specific requirements regarding one-of-a-kind artworks. This includes the ability to research and provide technical expertise for different framing materials and methods. Quotes for each frame style must be based on the materials and other specifications included in the Bid Form.
The Contractor will frame approximately 100 artworks over the term of the contract. Artworks will primarily range in size from 11 inches by 11 inches to 60 inches by 60 inches (and up to three [3] inches deep) and will be framed in a variety of styles, as reflected in the Bid Form. Bidders must demonstrate their specialized capabilities and experience using past projects as examples in the relevant experience section of Exhibit A – Bid Response Packet.
Fine Art Fabrication Services
Fine art fabricators with extensive experience with museum-quality fine art fabrication of multiple two-dimensional formats using a variety of materials who are interested in submitting a response to this solicitation must provide a price quote for at least one of the specified fabrication methods and finished sizes. The listed materials and methods are representative of those that may be used for future public art projects. Each fabrication project will be a unique artwork, and the Contractor must demonstrate the experience and capability to collaborate with ACAC staff and artists to address complex, project specific requirements regarding one-of-a-kind artworks. Bidders must demonstrate their specialized capabilities and experience using past projects as examples in the relevant experience section of Exhibit A – Bid Response Packet.
 
ACAC is a division of the County of Alameda. ACAC is dedicated to improving the quality of life in Alameda County by nurturing a thriving environment for the arts and for cultural activities; promoting economic opportunities for Alameda County’s artists and arts organizations through programs such as arts grants, public art, and art in education programs; encouraging public participation in the arts and actively advocating for the arts.
Established in 1994 by Alameda County’s “2% for Public Art” Ordinance, Alameda County’s Public Art Program provides for public art elements connected to capital improvement projects undertaken by Alameda County. The unique artworks are created by professional artists and are integrated into the design of the structure or landscaping, or are in proximity to the project, in any number of treatments and media. Artwork is purchased or commissioned through an open competitive process.

Description:
It is the intent of these specifications, terms, and conditions for Alameda County Behavioral Health Department (hereafter ACBHD or County) to establish a pool of contractors to provide residential treatment services for youth experiencing substance use disorders (SUD) ages 12–17, including youth with co-occurring mental health conditions and involvement in systems such as child welfare, probation, and education.
 
See Attachments for full description and summary

The California Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) Drug Medi-Cal Organized Delivery System (DMC-ODS)
[1]
 program delivers SUD treatment services to eligible Medi-Cal members by providing a continuum of care modeled after the American Society of Addiction Medicine (ASAM) criteria. 
Under the current agreement with DHCS, ACBHD intends to offer residential treatment services for youth with SUD. These services are designed to meet the unique developmental, behavioral, and clinical needs of youth ages 12–17, including youth with co-occurring mental health conditions and involvement in systems such as child welfare, probation, and education. Adolescent residential treatment services provide structured, 24-hour therapeutic environments that support stabilization, engagement in treatment, and transition to lower levels of care.
The program will provide services based on ASAM level 3.1 low-intensity, ASAM level 3.2 withdrawal management, and/or ASAM level 3.5 high-intensity adolescent treatment criteria. Programs must be ASAM certified and licensed by the California Department of Social Services Community Care Licensing (CCL) division as a Residential Community Treatment Facility in order to serve Alameda County clients.
[1]
 
https://www.dhcs.ca.gov/providers-partners/drug-medi-cal-organized-delivery-system/

Description:
It is the intent of these specifications, terms, and conditions to describe recruitment and staffing services for the placement of non-medical providers, i.e., psychologists, on either a permanent or a temporary basis to provide services requested by Alameda County Health Behavioral Health Department on an “as needed” basis.
The County intends to award a three-year contract (with the option to renew for two years) to a pool/multi-award of up to fifteen (15) Bidders selected as the most responsive and responsible Bidders whose response conforms to the RFP and meets the County’s requirements.

Behavioral Health Department (BHD or County) requires recruitment/staffing agencies to provide permanent and/or temporary placements within Forensic, Diversion, and Re-entry System of Care division when the traditional methods have not been effective in securing timely staffing resources. The recruitment/staffing services will be utilized to fill psychologist positions in the county-operated jail system where there are high service demand and short supply of staff.
The BHD forensic program sites are in Dublin, Pleasanton, Oakland, and San Leandro. The sites generally operate Monday through Friday, from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., excluding 
County Holidays 
,although hours of operation may vary by site. Some sites offer extended morning, evening and weekend hours, while others operate continuously on a 24-hour, seven-days-a-week (24/7) basis.
The Adult Forensic Behavioral Health (AFBH) provides mental health and substance use services 24 hours a day, 7 days a week to individuals incarcerated at Santa Rita Jail (SRJ). AFBH team works closely with the Alameda County Sheriff’s Office (ACSO) and SRJ medical provider. AFBH services include but are not limited to mental health screening at intake, variety of clinical assessments, including risk assessment, crisis intervention and stabilization, diagnosis and treatment planning, individual and group counseling, case management, care coordination, and re-entry planning. The BHD forensic programs are staffed by multi-disciplinary teams, and the psychologists hired through recruitment/staffing agencies will report to their assigned managers, supervisors, or directors within the forensic division.
The purpose of this RFP is to recruit licensed clinical psychologists with experience and ability to supervise interns/associates. Applicants must be licensed through the State of California. For each staffing request, the County may solicit qualified Contractors within the pool to submit one or more candidates meeting the specific assignment requirements. The County will select the Contractor offering the best overall value based on factors including candidate qualifications, relevant experience, availability, proposed bill rate, prior contract performance, responsiveness, and the County's operational needs. The County reserves the right to contact one, some, or all Contractors in the pool for any staffing request and to bypass the secondary competition when operational urgency, continuity of care, or unique qualifications make doing so in the County's best interest.

Event Name: IRFP 902793 Signage and Wayfinding Master Planning Services

Details.Format/Type: GSAP AD RFP 002 / Request For Proposal

Description:
It is the intent of these specifications, terms, and conditions to describe signage and wayfinding master planning services for the Alco Park Garage being requested by the County.
The County intends to award a three-year contract (with the option to renew for two years) to the Bidder selected as the most responsive and responsible Bidder whose response conforms to the IRFP and meets the County’s requirements.

The Alameda County General Services Agency - Building Maintenance Department (GSA-BMD) intends to procure professional consulting services to assess existing conditions and develop a comprehensive signage and wayfinding master plan for the Alco Park Garage, located at 165 13th Street in Oakland, California.
The Alco Park Garage is a multi-level public parking facility maintained by GSA-BMD that serves the public and County employees. The facility contains multiple vehicle entrances and exits, pedestrian access points, elevators, stairwells, parking levels, service areas, and operational spaces. A clear, consistent, and accessible signage system is necessary to support safe and efficient navigation throughout the facility.
Alco Park Garage is an approximately 406,528-square-foot, nine-level parking facility with 732 parking stalls, two elevators, three stairwells, one ramp, two vehicle entrances, and two vehicle exits.
Over time, signage throughout the garage has been installed incrementally by various County departments to address evolving operational, regulatory, and safety requirements. As a result, the existing signage system lacks consistency in appearance, messaging, materials, placement, and branding. Existing signs vary significantly in age, condition, design, and purpose. Some signs are outdated, redundant, damaged, difficult to locate, or no longer meet current operational requirements or accessibility standards. County departments have also identified additional signage needs to improve wayfinding, parking operations, safety, accessibility, and the overall user experience.
The County seeks to develop a comprehensive signage and wayfinding master plan that establishes a cohesive, functional, accessible, and code-compliant signage system for the Alco Park Garage. The selected Contractor shall evaluate existing conditions, identify deficiencies and opportunities for improvement, and develop recommendations for a unified signage and wayfinding program that supports current and future facility operations. The resulting master plan will establish standards and serve as the foundation for future signage design, fabrication, and installation projects.
Scope clarification:
 The selected Contractor will provide assessment, planning, design development, bidding support, and implementation support services only. Sign fabrication, procurement, and installation are not included in this contract.
Site Access:
 Alco Park Garage is open to the public during regular business hours, Monday through Friday, from 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. Bidders may, at their discretion, visit the facility during business hours to observe existing site conditions and familiarize themselves with the garage and its existing signage and wayfinding conditions. A site visit is optional and is not required to submit a proposal.
The Contractor shall deliver a County-accepted, implementation-ready signage and wayfinding master plan that accurately inventories all existing signs; identifies traceable accessibility, regulatory, safety, operational, and navigation deficiencies; establishes coordinated design, location, messaging, and technical standards; supports competitive procurement of future fabrication and installation services; and enables the County to verify that installed signage conforms to the approved documents.

Salvage and Recycling of Decommissioned Electrical Equipment
. The qualified Respondent will collect, transport, process, recycle, and dispose of decommissioned electrical equipment, including transformers, switchgear, conductors, metal enclosures, and other surplus utility materials. Services include safe handling of mineral oil and PCB‑contaminated equipment, proper dismantling and material segregation, monthly pickups from City facilities, and full regulatory‑compliant documentation.
This project supports Anaheim’s commitment to safe environmental practices, responsible recycling, and efficient management of utility assets.

## MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS FOR RESPONDENT
To be eligible for consideration, Respondents must meet all minimum qualifications specified in this Section and demonstrate a proven track record of successfully providing the requested Services to entities of comparable size and complexity, such as similarly sized public utilities.
Proposals that fail to demonstrate satisfaction of these minimum qualifications may be deemed non-responsive and rejected. Respondents must provide sufficient evidence in their proposals to verify that they meet all qualifications.
Minimum Qualifications
:
Respondent must have a minimum of five (5) years of verifiable experience performing salvage, recycling, transportation, and disposal of decommissioned electrical utility equipment, including but not limited to transformers, switchgear, conductors, cable, and oil‑filled apparatus.
Respondent must demonstrate past performance providing similar services to public utilities, municipal agencies, or investor‑owned utilities.
Applicable state and federal regulatory permits, including authorization to handle, transport, and process used transformer oil and PCB‑contaminated materials.
Compliance with all EPA, DOT, and OSHA requirements relevant to the Services.
Use of registered hazardous waste transporters when required under California law.
Respondent must have the equipment, vehicles, and staff necessary to safely transport and process electrical equipment and associated materials.
Respondent must demonstrate the ability to perform monthly pickups (or as requested) from Anaheim facilities.
Respondent must have access to a facility capable of processing, dismantling, and recycling electrical equipment and associated materials in accordance with regulatory requirements.
Respondent must provide a general description of the recycling or disposal processes used.

## Right to Accept, Reject, or Cancel
Anaheim may, in its sole discretion, accept or reject any or all proposals, in whole or in part, for any reason and without explanation. Anaheim reserves the right to cancel this RFP at any time, enter into agreements with one or more Respondents, or procure services through other means. Anaheim may also issue a new request for proposal that supersedes and replaces this RFP.

## Scope of Services
Provider shall furnish all labor, supervision, transportation, equipment, tools, materials, documentation, and related services necessary to collect, transport, process, recycle, recover, resell, and/or dispose of surplus utility materials designated by Anaheim under this Agreement. Surplus utility materials may include, but are not limited to, the following:
Overhead transformers
Padmount transformers
Switchgear
Conductors and cable
Metal enclosures
Electrical apparatus
Scrap metals
Oil-filled equipment
Miscellaneous utility equipment
Provider's Services may include, as applicable: pickup and transportation of materials from locations designated by Anaheim; dismantling and preparation of equipment; segregation and classification of materials; recycling and commodity recovery; hazardous materials handling; disposal; resale; downstream processing; and any other activities necessary to properly manage surplus Utility materials in accordance with the Agreement.
Provider shall perform all Services in a safe, professional, and workmanlike manner and in compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local laws, regulations, permits, and requirements, including environmental regulations, hazardous materials handling and disposal requirements, transportation regulations, and applicable industry standards and best practices.
Provider shall be responsible for providing all personnel, equipment, vehicles, facilities, and other resources necessary to perform the Services, unless otherwise expressly agreed to in writing by Anaheim.

## Background
APU provides electric and water service to approximately 340,000 residents and 15,000 businesses located in Anaheim, spanning a service territory of approximately 50 square miles. APU's mission is to provide safe, reliable, and environmentally responsible electric and water service to the Anaheim community. This procurement supports that mission by ensuring decommissioned utility equipment is managed in a manner that reduces environmental risk. and promotes responsible recycling.

## Collection and Transportation
Provider shall coordinate and perform pickups of surplus utility materials with Anaheim representatives at locations and times designated or approved by Anaheim. Equipment will generally be available for pickup at the Edwards Utilities Complex (EUC), located at 909 E. Vermont Avenue, Anaheim, CA 92805; however, Provider may be asked to pick up equipment from other Anaheim locations.
Anaheim will usually provide a forklift and operator to load units onto Provider's flat-bed trailer; however, Anaheim may instead request that the Provider furnish loading services, including equipment and labor, at the time of pickup. Safe and lawful packing, loading, securing, and other elements of transportation are Provider's responsibility. Provider's truck(s) should have the option of side gates to safely transport small items.
Shipments normally consist of a full truckload and accumulate on approximately a monthly basis. Provider may elect to include transportation costs within its unit bid prices, or alternatively, provide per-load transportation pricing (see rate table / Schedule A).
Provider may consolidate loads and commingle compatible material streams and optimize transportation routes and load composition to promote transportation efficiency, processing efficiency, and accurate settlement calculations; provided, however, that Provider shall not commingle materials in a manner that prevents accurate identification, measurement, valuation, or settlement of materials in accordance with the Schedule of Compensation.
Provider shall provide all manifests, bills of lading, weight tickets, receipts, certificates, and other shipping or transaction documentation reasonably requested by Anaheim, sufficiently detailed to verify the quantity, type, disposition, and applicable valuation of materials collected and processed.

## Protest Procedures
Any actual or prospective Respondent who alleges an error or impropriety in the solicitation or award of an Agreement may submit a protest to the appropriate Procurement Contact as set forth herein.
Protest Instructions
All protests shall be typed under the protester’s letterhead and submitted in accordance with the provisions stated herein and emailed to the Procurement Contact.  All protests shall include, at a minimum, the following information:
The name, address, telephone number, and email address of the protester;
The signature of the protester or the protester’s representative;
The solicitation number;
A detailed statement of the legal and/or factual grounds for the protest; and

In the event the protest of specifications is denied, and the protester wishes to continue in the solicitation process, they must still submit a bid or proposal prior to the close of the solicitation in accordance with the solicitation submittal procedures provided in the solicitation.
Protest of Award of Agreement
A protest for an award of an Agreement in relation to a solicitation must be received no later than three (3) business days after the Notice of Award is posted on the City’s online bidding system.
Protests relating to a proposed Agreement award received after the three (3) business day deadline 
will not
 be considered by the City.
If the three (3) business day period expires without the receipt of a protest, the department may move forward with the Agreement award or if necessary, file the item for approval by the City Council.
Protest Process
In the event of a timely protest, the City shall not proceed with the solicitation or award of the Agreement until the Procurement Contact issues a decision on the protest.
Upon receipt of a timely protest, the Procurement Contact will within five (5) business days of the receipt of the protest, issue a decision in writing which shall state the reason for the actions taken.
The City may, after providing written justification to be included in the purchasing file, make the determination that an immediate award of the Agreement is necessary to protect the substantial interests of the City.  The award of the Agreement shall in no way compromise the protester’s right to the protest procedures outlined herein.
If the protester disagrees with the decision of the Procurement Contact, the protester may submit a written notice to the City of Anaheim Purchasing Agent requesting an appeal.
Appeal Process 
If the protester wishes to appeal the decision of the Procurement Contact, the protester must submit, within three (3) business days from the receipt of the Procurement Contact decision, a written appeal to the City of Anaheim Purchasing Agent. 
All appeals must be emailed to

Within ten (10) business days, the City of Anaheim Purchasing Agent will review all materials in connection with the appeal, assess the merits of the appeal and provide a written determination that shall contain their decision.  The decision of the City of Anaheim Purchasing Agent will be final.

## Environmental and Hazardous Materials Handling
Electrical equipment offered for recycling generally contains mineral (transformer) oil, though some equipment may not. Where equipment is known to be leaking, it will be drained of oil or placed within appropriate secondary containment prior to pickup. Provider may elect to drain equipment of oil prior to pickup as required for safe loading and transportation. 
Oil in some equipment may contain polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), typically at low concentrations (less than 49 parts per million [ppm]) where present. Some equipment is classified as “non-PCB” based on manufacturer-supplied information or nameplate data. Oil in older equipment has been or will be tested for PCBs, and a report of PCB concentrations will be provided for each shipment. “Non-PCB” refers to items that contain or contained dielectric fluid with less than 5 ppm PCB.
Some equipment to be recycled (e.g., switches and circuit breakers) may have contained sulfur hexafluoride (SF₆). The City will evacuate SF₆ from equipment prior to offering it for salvage; however, residual by-products of SF₆ decomposition may remain and can present dermal and respiratory health hazards under certain circumstances. Although used SF₆ equipment is not characterized as hazardous waste, Provider is expected to have the means to safely remove any SF₆ decomposition residue at its facility as necessary to facilitate safe dismantling or further processing.
Provider shall comply with all applicable federal, state, and local environmental regulations, hazardous materials handling and disposal requirements, transportation regulations, and industry best practices in performing the Services.

## Testing Responsibilities - Environmental Compliance
Provider shall perform all Services in a safe, professional, and workmanlike manner and in compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local laws, regulations, permits, and requirements, including, without limitation, environmental regulations, hazardous materials handling and disposal requirements, transportation regulations, and applicable industry standards and best practices. As determined necessary by the City, the Provider shall obtain representative oil samples from designated equipment. Oil samples shall be analyzed for polychlorinated biphenyl (PCB) content by a certified laboratory using EPA‑approved analytical methods. Provider shall submit complete laboratory reports, including PCB concentrations, chain‑of‑custody documentation, and any related test records, prior to any removal, transport, or processing of the affected equipment. All sampling, handling, labeling, transportation, and management of oil samples shall be performed in compliance with applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations pertaining to PCB materials.

## Disposition of Equipment; Product Liability and Defect Disclosure
Respondents shall describe their proposed methods for handling, dismantling, recycling, and disposing of the decommissioned electrical equipment and materials, including whether any equipment or components may be refurbished, resold, or otherwise reused. Respondents shall identify the intended disposition of recovered materials and any proposed downstream recipients or processing facilities.
In accordance with Anaheim Administrative Regulation 425, and to the extent applicable, the City will require a written disclaimer holding the City harmless against product-liability claims before disposing of any equipment that might reasonably be subject to such claims through subsequent use. Any known defects in the equipment that are not readily apparent through visual inspection will be disclosed to potential buyers, as required by Administrative Regulation 425.
The selected Respondent shall cooperate with the City in satisfying these requirements, including executing any applicable written disclaimer in a form acceptable to the City before taking possession of or acquiring title to equipment intended for subsequent use, if required by the City. The selected Respondent shall also comply with all applicable requirements governing the handling, transportation, recycling, and disposal of the equipment and materials.

Description:
The Anaheim Housing Authority ("Authority") is soliciting proposals from qualified affordable housing developers ("Developers") to acquire, through a long-term ground lease, the Elm Street Commons affordable multifamily rental housing development located at 111–125 West Elm Street, Anaheim, California ("Project"). The selected Developer will partner with the Authority to preserve long-term affordability and stabilize the property.
The Project is a 52‑unit, 100% affordable rental community currently restricted to households earning 30%–60% of Area Median Income (AMI). The Authority recently acquired control of the property to prevent foreclosure, stabilize operations, and preserve affordability. The Authority intends to transfer long‑term operational responsibility to a qualified Developer with demonstrated expertise in affordable housing preservation.

Elm Street Commons was originally developed in 2006 with Redevelopment Agency financing and Low-Income Housing Tax Credits. Over time, the property experienced operational and financial challenges that threatened its long-term stability. Following a strategic default by the former ownership entity, the Authority exercised its option to assume ownership. It purchased the outstanding mortgage loan using Low and Moderate Income Housing Asset Funds, preventing foreclosure and protecting residents and affordability restrictions.

This Contract has been negotiated and executed in the state of California and shall be governed by and construed under the laws of the state of California. In the event of any legal action to enforce or interpret this Contract, the sole and exclusive venue shall be a court of competent jurisdiction located in Orange County, California, and the Parties hereto agree to and do hereby submit to the jurisdiction of such court, notwithstanding Code of Civil Procedure Section 394.  Furthermore, the parties specifically agree to waive any and all rights to request that an action be transferred for adjudication to another County.

## INTRODUCTION
The City of Anaheim, Public Works Department, (hereinafter referred to as City) is requesting competitive bids from qualified vendors (hereinafter referred to as Bidder) for RDU/ surveillance trailer cameras. The awarded Purchase Order, will be between the City and awarded Bidder, (hereinafter referred to as Contractor) in accordance with the 
City Terms & Conditions
, and specifications. This is a fully electronic solicitation – only electronic bids submitted through the City’s online bidding system will be allowed; no other form of bid submittals will be accepted. Prior to submitting a bid, Bidders are advised to carefully read the instructions below, including the 
City Terms & Conditions
 and any solicitation attachments and/or exhibits.

## Scope of Contract
This Contract specifies the terms and conditions by which the City will procure 
RDU/trailer camera 
 from the Contractor, as further detailed in the Scope of Work, identified and incorporated herein by this reference as "Attachment A".  All services provided under this Contract shall conform to the Scope of Work as set forth in this contract.

## Parties and Purpose
This Contract is entered into as of the date fully executed by and between the City and Contractor, based on the terms and conditions of the City RCA-017-23010021 and this Contract. The Contract allows individual City departments to utilize the Contractor’s services by executing subordinate agreements against this Contract.
Subordinate City Master Agreements (MAs)
City departments are authorized to enter into individual subordinate MAs under this Contract. Attachment B to this Contract provides a MA template to be utilized. Each subordinate MA shall at a minimum:
Specify a 
not-to-exceed dollar amount
; and
Include 
invoice terms and instructions
; and
Reference this Contract as the governing agreement for the terms of service.

Bidders must be an authorized partner/reseller for Axis Communications capable of selling, delivering, and servicing the items as specified.

RDU/trailer camera

Afford Contractor written notice of the breach and ten (10) calendar days or such shorter time that may be specified in this Contract within which to cure the breach; and
Discontinue payment to the Contactor for and during the period in which Contractor is in breach; and
Offset against any monies billed by Contractor but unpaid by City those monies disallowed pursuant to the above.

## SUBSTITUTIONS
Bids offering equivalent items meeting the standards of quality specified in the solicitation may be considered, unless otherwise specified, providing the bid clearly describes the article offered and how it differs from the specified brand.  Unless Bidder specifies otherwise, it is understood that the Bidder is offering the brand item as specified in the solicitation.  If Bidder bids an “equal,” Bidder must state the brand name and must submit complete specifications and/or provide samples with the bid.  Determination of equality shall be at the sole discretion of the City, and the City reserves the right to request a sample for determining equality with the specified brand.  If it has been justified and accepted by the requesting agency/department and/or a City standards committee that only one brand can meet the City’s requirements, “no exceptions” shall be noted in the specifications.

Contractor’s Project Manager shall be assigned to this project for the duration of Contract and shall diligently pursue all work and services to meet the project timelines. City’s Project Manager shall have the right to require the removal and replacement of Contractor’s Project Manager from providing services to City under this Contract. City’s Project Manager shall notify Contractor in writing of such action.  Contractor shall accomplish the removal within five (5) business days after written notice by City’s Project Manager. City’s Project Manager shall review and approve the appointment of the replacement for Contractor’s Project Manager.  City is not required to provide any additional information, reason or rationale in the event it requires the removal of Contractor’s Project Manager from providing further services under Contract.

## PROTEST PROCEDURES
Any actual or prospective bidder or proposer who alleges an error or impropriety in the solicitation or award of a contract may submit a protest to the appropriate Procurement Contact as set forth herein.
Protest Instructions
All protests shall be typed under the protester’s letterhead and submitted in accordance with the provisions stated herein and emailed to the Assigned Buyer/Purchasing Liaison.  All protests shall include, at a minimum, the following information:
The name, address, telephone number, and email address of the protester;
The signature of the protester or the protester’s representative;
The solicitation number;
A detailed statement of the legal and/or factual grounds for the protest; and
The form of relief requested.
Protest of the Solicitation Specifications
All protests related to the solicitation specifications must be submitted to the appropriate soliciting department’s Assigned Buyer/Purchasing Liaison no later than three (3) business days prior to the close of the solicitation. 
Protests received after the three (3) business days deadline will not be considered by the City.
In the event the protest of specifications is denied, and the protester wishes to continue in the solicitation process, they must still submit a bid or proposal prior to the close of the solicitation in accordance with the solicitation submittal procedures provided in the solicitation.
Protest of Award of Contract 
A protest for an award of contract in relation to a solicitation must be received no later than three (3) business days after the Notice of Award is posted on the City’s online bidding system.
Protests relating to a proposed contract award received after the three (3) business day deadline 
will not
 be considered by the City.
If the three (3) business day period expires without the receipt of a protest, the department may move forward with the Contract award or if necessary, file the item for approval by the City Council.
Protest Process
In the event of a timely protest, the City shall not proceed with the solicitation or award of the contract until the Procurement Contact issues a decision on the protest.
Upon receipt of a timely protest, the Assigned Buyer/Purchasing Liaison will within five (5) business days of the receipt of the protest, issue a decision in writing which shall state the reason for the actions taken.
The City may, after providing written justification to be included in the purchasing file, make the determination that an immediate award of the contract is necessary to protect the substantial interests of the City.  The award of a contract shall in no way compromise the protester’s right to the protest procedures outlined herein.

## PROTEST PROCEDURES
Any actual or prospective bidder or proposer who alleges an error or impropriety in the solicitation or award of a contract may submit a protest to the appropriate Procurement Contact as set forth herein.
Protest Instructions
All protests shall be typed under the protester’s letterhead and submitted in accordance with the provisions stated herein and emailed to the Assigned Buyer/Purchasing Liaison.  All protests shall include, at a minimum, the following information:
The name, address, telephone number, and email address of the protester;
The signature of the protester or the protester’s representative;
The solicitation number;
A detailed statement of the legal and/or factual grounds for the protest; and
The form of relief requested.
Protest of the Solicitation Specifications
All protests related to the solicitation specifications must be submitted to the appropriate soliciting department’s Assigned Buyer/Purchasing Liaison no later than three (3) business days prior to the close of the solicitation. 
Protests received after the three (3) business days deadline will not be considered by the City.
In the event the protest of specifications is denied, and the protester wishes to continue in the solicitation process, they must still submit a bid or proposal prior to the close of the solicitation in accordance with the solicitation submittal procedures provided in the solicitation.
Protest of Award of Contract 
A protest for an award of contract in relation to a solicitation must be received no later than three (3) business days after the Notice of Award is posted on the City’s online bidding system.
Protests relating to a proposed contract award received after the three (3) business day deadline 
will not
 be considered by the City.
If the three (3) business day period expires without the receipt of a protest, the department may move forward with the Contract award or if necessary, file the item for approval by the City Council.
Protest Process
In the event of a timely protest, the City shall not proceed with the solicitation or award of the contract until the Procurement Contact issues a decision on the protest.
Upon receipt of a timely protest, the Assigned Buyer/Purchasing Liaison will within five (5) business days of the receipt of the protest, issue a decision in writing which shall state the reason for the actions taken.
The City may, after providing written justification to be included in the purchasing file, make the determination that an immediate award of the contract is necessary to protect the substantial interests of the City.  The award of a contract shall in no way compromise the protester’s right to the protest procedures outlined herein.
If the protester disagrees with the decision of the Procurement Contact, the protester may submit a written notice to the City of Anaheim Purchasing Agent requesting an appeal.
Appeal Process 
If the protester wishes to appeal the decision of the Procurement Contact, the protester must submit, within three (3) business days from the receipt of the Procurement Contact decision, a written appeal to the City of Anaheim Purchasing Agent. 
All appeals must be emailed to 
purchasing@anaheim.net
.
Within ten (10) business days, the City of Anaheim Purchasing Agent will review all materials in connection with the appeal, assess the merits of the appeal and provide a written determination that shall contain their decision.  The decision of the City of Anaheim Purchasing Agent will be final.

The Air District is tasked with regulating stationary sources of air pollution in the nine counties that surround San Francisco Bay: Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin, Napa, San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara, southwestern Solano, and southern Sonoma counties. It is governed by a 24-member Board of Directors composed of locally elected officials from each of the nine counties. The Air District’s mission is to improve air quality to protect public health, reduce historical and current environmental inequities, and mitigate climate change and its impacts.
The Air District aims to achieve its mission through many strategic goals, including: reducing and eliminating health problems caused by air pollution, achieving and maintaining air quality standards, leading the Bay Area’s efforts to fight global climate change, creating high-quality regulatory programs, and applying environmental best practices in all operations. To do so, the Air District regulates air pollution emissions from stationary emission sources such as factories, refineries, and power plants, and from smaller facilities like gas stations and dry cleaners. The Air District ensures that such facilities comply with air pollution laws and regulations, provides incentives to replace older, higher-emitting vehicles and equipment with cleaner alternatives, and gives grants and provides outreach to encourage healthy clean air choices by businesses and consumers. The Air District implements these efforts with an equity focus, aiming to reduce air quality disparities and promote environmental justice by targeting local air pollution in overburdened communities.

## Project
Air quality in the Bay Area has improved dramatically since the late 1960s, due in large part to the success of the Air District’s regulatory program and California’s strict tail-pipe emissions standards. However, the region is challenged by air pollution and has exceedances of federal ozone and particulate matter standards, and the more stringent health-based California air quality standards.  
The Spare the Air program communicates the health implications of ozone and fine particulate matter to the public and encourages Bay Area residents to change their behavior to benefit air quality, such as limiting driving and reducing or eliminating wood burning indoors and outdoors. 
As pollution from industrial sources has been reduced, transportation, motor vehicles, consumer products and small engines now comprise about 50 percent of the Bay Area’s air pollution problem. To continue air quality improvements in the Bay Area, reducing vehicles on Bay Area roads, as well as reducing residential and consumer sources of air pollution, are crucial. The Air District encourages the public to make changes in their behavior to benefit air quality such as: driving less by working remotely, taking transit, carpooling, walking or biking, and reducing or eliminating wood burning. 
The Air District seeks proposals from qualified and experienced contractors in the field of Advertising, Communications, Social Media, Digital Promotion, and Survey Research to assist the Air District with its Spare the Air program. The Spare the Air program encourages the public to make behavior changes that will have a beneficial impact and improve air quality and is one of the Air District’s most effective and widely recognized public outreach programs.

## Media/Public Relations
The contractor will work with the Air District Communications Office to develop, produce and implement media/public relations that support the overall messaging goals of the Spare the Air program. Media/public relations will support each Spare the Air program through media events, news interviews, speaking engagements, Op-Eds, and other relevant messaging opportunities.
The contractor will design the program and produce and implement all aspects of the media/public relations components — including but not limited to, concept, writing, design, production and media pitching. The contractor will take part in team meetings with Air District staff and other Air District contractors on a weekly basis or as needed.

## Spare the Air Program Overview
Spare the Air 
Program
 
Since its inception in 1991, the Spare the Air program has become one of the Air District’s most effective and widely recognized public outreach programs. During warmer months, the Air District issues Spare the Air Alerts on days when ozone pollution is forecast to exceed federal standards. During these Spare the Air Alerts, the Air District urges residents to reduce their driving by working remotely, taking transit, carpooling, walking or biking to reduce air pollution. People sensitive to air pollution, such as children and the elderly, are cautioned to limit outdoor exposure. 
 
Spare the Air Alerts and daily air quality forecasts are posted on the Spare the Air website, 
www.sparetheair.org
,
 recorded on 
the 1-800-HELP-AIR 
telephone line, and announced on local media outlets. Bay Area residents can also sign up on the Spare the Air website to be notified by automatic e-mail Air Alerts, phone alerts and/or text alerts. Past Spare the Air campains can be viewed on the Spare the Air YouTube channel here: 
https://www.youtube.com/@SpareTheAirBayArea/videos
. Through the Spare the Air Employer Program, employers are encouraged to educate their employees on remote work and alternative commute options and notify them when a Spare the Air Alert is called. There is an existing membership list of over 2,000 members in the Spare the Air Employer Program, and the campaign is targeting employers in communities most impacted by air pollution as well as minority and women-owned businesses.
 
Through the Spare the Air program, the Air District encourages the public to make behavior changes that will have a beneficial impact and improve air quality. 
Spare the Air is a behavior change messaging campaign that focuses on reducing single occupancy driving, reducing wood smoke emissions and other clean air behaviors. 
The Employer Program 
consists of employer coordinators informing their workforce of impending Spare the Air Alerts, educating employees about the ways individuals can improve air quality, and motivating them to take action.
Spare the Air in the wintertime is a regulatory program that bans wood burning on days when a Spare the Air Alert is called and discourages wood burning at all times.  
 
Spare the Air Summer 
Program
 
Typically, the smog/summer season begins in May and runs through October. In recent years, emphasis on working remotely, reducing driving, taking transit, carpooling and the promotion of electric vehicles has continued throughout the year. Additionally, in 2019, the Air District amended the Wood Burning Rule making it illegal to burn wood year-round when particulate matter is forecast to reach unhealthy levels in an effort to address wildfire smoke impacts. 
 
The goals of the Spare the Air summer program include:
Reduce the number of cars on Bay Area roads by promoting commute alternatives such as remote work, transit, carpooling, walking and biking.
Motivate behavior change of Bay Area drivers to reduce their driving to minimize air pollution and traffic congestion.
Educate Bay Area residents about the Bay Area’s air quality challenges and solutions.
Promote wildfire smoke preparedness tips and related information about Spare the Air Alerts.  
Educate the public and build awareness of Spare the Air program.
Achieve measurable success in motivating individuals to drive less and reduce their contribution to air pollution.
Expand Air District efforts to communicate air pollution information to non-English-speaking populations.
Promote adoption of electric vehicles in the Bay Area.
Promote the use of bikes and e-bikes versus driving, particularly for disadvantaged communities and residents disproportionally affected by unhealthy air quality. 
 
Spare the Air Winter Program
 
The nine counties of the San Francisco Bay Area are home to seven million residents and an estimated 1.4 million fireplaces and woodstoves. Particulate matter pollution from wood-burning devices is the largest source of wintertime pollution and a major health concern in the region. 
 
To protect public health, the Wood Burning Rule was passed in 2008, which banned wood burning from November through April when particle pollution was forecast to be unhealthy. In 2019, the Air District amended the Wood Burning Rule making it illegal to burn wood year-round when particulate matter is forecast to reach unhealthy levels in an effort to address wildfire smoke impacts.
Wood burning is always discouraged even when it is not illegal. The Air District has many ways the public can be notified about a Spare the Air Alert in the wintertime. These include the 877-4NO-BURN hotline, phone, text and email alerts, website banners, social media sites, a widget and a Spare the Air mobile application. The selected contractor will assist with promoting these tools to help reduce wood burning in the Bay Area.
The goals of the Spare the Air winter program include:
Reduce wood smoke in the region by motivating residents to reduce the use of wood burning stoves, fireplaces and outdoor fire pits and encouraging the use of alternatives such as electric heating devices. 
Achieve measurable behavior change in motivating individuals to reduce their contribution to Bay Area wintertime air pollution. 
Inform the public about the Wood Burning Rule (burn ban, health impacts and notification methods).
Inform Bay Area residents about the localized impacts from wood burning at the neighborhood and regional level as well as inside the home.
Outreach and promotion of Air District wood stove change-out programs. 
Expand Air District efforts to communicate air pollution information to non-English-speaking populations.

## Social Media/Digital Promotion
The contractor will develop and implement social media messaging plans, promotions and contests, build social media following and engagement, and manage social media accounts that encourage behavior change through the Spare the Air program (summer and winter). 
Complete management of the Spare the Air social media platforms including organic content and video creation, execution of digital ad campaigns and boosted posts, comment management and social listening/monitoring.
The contractor will:
Develop social media strategies including but not limited to, concept, writing, design, production and technical services.
Create and curate engaging content  and videos for social media platforms.
Develop and manage content calendars to ensure timely publication.
Ensure digital content is engaging, relevant and supports the objectives of the Spare the Air campaigns.
Implement social listening tools to monitor mentions of relevant topics.
Monitor engagement and define key performance indicators for each platform.
Take part in team meetings with Air District staff and other Air District contractors weekly or as needed.
Work with Air District staff to ensure social media efforts are consistent with Air District social media outreach efforts.
The contractor will have access to the Air District's content library which includes high-quality photos and videos, though new additional assets will need to be developed/curated, if needed.

## Public Opinion Measurement Surveys
The contractor will measure the effectiveness of the Air District’s Spare the Air program, assess public behavior patterns, and the effectiveness of the marketing campaign. The contractor will conduct surveys strategically year-round during Spare the Air Alert and on non-alert days when air quality is good for the Spare the Air program. The survey in the summer collects data primarily on behavior change related to solo driving/the reduction of vehicle miles traveled (VMTs), and the survey in the winter collects data on residential wood burning. The additional survey in the third year is for an in-language survey. Top line survey results are required each winter and summer season to evaluate the effectiveness of the campaign.
The contractor will conduct in-language surveys in Spanish, Mandarin and Cantonese for each survey cycle, allowing respondents to choose the language of their preference. For the third cycle of the surveys, an oversample of in-language Spanish and Chinese respondents will be discussed, as needed, to increase the in-language sample and provide a greater statistical reliability for comparisons based on language subgroups.  Interviews will be conducted with survey respondents.

Design survey methodology and work with Air District staff to develop and refine survey questionnaires, as appropriate.

The Air District has an established survey, however, the Air District is open to recommendations to new methods for gathering survey data. The survey must be scientifically valid. Spare the Air program surveys have included broad questions about emission reduction activities, reason for emission reduction activity, behavior change motivation and Spare the Air program awareness.

Solicitation Text:
## Background
The City is requesting the repair and rehabilitation of Well C-4 located at 5400 W. Wilson Street. Banning, CA. City staff noticed that the well had started vibrating and making a bad bearing noise within the pump. The well has been shut off until repairs are made. This well has not been pulled and inspected for several years and is due for full rehab and rebuilding.
Pricing will include the following: Travel to Banning to disconnect the electrical motor make up, removal of the pump, column, tube and shaft and motor. Equipment will then be transported to your shop for teardown and inspection and written reports and pictures of the findings sent to the city. A pre-rehab video, bail any fill and debris, brush for a period of 36 hours and bail to remove all fill and debris after cleaning. Addition of liquid acid descaler chemical treatment to open all screen perforations including the formation behind the well casing and brush to distribute the chemical along the casing walls. Allowing chemicals to remain in the well for 24 hours and then airlift solution out of the well into baker tanks to neutralize the chemical before discharge. Perform post down hole video survey to verify the completeness of the rehab.
The City is going to be working with Besst Inc. to profile the well once it has been rehabbed, in an attempt to lower the Hexavalent Chromium within the well. We will require the pump company to drill a hole in the existing well head or as an option to provide a modified new well head with a 12” discharge head that will allow access to install 620 feet of 1 ½” ID, Flush Thread PVC to get 10-feet below the pump for pulling water samples and flow which would be performed by Besst Inc. The bottom of the access pipe shall be cut at a 45-degree angle and made smooth with no burrs.  The section of the access pipe that transits past the bowls shall be 1 ½” ID Flush Thread Steel Pipe to prevent cursing of the pipe by the bowls.  Pipe couplers, glues and tapes are not permitted. Concurrently, the pump company will then be required to install a test pump for use for approximately 5 days. The test pump shall have the capability of 1,200 GPM and shall be accompanied by a VFD with a lower end pumping rate capability of 800 GPM. The awarded contractor shall provide an onsite operator during BESST’s well testing. The well testing will be completed over a two-day period at approximately 10-hours of field time per day.  The City will contract the analytical laboratory for all sample analyses.
At the end of test pumping the well company will pull the test pump and reinstall well C-4 well pumping equipment. The City will require testing of the following after reinstallation which will be Volts, Amps, Heat, Vibration and pump efficiency testing.

## Scope of Services
A. Monthly Bus Cleaning Services (Saturday Services)
The contractor shall provide interior and exterior cleaning services for the City’s transit fleet on a monthly basis. Services shall include, but are not limited to:
Exterior washing of buses, including windows, wh
eels, and body surfaces (environmental friendly chemicals)
Interior sweeping, mopping, and vacuuming (including handicap ramp and equipment, if applicable)  
Cleaning and sanitizing of seats, handrails, stanchions, driver compartments, and high-touch surfaces
Cleaning of interior windows and mirrors (streak-free)
Removal of trash and debris from vehicles
Spot cleaning of graffiti and stains
Reporting any visible damage, vandalism, or maintenance concerns observed during cleaning activities
Two buses will be in service until they return to the corporate yard around 12:30 PM on Saturday. When those two drivers return to the corporate yard, they will switch to two buses that have already been cleaned to continue providing services to the public while those two buses receive cleaning services. 
The City will provide the contractor with a current fleet list, including vehicle types and quantities, prior to contract execution.
B. Weekly Transit Shelter Cleaning Services (Monday Services)
The contractor shall provide weekly cleaning services for transit shelters located throughout the City. Shelter locations and inventory shall be identified in the appendices attached to this SOW.
Services shall include, but are not limited to:
Sweeping and pressure washing shelter pads and surrounding areas
Cleaning shelter glass, panels, benches, and structural components
Removal of litter, dirt, cobwebs, stickers, flyers, and graffiti
Cleaning of transit signage and display areas where accessible
Reporting damaged shelters, vandalism, or unsafe conditions to the City
Chemicals used must be safe for use around transit riders and structure
Solar Panels
The contractor shall inspect the bus shelters equipped with solar panels and solar lighting quarterly. Solar panels must be washed free of dust with a squeegee or pressure washed at least monthly. Required to view and document the quarterly inspection at each shelter with solar lighting, verifying each light is illuminated during darkness (Use the test button on the solar lights to see if they are working during the daytime). Will provide a copy of the inspection log to the City each month following the month of last inspection.
C. Weekly Trash Collection and Disposal Services (Monday Services)
The contractor shall provide weekly trash collection and disposal services for transit trash receptacles throughout the transit system. The Contractor shall be responsible for the collection, removal, transportation, and proper disposal of all waste collected from transit trash receptacles under this contract.
Services shall include:
Emptying trash receptacles
Replacing trash liners as needed (damaged trash liners must be replaced immediately with a new liner to prevent spillage of waste) 
Collecting, transporting, and properly disposing of all waste removed from transit trash receptacles at a legally authorized solid waste facility and in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local requirements.
Cleaning and wiping exterior surfaces of receptacles
Removal of litter immediately surrounding the receptacles
Reporting damaged or overflowing receptacles to the City
The Contractor shall not place waste collected from transit stops or shelters into residential or commercial waste containers belonging to adjacent properties or businesses. The Contractor shall comply with all applicable City solid waste requirements regarding the collection, transportation, and disposal of waste generated through this contract. Nothing in this contract authorizes the Contractor to provide solid waste collection services to residential or commercial customers within the City outside the scope of this agreement.

The pressure washing shall not be so powerful as to etch the concrete or remove finishes such as paint or powder coating from bus stop amenities. Pressure washing shall not include the vehicular travel area and will be caution of traffic and foot traffic.

## Background and Purpose
On June 23, 2026, the Banning City Council adopted Resolution No. 2026-102 declaring a fiscal emergency and directing staff to implement Banning's Workout Plan to Fiscal Sustainability. As part of that effort, the City Council has directed staff to evaluate new, unrestricted General Fund revenue strategies, including a voter-approved local transactions and use tax (commonly referred to as a "sales tax") of one percent (1%).
Because the proceeds of the proposed tax would be deposited into the General Fund for general municipal purposes, with no funds legally restricted to a specific use, the measure would constitute a "general tax" under Article XIII C of the California Constitution, requiring approval by a majority (50% plus one) of voters. This differs from a "special tax" dedicated to a specific purpose, which requires two-thirds voter approval when placed on the ballot by the governing body.
The City's current combined sales tax rate is 7.75% (6.00% state, plus existing county and district components). The proposed 1% City measure would bring the combined rate to 8.75% within Banning city limits.
The City is considering placing the measure before voters at the earliest legally and practically feasible election, potentially the November 2027 election. However, the City's regularly scheduled general municipal election for members of the City Council now occurs in even-numbered years, consolidated with the statewide general election (the City's most recent general municipal election was in November 2026). Article XIII C, Section 2(b) of the California Constitution requires that a general tax election be "consolidated with a regularly scheduled general election for members of the governing body," unless the governing body declares an emergency by unanimous vote. Because November 2027 is not the City's regularly scheduled council election date, the legal availability of a November 2027 election — potentially relying on the City's declared fiscal emergency (Resolution No. 2026-102) to support a unanimous emergency finding — versus deferring to the November 2028 consolidated general election, is a threshold question that must be resolved early in this engagement (see Task 1).
The City is seeking a qualified consultant, or team of consultants, to perform all research, technical, procedural, public-education, and coordination work necessary to responsibly bring a well-supported and legally compliant measure to the ballot, and to support the City through certification and initial implementation should the City Council choose to proceed with the measure.

## Project Objectives
Through this engagement, the City seeks to:
Determine, through non-partisan community and voter research, whether likely voters are prepared to support a general-purpose transactions and use tax in November 2027 (or the next feasible election), and at what rate and structure.
Confirm the legal and procedural feasibility of a November 2027 election date, including the emergency-declaration analysis described above, and identify a recommended election date.
Prepare the technical analyses, revenue projections, and CDTFA (California Department of Tax and Fee Administration) coordination necessary to support a legally defensible ordinance and ballot measure for City Council’s consideration.
The following objectives are subject to City Council approval to place the measure on the ballot:
Support the City Attorney in drafting the enabling ordinance, ballot resolution(s), ballot question, and related procedural documents required under the Elections Code and Revenue and Taxation Code.
Design and execute a public education and community engagement program that complies with Government Code Section 54964 (factual and informational only; no advocacy using public funds).
Coordinate all logistics, deadlines, and cost estimates with the Riverside County Registrar of Voters and the City Clerk to ensure timely, compliant ballot placement.
Support the City through election-night reporting, canvass, certification, and initial implementation, including CDTFA registration and revenue-allocation guidance.

 If the City Council does not approve moving forward with the measure, the consultant shall have no obligation to complete these tasks.

## Task 2 — Community and Voter Research 
Design and administer a statistically valid baseline survey of likely City voters (generally 400–600 completed interviews) measuring awareness of the City's fiscal condition, baseline support/opposition for a sales tax measure, sensitivity to rate (e.g., 0.75% vs. 1.0%), and the relative persuasiveness of potential priorities (public safety, streets and infrastructure, parks and recreation, fiscal stability/reserves, etc.).
Test candidate messaging and, if warranted by initial results, conduct a follow-up or tracking survey closer to the filing deadline.
Conduct stakeholder interviews and/or focus groups with community organizations, business groups, and other opinion leaders identified in coordination with the City.
Deliver a written findings report, including a clear recommendation on whether to proceed, and on rate and structure, presented at a public City Council meeting.

Prepare multi-year revenue projections for the proposed 1% rate (and, if survey results in Task 2 warrant, alternative rates), using taxable sales data and CDTFA allocation methodology, including a downside/sensitivity scenario.
Prepare a comparative analysis of transactions and use tax rates and structures — general versus special tax, sunset clause versus permanent, and general-purpose versus a general tax paired with a non-binding advisory expenditure measure — used by comparable Riverside County and Inland Empire jurisdictions.
Analyze the fiscal and service-level impact of the measure succeeding versus failing, tied to the City's Workout Plan to Fiscal Sustainability, for use in Council staff reports and public education materials.
Deliver a rate and structure recommendation memorandum to the City Manager and City Council.

The City will provide access to relevant financial data, taxable sales reports (to the extent available), and prior budget and audited financial statements.
The City will designate staff liaison(s) in the Finance Department and City Manager's Office as the consultant's primary points of contact.
The City Attorney retains final review and approval authority over all legal instruments (ordinances, resolutions, ballot questions) and all public-facing educational materials.

In addition to the City’s standard RFP submission requirements, proposals shall include:

Government Code Section 54964 prohibits the use of public funds to support or oppose the approval or rejection of a ballot measure. ## SECTION 3 - AWARD AND EXECUTION OF CONTRACT
3-01 AWARD OF CONTRACT OR REJECTION OF PROPOSALS
No bidder may withdraw their Bid Proposal for a period of sixty (60) days after the date set for the opening of bids. The contract for the work will either be awarded or the bids rejected by the City.
The contract for the work, if awarded, will be awarded to the lowest responsible bidder whose proposal complies with all requirements prescribed and with the Notice Inviting Bids. The City, however, reserves the right to select the schedules under which bids are to be compared, to reject any or all bids, and to waive any irregularity, discrepancies or technical errors in the bids received. If, in the opinion of the City, a bid is unbalanced or if the bidder is not responsible, it shall be considered sufficient grounds for rejection of the entire bid.
Before award of the contract, any bidder, upon request, may be required to furnish additional information regarding the bidder's financial condition and previous construction experience or such other evidence of the Contractor's qualifications as may be requested by the City.
3-02 EXECUTION OF CONTRACT
A bidder, to whom award is made, shall execute the written Agreement with the City on the form which is part of these Contract Documents, and shall furnish required bonds and insurance certificates within seven (7) days from the date of receipt of Notice of Award from the City. The Agreement, along with required bonds, Certificates of Insurance, and other documents to be executed by the Contractor, shall be executed in original-quadruplicate (4), three (3) each shall be filed with the City, and one each will be returned to the Contractor.
3-03 FAILURE TO EXECUTE THE AGREEMENT
If a bidder, to whom award is made, fails or refuses to execute the Agreement, or to furnish required bonds or insurance certificates within the time indicated in Section 3-02, the money represented by the bidder's security shall be forfeited and become the property of the City. At the discretion of the City, an award may be made to the second lowest responsible bidder. If the second lowest bidder fails to execute the Agreement, or to furnish required bonds, the City may likewise award the Agreement to the third lowest bidder. The second lowest bidder, to whom an Agreement is awarded, will then forfeit their bidder's security. If the third lowest bidder fails to execute the Agreement, or to furnish required bonds, the third lowest bidder, to whom an Agreement is awarded, will then forfeit their bidder's security.
3-04 BONDS
The successful bidder, concurrently with the execution of the Agreement, shall furnish a Payment for Labor and Materials Bond and a Faithful Performance Bond each in an amount equal to one hundred percent (100%) of the Agreement price. The successful bidder, prior to issuance of a Notice of Completion, shall furnish a Warrantee Bond in an amount equal to twenty percent (20%) of the final Agreement price. Bonds shall be furnished by surety companies satisfactory to the City on the forms furnished as a part of the Contract Documents.
Surety companies, to be acceptable to the City, must be authorized to do business and have an agent for service of process in California, and be on the accredited list of the U.S. Treasury Dept. Their bonds will be limited to such amounts as would be acceptable to the Treasury Department.
3-05 INSURANCE 
The successful bidder will be required to furnish proof of full compliance with all insurance requirements as specified in this Section. The form of certificates of insurance & endorsements required are included in the Contract Documents and should be carefully examined by bidder. No substitutions for the certificates and endorsements will be permitted. All insurers must be satisfactory to the City.

The Contractor shall not commence or continue to perform any work unless, at the Contractor's own expense, has in full force and effect, all required insurance with the companies satisfactory to the City. The Contractor shall not permit any subcontractor to perform work on this project unless the worker's compensation insurance requirements have been compiled with by such subcontractor.

Any policy inception date, continuity date, or retroactive date must be before the effective date of this agreement, and Contractor agrees to maintain continuous coverage through a period no less than three years after completion of the services required by this agreement.

Contractor shall provide Builders Risk Insurance utilizing an “All Risk” (Special Perils) coverage form, with limits equal to the completed value of the project and no coinsurance penalty provisions.

Policy shall be provided for replacement value on an "all-risk" basis. The City shall be named as Loss Payee on the policy and there shall be no coinsurance penalty provision in any such policy. Policy must include: (1) coverage for removal of debris, and insuring the buildings, structures, machinery, equipment, materials, facilities, fixtures, and all other properties constituting a part of the project; (2) coverage with limits sufficient to insure the full replacement value of any property or equipment stored either on or off the project site. Such insurance shall be on a form acceptable to City to ensure adequacy of terms and limits. Contractor shall not be required to maintain property insurance for any portion of the Project following transfer of control thereof to City.

## Contractor’s or Consultant’s Pollution Legal Liability
Pollution Coverage shall be provided on a Contractors Pollution Liability form or other form acceptable to City providing coverage for liability arising out of sudden, accidental and gradual pollution and remediation. All activities contemplated in this agreement shall be specifically scheduled on the policy as “covered operations.” The policy shall provide coverage for the hauling of waste from the project site to the final disposal location, including non-owned disposal sites.
