On-Site Visits may include inspections of records, inspections of the work site and observation of work activities, interviews of workers and others involved with the Project, and any other activities deemed necessary by the Labor Commissioner/DLSE to ensure compliance with prevailing wage requirements. The Labor Commissioner/DLSE shall have free access to any construction site or other place of labor and may obtain any information or statistics pertaining to the lawful duties of the Labor Commissioner/DLSE.
Any lawful activities conducted or any requests made by the Labor Commissioner/DLSE shall not be the basis for any delays, claims, costs, damages or liability of any kind against the District by the Contractor. Contractor and all Subcontractors shall cooperate and comply with any lawful requests by the Labor Commissioner/ DLSE. The failure of the Labor Commissioner, DLSE, or any other entity related to the Department of Industrial Relations to comply with any requirement imposed by the California Code of Regulations, Title 8, Chapter 8 shall not of itself constitute a defense to the failure to pay prevailing wages or to comply with any other obligation imposed by Division 2, Part 7, Chapter 1 of the Labor Code.
Prior to commencing any work on the Project, the Contractor shall post the required notice/poster required under the California Code of Regulations and Labor Code section 1771.4 in both English and Spanish at a conspicuous, weatherproof area at the Project site. The required notice/poster is available on the Labor Commissioner’s website.

## ARTICLE 37 PAYROLL RECORDS
Pursuant to §1776 of the Labor Code, each Contractor and Subcontractor shall keep an accurate payroll record showing the name, address, social security number, work classification and straight time and overtime hours worked each day and week, and the actual per diem wages paid to each journeyman, apprentice, worker or other employee employed by him or her in connection with the Project.
All payroll records as specified in Labor Code §1776 of the Contractor and all Subcontractors of any tier shall be certified and furnished directly to the Labor Commissioner in accordance with Labor Code §1771.4(a)(3) on a monthly basis (or more frequently if required by the District or the Labor Commissioner) and in a format prescribed by the Labor Commissioner. Payroll records as specified in Labor Code §1776 shall be certified and submitted to the District with each application for payment.  All payroll records shall be available for inspection at all reasonable hours at the principal office of the Contractor on the following basis:
A certified copy of an employee’s payroll record shall be made available for inspection or furnished to the employee or his or her authorized representative on request.
A certified copy of all payroll records shall be made available for inspection or furnished upon request to a representative of District, the Division of Labor Standards Enforcement and the Division of Apprenticeship Standards of the Department of Industrial Relations.
A certified copy of all payroll records shall be made available upon request by the public for inspection or for copies thereof. However, a request by the public shall be made through the District, the Division of Apprenticeship Standards or the Division of Labor Standards Enforcement. If the requested payroll records have not been provided pursuant to Paragraph (2) above, the requesting party shall, prior to being provided the records, reimburse the costs of the preparation by the Contractor, Subcontractors, and the entity through which the request was made. The public shall not be given access to such records at the principal office of the Contractor.
The certified payroll records shall be on forms provided by the Division of Labor Standards Enforcement or shall contain the same information as the forms provided by the Division.
The Contractor or Subcontractor(s) shall file a certified copy of all payroll records with the entity that requested such records within 10 days after receipt of a written request.
Any copy of records made available for inspection as copies and furnished upon request to the public or any public agency by the District, the Division of Apprenticeship Standards or the Division of Labor Standards Enforcement shall be marked or obliterated to prevent disclosure of an individual’s name, address and social security number. The name and address of the Contractor awarded the Contract or the Subcontractor(s) performing the Contract shall not be marked or obliterated. Any copy of records made available for inspection by, or furnished to, a joint labor-management committee established pursuant to the federal Labor Management Cooperation Act of 1978 (Section 175a of Title 29 of the United States Code) shall be marked or obliterated only to prevent disclosure of an individual’s name and social security number. Notwithstanding any other provision of law, agencies that are included in the Joint Enforcement Strike Force on the Underground Economy established pursuant to Section 329 of the Unemployment Insurance Code and other law enforcement agencies investigating violations of law shall, upon request, be provided non-redacted copies of certified payroll records.
The Contractor shall inform the District of the location of all payroll records, including the street address, city and county, and shall, within five working days, provide a notice of a change of location and address.
The Contractor or Subcontractor(s) shall have 10 days in which to comply subsequent to receipt of a written notice requesting payroll records. In the event that the Contractor or Subcontractor(s) fails to comply within the 10-day period, the Contractor or Subcontractor(s) shall, as a penalty to the District, forfeit One Hundred Dollars ($100.00) for each calendar day, or portion thereof, for each worker, until strict compliance is effectuated. Upon the request of the Division of Apprenticeship Standards or the Division of Labor Standards Enforcement, these penalties shall be withheld from progress payments then due. The Contractor is not subject to a penalty due to the failure of a Subcontractor to comply with this section.
The responsibility for compliance with this Article shall rest upon the Contractor.

## ARTICLE 38 WITHHOLDING OF CONTRACT PAYMENTS & PENALTIES
The District may withhold or delay contract payments to the Contractor and/or any Subcontractor if:
The required prevailing rate of per diem wages determined by the Director of the Department of Industrial Relations is not paid to all workers employed on the Project; or
The Contractor or Subcontractor(s) fail to submit all required certified payroll records with each application for payment, but not less than once per month; or
The Contractor or Subcontractor(s) submit incomplete or inadequate payroll records; or
The Contractor or Subcontractor(s) fail to comply with the Labor Code requirements concerning apprentices; or
The Contractor or Subcontractor(s) fail to comply with any applicable state laws governing labor on public works projects.

## ARTICLE 39 APPRENTICES
Apprentice Wages and Definitions.
 All apprentices employed by the Contractor to perform services under the Contract shall be paid the standard wage paid to apprentices under the regulations of the craft or trade at which he or she is employed, and as determined by the Director of the Department of Industrial Relations, and shall be employed only at the work of the craft or trade to which he or she is registered. Only apprentices, as defined in §3077 of the Labor Code, who are in training under apprenticeship standards that have been approved by the Chief of the Division of Apprenticeship Standards and who are parties to written apprenticeship agreements under Chapter 4 (commencing with §3070) of Division 3, are eligible to be employed under this Contract. The employment and training of each apprentice shall be in accordance with the apprenticeship standards and apprentice agreements under which he or she is training or in accordance with the rules and regulations of the California Apprenticeship Council.
Employment of Apprentices.
 Contractor agrees to comply with the requirements of Labor Code §1777.5. The Contractor awarded the Project and all Subcontractors, in performing any of the Work under the Contract or subcontract, employs workers in any apprenticeable craft or trade, the Contractor and Subcontractor shall employ apprentices in the ratio set forth in Labor Code §1777.5 and may apply to any apprenticeship program in the craft or trade that can provide apprentices to the Project site for a certificate approving the Contractor or Subcontractor under the apprenticeship standards for the employment and training of apprentices in the area or industry affected. However, the decision of the apprenticeship program to approve or deny a certificate shall be subject to review by the Administrator of Apprenticeship. The apprenticeship program or programs, upon approving the Contractor or Subcontractor, shall arrange for the dispatch of apprentices to the Contractor or Subcontractor. The Contractor or Subcontractor covered by an apprenticeship program’s standards shall not be required to submit any additional application in order to include additional public works contracts under that program. “Apprenticeable craft or trade” as used in this Article means a craft or trade determined as an apprenticeable occupation in accordance with the rules and regulations prescribed by the California Apprenticeship Council. The ratio of work performed by apprentices to journeyman employed in a particular craft or trade on the Project shall be in accordance with Labor Code §1777.5.
Submission of Contract Information.
 Prior to commencing work on the Project, the Contractor and Subcontractors shall submit contract award information to an applicable apprenticeship program that can supply apprentices to the Project and make the request for the dispatch of apprentices in accordance with the Labor Code.  The information submitted shall include an estimate of journeyman hours to be performed under the Contact, the number of apprentices proposed to be employed, and the approximate dates the apprentices would be employed. A copy of this information shall also be submitted to the District if requested. Within 60 days after concluding work on the Project, the Contractor and Subcontractors shall submit to the District, if requested, and to the apprenticeship program a verified statement of the journeyman and apprentice hours performed on the Project.
Apprentice Fund.
 The Contractor and all Subcontractors, who, in performing any of the Work under the Contract, employs journeymen or apprentices in any apprenticeable craft or trade shall contribute to the California Apprenticeship Council the same amount that the director determines is the prevailing amount of apprenticeship training contributions in the area of the Project. The Contractor and Subcontractors may take as a credit for payments to the Council any amounts paid by the Contractor or Subcontractor to an approved apprenticeship program that can supply apprentices to the Project. The Contractor and Subcontractors may add the amount of the contributions in computing his or her bid for the Contract.
Prime Contractor Compliance.
 The responsibility of compliance with this Article and §1777.5 of the Labor Code for all apprenticeable occupations is with the Prime Contractor. Any Contractor or Subcontractor that knowingly violates the provisions of this Article or Labor Code §1777.5 shall be subject to the penalties set forth in Labor Code §1777.7.

## ARTICLE 40 PROTECTION OF PERSONS AND PROPERTY
The Contractor shall be responsible for all damages to persons or property that occur as a result of its fault or negligence in connection with the prosecution of this Contract and shall take all necessary measures and be responsible for the proper care and protection of all materials delivered and Work performed until Final Completion and final acceptance by the District. All Work shall be solely at the Contractor’s risk, with the exception of damage to the Work caused by “acts of God” as defined in Government Code section 4151(b). Contractor’s liability for any injury or damage proximately caused by any “act of God” shall be limited to five percent (5%) of the Contract Price pursuant to Government Code section 4150.
Contractor shall take, and require Subcontractor to take, all necessary precautions for safety of workers on the Project and shall comply with all applicable federal, state, local and other safety laws, standards, orders, rules, regulations, and building codes to prevent accidents or injury to persons on, about, or adjacent to premises where Work is being performed and to provide a safe and healthful place of employment. In addition to meeting all requirements of OSHA, Cal-OSHA, state, and local codes, Contractor shall furnish, erect and properly maintain at all times, as directed by District or Architect or required by conditions and progress of Work, all necessary safety devices, safeguards, construction canopies, signs, audible devices for protection of the blind, safety rails, belts and nets, barriers, lights, and watchmen for protection of workers and the public and shall post danger signs warning against hazards created by such features in the course of construction. Contractor shall designate a responsible member of its organization on the Project, whose duty shall be to post information regarding protection and obligations of workers and other notices required under occupational safety and health laws, to comply with reporting and other occupational safety requirements, and to protect the life, safety and health of workers. Name and position of person so designated shall be reported to District by Contractor. Contractor shall correct any violations of safety laws, rules, orders, standards, or regulations. Upon the issuance of a citation or notice of violation by the Division of Occupational Safety and Health, such violation shall be corrected promptly.
In an emergency affecting safety of life, of Work, or of adjoining property, Contractor, without special instruction or authorization from Architect or District, is hereby permitted to act, at its discretion, to prevent such threatened loss or injury; and Contractor shall so act if so authorized or instructed by Architect or District. District will not hold Contractor liable for damages proximately caused by Contractor’s actions if such actions were reasonably necessary to prevent loss of life or injury to person or damage to Work or adjoining property. Any compensation claimed by Contractor on account of emergency work shall be determined by agreement.
Contractor shall provide such heat, cooling, covering, and enclosures as are necessary to protect all Work, materials, equipment, appliances, and tools against damage by weather conditions.
Contractor shall take adequate precautions to protect existing roads, sidewalks, curbs, pavements, utilities, adjoining property and structures (including, without limitation, protection from settlement or loss of lateral support), and to avoid damage thereto, and repair any damage thereto caused by construction operations. All permits, licenses, or inspection fees required for such repair work shall be obtained and paid for by Contractor.
Contractor shall (unless waived by the District in writing):
When performing new construction on existing sites, become informed and take into specific account the maturity of the students on the site; and perform Work which may interfere with school routine before or after school hours, enclose working area with a substantial barricade, and arrange Work to cause a minimum amount of inconvenience and danger to students and faculty in their regular school activities. The Contractor shall comply with specifications and directives of the District regarding the timing of certain construction activities in order to avoid unnecessary interference with school functioning.
Provide substantial barricades around any shrubs or trees indicated to be preserved.
Deliver materials to building area over route designated by Architect of District.
Take preventive measures to eliminate objectionable dust.
Confine apparatus, the storage of materials, and the operations of workers to limits indicated by law, ordinances, permits or directions of Architect; and shall not interfere with the Work or unreasonably encumber premises or overload any structure with materials; and enforce all instructions of District and Architect regarding signs, advertising, fires, and smoking and require that all workers comply with all regulations while on construction site.
Take care to prevent disturbing or covering any survey markers, monuments, or other devices marking property boundaries or corners. If such markers are disturbed by accident, they shall be replaced by an approved land surveyor or civil engineer and all maps and records required therefrom shall be filed with county and local authorities, at no cost to the District. All filing and plan check fees shall be paid by Contractor.

## ARTICLE 43 CONTRACTOR CLAIMS & DISPUTES
Decision of Architect.
 “Disputes” or “Claims” as defined in Articles 1 and 44 between District and Contractor involving money or time, including those alleging an error or omission by the Architect shall be referred initially to the Architect for action as provided in Article 43.B within ten (10) days after Contractor’s Article 46 request for change or extra Work is denied. If there is a construction manager (CM), the CM shall receive the Dispute and may review and also assemble opinions and documents to assist the Architect. A decision by the Architect, as provided in Article 43.B, shall be required as a condition precedent to proceeding with remedies set forth in Article 44 as to all such matters arising prior to the date Retention Payment Application is due, regardless of whether such matters relate to execution and progress of the Work, or the extent to which the Work has reached completion. The condition precedent of an Architect decision shall be waived if: (1) the position of Architect is vacant; (2) the Architect has failed to take action required under Article 43.E within the time periods required therein; or (3) the Dispute or Claim relates to a stop notice claim not arising from any extra Change Order/ Construction Change Document or directive for which approval has not been provided.
Architect’s Review.
 The Architect (and CM) will review the Dispute and take one or more of the following preliminary actions upon receipt of a Dispute: (1) request additional supporting data from the claimant; (2) submit a schedule to the parties indicating when the Architect expects to take action; (3) reject the Dispute in whole or in part, stating reasons for rejection; (4) recommend approval of the Dispute; or (5) suggest a compromise. The Architect may also, but is not obligated to, notify the surety of the nature and amount of the Dispute. Architect review of Disputes and Claims shall be impartial and meant to resolve Disputes and Claims. Pursuant to the case, Huber, Hunt & Nichols, Inc. v. Moore (1977) 67 Cal.App.3d 278, the Architect is provided a quasi-judicial immunity for interpreting and deciding Disputes and Claims between the District and Contractor.
Documentation if Resolved.
 If a Dispute has been resolved, the Architect (and/or CM) will prepare a Change Order or obtain appropriate documentation to document the terms for Board approval.
Actions if Not Resolved.
 If a Dispute has not been resolved pursuant to Article 43.B, the Contractor shall, within ten (10) days after the Architect’s initial response, assemble all the documents involved in the Dispute including copies of all back-up documentation of costs and the basis for the Dispute and take one or more of the following actions: (1) modify the initial Dispute; (2) notify the Architect that the initial Dispute stands; or (3) supplement with additional supporting data and re-submit to the Architect under Article 43.B.
Architect’s Written Decision.
 If a Dispute has not been resolved after consideration of the foregoing and of other evidence presented by the parties or requested by the Architect, the Architect (or Architect through CM) shall provide a written decision twenty (20) days after compliance with Article 43.D. Upon expiration of such time period, the Architect (or Architect through CM) will render to the parties its written decision relative to the Dispute, including any change in the Contract Price or Contract Time or both. The Architect may also request reasonable additional time to complete Architect’s written decision. If the resolution of the Dispute by the Architect is not satisfactory to the Contractor and copies of all back-up documentation of costs and the basis for the Dispute is fully articulated in a package of material that is complete, the Contractor may then submit a Claim to the District under Article 44.
Continuing Contract Performance.
 Pending final resolution of a Dispute or Claim, including, negotiation, mediation, arbitration, or litigation, the Contractor shall proceed diligently with performance of the Contract, and the District shall continue to make any undisputed payments in accordance with the Contract (less any withholdings or offsets). If the Claim is not resolved, Contractor agrees it will neither rescind the Contract nor stop the progress of the Work, but Contractor’s sole remedy shall be to submit such controversy to determination by a court of competent jurisdiction in the county where the Project is located, after the Project has been Completed, and not before.
Claims for Extension of Time.
 If Contractor and District cannot agree upon an extension of time, whether compensable or not, then Contractor must have first completed the procedures set forth in Article 50. Upon completion of the procedures set forth under Article 50, Contractor must then comply with the requirements in this Article including those set forth under Article 44.

## ARTICLE 44 CLAIMS PROCEDURES & REQUIREMENTS
Pursuant to the remedies under Public Contract Code section 9201 and Government Code section 930.2, Contractor, through execution of this Agreement, also agrees to comply with the Claims requirements of this Article to quickly and efficiently resolve Disputes and Claims. Further, to provide a level of accuracy to the records submitted, the District shall have the right to audit books and records based on the actual costs incurred and to reduce the uncertainty in resolving Disputes and Claims with limited information.
Procedures and Requirements Applicable to all Claims.
Definition of Claim:
 A “Claim” is where a Dispute between the parties rises to the level where backup documentation is assembled and provided to the District as a separate demand by the Contractor for: (a) a time extension, including, without limitation, for relief from damages or penalties for delay assessed by the District under the Contract; (b) payment by the District of money or damages arising from Work done by, or on behalf of, the Contractor pursuant to the Contract and payment for which is not otherwise expressly provided for or to which the Contractor is not otherwise entitled to; or (3) an amount of payment disputed by the District.
Filing Claim is Not Basis To Discontinue Work:
 The Contractor shall promptly comply with Work under the Contract or Work requested by the District even though a written Claim has been filed. The Contractor and the District shall make good faith efforts to resolve any and all Claims that may arise during the performance of the Work covered by this Contract.
Claim Notification:
 The Contractor shall within seven (7) calendar days after the written decision of the Architect, or if the time period for Architect’s decision has passed under Article 43.E, submit a notification in writing sent by registered mail or certified mail with return receipt requested, with the District (and the District’s CM) stating clearly the basis for the Claim and including all relevant and required documents. If the notification is not submitted within seven (7) days after the written decision of the Architect or the passage of time under Article 43.E, the Contractor shall be deemed to have waived all right to assert the Claim, and the Claim shall be denied. Claims submitted after the Retention Payment date shall also be considered null and void by the District. All Claims shall be reviewed pursuant to Articles 43.A through 43.E.
The Formal Notification of Claim must be presented as follows:
The term “Claim” must be at the top of the page in no smaller than 20 point writing.
All documentation submitted pursuant to this Article to the Architect shall be submitted with the “Claim.”
A stack of documents, copy of all Project documents, or the submission of random documents shall not constitute an adequate reference to supporting documentation.
Any additional or supporting documentation that Contractor believes is relevant should be submitted at this time.
Reasonable Documents to Support Claim:
 The Contractor shall furnish reasonable documentation to support the Claim. The Contractor shall provide all written detailed documentation which supports the Claim, including but not limited to: arguments, justifications, cost, estimates, Schedule analysis and detailed documentation. The format of the required reasonable supporting documentation to support the Claim shall include, without limitation:
Cover letter.
Summary of factual basis of Claim and amount of Claim.
Summary of the basis of the Claim, including the specific clause and section under the Contract under which the Claim is made.
Documents relating to the Claim, including:
Specifications sections in question.
Relevant portions of the plans/drawings.
Applicable Clarifications (RFI’s).
Other relevant information, including responses that were received.
Contractor Analysis of Claim merit including Contractor’s analysis of any Subcontractor Claims that are being passed through, any analysis performed by outside consultants, and any legal analysis that Contractor deems relevant.
Break down of all costs associated with the Claim. For Claims relating to time extensions, an analysis and supporting documentation evidencing any effect upon the critical path in conformance with the requirements of Article 50 shall be included along with a chronology of events and related correspondence.
Applicable daily reports and logs. If the daily reports or logs are not available, lost or destroyed, there shall be a presumption that the lost documentation was unfavorable to the Contractor. See California Civil Jury Instruction 204.
For Claims involving overhead, cost escalation, acceleration, disruption or increased costs, a full version of job costs reports organized by category of work or Schedule of Values with budget information tracked against actual costs. Any and all supporting back-up data, including the original bid (and associated original unaltered metadata). The metadata and bid information shall be provided confidentially and subject to a protective order to prevent dissemination to other contractors or to the public. However, the bid documentation should remain intact and available for review and inspection in case of this type of increased cost Claim. This data on the bid shall be made available to any District attorneys or experts and shall also be utilized as evidence for any legal proceedings. If the bid documentation is not available, lost or destroyed, there shall be a presumption that the lost bid documentation was unfavorable to the Contractor. See California Civil Jury Instruction 204.
Certification:
 The Contractor (and Subcontractors, if applicable) shall submit with the Claim a certification under penalty of perjury:
That the Contractor has reviewed the Claim and that such Claim is made in good faith;
Supporting data are accurate and complete to the best of the Contractor’s knowledge and belief;
The amount requested accurately reflects the amount of compensation for which the Contractor believes the District is liable; and
That the Contractor is familiar with Government Code section 12650 et seq. and Penal Code section 72, and that false claims can lead to substantial fines and/or imprisonment.
Signature of Certification:
 If the Contractor is not an individual, the certification shall be executed by an officer or general partner of the Contractor having overall responsibility for the conduct of the Contractor’s affairs.
Upon receipt of a Claim and all supporting documents as required above, the District shall conduct a reasonable review of the Claim and, within a period not to exceed 45 days, shall provide the Contractor a written statement identifying what portion of the Claim is disputed and what portion is undisputed. Upon receipt of a Claim, the District and Contractor may, by mutual agreement, extend the time period provided in this paragraph.
If the District needs approval from its governing Board to provide the Contractor a written statement identifying the disputed portion and the undisputed portion of the Claim, and the governing Board does not meet within the 45 days or within the mutually agreed to extension of time following receipt of a Claim sent by registered mail or certified mail, return receipt requested, the District shall have up to three days following the next duly publicly noticed meeting of the governing Board after the 45-day period, or extension, expires to provide the Contractor a written statement identifying the disputed portion and the undisputed portion.
Any payment due on an undisputed portion of the Claim shall be processed and made within 60 days after the District issues its written statement. If the District fails to issue a written statement, paragraph o below shall apply.
If the Contractor disputes the District’s written response, or if the District fails to respond to a Claim issued pursuant to this Article within the time prescribed, the Contractor may demand in writing an informal conference to meet and confer for settlement of the issues in dispute. Upon receipt of a demand in writing sent by registered mail or certified mail, return receipt requested, the District shall schedule a meet and confer conference within 30 days for settlement of the Claim.
Within 10 business days following the conclusion of the meet and confer conference, if the Claim or any portion of the Claim remains in dispute, the District shall provide the Contractor a written statement identifying the portion of the Claim that remains in dispute and the portion that is undisputed. Any payment due on an undisputed portion of the Claim shall be processed and made within 60 days after the District issues its written statement. Any disputed portion of the Claim, as identified by the Contractor in writing, shall be submitted to nonbinding mediation, with the District and the Contractor sharing the associated costs equally. The District and Contractor shall mutually agree to a mediator within 10 business days after the disputed portion of the Claim has been identified in writing. If the parties cannot agree upon a mediator, each party shall select a mediator and those mediators shall select a qualified neutral third party to mediate with regard to the disputed portion of the Claim. Each party shall bear the fees and costs charged by its respective mediator in connection with the selection of the neutral mediator. If mediation is unsuccessful, the parts of the Claim remaining in dispute shall be subject to applicable procedures in Article 44.D.
For purposes of this Article, mediation includes any nonbinding process, including, but not limited to, neutral evaluation or a dispute review board, in which an independent third party or board assists the parties in dispute resolution through negotiation or by issuance of an evaluation. Any mediation utilized shall conform to the timeframes in this section.
Unless otherwise agreed to by the District and the Contractor in writing, the mediation conducted pursuant to this Article shall excuse any further obligation under Section 20104.4 to mediate after litigation has been commenced.
This Claims process does not preclude the District from requiring arbitration of disputes under private arbitration or the Public Works Contract Arbitration Program, if mediation under this Article does not resolve the parties’ Claim. This Claims process does not preclude the District from submitting individual Disputes or Claims to binding arbitration pursuant to Article 44.C below.
Failure by the District to respond to a Claim from the Contractor within the time periods described in this subdivision or to otherwise meet the time requirements of this Article shall result in the Claim being deemed rejected in its entirety. A Claim that is denied by reason of the District’s failure to have responded to a Claim, or its failure to otherwise meet the time requirements of this Article, shall not constitute an adverse finding with regard to the merits of the Claim or the responsibility or qualifications of the Contractor.
If a Subcontractor or a lower tier subcontractor lacks legal standing to assert a Claim against a District because privity of contract does not exist, the Contractor may present to the District a Claim on behalf of a Subcontractor or lower tier subcontractor. A Subcontractor may request in writing, either on his or her own behalf or on behalf of a lower tier subcontractor, that the Contractor present a Claim for Work which was performed by the Subcontractor or by a lower tier subcontractor on behalf of the Subcontractor. The Subcontractor requesting that the Claim be presented to the District shall furnish reasonable documentation to support the Claim. Within 45 days of receipt of this written request, the Contractor shall notify the Subcontractor in writing as to whether the Contractor presented the Claim to the District and, if the Contractor did not present the Claim, provide the Subcontractor with a statement of the reasons for not having done so.
Upon receipt of a Claim, the parties may mutually agree to waive, in writing, mediation and proceed directly to the commencement of a civil action or binding arbitration, as applicable.
The Contractor’s Claim shall be denied if it fails to follow the requirements of this Article
Within thirty (30) days of receipt of the Claim and the information under this Article, the District may request in writing any additional documentation supporting the Claim or documentation relating to defenses to the Claim which the District may assert. If additional documents are required, the time in which the Claim is evaluated may be extended by a reasonable time so the Claim and additional documents may be reviewed
Claims Procedures in Addition to Government Code Claim.
 Nothing in the Disputes and Claims procedures set forth in Articles 43 and 44 or other provisions in the General Conditions shall act to waive or relieve the Contractor from meeting the requirements set forth in Government Code section 900 et seq.
Binding Arbitration of Individual Claim Issues.
 At the District’s sole option, the District may submit individual disputes, or claims, to binding arbitration and Contractor agrees to the resolution determined for each individual dispute by Arbitrator, including resolution of time and delays. If binding arbitration is utilized, such resolution is a full and final resolution of the particular claim or dispute. Under no circumstances may the Contractor stop work, rescind its contract or otherwise slow the progress of Work during resolution of individual claims in binding Arbitration. This individual dispute arbitration process is not an arbitration clause and shall not be construed as an agreement to arbitrate. This individual disputes arbitration process is for the sole purpose of streamlining and resolving disputes or claims during construction and shall be requested on specific individual items by the District prior to Completion of the Project.
Resolution of Disputes in Court of Competent Jurisdiction.
 If Claims are not resolved under the procedure set forth and pursuant to Articles 43 and 44, such Claim or controversy shall be submitted to a court in the county of competent jurisdiction after the Project has been Completed, and not before.
Warranties, Guarantees and Obligations.
 The duties and obligations imposed by these General Conditions and the rights and remedies available hereunder to the parties hereto, and, in particular but without limitation, the warranties, guarantees and obligations imposed upon Contractor by the General Conditions and amendments thereto; and all of the rights and remedies available to District and Architect thereunder, are in addition to, and are not to be construed in any way as a limitation of, any rights and remedies available to any or all of them which are otherwise imposed or available by laws or regulations by special warranty or guarantee or by other provisions of the Contract Documents, and the provisions of this Article will be as effective as if repeated specifically in the Contract Documents in connection with each particular duty, obligation, right and remedy to which they apply.

## ARTICLE 45 PAYMENTS TO CONTRACTOR
Unless otherwise specified, each month within thirty (30) days after approval of the Request for Payment, Contractor shall be paid a sum equal to ninety-five percent (95%) of the value of the Work performed (as certified by Architect and Inspector and verified by Contractor) up to the last day of the previous month, less the aggregate of previous payments. The value of the Work completed shall be the Contractor’s best estimate. ## Scope of Work
Project Overview: 
The City of Hayward (the “City”) is seeking industry feedback regarding the feasibility, attractiveness, and potential delivery structure for a proposed public-private partnership (“P3”) project. This market sounding is for informational purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation or commitment by the City.
Project Description:
1. Project Background:

The existing Hayward Police Headquarters at 300 West Winton Avenue no longer meets the space, operational, staffing and security requirements for the Hayward Police Department (the “HPD”).  Built in 1975 when the population was approximately 93,000 and HPD staffing was 110, the existing HPD facility is near the end of its useful life and functionally obsolete. The existing facility is undersized, poorly configured, outdated, and requires security and technology improvements to meet HPD’s current needs. The City’s population has grown by 75% at 163,000 and staffing has increased to 334. Operational and space-related deficiencies include:

•	Insufficient operational spaces for staff and no public meeting spaces;
•	Inadequate separation of public, secure, and restricted circulation zones;
•	Limited public waiting, queuing, and interview areas;
•	Insufficient juvenile interview and detention facilities;
•	Inadequate file and equipment storage;
•	Inefficient departmental layouts, with key functions located at inefficient distances from each other; and
•	Outdated holding and booking facilities for detainees.
 
Building system deficiencies include:

•	Need for more energy-efficient mechanical and electrical systems;
•	Required ADA upgrades;
•	Building issues, including leaks into sensitive technology rooms;
•	Old sewer and plumbing systems that fail regularly;
•	Multiple temporary, portable structures used for police functions;
•	Lack of exterior standoff distances for security and blast threats;
•	Inadequate site parking for departmental and staff vehicles;
•	Inadequate square footage for today’s needs; and
•	Inadequate Communications Center.

2. Project Characteristics: 

A new Public Safety Center (“PSC”, the “Project”) is needed to address the deficiencies described above. The Project is anticipated to include the following features:
•	Police Headquarters;
•	Jail;
•	Indoor shooting range;
•	Increased services for the Youth and Family Services Bureau; 
•	Animal services relocated into the new PSC;
•	Crime Scene Technician Lab integrated into the new PSC; and
•	Some satellite campuses tasks relocated to the new PSC.

The City contracted with LPA, Inc., to develop a conceptual design detailing the programming, space needs, site analysis, and initial cost estimate of the Project. Project space needs were projected to accommodate staffing growth through the year 2050 that is allocated as follows:

•	91,000 gsf essential services building (Public space, Space for Administration staff & all HPD divisions, crime lab, dispatch, jail and shared staff areas);
•	30,000 gsf non-essential services building (K9, Special Response Unit, Property & Evidence, Indoor Range);
•	29,000 gsf animal services building;
•	100-yard outdoor range;
•	Tactical Simulation Building; and
•	Parking for staff and Police vehicles.

The City identified the former California Air National Guard (“CANG”) site located at the Hayward Executive Airport (1535 West Winton Avenue and Tuskegee Airmen Drive) as the potential Project site. The City designated approximately eight to ten acres of the eastern half of the 16.8-acre CANG site for this purpose. The remaining portion of the site should remain available for Hayward Executive Airport development.

3. Funding: 

The original cost estimate for the PSC to be constructed at the CANG site utilizing Design-Bid-Build delivery method was as follows:

Buildings & Parking Structure	$212 million
Site Work, including outdoor range and tactical simulation building    	$53 million
Soft Cost		$72 million
Project Total 	    	$337 million

Since the Project cost estimate for the original program exceeded the funding identified in the City’s Capital Improvement Program, the Project was re-evaluated to prioritize programming and reduce scope that could be completed in a future phase. Since the current allocated funding is short of the estimated cost, the City is open to downsizing the project as follows; however, giving higher priorities to services with *: 

•	Animal Services* - removed from the Project with the option to be included in a later phase or located at an alternative site;
•	Public Spaces* - reduction of the public lobby space and removal of one of the community meeting rooms;
•	Youth & Family Services Bureau* - reductions include the removal of the overflow counseling rooms, the waiting room, and the dedicated breakroom;
•	Workstations- spaces reduced while maintaining all functionality;
•	Firearms Training - indoor firearms range reduced to a 25-yard range (originally planned to be 50 yards). The 100-yard outdoor range is included in the Project (at the CANG site) with a four lane 50-yard outdoor range planned for a future phase. The tactical simulation building is re-allocated to a future phase;
•	Property & Evidence - reduction in the number of workstations, drying cabinets, and evidence lockers;
•	K-9 - removed and re-allocated to a future phase;
•	Special Response Unit - the unit’s dedicated briefing room was removed from the
Project scope with the assumption the unit could use the patrol briefing room when needed;
•	Jail - a reduction in storage space, kitchen size, and number of cells. This reduced the maximum capacity of the jail from 49 people to 35 people;
•	Communications Center - reduction in the size of the break room and the number of dispatch consoles from 16 to 14; and
•	Vehicle Exam – reduction of the exam bay from 2 to 1.

With the above prioritized programming, the Project’s total cost at the CANG site is now estimated at $247 million.  Both the original and prioritized programming/space needs are open for further consideration.

The City is considering engaging Developers, Equity Investors, Contractors within the next 6-18 months under a pre-development structure to work collaboratively to advance scope, funding and financial feasibility for a future P3 project. The City has sufficient funding available to fund a staged pre-development phase, but as noted above, the City is continuing to pursue funding for the capital aspects of the Project.

## Scope of Work
The City will manage the outage, including scheduling, switching, and lockout/tagout. The Contractor shall coordinate all removal, transportation, repair, delivery, installation, and startup activities.
The City will de-energize and disconnect the transformer before rigging and shipping by the Contractor.
Provide a detailed work plan before beginning work, including the anticipated time the transformer will be out of service, lifting/rigging plan, transportation plan, safety procedures, and sequence for removal and reinstallation.
After the City has disconnected the transformer, rig, remove, transport, repair, return, reinstall, reconnect, test, and place the transformer into service. The Contractor shall protect the transformer and surrounding equipment from damage throughout the work. Include insurance coverage during transit.
Replace the transformer windings with new copper windings and provide new insulation materials appropriate for the transformer’s voltage, kVA rating, cooling class, and service conditions.
Restore the transformer to its specified ratings, including 12,000-480Y/277 V operation, 1,500/1,680/1,932 kVA rating, KNAN/KNAF cooling, and 5.67% impedance.
Supply and install new Envirotemp FR3 dielectric fluid (approximately 466 gallons).
Process, vacuum-fill, and test the transformer fluid in accordance with the fluid manufacturer’s recommendations and applicable industry standards.
Clean, prepare, and paint the transformer exterior with a durable light-gray finish
 (ANSI 70 or City approved equal) s
uitable for outdoor industrial service. Repair or replace damaged labels, warning signs, and nameplates as necessary.
Inspect, test, and document the condition of the existing gauges, tap changer, cooling fans, control box, bushings, and associated accessories.
Components found to be in acceptable working condition may be reused.
Components found to be defective or unsuitable for reuse shall be identified promptly. The Contractor shall provide the City with the proposed replacement cost for review and written authorization prior to replacement.
Replace authorized defective components with new components compatible with the transformer and suitable for its voltage, cooling, and operating conditions.
Ensure all work conforms to the transformer manufacturer’s requirements, applicable IEEE standards, NETA acceptance-testing requirements, NFPA 70, and the California Electrical Code.
Provide all required lifting, rigging, crane support, temporary protection, and traffic/site control necessary to complete the work safely.
3.2.A. Before return to service, the Contractor shall perform and document, at minimum, the following tests as applicable to the repair:
Turns-ratio and polarity tests
Winding-resistance test
Insulation-resistance and polarization-index tests
Power-factor/dissipation-factor testing of windings and bushings
Transformer oil/fluid dielectric-strength and moisture testing
Verification of tap-changer operation and tap settings
Functional testing of gauges, alarms, cooling fans, controls, and associated protective devices
Temperature rise test, or document equivalent, if required by the City
Phase rotation and voltage verification
No-load energization and operational startup testing
Verification that the completed transformer impedance is 5.67%, within applicable manufacturing tolerances
Dissolved gas test 30 days after the transformer is back in service
Prior to completion of work:
Thoroughly clean the transformer and work area
Repair damage to finishes with products recommended by the manufacturer
Remove all debris
Provide a walkthrough and training for City staff on the refurbished transformer's gauges, alarms, fans, and maintenance.
3.2.B. Before the work begins the Contractor shall provide the following:
Detailed work plan, including the requested outage window and duration for the City-managed outage
Lifting/rigging and transportation plan
Repair procedure and quality-control plan
List of proposed materials and replacement components
Schedule
Safety plan
Shop/facility testing plan
3.2.C. Before final acceptance, the Contractor shall provide:
Complete test reports and test data
Repair summary identifying all replaced and reused components
Fluid certification and test results
Final transformer nameplate data, if revised
Warranty information: minimum one-year warranty on parts and workmanship from the date of acceptance
Operations and maintenance information for new or replaced components
Startup report and recommended maintenance requirements

Description:

. ## CCTV NVR Hardware Refresh
1. Project Overview
The objective of this project is to upgrade and replace aging Network Video Recorder (NVR) compute infrastructure across five locations. The current hardware consists of mixed operating systems (Windows 10 Pro and Windows Server) and varying levels of compute resources. The vendor will be responsible for assessing site conditions, procuring, configuring, and migrating operations to new enterprise grade hardware for four locations, and performing a RAM upgrade on one existing server. A critical requirement is ensuring all hardware is fully certified for and compatible with the latest version of Milestone XProtect, and configuring the new servers to seamlessly archive to the City's existing Network Attached Storage (NAS). We are currently on Milestone version 2019R1 and need to upgrade to the newest Milestone version, which will also be done during the hardware upgrade ( new licensing for the new Milestone version has already been purchased by the City).
2. Hardware & Architecture Requirements
To ensure longevity, investment protection, and full compatibility with milestone Protect(both current and future releases), it is the vendors responsibility to verify that all proposed NVR hardware, drivers, and operating systems meet or exceed the following baseline criteria:
Operating System:
 Transition away from Windows 10 Pro to a Windows Operating System based on specific location needs. The specific version of Windows is to be recommended by the vendor and approved by the city, ensuring it represents the best practice for the current Milestone deployment.
Processor:
 An Intel processor or equivalent with sufficient processing power to handle the latest Milestone version and the specific workload demands of each server. Support for Intel Quick Sync Video is highly recommended if hardware accelerated video motion detection is utilized.
3. Site-Specific Scope of Work
3.1. Skate Park (13 cameras)
Current Hardware:
 Dell PowerEdge T140 | OS: Windows Server 2019 Standard | SN: CT2FVD3
Action:
 
Full Replacement.
Deliverables:
 Decommission the existing PowerEdge T140. Provision and install a new tower or short-depth rack server Migrate Milestone configurations and ensure proper storage mapping to the existing NAS for long-term archiving.
3.2. Sports Park (33 cameras)
Current Hardware:
 Dell PowerEdge R7460XS | OS: Windows Server 2022 Standard | SN: GQM4Q54
Action:
 
RAM Upgrade Only.
Deliverables:
 Audit current memory configuration and topology. Procure and install compatible ECC RDIMMs to meet the requested RAM target of 64GB. Verify memory health in iDRAC and ensure OS/Milestone recognizes the expanded capacity.
3.3. Heroes Park (7 cameras)
Current Hardware:
 | OS: Windows 10 Pro | RAM: 8GB
Action:
 
Full Replacement (Hardware to be recommended by Vendor).
Deliverables:
 Vendor must recommend and evaluate the environmental and spatial constraints of the current network enclosure. Based on this assessment, replace the existing hardware with the most appropriate enterprise-grade form factor that meets Milestone compute requirements. Upgrade OS licensing to a vendor-recommended and city-approved Windows edition if needed based on the location's concurrent connection and processing demands. Connect to the existing NAS target.
3.4. El Toro Park (4 Cameras)
Current Hardware:
| OS: Windows 10 Pro | RAM: 8GB
Action:
 
Full Replacement (Hardware to be recommended by Vendor).
Deliverables:
 Vendor must recommend and evaluate the environmental and spatial constraints of the current network enclosure. Based on this assessment, replace the existing hardware with the most appropriate enterprise-grade form factor that meets Milestone compute requirements. Upgrade OS licensing to a vendor-recommended and city-approved Windows edition if needed based on the location's demands. Migrate all camera streams and integrate seamlessly into the centralized Milestone Management Server, configuring archive paths to the NAS.
3.5. City Hall Civic Center (67 Cameras)
Current Hardware:
 2x Dell PowerEdge R540 | OS: Windows 10 Pro | SN: JDF60W2, JDF50W2
Action:
 
Full Replacement of Both Units.
Deliverables:
 Replace the two legacy R540s with current-generation hardware optimized for compute and storage. Upgrade OS licensing to a vendor-recommended and city-approved Windows edition. Configure load balancing or failover within Milestone if the two servers operate in a cluster, and verify archiving to the NAS.
4. Vendor Execution & Migration Responsibilities
Pre-Deployment Site Walk & Audit:
 The selected vendor is required to conduct a physical site visit to inspect all current devices and installation environments across all locations. Based on this inspection and the City's operational needs outlined in this SOW, the vendor will provide final hardware and OS recommendations for each site. Once approved, the vendor must export current Milestone configuration backups (.bcp) prior to initiating any hardware changes.
NAS Integration & Archiving:
 Vendor is responsible for mapping the required shares from the City's existing NAS to the new server environments and configuring Milestone's archiving schedules to handle the two year retention offload.
IP & Networking:
 Retain or properly document all static IP assignments for the recording servers so that camera streams reconnect without requiring camera-side reconfiguration.
Testing & Sign-off:
 Verify all camera feeds, motion detection rules, local live-buffer recording, NAS archive integrity, and client connectivity (Smart Client/Web Client) are functioning correctly under the new hardware.
Equipment:
 No refurbished or used equipment can be used for this project
Milestone Compatibility Lifecycle Assurance:
 The vendor is solely responsible for ensuring that all proposed, procured, and deployed hardware, operating systems, and firmware are 100% compatible with the latest released version of Milestone XProtect at the time of installation.
Warranty and Support:
 All equipment must be covered under warranty. The selected vendor is required to provide responsive technical support throughout the operational lifecycle if needed.
Documentation: 
Provide final as-built documentation after the project is completed.

## Understanding the City's Goals
The City aims to update it's Strategic Business Plan for FY 2027-28 to FY 2033-34 by April/ May of 2027.
In an effort to do this, the City seeks a strategic planning consultant to assist with the following tasks:
Providing strategic planning workshop services for City management (executive management and department directors)
Providing strategic planning session for City middle managers and frontline staff
Conducting interviews with City's executive team and City Council members
Provide feedback on analyses produced by City staff
Format and framework for the services are not set in stone. Only broad objectives are set forth in this scope of work to allow for Consultant's expertise when submitting a response to this project request.

## City Management Strategic Planning Workshop Services
Consultant, in concurrence with City project manager, shall design and conduct a single half-day (3-4 hour) workshop with the City's Management Team (Executive Management and Department Leadership of the City, 15 total) during a Management Team Retreat which shall take place on a Wednesday date in late Fall/early Winter (October-December 2026) and should occur in person. The workshop should be designed to include the following key elements:
Identifying core services
Identifying current and future challenges
Identifying opportunities for transformational initiatives
Identifying goals as an organization and within each department
How to motivate staff and create an actionable strategic initiatives
Strategies for managing change in teams and organization-wide
Navigating internal and external pressures
Team building and collaboration activities to address current and future challenges

## City-Wide Strategic Planning Session
Consultant, in concurrence with City project manager, shall design and conduct a single 1-1.5 hour session for all City staff to take place during the lunch hour as a "Lunch and Learn" opportunity for all City staff (approximately 80 full-time employees). Session shall take place in the winter (mid December 2026 to early January 2027) and should occur in person. The session should be designed to include the following key elements:
Fundamentals of strategic planning
Defining departmental/division's purpose
Identifying core services
Difference between core services and transformational initiatives
Overview of identifying performance measures

## Interviews and Additional Optional Tasks
At the City's direction, Consultant shall assist with the following tasks, as requested:
Conduct INITIAL virtual or in person interviews with City's executive team and City Council members (Approximately 30 min each)
9 Management Team members
5 City Council members (virtual or in person shall be at the preference of each City Council member)
Objective: To identify key priorities and perspectives to help inform City priorities and high level strategies to include in the City's strategic plan
Deliverables: 
Summary/ synthesis of comments from all interviews
List of key threats, weaknesses, and "blind spots" which may not have been identified prior to interviews
Facilitate Joint Commissioners Workshop with City Commissions (OPTIONAL)
Scheduled for Tuesday, February 23, 2027, 6:30pm
2-3 hour workshop, in addition to preparation for workshop as needed, to be supported by City staff
Facilitate an exercise/activity to gather City Commissioners' input (total of 15 commissioners, 3 commissions of 5)
Facilitate Strategic Planning Workshop with City Council (OPTIONAL)
Scheduled for Tuesday, March 23, 2027, 6:30 pm
2-3 hour workshop, in addition to preparation for workshop as needed, to be supported by City staff
Facilitate an exercise/activity to gather City Councilmembers' input
Conduct FOLLOW UP virtual or in person interviews with City Council members (Approximately 30 min each)
5 City Council members (virtual or in person shall be at the preference of each City Council member)
MUST take place in late March/ early April (in preparation for Budget Workshop on Tuesday, April 27, 2027) 
Objective: To review key priorities and perspectives to help inform and adjust high level strategies in the City's strategic plan
Deliverables: 
Summary/ synthesis of comments from all interviews
Actionable insights or recommendations to shift changes to strategic initiatives

## City Responsibilities
City shall be responsible for providing all meeting facilities, supplies, and refreshments (including lunches for the Workshop and the Training).
City shall have the opportunity to provide feedback and direction for all presentation materials and content prior to the Workshop and Training. City may provide up to two (2) revisions to each presentation, as needed.

## Consultant Responsibilities
Consultant shall be responsible for all travel and transportation costs not included in the fee for services.
Consultant shall provide a summary document detailing the results of the Workshop, Training, and any interviews conducted under the optional services in this scope of services.

## Scope of Work
General Project Descriptions
The City is looking for Contract Administration and Construction Inspection ("CA/CI") services for two (2) CIP projects. The City reserves the right to select and award each project individually to a consulting firm or both projects to a single consulting firm. Therefore, the Consultant shall develop an independent proposal for CA/CI services for each CIP project, as if they were standalone projects. The Consultant shall note that the evaluation of the cost proposal will be per project and not the cumulative cost proposal from both projects.
To assist with project understanding, the City has attached 95% plans for your use (please refer to the Attachments section of this RFP). The Consultant shall use these plans to understand the intent of the project and what may be included as part of the final bid documents. The Consultant is responsible for providing a complete proposal for contract administration, construction management, and construction inspection for the listed projects below:
Project #1: Second Left-turn Lanes in All Directions at Los Alisos and Muirlands
Project #2: Meadows Traffic Improvements - Bake/Toledo
The main improvement for each of these projects includes the following, but are not limited to mobilization, demobilization and cleanup, surveying and monument preservation, traffic control and public notifications, traffic signing and striping, AC grind and overlay, AC removal and replacement, removal and replacement of ADA ramps, sidewalks, curb and gutter, raised medians, hardscape median treatments, replacement adjustment of utilities, traffic signal upgrades, traffic detection loops, landscaping and irrigation modifications, water quality management plans, and other related improvements to complete these project as necessary.
It is the City’s intent to bid Project #1 and Project #2 as separate packages to be awarded as separate construction contracts.  The construction contract for Project #1 is estimated to be approximately 300 working days.  The construction contract for Project #2 is estimated to be approximately 60 working days.  It is anticipated that the two projects will be constructed at separate times with some potential overlap. The order is undetermined at this time. The Pricing Proposal for each project includes a task for "Additional Construction Duration" (Task 1.3) with an allowance of working days for CA/CI services to be used in the event additional working days are added to the construction contract by change order.
Project #2 may include resurfacing of Bake Parkway between Toledo Way and Cromwell. The Pricing Proposal for Project #2 includes a task (Task 1.4) to be utilized in the event this work is included in the construction contract.
It is anticipated that both projects will be completed within a 3-year timeframe, by the end of FY 2029-30. Fee proposals should provide hourly rates for the current fiscal year and indicate any requested rate increases to take effect at the start of each subsequent fiscal year.
In addition, the City further defines the expectations for CA/CI services as follows:
Contract Administration
Perform a comprehensive review of available construction plans, specifications, and supporting documents during the final design preparation to evaluate completeness and constructability.  Evaluate consistency between drawings, specifications, and contract documents.  Identify conflicts, discrepancies, omissions, and ambiguities.  Verify bid item quantity take-off amounts, ensure bid schedules and pay applications fully account for all items to be constructed or provided by the contractor, and ensure engineering design standards provided by the City's engineering design consultant meet current construction standards and methods. Provide a written report summarizing all findings and include recommendations for resolving identified constructability issues.
Assist the City in securing bids, preparing necessary addenda, answering bidders’ questions, providing analysis of bid results, and furnishing a recommendation on the award of construction contract.
Upon award of the construction contract and issuance of the Notice to Procure, provide comprehensive oversight of the Contractor’s procurement activities for materials and equipment. Review and track submittals to verify compliance with the contract documents. Review and monitor the Contractor's procurement schedule and procurement log, with focus on long-lead and critical path materials and equipment. The Pricing Proposal for each project includes a task titled "Extended Procurement Period" with an allowance of working days for CA/CI services to be used in the event the construction start date is delayed due to long-lead procurement times for materials and equipment.
Prepare special concerns to be presented at preconstruction conference.  Determine requirements, and identify any necessary permits from City, various utility companies, state and federal agencies as required to construct and operate the improvements up front prior to preconstruction conference.  Prior to commencement of construction, assist the City in preparing a notice to utilities identifying the impact of the project on their utilities and for any relocation required.
Hold preconstruction conference, present special project requirements, and prepare minutes.  This will include the preparation of an agenda and reviewing/commenting on the Contractor’s schedule, including an Initial 4-week look-ahead schedule.
Provide contract administration for proper enforcement of the contract plans and specifications.  This will include, but is not limited to, assisting the City in reviewing bonds and insurance to verify compliance with specifications, verifying that the contractor has obtained all the required permits for the construction of the project, reviewing submitted certified payroll records (CPRs) for compliance with the applicable wage rates.
Provide labor compliance services to ensure that all labor compliance regulations are thoroughly adhered to in accordance with the requirements set forth by the Department of Industrial Relations (DIR). Monitor, document, and verify compliance with prevailing wage laws, certified payroll reporting, and other relevant labor regulations to ensure that the project meets all state labor standards. This will include regular reviews and audits of contractor submissions to maintain full compliance throughout the project's duration.
Provide engineering support, as needed, to make as-built revisions to the original plans.
Provide the necessary consulting services required to coordinate the efforts between the City and Contractor.  Maintain a correspondence, information, and document tracking system to ensure that correspondence requiring responses, requests, and submittals are answered in a timely manner and that project files are maintained in an orderly manner.
Administer, review and track Requests for Information (RFI’s), Requests for Clarifications (RFC’s), and shop drawings.
Review and recommend approval of progress payment requests to City.  Prior to the Notice to Proceed, the contractor will submit for approval by the City a schedule of values for all lump sum items.  The consultant’s construction management staff and contractor shall meet after the agreed upon cut-off date to review and verify quantities of work completed this period.  Once agreed upon, the contractor shall submit an invoice for work completed.  The consultant shall then initiate the progress pay procedures.
For Federally Funded projects, the work will be in accordance with Caltrans' Construction Oversight Information Notices (COIN) including No. 1: Keeping Adequate Construction Records; COIN No. 2: FHWA Risk Management Plan for Recovery Act Projects; COIN No. 3 Quality Assurance Program (QAP); COIN No. 4 Do Not Use Local Hiring Preferences; COIN No.10 Frequently Observed Deficiencies in Contract Administration; COIN No 11: Administration of Contract Time, and any other applicable construction related COIN publications.
Attend meetings with the Contractor and Inspector at the site, as needed, to maintain continuity for control on overall progress of the work.
Provide necessary coordination with other agencies, including submitting permit applications and other potential grant application documents and documentation as well.
Consult with City regarding disposition of Contract Change Orders (CCO’s) and Stop Notices.  All contract change orders must be issued by the City’s Project Manager or authorized representative.  The consultant has no authority to issue Change Orders.  Owner-initiated changes will be initiated by the City.  The consultant shall negotiate and document cost increases or credits with the contractor and assess schedule impact.  All Stop Notices must be immediately reported to the City’s Project Manager.
Provide labor compliance services to ensure that all labor compliance regulations are thoroughly adhered to in accordance with the requirements set forth by the Department of Industrial Relations (DIR).  Monitor, document, and verify compliance with prevailing wage laws, certified payroll reporting, and other relevant labor regulations to ensure that the project meets all state labor standards.  This includes regular reviews and audits of contractor submissions to maintain full compliance throughout the project’s duration.
Review the Contractor’s initial and updated construction schedules for compliance with the contract documents and verify that the schedules accurately represent the scope of work.  Monitor the overall project schedule and provide the City with monthly schedule progress reports.  Prepare weekly statement of working days documenting the construction progress, time of completion, delays, and time extensions.
Assist the City in maintaining a good relationship with the public.  Answer citizen inquiries and complaints for the City relating to the project.
Coordinate the schedules and response of other City consultants or contractors (designers, surveyors, and materials testing laboratories) to ensure that the project proceeds on schedule.
Coordinate construction with adjacent businesses or residences to ensure that they are afforded access to their property at all times, and to enforce the working hour and noise restrictions provided in the specifications.
Enforce the provisions of the specifications that require contractor to post or distribute public notices.  Enforce the requirement for re-noticing when construction schedules change.
Coordinate with public utilities and other public agencies to resolve construction questions, scheduling conflicts, or safety issues.
Coordinate with the contractor to ensure that Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plans, Water Quality control measures, and air pollution measures are effectively and consistently implemented.
At the completion of the project, coordinate inspection of the work to determine if any work is incomplete.  Prepare a punch list of the incomplete work and provide to the Contractor and City.  Coordinate subsequent inspections to confirm that incomplete work has been completed satisfactorily.
At the completion of the project, turn over all documents including final redline as-builts. A final project report will be prepared summarizing the project and performance of the contractor.
Construction Inspection
Provide daily field observation during construction monitoring the general progress of the work to determine if the work is proceeding in accordance with the contract documents.  
Inspect the location, line, grade of the facilities that are constructed.
Maintain accurate records of the quantities of materials that are constructed.
Maintain accurate records of the project schedule, days worked by contractor, and working days lost to weather or similar delays.
Maintain accurate records of the equipment on the job; and the idle or working time of the equipment.
Maintain accurate records or accidents or claims that are related to the construction.
For Federally Funded projects, the work will be in accordance with Caltrans' Construction Oversight Information Notices (COIN) including No. 1: Keeping Adequate Construction Records; COIN No. 2: FHWA Risk Management Plan for Recovery Act Projects; COIN No. 3 Quality Assurance Program (QAP); COIN No. 4 Do Not Use Local Hiring Preferences; COIN No.10 Frequently Observed Deficiencies in Contract Administration; COIN No 11: Administration of Contract Time, and any other applicable construction related COIN publications.
Coordinate contractor requests for interpretation of the plans and / or specifications in a manner that will document the resolution of questions and keep the project on schedule.
As required by the project specifications or funding conduct labor compliance interviews.
Review and monitor all traffic control and public safety plans for compliance with all safety laws and regulations.  Review all detour, lane closures, temporary access, signing, delineation, and traffic control plans.  Inspector will enforce traffic control safety requirements in and around construction zones.
Review pedestrian and handicap facilities potentially impacted by the project to ensure that pedestrian traffic and handicap traffic is safely and reasonably afforded access through the project.
Through independent inspections ensure that the contractor maintains traffic control, pedestrian access, and storm runoff at all times (during weekends, holidays, and storms).
Ensure that the contractor protects its worksite from pedestrians and motorists at all times and nighttime traffic controls are secured at the end of each workday.  Whenever trench plates are used on the roadway, the inspector shall ensure that the trench plates are properly ramped and secured to the pavement at the end of each workday.
Enforce water quality best management practices, storm water pollution prevention plans, and water quality management plans at all times. 
Meet with Contractor at the beginning of each workday and review proposed work plans, including specific details that may affect progress.
Review actual Contractor performance throughout working days and discuss discrepancies with the Contractor as they occur.
Maintain copies of all permits needed to construct the project and enforce all special requirements of each permit.
Assist City in maintaining good relations with residents and businesses in the surrounding neighborhood.  Respond to citizen complaints and inquiries regarding the project and ensure residents impacted by construction are informed of the project’s progress and potential impacts.
Review construction schedules and enforce requirements for updating schedules and maintaining appropriate progress of the work.
Evaluate work in progress and give a weekly status report to the City for the City’s use in determining any effect of scheduling delays and any needed enforcement or corrective action.
Maintain field file bound workbooks during construction, including quantities constructed, daily and weekly reports, working-day reports, change order documentation, and other documentation and photographs.
Review, evaluate, and discuss with the City all requests for changes of work, including costs involved, and prepare change orders. 
Maintain detailed records of workers and hours, and equipment and materials utilized under force account change orders.
Review and recommend approval of progress payments.
Recommend and schedule, with the City and applicable agencies, the final inspection.  
Provide a final report summarizing all issues for project closeout.  The report will document final inspections and the final punch lists of items to be completed and verify that all items on the final punch lists have been completed or corrected.  The consultant shall assist the City in following up on defective work performed by contractor covered by warranties.  The contractor will provide a follow up report to City following final inspection stating that the installation of improvements was completed in accordance with the plans and specifications and provide necessary data for City acceptance of the project.

## SUBMITTAL METHOD

## Independent Contractor Classes
Contractor shall supply recreation and community services classes as requested by City in accordance with the City's 
Milpitas’ Recreation and Community Services Independent Contractor Handbook
, as may be updated from time to time at the City's sole discretion. Please note that the Handbook is currently undergoing revisions. The City will amend this solicitation to add the link for the updated Handbook when it is available.

Contractors who are selected to provide classes may set their own class prices, but the City may provide feedback if they believe the price point is too high for participants. The City contracts with independent contractors at a rate of 65% of the resident fees collected for classes held at City facilities. The City also requires a non-resident fee for individuals who do not reside in the City of Milpitas.
See Attachment B - Recreation Contract Exemplar and Attachment C - Example Milpitas Recreation Class Proposal Form for additional requirements/information. These documents are subject to change as required at the City's sole discretion.

Through this Request for Proposal ("RFP"), the City of Milpitas ("City") seeks to contract with multiple qualified vendors to deliver an estimated 21,472 meals per year based on 88 meals/day for 244 service days for the City and County of Santa Clara's ("County") Senior Nutrition Program at the Barbara Lee Senior Center located at 40 N. Milpitas, Blvd., Milpitas, California 95035. The selected contractor(s) shall furnish all labor, supervision, methods, processes, implements, tools, machinery, equipment, transportation, materials, and facilities required for the preparation and delivery of the meals. Current Health Permit
:  Must be a current and valid health permit issued by the applicable local environmental health agency for each food preparation facility that will prepare meals for the Senior Nutrition Program.

Commercial Kitchen Authorization
:  Required if applicable.  If the vendor prepares meals from a rented, shared, commissary, or other third-party commercial kitchen, the vendor must provide a current agreement or other documentation demonstrating authorization to use the permitted facility.

Any adjustment in quantities and/or days/times will not entitle the awarded contractors to an adjustment in per meal costs.
The initial term of the awarded contracts is expected to begin on April 1, 2027 and be for a period of three years with one additional three-year option to extend for a total of six years, subject to the appropriation of funds.
