## Scope of Work
Contractor shall provide meals and services in accordance with the City of Milpitas (“City”) and County of Santa Clara’s (“County”) Senior Nutrition Program. See Attachments C and D, the 
County of Santa Clara’s website
, the 
U.S. Dietary Guidelines for Americans
, and below for additional details and requirements.
GENERAL REQUIREMENTS
Meals shall be delivered to the Barbara Lee Senior Center at 40 N. Milpitas, Blvd., Milpitas, California 95035.
Meals must be delivered between 10:00 and 11:30 a.m. up to five days per week, as determined by the City.
Contractor must have the capacity to serve up to 100 meals per day.
Contractor shall provide meals that include nutritional portions of proteins, vegetables, starch, fruit, dairy (milk or approved milk substitute) in alignment with the City and County’s Senior Nutrition Program requirements.
Meals can be provided in bulk or individually packaged.
During the term of the Agreement, Contractor shall have and maintain the following:
Current Health Permit
Current Food Facility Inspection Status
Current Fire Permit
Current License to Operate
Current Commercial Kitchen Authorization (if applicable)
PRODUCTION FACILITY, EQUIPMENT, AND ENVIRONMENT
.
Contractor shall furnish all food, labor, supplies, equipment, and food production, staging, and storage facilities necessary for the preparation, storage, and delivery of meals.
Contractor is solely responsible for any lease, rent, mortgage or any other payment necessary to operate its food production facility for the meal delivery services described herein.
Contractor shall repair, maintain, and upkeep its facilities solely at its own cost, whether cyclical or emergency in nature.
All food production and delivery equipment necessary for the meal delivery services described herein shall be provided by the Contractor and shall include, but not be limited to, dishwashers, refrigerators, freezers, stoves, food mixers, storage facilities, and vehicles.
Contractor shall provide all administrative or office equipment necessary for them to provide the meals and services specified herein.
Contractor shall replace, repair, maintain, and upkeep all equipment necessary for the direct or indirect preparation, production, storage and delivery of the meal services described herein.
Contractor equipment utilized for the delivery of food shall conform to and ensure that the following criteria are met:
Hot foods shall be delivered at 140 degrees Fahrenheit or more.
Cold foods shall be delivered at 40 degrees Fahrenheit or below.
Pasteurized milk shall not be held above 45 degrees Fahrenheit.
Containers for bulk meals shall be cleaned by the site staff and picked up by the Contractor at the time of the delivery of the next meal.
Meal carriers must be cleaned by the Contractor after each use, and meal containers must be sanitized daily by the Contractor.
FOOD, HEALTH, AND SANITATION.
Authorized representatives of the County and the City shall have the right to inspect the Contractor’s food preparation facilities at any time during the contract period.
Contractor shall conform to all health and sanitation requirements of the current California Retail Food Code and any other applicable Federal, State or County regulations.
Contractor shall submit a copy of all new health reports to the City and the County within 
three days
 of receipt.
FOOD SERVICE SPECIFICATIONS MEAL PLANNING REQUIREMENTS. 
Menus must comply with the current requirements of Older Americans Act Section 339, Title 22, Division 1.8, Ch 4, Article 5, Section 7638.5, California Department of Aging Title III, and current County Nutrition Standards as provided in Attachment C – Menu Requirements.
Contractor shall submit menus and requested menu changes to designated County staff at least 9 weeks prior to use.
Contractor shall address any changes requested in the menus by designated County staff regarding nutrition requirements and/or consumer preference.
MENUS
.
Congregate Catered Meal Requirements:
Two-day menus with a cycle of 4-7 weeks must be used for the congregate hot meals.
Menus for hot meals must be submitted and completed using the component method to determine nutritional content.
Each meal must contain at least one-third (1/3) of the current daily Recommended Dietary Allowance (RDA) for people 51 years of age or older as determined by the National Academy of Science - National Research Council.
Menus shall provide an average of at least 550 kilocalories (kcal) per meal.
Requirements for All Menus:
Seasonal menus are preferred.
Food must be attractive, palatable, and appealing.
Low amounts of salt must be used in the preparation of food.
Every effort must be made to plan the menus with as low in fat content as possible.
Oil used in food preparation shall be liquid and polyunsaturated fat and/or monounsaturated fat for all meals.
Contractor shall use a minimum of simple sugars and concentrated sweets, particularly for people requesting low sugar (diabetic) meals.
Contractor must adhere to Attachment C regarding Nutrition Requirements of Meals at all times.
Whenever possible, ethnic and holiday menus should be incorporated under advisement by designated County staff.
Fresh fruit should be included with all meals.
Milk, if included with the meal, should be 8 oz. per serving.

and all accompanying endorsements

.  If a complete response cannot be provided without referencing supporting documentation, you must attach such documentation with your Proposal and indicate where the supplemental information can be found.

## Scope of Work
Overview
Contractor shall provide scheduled and as-requested inspection, maintenance, testing, repair, recharging, replacement, inventory, disposal and other related parts, equipment, and services services for City-owned portable fire extinguishers at various City facilities and for City fleet vehicles. Services shall be performed in accordance with all applicable federal, state, and local laws, regulations, codes, and standards, including the applicable provisions of the California Code of Regulations (CCR), Title 19, Division 1, Chapter 3, Regulations and Standards of the State Fire Marshal, applicable California State Fire Marshal (CSFM) requirements, and the manufacturer's applicable instructions and service requirements.
Contractor shall provide all labor, materials, supplies, parts, supervision, tools, equipment, transportation, and other resources necessary to perform the required services.
Contractor Requirements
Licensing and Certification.
 Contractor shall maintain a valid California State Fire Marshal (CSFM) Portable Fire Extinguisher Concern License for each applicable business location. Personnel servicing portable fire extinguishers under the Contract shall maintain a valid CSFM Certificate of Registration appropriate for the services they perform. All licenses and certifications shall remain current throughout the term of the Agreement.
DIR Registration and Prevailing Wage.
 Contractor shall have and maintain current DIR Public Works Contractor Registration, as required by applicable law, throughout the term of the Agreement. Services provided under this Contract are subject to applicable prevailing wage requirements. Contractor shall comply with all applicable prevailing wage, payroll reporting, and other DIR requirements.
Uniforms.
 Contractor personnel working at or on City-owned or leased premises shall wear distinctive uniforms with the Contractor's name visibly affixed to the uniform.
Hydrostatic Testing.
 Contractor shall be capable of providing hydrostatic testing required under this Scope using appropriately licensed, certified, or otherwise authorized personnel and suitable testing equipment and facilities, as required by applicable law, regulation, and manufacturer requirements. Hydrostatic testing may be performed by the Contractor or by an appropriately licensed, certified, or otherwise authorized subcontractor, if applicable.
Subcontracting.
 Subcontracting is permitted only for hydrostatic testing. Any subcontractor performing hydrostatic testing shall maintain all licenses, certifications, approvals, registrations, and authorizations required to perform the applicable testing, including DIR registration and compliance with applicable prevailing wage requirements, if required by law.

Extinguisher Types
Contractor shall be capable of servicing, as applicable, the following types of portable fire extinguishers:
Dry Chemical
Carbon Dioxide (CO₂)
Halon
Water and Water-Based
Wet Chemical Kitchen (Class K)
The City reserves the right to add or delete equipment during the term of the Contract, as necessary.
Annual Inspection and Maintenance
Contractor shall:
Perform annual maintenance and associated inspection of City-owned portable fire extinguishers in accordance with applicable requirements.
Perform the inspection, maintenance procedures, corrective actions, tagging, and documentation applicable to each extinguisher.
Perform internal examination, disassembly, maintenance, or recharging when required based on the applicable service interval, extinguisher type, condition, manufacturer's requirements, or inspection findings.
Ensure extinguishers are returned to a fully charged and operable condition following applicable service.
Periodic Internal Maintenance and Hydrostatic Testing
Contractor shall:
Perform periodic internal maintenance and hydrostatic testing at the intervals applicable to each extinguisher based on its type, construction, markings, applicable regulations, manufacturer's requirements, and service history.
Verify the applicable maintenance and hydrostatic-testing interval for each extinguisher before performing the required service.
Perform an internal examination before hydrostatic testing when required by applicable requirements.
Remove extinguishers from service when necessary for required maintenance, testing and replace, if necessary, upon City approval.
Where DOT-regulated cylinders or equipment are involved, comply with all applicable U.S. Department of Transportation requirements and maintain all required approvals, authorizations, and records.
Maintain and provide, upon request, hydrostatic testing records identifying the date of test, person performing the test, and extinguisher serial number or other identifying information. 
When an extinguisher is removed from service, Contractor shall coordinate with designated City staff regarding temporary replacement or alternate protection, as applicable.
Inventory
During the first annual service cycle under the Contract , Contractor shall coordinate with City staff to verify and document, at a minimum, the following for each extinguisher:
Location;
Type and capacity;
Condition;
Mounting/bracket; and
Manufacturer and model, where available.
Contractor shall identify deficiencies related to extinguisher type, capacity, quantity, mounting, labeling, accessibility, and location and provide recommendations to City staff.
Contractor shall provide the completed inventory in Excel format or another mutually agreed-upon format.
Contractor shall update the inventory annually for City facilities. City vehicle extinguishers shall be excluded from the annual facility inventory unless otherwise requested by the City.
Recharging, Repair, and Servicing
Contractor shall:
Recharge, repair, and service extinguishers as needed based on inspection findings, applicable service intervals, condition, use, or other applicable requirements.
Provide all labor, parts, materials, supplies, and equipment necessary to complete the service.
Use manufacturer-recommended replacement parts or parts of equal quality, compatibility, and performance.
Provide routine repair and replacement parts at the Contractor’s actual cost, with a markup not to exceed ten percent (10%).
Provide a one-year warranty on recharge services performed under the Contract. The warranty shall cover defects attributable to the Contractor's workmanship or materials and shall not apply to damage, misuse, or other conditions unrelated to the Contractor's service.
Provide an itemized invoice identifying the extinguisher serviced, work performed, parts and materials used, and applicable charges.
Offer to Return Replaced Parts.
 Contractor shall comply with applicable California State Fire Marshal requirements regarding the written offer to return replaced parts to the City, except where parts are required to be returned to the manufacturer under a warranty arrangement.
Service Tags
Contractor shall:
Affix a service tag to each extinguisher following required inspection, maintenance, servicing, or recharge.
Complete service tags with all information required by applicable requirements for the service performed.
Replace damaged, missing, or illegible service tags when identified.
New Purchase or Replacement of Fire Extinguishers
Contractor shall:
Perform scheduled replacement of fire extinguishers identified by the City in accordance with the applicable replacement schedule.
Notify the designated City staff when an extinguisher requires replacement.
Obtain prior written approval from the City before replacing an extinguisher when the estimated repair cost exceeds fifty percent (50%) of the cost for a new, equivalent extinguisher.
Provide new and unused extinguishers suitable for the applicable hazard and installation.
Install replacement extinguishers using manufacturer-authorized fixtures and brackets appropriate for the applicable building or vehicle installation.
Provide per-unit pricing for new extinguishers, including delivery and mounting brackets, at the Contractor’s actual cost, with a markup not to exceed ten percent (10%).
Safety Data Sheets
Contractor shall:
Provide the City with current Safety Data Sheets (SDS) for applicable extinguishing agents, chemicals, or other products supplied or used under the Contract.
Provide SDS documentation to designated City staff upon request.
Extinguisher Recalls
Contractor shall:
Notify the City of manufacturer recalls, safety notices, or service advisories affecting City-owned extinguishers of which Contractor becomes aware.
Identify affected extinguishers and provide recommendations for appropriate corrective action.
Provide information regarding the disposition of recalled extinguishers when applicable.
As-Requested Response Times
Contractor shall:
Respond to routine service requests within twenty-four (24) business hours of notification.
Pick up equipment requiring off-site service within twenty-four (24) business hours of notification.
Return equipment removed from City facilities for off-site service within ten (10) business days of pickup.
Respond to emergency service requests within four (4) business hours of notification by City.
Coordinate service activities with designated City staff to minimize disruption to City operations.
**For purposes of this Scope of Work, "business hours" means Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. through 5:00 p.m. Pacific Time, excluding City-observed holidays.
Disposal of Fire Extinguishers
Contractor shall:
Dispose of extinguishers that have reached the end of their serviceable life or are otherwise determined to be unsuitable for continued use.
Discharge and disassemble extinguishers prior to disposal when required by applicable requirements.
Recycle or recover component parts and extinguishing agents when practicable and legally permitted.
Handle Halon and other regulated extinguishing agents in accordance with all applicable federal and state recovery, handling, transportation, and disposal requirements.
Provide disposal or recycling documentation upon request by City.
Records and Reports
Contractor shall:
Maintain records of all services performed on City-owned portable fire extinguishers.
Records shall identify, at a minimum, the following:
Extinguisher identification/serial number or other unique identifier;
Location;
Type and capacity;
Date of service;
Service performed;
Parts/materials provided;
Testing performed;
Hydrostatic test date, when applicable;
Name/identification of person performing the hydrostatic test, when applicable;
Deficiencies identified; and
Corrective action taken.
Provide completed service records and reports to designated City staff upon request.
Schedule of Services
Contractor shall:
Coordinate annual inspections with designated City staff before each annual service cycle.
Schedule periodic maintenance, hydrostatic testing, repairs, recharging, and other services based on the requirements applicable to each extinguisher.
Provide advance notice of scheduled service dates.
Complete assigned tasks by the deadline mutually agreed upon by the Contractor and City.
Immediately notify appropriate City staff of any anticipated delay.

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN
 that the City of Modesto, County of Stanislaus, State of California, will receive electronic sealed Bids for the following work: 
Housing Rehabilitation Program- 1137 Bel Air Ct, Modesto, CA 95350
.
The City of Modesto Housing Rehabilitation Program provides financial assistance to eligible homeowners for the repair and improvement of their properties. Funded through federal resources, the program is designed to correct health, safety, and code deficiencies, extend the useful life of homes, and improve overall living conditions for low- to moderate-income households. The program plays a critical role in preserving Modesto’s existing housing stock, preventing deterioration, and supporting long-term neighborhood stability.
To meet increasing program demand, the City is seeking 
qualified and properly licensed general contractors
 to participate by bidding on rehabilitation projects. Contractors working with the program have the opportunity to support community revitalization, expand their scope of work, and build long-term partnerships with the City.
Typical scopes of work may include, but are not limited to: roofing, plumbing, electrical, HVAC replacement, water heater upgrades, window and door replacements, accessibility modifications, structural and code corrections, interior and exterior repairs, and other work necessary to bring homes into compliance with local and federal housing standards. Projects vary in size and complexity, offering opportunities for contractors with diverse skill sets.
Participating contractors must be able to perform work in accordance with City standards, building codes, federal program requirements, and grant-funded project guidelines. All projects require adherence to clear specifications, timely performance, and professional communication with City staff and homeowners.
The City encourages all interested contractors to apply, expand their business opportunities, and contribute to improving the quality of housing within the Modesto community.

1. HUD Funding and Section 3 Requirements
This project is funded through the 
U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)
. The City of Modesto strongly encourages participation from 
Section 3 businesses
 and contractors that employ 
Section 3 residents
, consistent with HUD’s objective of expanding economic opportunities for low-income individuals and communities.

California Contractor’s License, Class “B” – General Building Contractor
, at the time of bid submission and must maintain the required license in good standing for the duration of the project.
Failure to maintain proper licensure may result in disqualification or termination of the contract.

All General Contractors seeking to participate in the City of Modesto Housing Rehabilitation Program must maintain insurance coverage in accordance with City standards.
Required coverage includes:
General Liability Insurance
Workers’ Compensation Insurance
Automobile Liability Insurance 
Proof of insurance must be submitted and approved through the City’s 
Public Improvement Notification System (PINS)
 prior to contract award. Contractors who do not maintain compliant insurance documentation are not eligible to receive project awards.
4. Site Verification
Bidders are strongly encouraged to attend mandatory bid walk and verify existing site conditions prior to submitting a proposal.
Submission of a bid shall constitute acknowledgment that the contractor has reviewed:
existing site conditions
access limitations
field measurements
constructability factors
project requirements

An Engineer’s Estimate will not be released for this project. Each bidder shall independently determine pricing based on:

field verification

applicable industry standards

non-responsive
not in the best interest of the program
inconsistent with cost reasonableness standards

The City of Modesto Housing Rehabilitation Program provides financial assistance to eligible homeowners for the repair and improvement of their properties. Funded through federal resources, the program is designed to correct health, safety, and code deficiencies, extend the useful life of homes, and improve overall living conditions for low- to moderate-income households. The program plays a critical role in preserving Modesto’s existing housing stock, preventing deterioration, and supporting long-term neighborhood stability.
To meet increasing program demand, the City is seeking 
qualified and properly licensed general contractors
 to participate by bidding on rehabilitation projects. Contractors working with the program have the opportunity to support community revitalization, expand their scope of work, and build long-term partnerships with the City.
Typical scopes of work may include, but are not limited to: roofing, plumbing, electrical, HVAC replacement, water heater upgrades, window and door replacements, accessibility modifications, structural and code corrections, interior and exterior repairs, and other work necessary to bring homes into compliance with local and federal housing standards. Projects vary in size and complexity, offering opportunities for contractors with diverse skill sets.
Participating contractors must be able to perform work in accordance with City standards, building codes, federal program requirements, and grant-funded project guidelines. All projects require adherence to clear specifications, timely performance, and professional communication with City staff and homeowners.
The City encourages all interested contractors to apply, expand their business opportunities, and contribute to improving the quality of housing within the Modesto community.

U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)
. The City of Modesto strongly encourages participation from

 and contractors that employ

The City of Modesto Housing Rehabilitation Program provides financial assistance to eligible homeowners for the repair and improvement of their properties. Funded through federal resources, the program is designed to correct health, safety, and code deficiencies, extend the useful life of homes, and improve overall living conditions for low- to moderate-income households. The program plays a critical role in preserving Modesto’s existing housing stock, preventing deterioration, and supporting long-term neighborhood stability.
To meet increasing program demand, the City is seeking 
qualified and properly licensed general contractors
 to participate by bidding on rehabilitation projects. Contractors working with the program have the opportunity to support community revitalization, expand their scope of work, and build long-term partnerships with the City.
Typical scopes of work may include, but are not limited to: roofing, plumbing, electrical, HVAC replacement, water heater upgrades, window and door replacements, accessibility modifications, structural and code corrections, interior and exterior repairs, and other work necessary to bring homes into compliance with local and federal housing standards. Projects vary in size and complexity, offering opportunities for contractors with diverse skill sets.
Participating contractors must be able to perform work in accordance with City standards, building codes, federal program requirements, and grant-funded project guidelines. All projects require adherence to clear specifications, timely performance, and professional communication with City staff and homeowners.
The City encourages all interested contractors to apply, expand their business opportunities, and contribute to improving the quality of housing within the Modesto community.

This project is funded through the 
U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)
. The City of Modesto strongly encourages participation from

Proof of insurance must be submitted and approved through the City’s 
Public Improvement Notification System (PINS)
 prior to contract award. Contractors who do not maintain compliant insurance documentation are not eligible to receive project awards.

twenty-one (21) working days
 after receipt of a written request for dispute resolution and shall notify the claimants of the time and place of the hearing 
at least ten (10) days
 in advance.  The party against whom the claim is filed may file an answering statement with the claimant(s) and with the City’s Community and Economic Development Department Housing and Urban Development Supervisor 
not later than five (5) working days

tribunal

## Section 36.

For the purposes of the Protest Procedures, the following terms are defined:

Contain a concise statement of the grounds for protest;
Include all supporting documentation, if any.  Documentation submitted after filing will not be reviewed.

Protest to Director of Engineering Services

Appeal to Deputy City Manager
The Director of Engineering Services, or designee’s, decision may be appealed in writing to the City of Modesto’s Deputy City Manager no later than 10 business days after Notice of Decision is sent to the protestor.  The Deputy City Manager shall review the appeal, accompanying supporting documents, if any, and the written record of the protest review by the Director of Utilities, or designee.
A written record of the Deputy City Manager’s review shall be created and maintained.  The Deputy City Manager shall give notice in writing of his or her decision to the protestor within 15 business days after City Clerk’s receipt of appeal.
Appeal to City Council

2026 Supportive Housing Notice of Funding Availability 
OC HOUSING AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT (OCHCD) announces the release of the 2026 Supportive Housing Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) making available up to $20.9 million dollars of Federal HOME Investment Partnership Program (HOME), HOME American Rescue Plan Program (HOME-ARP), Mental Health Services Act (MHSA)/Behavioral Health Services Act (BHSA), 15G Reserves and Housing Successor Agency (HSA) Funds, to promote the acquisition, new construction, and acquisition/rehabilitation of Supportive Housing and will also provide up to 100 Housing Choice, Mainstream and/or Veterans Affairs Supportive Housing Project Based Vouchers for extremely low-income households who are homeless.
Funds are available until the NOFA closes, is replaced by a new NOFA, or until all available funds are committed via Board of Supervisors action, whichever occurs first. Interested and qualified applicants who can successfully demonstrate their ability to provide supportive housing for extremely low-income households who are experiencing homelessness are encouraged to submit proposals.
Small-scale housing is an eligible activity under this NOFA, so long as it meets NOFA criteria and the guiding principles in the Commission to Address Homelessness Small-Scale Housing Unit Report received and filed by the Board of Supervisors on January 28, 2025.

Small Business Requirements:

## Title VI Solicitation Notice (Federal Contract Provision Guidelines Section A5.3.1)
Title VI Solicitation Notice: The (Title of Recipient), in accordance with the provisions of Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 (78 Stat. 252, 42 U.S.C. §§ 2000d to 2000d-4), 28 CFR § 50.3, and 49 CFR Part 21, hereby notifies all bidders that it will affirmatively ensure that any contract entered into pursuant to this advertisement, all contractors will be afforded full opportunity to submit bids in response to this invitation and will not be discriminated against on the grounds of the owner’s race, color, national origin, sex, creed, age, or disability in consideration for an award.

## ELIGIBILITY TO SUBMIT APPLICATIONS 
To be eligible to submit an application for these services, the applicant must be an Adult Residential Facility licensed by the State Department of Social Services as set forth in CCR, Title 22 Division 6. 
County will not review any application submitted by an individual or entity found not to be eligible to submit an application. 
In addition, to be eligible to contract with the County, an individual or entity must not be listed on the current Cumulative Sanction List of the Office of the Inspector General (U.S. Department of Health and Human Services), the General Services Administration’s list of parties excluded from federal programs, or the California Medi-Cal Suspended and Ineligible Provider List.
 
Accordingly, 
County will not review any application submitted by an individual or entity found to be on any of these lists and the application will automatically be rejected
. County will notify the applicant of this determination in writing.
The County plans to use the following databases to identify individuals and entities that are not eligible to contract with the County:
https://exclusions.oig.hhs.gov/
https://sam.gov/search/
Medi-Cal Suspension Search Database
It is the sole responsibility of all applicants to verify that they are not on any of these lists prior to preparing and submitting an application in response to this RFA. Correction of any errors found on any of the lists, above, is the sole responsibility of the applicant and must be made prior to submission of the application.
In addition, in order to be eligible to enter into a contract with the County, an individual or entity must not have any pending charge(s) or conviction(s) for violation of criminal law(s) and/or any sanction(s) or disciplinary action(s) imposed or taken against them by any federal or state law enforcement, regulatory or licensing agency or body, including exclusion from Medicare and Medicaid programs. must self-disclose with explanation, 
or

## TARGET POPULATION 
CONREP is for persons found by courts to be Not Guilty by Reason of Insanity, Incompetent to Stand Trial, Mentally Disordered Sex Offenders, or Civilly Committed Mentally Disordered Offenders.  Services shall be provided to:
Adults, ages eighteen (18) years of age and older, who are ordered by the Superior Court or Board of Parole Hearings (BPH) to CONREP, under the jurisdiction of the Behavioral Health Services (BHS) within the HCA, and the Department of State Hospitals (DSH).
All Clients shall be referred by the County.

## PROTEST PROCEDURES
PROTEST PROCEDURES
All protests shall be typed under the protestor’s letterhead and submitted in accordance with the provisions stated herein. All protests shall include at a minimum the following information: 
The name, address, and telephone number of the protestor;
The signature of the protestor or the protestor’s representative;
The solicitation or contract number;
A detailed statement of the legal and/or factual grounds for the protest; and, 
The form of relief requested. 
Protest of Solicitation Specifications: 
All protests related to solicitation specifications must be submitted to the 
Deputy Procurement Agent (DPA), 
Carmina Corona
 at 
ccorona@ochca.com
, no later than five (5) business days prior to the application submission deadline of the solicitation. Protests received after the five (5) business-day deadline will not be considered by the County. 
In the event the protest of specifications is denied, and the protestor wishes to continue in the solicitation process, the protestor must still submit an application prior to the close of the solicitation in accordance with the solicitation submittal procedures provided in this solicitation. 
Protest of Award of Contract: 
Protests related to the award of a contract must be submitted to the 
Deputy Procurement Agent, 
Carmina Corona
 at 
ccorona@ochca.com
, no later than five (5) business days after the Notice of Solicitation Ranking Results is provided by the DPA.
Protests relating to a proposed contract award received after the five (5) business day deadline 
will not
 be considered by the County. 
If the five (5) business day period expires without the receipt of a protest, the department may move forward with the contract award or if necessary, file the item for approval by the Board of Supervisors.
Protest Process 
In the event of a timely protest, the County shall not proceed with the solicitation or award of the contract until the DPA issues a decision on the protest. 
Upon receipt of a timely protest, the DPA will, within ten (10) business days of receipt of the protest, issue a decision in writing which shall state the reasons for the actions taken. 
The County may, after providing written justification, make the determination that an immediate award of the contract is necessary to protect the substantial interests of the County. The award of a contract shall in no way compromise the protester’s right to the protest procedures outlined herein. 
If the protestor disagrees with the decision of the DPA, the protestor may submit a written appeal to the County Procurement Officer requesting an appeal to the Procurement Appeals Board, in accordance with the process stated below. 
 
APPEALS PROCESS
If the protestor wishes to appeal the protest decision of the Deputy Procurement Agent, the protestor must submit, within three (3) business days from receipt of the Deputy Procurement Agent’s decision, a written appeal to the Office of the County Procurement Officer. 
Written appeals must be sent by mail to the address below with a courtesy copy by email;
 
County of Orange/County Executive Office
County Procurement Office
400 W. Civic Center Drive, 5th Floor
Santa Ana, CA 92701
Attn: County Procurement Officer
CPOAppeals@ceo.oc.gov
 
Within fifteen (15) business days, the County Procurement Officer will review all materials in connection with the appeal, assess the merits of the protest and provide a written determination that shall contain his or her decision on whether the appeal shall be forwarded to the Procurement Appeals Board.
The decision of the County Procurement Officer on whether to allow the appeal to go forward will be final and there shall be no right to any administrative appeals of this decision.

OCLSB or DVBE Preference provides for the following

Invitation for Bid – IFB
A five percent (5%) deduction in the original bid price shall be applied to all confirmed OCLSB or DVBE bidders for evaluation purposes. If the lowest bidder is a certified OCLSB or DVBE bidder, the contract will be awarded at the certified OCLSB or DVBE’s original bid price. The maximum allowable preference deduction is $100,000.
Request for Proposal - RFP
An additional five percent (5%) shall be applied to the tallied cost score of each certified OCLSB or DVBE to obtain their final score. If the final score of any OCLSB or DVBE matches the final score of a non-OCLSB or non-DVBE, preference shall be given to the certified OCLSB. If two or more OCLSB or DVBEs have the same final score, the County shall determine the contract award based on the County’s best interest.

Business Certified as OCLSB and DVBE
If a State-certified OCLSB is also a State-certified DVBE, the preference given to that business shall be 8% instead of 5%.
Subcontractors

## SERVICES TO BE PROVIDED 
The services shall include but not be limited to:
Develop a facility program plan to ensure the availability of appropriate services to clients placed in the facility.
Implement the client individual service plan.  Such plan shall be developed by Health Care Agency’s designated care coordinator in conjunction with the client and the facility administrator.
Provide a facility with safe sleeping quarters, and a separate bed for each client and a lounge area for clients.
Meet the specialized needs of mentally disordered adults, as specified in the client individual service plan.  Such services may include, but shall not be limited, to the following:
Providing or arranging transportation to meet the client's mental health needs and to facilitate participation in mental health programs.
Encouraging the client to take increasing responsibility for the client's own treatment by supporting self–established goals and the use of support and treatment systems.
Encouraging the client's use of public transportation, use of leisure time in a constructive manner, and maintenance of adequate grooming.
Assisting the client to learn social relationship skills, such as communication with others and appropriate social behavior.
Participating with HCA staff in meetings in the facility.
Assisting the client in developing skills of budgeting, personal shopping, monetary transactions, menu planning, and shopping for, and the preparation of, basic meals.
Assisting the client in becoming responsible for self-medication, as prescribed by the treating physician.
Providing close supervision of, and intensive interactions with, clients who require the management of difficult behavioral problems, consistent with the client's individual service plan and signed court ordered terms and conditions.  The facility staff will report to CONREP clients who are not back at the facility by curfew, and/or any behavior that is indicative of decompensation, rule violations, and/or violations of terms and conditions.

## TARGET POPULATION 
Inpatient Behavioral Health Services
 shall be provided to 
residents from all areas of Orange County who require this highly restrictive level of care to ensure their safety and/or the safety of others. Many individuals served may present with co-occurring medical conditions and/or substance use disorders. In some instances, adults and older adults may present with a primary severe substance use disorder, necessitating involuntary treatment.

Services shall be provided to Orange County residents, ages 13 - 17 living with a serious emotional disturbance; adults ages 18-64; and older adults ages 65 and older living with a serious mental health and/or severe substance use disorder and who meet criteria for involuntary acute inpatient psychiatric care under Sections 5150 or 5585 of the Welfare and Institutions Code. Services shall also be provided to individuals who voluntarily seek treatment. These individuals may be considered a danger to themselves or others or may be gravely disabled.

## APPLICATION FOCUS AND BACKGROUND
The County of Orange (County) 
Health Care Agency
 (HCA) is seeking applications from qualified organizations to provide 
Inpatient Behavioral Health Services
. 
The primary goal of this program is to provide services to Medi-Cal eligible youth, adults and/or older adults, with a serious mental health condition, often a co-occurring medical/substance use disorders, or stand-alone severe substance use disorder requiring acute inpatient psychiatric treatment in a safe, secured environment to stabilize symptoms occurring as a result of their mental health condition. 
The County intends to establish two (2) Master Contracts which are dependent on State licensure but have the same required services as outlined below, pursuant to which County intends to execute contracts with all applicants who meet eligibility and submission requirements. The Master Contracts will be for one of the following service provisions:
Inpatient Behavioral Health Services, for the facilities that are an Acute Free-Standing Psychiatric Hospital (AFSPH)
Medi-Cal Mental Health Managed Care Inpatient Hospital Services for the facilities that are a General Acute Care Hospital (GACH)
 
The County intends that the successful Applicant shall provide Inpatient Hospital Services or Inpatient Behavioral Health Services to include but not limited to: high quality, compliant, person centered, trauma informed inpatient psychiatric services (including co-occurring Substance Use Disorder (SUD) care or stand-alone SUD care), from admission through stabilization and transition to lower level of care, with strong coordination, discharge, and follow up as proposed in accordance with contract requirements set forth in the solicitation and Model Contract, including Attachments.

## SERVICES TO BE PROVIDED 
The successful Applicant shall provide high quality, compliant, person-centered, trauma-informed inpatient psychiatric services (including co-occurring SUD care and/or care for medical conditions or stand-alone severe substance use disorder care), from admission through stabilization and transition to lower level of care, with strong coordination, discharge and follow-up.
Certification/Accreditation: Applicant shall be certified for participation under 42 CFR Part 482. If not certified, applicant must hold accreditation from a nationally recognized accrediting body and meet all applicable State licensure and/or accreditation requirements. 
Quality Standards: Applicant shall meet all quality standards required by County, State, and Federal entities.  
Care Model: Services shall be person-centered, recovery-oriented, non-coercive, trauma-informed, medically necessary, co-occurring capable and time-limited to achieve psychiatric stabilization sufficient for discharge or transfer to a lower level of care.
Assessment & Level of Care: Applicant shall utilize a standardized assessment tool approved by the Behavioral Health Plan (BHP) to determine appropriate level of care and length of stay, used in conjunction with the concurrent review process. 
Psychiatric Evaluation: A licensed psychiatrist shall complete a psychiatric evaluation within 24 hours of admission, including psychiatric history, diagnosis, and initial plan of treatment.  This evaluation must be completed in accordance with the current Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM). 
Daily Rounds: Daily rounds shall be conducted by licensed psychiatrists or advanced psychiatric providers (Psychiatric Nurse Practitioners or Psychiatric Physician Assistants) under the supervision of a licensed psychiatrist.
Medical Health and Physical (H&P): A medical history and physical examination shall be completed within twenty-four (24) hours of admission.
Comorbidity Screening and Capacity: Applicant shall screen for comorbid physical health conditions, SUD and suicidal ideation and demonstrate capacity to address comorbid needs during short-term stay via on-site staff, telemedicine, and/or partnerships with local physical health providers. 
Psychosocial Assessment: A Psychosocial Assessment shall be completed within seventy-two (72) hours of admission by a Licensed or Licensed Waivered Practitioner of the Healing Arts (LPHA). 
Laboratory/Diagnostics: Provide laboratory and diagnostic services as clinically indicated. 
Medication Services: Provide psychiatric medication evaluation and monitoring, including ongoing laboratory testing as clinically necessary. 
Medication for Addiction Treatment (MAT): Initiate, continue, and link clients to continued MAT for substance use disorders as appropriate. 
Therapy—Individual & Group: Provide individual and group therapy. 
Substance Use Interventions: Deliver substance use treatment interventions.
Collateral Interventions: Provide collateral therapy and interventions (including provision or supervision of family therapy sessions as indicated for youth).
Activity Therapy: Provide activities therapy as clinically appropriate.
Care Coordination Documentation: Document coordination of care with the Managed Care Plan (MCP) and community-based providers.
Pre-discharge Planning and Aftercare: Implement extensive pre-discharge planning using the Model Care Coordination Plan or an equivalent tool containing the same requirements.  
Provide each patient with an aftercare plan prior to discharge that includes, to the extent known: 
Nature of illness, required follow-up, and expected course of recovery.
Medications, side effects, and dosage schedules.
Notation that informed consent for medications was obtained.
Confirmation that informed consent includes information on medication side effects.
Expected course of recovery.
Treatment recommendations relevant to the patient’s care.
Documented referrals to medical and behavioral health providers using a closed-loop referral process through a BHP-determined application or vendor. 
Housing assessment for members at risk of homelessness or returning to unsafe/unstable housing, with documented referrals to community-based housing providers using closed-loop/e-referrals when available.
Post-discharge Outreach: Contact members within seventy-two (72) hours of discharge to ensure follow-up care is accessed, using the most effective means (e.g., email, text messaging, telephone). Report outcomes to County BHP via the closed-loop referral method designated by the plan.
Assertive Discharge Planning (Suicide Risk): Provide person-centered, tailored, participatory discharge planning for any member at risk of death by suicide, which may include: 
Immediate access to structured clinical interventions within a stepdown level of care.
Appointments with primary care or other medical follow-up.
Arranged access to prescription medications.
 Family/support system engagement and psychoeducation.
Peer support engagement.
Vocational or educational support.
Crisis response planning.
Risk factor analysis and safety contracting.
Strategies to address social determinants of health.
Preferred methods for proactive outreach within the first hours or days post-discharge.
Continuing Care and Coordination: Provide continuing care planning and coordinate behavioral health services, including:
Admission, discharge, and transfer notifications from acute care hospitals, psychiatric hospitals, state hospitals, and skilled nursing facilities.
Data sharing among Medi-Cal Partners, including BHPs and MCPs.
Service coordination with all applicable providers regardless of Medi-Cal participation.
Administrative Services Organization (ASO) Coordination: Notify the County appointed ASO within 24 hours of admission and maintain ongoing coordination for utilization management. 
Aftercare Linkage: Provide referral and linkage to mental health and substance use treatment providers and other support services prior to discharge. 
Individualized Treatment Plan (ITP): Initiate an ITP within twenty-four (24) hours of admission; obtain signatures from the treatment team and client (or document why signatures could not be obtained) within seventy-two (72) hours. All services must be compatible with ITP. 
Voluntary/Involuntary Treatment: Assess for voluntary and involuntary treatment needs and proceed in accordance with applicable laws and policies.
Crisis Intervention: Provide crisis intervention services.
Education & Support: Deliver education and support to clients and families/caregivers as appropriate.
Transportation: Arrange or provide transportation services as needed to support access to care.
Psychological Services: Provide psychological services as clinically indicated.
Psychometrics: Conduct psychometric testing upon admission to establish clinical baseline, inform treatment decision-making, and support evidence-based practices.
24/7 Psychiatric Coverage: Ensure on call psychiatric coverage 24/7, supported by other qualified personnel.
Interdisciplinary Interventions: Provide nursing, psychological, and social interventions consistent with the ITP.
Aftercare Scheduling: Arrange dates and times for aftercare appointments to County programs within 24 business hours of discharge.
Court-Related Services: Prepare required court documents and provide expert witness testimony services, including but not limited to writs of habeas corpus, capacity hearings, conservatorship, probable cause hearings, court ordered evaluations, and appeal/post certification proceedings.
Juvenile Court Documentation: Prepare documentation required by Juvenile Court to authorize psychotropic medication for youth under court jurisdiction (JV220).
Recovery and Trauma-Informed Focus: All services shall be recovery oriented, and trauma informed, promote client empowerment, and be tailored to individual needs.
Peer Mentor Collaboration: Collaborate with County contracted Peer Mentors, as available, to provide direct support, education, advocacy, and resource/linkage assistance. 
Orange County (OC) Medi-Cal Admission Notification: Provide next day notification to HCA for each OC Medi-Cal admission.
SUD Treatment Capacity and MAT: Demonstrate capacity to treat severe standalone SUD or cooccurring SUD using harm reduction or abstinence-based models, including MAT therapy. Facilities must initiate, continue, and refer for MAT as approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and/or updated DHCS requirements. 
Resource Familiarity: Be familiar with County and community resources to support SUD treatment and recovery.
SUD Therapies and Expertise: Include SUD therapies and ensure access to SUD experts.
Bed Capacity Tracking: Maintain capacity to participate in statewide tracking of inpatient and crisis stabilization bed availability in accordance with State and Federal Health IT (HIT) Plan standards/regulations upon DHCS launch of a bed capacity data solution.
Average Length of Stay (ALOS): Monitor and report monthly on ALOS, with a goal of ≤30 days across all treatment episodes. Report ALOS by County Health Plan, including unfunded clients.
Readmission Monitoring and ALOS Integrity: Monitor readmission rates for all treatment episodes. Under no circumstances shall a facility discharge a member for the purpose of readmitting them to meet the ALOS goal.
Electronic Notification Compliance: Comply with Electronic Notification requirements under 42 CFR 482.61(f), as specified in the CMS Interoperability and Patient Access Final Rule.
County Access and Rights Advocacy: Allow facility access, as requested, to County Contract Monitors and Patient Rights Advocates to conduct chart reviews and meet with clients and staff within seventy-two (72) hours’ of the facility receiving notice Unannounced inspections, evaluations, or requests for information may be made in those situations where arrangement of an appointment beforehand is not possible or is inappropriate due to the nature of the inspection or evaluation.
Information Systems and Data Exchange: Maintain effective Information Systems, including use of an Electronic Medical Record (EMR), Health Information Exchange (HIE), and data exchange capabilities to support care coordination and compliance with performance measures as determined by HEDIS (Healthcare Effectiveness Data and Information Set) and NCQA (National Committee for Quality Assurance).
Public Guardian Notification: Facilities must notify Public Guardians’ office immediately, twenty four (24) hours a day/ seven (7)-days per week/ three hundred sixty five (365) days per year, at Main Line (714) 567-7600 or After Hours Line (714) 628-7000, of changes in placement, emergencies, or changes of the client’s condition, for any publicly conserved client, in addition to notifying OC HCA contract monitor.
Regional Center Coordination: Facilities shall make reasonable efforts to notify the Regional Center Service Coordinator and Nurse Consultant of a Regional Center Client’s admission within twenty-four (24) hours of admission or within twenty- four (24) hours of identifying that a Client is a Regional Center Client.

Funds are available until the NOFA closes, is replaced by a new NOFA, or until all available funds are committed via Board of Supervisors action, whichever occurs first. Interested and qualified applicants who can successfully demonstrate their ability to provide supportive housing for extremely low-income households who are experiencing homelessness are encouraged to submit proposals.
 
Small-scale housing is an eligible activity under this NOFA, so long as it meets NOFA criteria and the guiding principles in the Commission to End Homelessness Small-Scale Housing Unit Report received and filed by the Board of Supervisors on January 28, 2025.

## Purpose and Background
The Orange County Sheriff’s Department has facilities requiring routine inspection, testing, cleaning, certification, service, corrective maintenance, chemical treatment, water quality management, and emergency services on cooling towers and associated equipment, including but not limited to cooling tower basins, fill media, drift eliminators, distribution systems, fans, motors, drives, heat exchangers, water treatment systems, and associated piping, valves, and controls. Minimum frequency and tasks to be in accordance with all manufacturer specifications and recommendations, County tasks and duties, State, Federal, and Local laws, and regulatory requirements, including California Health and Safety Code Section 116057 (Cooling Tower Water Treatment) and all applicable guidelines from the California Department of Public Health.
In addition to routine scheduled service and planned corrective maintenance, Contractor shall be available for emergency services twenty-four (24) hours a day, seven (7) days a week, three-hundred sixty-five (365) days a year.
Contractor shall perform scheduled and on-call tasks and duties at the following service locations and may respond to various other locations not listed below for as-needed services to include any current or future Sheriff maintained facility.

## Protest Procedures
PROTEST PROCEDURES
All protests shall be typed under the protestor’s letterhead and submitted in accordance with the provisions stated herein. All protests shall include at a minimum the following information: 
The name, address, and telephone number of the protestor;
The signature of the protestor or the protestor’s representative;
The solicitation or contract number;
A detailed statement of the legal and/or factual grounds for the protest; and, 
The form of relief requested. 
Protest of Solicitation Specifications: 
All protests related to solicitation specifications must be submitted to the 
Deputy Procurement Agent (DPA), 
Mary Barreto
 at 
mbarreto@ocsheriff.gov
, no later than five (5) business days prior to the Closing Date of the solicitation. Protests received after the five (5) business-day deadline will not be considered by the County.
In the event the protest of specifications is denied, and the protestor wishes to continue in the solicitation process, the protestor must still submit a bid/response prior to the close of the solicitation in accordance with the solicitation submittal procedures provided in this solicitation. 
Protest of Solicitation Results: 
Protests related to solicitation results must be submitted to the 
Deputy Procurement Agent, 
Mary Barreto
 at 
mbarreto@ocsheriff.gov
, no later than five (5) business days after the Notice of Solicitation Results is provided by the DPA.
Protests relating to solicitation results received after the five (5) business day deadline 
will not
 be considered by the County. 
If the five (5) business day period expires without the receipt of a protest, the department may move forward with contract negotiation and award or if necessary, file the item for approval by the Board of Supervisors.
Protest Process 
In the event of a timely protest, the County shall not proceed with the solicitation or award of the contract until the DPA issues a decision on the protest. 
Upon receipt of a timely protest, the DPA will, within ten (10) business days of receipt of the protest, issue a decision in writing which shall state the reasons for the actions taken. 
The County may, after providing written justification, make the determination that an immediate award of the contract is necessary to protect the substantial interests of the County. The award of a contract shall in no way compromise the protester’s right to the protest procedures outlined herein. 
If the protestor disagrees with the decision of the DPA, the protestor may submit a written appeal to the County Procurement Officer requesting an appeal to the Procurement Appeals Board, in accordance with the process stated below. 
 
 
APPEALS PROCESS
If the protestor wishes to appeal the protest decision of the Deputy Procurement Agent, the protestor must submit, within three (3) business days from receipt of the Deputy Procurement Agent’s decision, a written appeal to the Office of the County Procurement Officer. 
Written appeals must be sent by mail to the address below with a courtesy copy by email;
 
County of Orange/County Executive Office
County Procurement Office
400 W. Civic Center Drive, 5th Floor
Santa Ana, CA 92701
Attn: County Procurement Officer
CPOAppeals@ceo.oc.gov
 
Within fifteen (15) business days, the County Procurement Officer will review all materials in connection with the appeal, assess the merits of the protest and provide a written determination that shall contain his or her decision on whether the appeal shall be forwarded to the Procurement Appeals Board.
The decision of the County Procurement Officer on whether to allow the appeal to go forward will be final and there shall be no right to any administrative appeals of this decision.

## Service Requirements
Contractor shall provide scheduled maintenance and corrective maintenance on County cooling towers and corresponding equipment, including but not limited to cooling tower basins, fill media, drift eliminators, distribution systems, nozzles, fans, motors, variable frequency drives (VFDs), gearboxes, belts, sheaves, water treatment chemical feed systems, biocide injection systems, conductivity controllers, bleed-off controls, float valves, makeup water assemblies, strainers, heat exchangers, associated piping, isolation valves, and instrumentation, to ensure optimal performance.
Contractor shall perform full mechanical cleaning and disinfection of cooling tower basins, fill media, and associated surfaces no less than twice annually, or more frequently as required by the County.
Contractor shall provide seasonal start up, shut down, layup, and winterization services for each cooling tower system, including draining, cleaning, and treatment of idle systems to prevent stagnation and microbial growth.
Frequency shall be in accordance with manufacturer requirements, warranties, ASHRAE 188 Water Management Plan requirements, California Health and Safety Code requirements and County requirements.
Contractor shall perform routine maintenance and service on equipment such that equipment and systems are preserved and restored to effective operational conditions and may be effectively used for its designated purpose.
Contractor shall develop, implement, and maintain a site-specific Water Management Plan (WMP) in accordance with ASHRAE Standard 188, including all required hazard analysis, control measures, monitoring procedures, corrective actions, and verification records, for each cooling tower system.
Contractor shall perform and document all required water quality testing, including but not limited to Legionella bacteria testing, conductivity, pH, biocide residual levels, corrosion inhibitor levels, and total dissolved solids (TDS), at frequencies required by California Health and Safety Code Section 116057, ASHRAE Standard 188, and the County-approved Water Management Plan.
In the event water quality test result, including Legionella bacteria, exceed any regulatory or County established  limits, Contractor shall immediately notify the County project lead, in writing, within two (2) hours of receipt of results, and shall implement corrective action, including remedial disinfection and/or shock treatment, in accordance with all regulatory agencies requirements and  perform confirmatory retesting.
Contractor shall assist County in registering and annually updating each cooling tower system with the California Department of Public Health (CDPH) registry, and any applicable local environmental health agency, as required under California Health and Safety Code Section 116057.5.
Contractor, upon authorized County project lead approval, may provide engineering, design and fabrication services for new, inoperative, inadequate and/or failing County systems.
All service, maintenance, service and chemical treatment shall be in strict accordance with all manufacturer specifications, recommendations and requirements, including, but not limited to, frequency, means, methods and consumable usage.
Contractor may be required to work with other Contractors and County departments to ensure seamless system integration and operation of various County systems.
Contractor shall provide sufficient, qualified, trained, experienced, certified if applicable, and background cleared personnel to service systems and equipment under the contract.
Contractor shall provide, all labor, supplies, supervision, tools, transportation (including parking and travel), Personal Protection Equipment (PPE) and all necessary material and equipment to perform routine maintenance and service, including any special diagnostic or adjustment tools, equipment, instruments, and consumables required under manufactures maintenance specification, recommendations and County requirements.
Contractor shall have readily available Safety Data Sheet (SDS) for any chemical or other potentially dangerous substances while performing any service on behalf of the County.
Contractor shall provide and perform installation of software and firmware maintenance in accordance with manufacturer specifications and recommendations, as required.
Contractor shall leave all equipment and software in unlocked condition. If passwords or access protection is required all control information shall be immediately documented and provided to authorized County project lead, at no additional cost.
Contractor shall provide the County with a detailed proposed Scheduled Maintenance schedule for County approval, prior to commencement of work, including the number of hours per locations and number of technicians required to perform service under the terms of the contract.
Under no condition, shall Contractor attempt to assign or subcontract any portion of maintenance or service under the contract without prior written approval, by authorized County project lead.
Contractor shall provide detailed reporting on as-needed additional maintenance or service, to be coordinated with authorized County project lead. All quotes for additional services shall contain detailed labor and material charges and approved by County project lead prior to commencement of maintenance or service. 
At the request of the County, Contractor may respond to urgent corrective maintenance prior to submitting quotes for initial call out response.
Contractor shall immediately notify authorized County project lead of any site conditions or changes affecting Contractor’s ability to perform services.

The OCLSB shall itself own and operate at least 1 fully licensed, insured, and operational truck used on the Contract.
The OCLSB receives credit for the total value of the transportation services it provides on the Contract using trucks it owns, insures, and operates using drivers it employs.
The OCLSB may lease trucks from another OCLSB firm including an owner-operator who is certified as an OCLSB. The OCLSB who leases trucks from another OCLSB receives credit for the total value of the transportation services the lessee OCLSB provides on the contract.
The OCLSB may also lease trucks from a non-OCLSB firm, including an owner-operator. The OCLSB who leases trucks from a non-OCLSB is entitled to credit for the total value of transportation services provided by non-OCLSB lessees not to exceed the value of transportation services provided by OCLSB owned trucks on the contract. Additional participation by non-OCLSB lessees receive credit only for the fee or commission it receives as a result of the lease arrangement.
A lease shall indicate that the OCLSB has exclusive use of and control over the truck. This does not preclude the leased truck from working for others during the term of the lease with the consent of the OCLSB so long as the lease gives the OCLSB absolute priority for use of the leased truck.

## PROTEST PROCEDURES
PROTEST PROCEDURES
All protests shall be typed under the protestor’s letterhead and submitted in accordance with the provisions stated herein. All protests shall include at a minimum the following information: 
The name, address, and telephone number of the protestor;
The signature of the protestor or the protestor’s representative;
The solicitation or contract number;
A detailed statement of the legal and/or factual grounds for the protest; and, 
The form of relief requested. 
Protest of Solicitation Specifications: 
All protests related to solicitation specifications must be submitted to the 
Deputy Procurement Agent (DPA), 
Diana Bagh
 at 
diana.bagh@pw.oc.gov
, no later than five (5) business days prior to the Closing Date of the solicitation. Protests received after the five (5) business-day deadline will not be considered by the County.
In the event the protest of specifications is denied, and the protestor wishes to continue in the solicitation process, the protestor must still submit a bid/response prior to the close of the solicitation in accordance with the solicitation submittal procedures provided in this solicitation. 
Protest of Solicitation Results: 
Protests related to solicitation results must be submitted to the 
Deputy Procurement Agent, 
Diana Bagh
 at 
diana.bagh@pw.oc.gov
, no later than five (5) business days after the Notice of Solicitation Results is provided by the DPA.
Protests relating to solicitation results received after the five (5) business day deadline 
will not
 be considered by the County. 
If the five (5) business day period expires without the receipt of a protest, the department may move forward with contract negotiation and award or if necessary, file the item for approval by the Board of Supervisors.
Protest Process 
In the event of a timely protest, the County shall not proceed with the solicitation or award of the contract until the DPA issues a decision on the protest. 
Upon receipt of a timely protest, the DPA will, within ten (10) business days of receipt of the protest, issue a decision in writing which shall state the reasons for the actions taken. 
The County may, after providing written justification, make the determination that an immediate award of the contract is necessary to protect the substantial interests of the County. The award of a contract shall in no way compromise the protester’s right to the protest procedures outlined herein. 
If the protestor disagrees with the decision of the DPA, the protestor may submit a written appeal to the County Procurement Officer requesting an appeal to the Procurement Appeals Board, in accordance with the process stated below. 
 
 
APPEALS PROCESS
If the protestor wishes to appeal the protest decision of the Deputy Procurement Agent, the protestor must submit, within three (3) business days from receipt of the Deputy Procurement Agent’s decision, a written appeal to the Office of the County Procurement Officer. 
Written appeals must be sent by mail to the address below with a courtesy copy by email;
 
County of Orange/County Executive Office
County Procurement Office
400 W. Civic Center Drive, 5th Floor
Santa Ana, CA 92701
Attn: County Procurement Officer
CPOAppeals@ceo.oc.gov
 
Within fifteen (15) business days, the County Procurement Officer will review all materials in connection with the appeal, assess the merits of the protest and provide a written determination that shall contain his or her decision on whether the appeal shall be forwarded to the Procurement Appeals Board.
The decision of the County Procurement Officer on whether to allow the appeal to go forward will be final and there shall be no right to any administrative appeals of this decision.

## GENERAL DESCRIPTION OF SERVICES
The Respondent will be contacted by County Project Management staff on an “as-needed” basis as projects arise to provide A-E services for professional services. Requirements will be discussed by the Parties and Respondent shall prepare a written 
Scope Statement
 that will include the specific work to be performed, including the costs and time required to complete the project/task. County Project Management staff will then review the Respondents’ 
Scope Statement
, proceed with negotiation of task costs and when satisfied, issue a Contract Task Order (CTO) against this Contract.
The Respondent shall serve as lead of a design team that may include other construction design professionals working together to ensure that the original design is carried through to the finished product, with no alterations in materials or design that would lead to safety issues or compromise the quality of the building or building component. Other team members who may be retained by the lead to support a project as a consultant may include, but are not limited to, landscape architects, lighting designers, data consultants, security consultants, controls engineers, commissioning consultants, traffic engineers, surveyors, estimators, special inspection, etc.
The Respondent shall be responsible for the preparation of comprehensive building assessments, designs, drawings, specifications, cost estimates, and reports within the scope of the Contract Task Order (CTO). In the preparation of construction drawings and specification, the Respondent shall also be responsible for:
Obtaining data by reviewing record drawings, visiting the site of the construction and by conferences with the User/Client and facility maintenance staff or by other actions as necessary to develop the design;
Checking of shop drawings, submittals, materials and other data submitted by the Construction Contractor for approval.
Furnishing consultation and advice to County to clarify the intent of the drawings and specifications and on questions that may arise during the construction of the project.
Space planning, programming and code compliance review and upgrades.
The meeting of submittal dates included in the 
Scope Statement 
of the Contract Task Order, including the work of consultants.
Coordination with various agencies having authority of jurisdiction for planning services, entitlement, fire life safety, CEQA, ADA, etc..
Construction administration services, testing and commissioning.
Close out services, as-built plans, material lists, project acceptance, etc.
The coordination of the various elements of the design to assure compatibility of architectural, structural, electrical, mechanical/plumbing, and other design features.
Other services as specifically included in the Contract Task Order related to project Initiation, Planning/Design, Bid/Award, Construction and Closeout.
The Respondent shall restrict themselves to the 
Scope Statement 
of the Contract Task Order. Any changes in the 
Scope Statement 
shall require prior written authorization by County.

## CONTRACT TASK ORDER
Respondent shall be assigned work via a task order by County which shall subsequently be referred to as the “Contract Task Order” (hereinafter “CTO”). A CTO for each project shall be developed by Respondent in conjunction with County Project Management staff. The County Project Manager shall manage all Respondent’s work including monitoring the CTO work schedule, quality of deliverables, review of invoiced amounts, adherence to set budget, and internal review of submittal packages. Respondent shall follow all requirements as outlined in the CTO; this general Scope of Work, the project specific 
Scope Statement
, and the Architect-Engineer Guide (Rev July 2018).
The CTO shall include a detailed 
Scope Statement,
 describing tasks to be performed with a specific list of deliverables for each task, schedule of work and cost to complete the work. The schedule of work shall allow enough time for meetings with County Management staff to review the work progress, provide technical and policy direction, resolve problems and ensure adherence to the work completion schedule. The CTO shall include a cover sheet provided by County Project Management staff with the appropriate signature blocks and contract information. Once both Parties agree, and all Parties have signed the CTO, County Management staff shall provide Respondent with a Notice to Proceed (NTP) to begin work. Respondent shall submit all plans, reports and other documents produced under the CTO to the assigned County Project Manager within the timeframe indicated in the CTO or as directed by County Project Management staff.
