## SCOPE OF WORK
Respondent shall provide professional structural engineering and related consulting services on an as-needed basis for County facilities, structures, infrastructure, and improvement projects. Services may involve new construction, additions, renovations, alterations, repairs, rehabilitation, seismic improvements, adaptive reuse, deferred maintenance, damage assessments, and evaluation of existing structures. Projects may include facilities designated as essential or non-essential and may vary in size, complexity, construction type, occupancy, age, and condition. The specific services, tasks, deliverables, schedule, staffing, and compensation required for each project shall be identified in the applicable Contract Task Order (CTO). Respondent shall perform only those services authorized in writing by the County.
Services may include, but are not limited to, the following:
A. Existing Conditions Investigation and Structural Assessment
Review available record drawings, calculations, reports, studies, specifications, maintenance records, and other available project information.
Conduct site visits, field investigations, visual observations, and structural condition assessments.
Document existing structural systems, materials, visible deterioration, damage, deficiencies, and potential unsafe conditions.
Evaluate structural components and systems, including foundations, slabs, floors, roofs, walls, framing, columns, beams, connections, equipment supports, anchorage, and other structural or nonstructural components.
Assess structures for corrosion, cracking, settlement, deflection, water intrusion, fire damage, impact damage, seismic damage, weather-related damage, or other deterioration.
Recommend additional investigation, testing, surveying, material sampling, destructive or nondestructive testing, or specialty consultant services when necessary. Destructive testing shall not be performed without prior written authorization from the County.
Prepare existing-condition reports, structural assessment reports, deficiency lists, photographs, sketches, repair recommendations, preliminary cost estimates, and prioritized corrective-action plans.
B. Structural Analysis and Engineering Studies
Perform structural analyses and calculations for existing and proposed buildings, structures, parking structures, and structural components.
Evaluate gravity-load and lateral-force-resisting systems, including wind and seismic loading.
Determine allowable structural loading and capacity for roofs, floors, walls, foundations, equipment supports, storage systems, photovoltaic systems, mechanical equipment, and other improvements.
Perform foundation evaluations, settlement analyses, structural feasibility studies, and alternative structural-system analyses.
Evaluate structural and nonstructural components for seismic performance and code compliance.
Perform seismic assessments, evaluations, retrofit studies, and strengthening analyses when required by the CTO.
Evaluate proposed penetrations, openings, attachments, modifications, equipment installations, and changes in use or occupancy that may affect the existing structural system.
Prepare engineering studies, technical memoranda, calculations, recommendations, and opinions regarding structural feasibility, safety, repair, rehabilitation, or replacement.
C. Structural Design and Construction Documents
Develop structural concepts, design criteria, design narratives, calculations, drawings, details, specifications, and other construction documents.
Provide structural design for new construction, additions, alterations, renovations, repairs, rehabilitation, seismic upgrades, and replacement projects.
Design foundations, slabs, retaining walls, framing systems, equipment pads, equipment supports, anchorage systems, canopies, platforms, stairs, guardrails, site structures, and other structural elements.
Prepare structural demolition plans, shoring concepts, temporary support requirements, sequencing requirements, and repair details when included in the CTO.
Coordinate structural design with architectural, civil, geotechnical, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, fire protection, security, telecommunications, and other project disciplines.
Identify design conflicts and coordinate resolutions before submission of construction documents.
Prepare technical specifications and special structural inspection and testing requirements.
Develop documents using AutoCAD, Revit, Building Information Modeling (BIM), or other County-approved software and file formats, as required by the CTO.
Provide quality-control and quality-assurance reviews of calculations, drawings, specifications, reports, and other deliverables before submission to the County.
D. Code, Regulatory, and Permitting Support
Perform services in accordance with applicable federal, State, and local laws, regulations, ordinances, codes, standards, guidelines, and County requirements in effect for the applicable project.
Identify applicable structural design criteria, loading requirements, seismic requirements, material standards, accessibility-related structural requirements, and special inspection requirements.
Coordinate with the County and agencies having jurisdiction, as authorized by the County.
Prepare and submit structural documents required for plan review, permitting, or regulatory approval.
Respond to plan-check comments and revise calculations, drawings, specifications, and other documents as required to obtain approval.
Participate in meetings with reviewing agencies, permitting authorities, County staff, and other project stakeholders when requested.
E. Cost Estimating, Scheduling, and Alternatives Analysis
Prepare opinions of probable construction cost at the project phases identified in the CTO.
Evaluate alternative structural systems, materials, repair methods, and construction approaches.
Provide recommendations based on structural performance, constructability, anticipated service life, operational impacts, schedule, and cost.
Identify potential structural risks, long-lead materials, construction constraints, and conditions that may affect project cost or schedule.
Assist the County with value engineering and development of cost-effective alternatives without compromising structural safety, code compliance, or project requirements.
F. Peer Review and Technical Consultation
Conduct independent peer reviews of structural calculations, drawings, specifications, reports, studies, and proposed repair or retrofit designs prepared by others.
Review structural designs for completeness, coordination, constructability, code compliance, and consistency with County requirements.
Prepare written review comments, technical findings, recommendations, and responses.
Participate in technical meetings and resolution of structural design issues.
Provide expert structural consultation, technical opinions, and recommendations on matters within the Respondent's professional qualifications.
G. Bid and Award Support
Assist the County in responding to bidder questions and requests for information.
Prepare addenda, revisions, sketches, clarifications, and supporting technical information.
Review proposed substitutions and requests for approved equals affecting the structural design.
Participate in pre-bid meetings, site walks, and other procurement-related meetings when requested.
Assist the County in reviewing bids for structural scope, completeness, and conformance with the construction documents.
H. Construction Phase Services
Attend preconstruction meetings, progress meetings, site meetings, and other construction-related meetings when requested.
Review structural shop drawings, product data, samples, delegated-design submittals, calculations, and other Respondent submittals for conformance with the design intent.
Respond to requests for information and provide clarifications, sketches, supplemental instructions, and proposed solutions to field conditions.
Conduct periodic site observations to evaluate whether observed structural work generally conforms to the approved construction documents.
Review proposed substitutions, change-order requests, Respondent proposals, and claims affecting the structural work.
Assist the County in evaluating unforeseen conditions, construction deficiencies, nonconforming work, and proposed corrective actions.
Coordinate with the County, Respondent, inspectors, testing laboratories, special inspectors, and other consultants regarding structural issues.
Prepare field observation reports, deficiency notices, punch-list items, and other documentation required by the CTO.
Review testing and special inspection reports and assist the County in resolving reported structural deficiencies.
Respondent site observations shall not relieve the construction Respondent of responsibility for construction means, methods, techniques, sequences, procedures, site safety, or compliance with the construction documents.
I. Project Closeout Services
Participate in final inspections and prepare structural punch-list items.
Review Respondent responses and corrective work related to identified structural deficiencies.
Review record drawings, as-built information, warranties, certifications, test reports, special inspection reports, and other structural closeout documents.
Prepare final structural reports, record documents, or updated drawings when required by the CTO.
Assist the County in determining whether structural work is substantially complete and ready for final acceptance.
J. Deliverables
Depending on the requirements of the individual CTO, deliverables may include:
Site investigation and existing-condition documentation.
Structural assessment and engineering reports.
Feasibility studies and alternatives analyses.
Structural calculations and design criteria.
Conceptual, schematic, design-development, and construction documents.
Drawings, details, technical specifications, and special inspection requirements.
Opinions of probable construction cost.
Project schedules and milestone submittals.
Plan-check responses and revised documents.
Bid-support and construction-support documentation.
Meeting minutes, field observation reports, photographs, and deficiency lists.
Punch lists, record documents, and final reports.
Electronic files in the format required by the County, including editable source files and PDF documents.
All deliverables shall be complete, accurate, coordinated, and suitable for their intended purpose. Respondent shall incorporate County review comments and provide revised deliverables within the schedule established in the CTO.

The OCLSB shall be responsible for the management and supervision of the entire trucking operation for which it is getting credit on a particular Contract and there shall not be a contrived arrangement for the purpose of counting OCLSB participation.
The OCLSB shall itself own and operate at least 1 fully licensed, insured, and operational truck used on the Contract.
The OCLSB receives credit for the total value of the transportation services it provides on the Contract using trucks it owns, insures, and operates using drivers it employs.
The OCLSB may lease trucks from another OCLSB firm including an owner-operator who is certified as an OCLSB. The OCLSB who leases trucks from another OCLSB receives credit for the total value of the transportation services the lessee OCLSB provides on the contract.
The OCLSB may also lease trucks from a non-OCLSB firm, including an owner-operator. The OCLSB who leases trucks from a non-OCLSB is entitled to credit for the total value of transportation services provided by non-OCLSB lessees not to exceed the value of transportation services provided by OCLSB owned trucks on the contract. Additional participation by non-OCLSB lessees receive credit only for the fee or commission it receives as a result of the lease arrangement.
A lease shall indicate that the OCLSB has exclusive use of and control over the truck. This does not preclude the leased truck from working for others during the term of the lease with the consent of the OCLSB so long as the lease gives the OCLSB absolute priority for use of the leased truck.

## PROTEST PROCEDURES
PROTEST PROCEDURES
All protests shall be typed under the protestor’s letterhead and submitted in accordance with the provisions stated herein. All protests shall include at a minimum the following information: 
The name, address, and telephone number of the protestor;
The signature of the protestor or the protestor’s representative;
The solicitation or contract number;
A detailed statement of the legal and/or factual grounds for the protest; and, 
The form of relief requested. 
Protest of Solicitation Specifications: 
All protests related to solicitation specifications must be submitted to the 
Deputy Procurement Agent (DPA), 
Shannon Thoene
 at 
shannon.thoene@occr.ocgov.com
, no later than five (5) business days prior to the Closing Date of the solicitation. Protests received after the five (5) business-day deadline will not be considered by the County.
In the event the protest of specifications is denied, and the protestor wishes to continue in the solicitation process, the protestor must still submit a bid/response prior to the close of the solicitation in accordance with the solicitation submittal procedures provided in this solicitation. 
Protest of Award of Contract: 
Protests related to the award of a contract must be submitted to the 
Deputy Procurement Agent, 
Shannon Thoene
 at 
shannon.thoene@occr.ocgov.com
, no later than five (5) business days after the Notice of Solicitation Results is provided by the DPA.
Protests relating to a proposed contract award received after the five (5) business day deadline 
will not
 be considered by the County. 
If the five (5) business day period expires without the receipt of a protest, the department may move forward with the contract award or if necessary, file the item for approval by the Board of Supervisors.
Protest Process 
In the event of a timely protest, the County shall not proceed with the solicitation or award of the contract until the DPA issues a decision on the protest. 
Upon receipt of a timely protest, the DPA will, within ten (10) business days of receipt of the protest, issue a decision in writing which shall state the reasons for the actions taken. 
The County may, after providing written justification, make the determination that an immediate award of the contract is necessary to protect the substantial interests of the County. The award of a contract shall in no way compromise the protester’s right to the protest procedures outlined herein. 
If the protestor disagrees with the decision of the DPA, the protestor may submit a written appeal to the County Procurement Officer requesting an appeal to the Procurement Appeals Board, in accordance with the process stated below. 
 
 
APPEALS PROCESS
If the protestor wishes to appeal the protest decision of the Deputy Procurement Agent, the protestor must submit, within three (3) business days from receipt of the Deputy Procurement Agent’s decision, a written appeal to the Office of the County Procurement Officer. 
Written appeals must be sent by mail to the address below with a courtesy copy by email;
 
County of Orange/County Executive Office
County Procurement Office
400 W. Civic Center Drive, 5th Floor
Santa Ana, CA 92701
Attn: County Procurement Officer
CPOAppeals@ceo.oc.gov
 
Within fifteen (15) business days, the County Procurement Officer will review all materials in connection with the appeal, assess the merits of the protest and provide a written determination that shall contain his or her decision on whether the appeal shall be forwarded to the Procurement Appeals Board.
The decision of the County Procurement Officer on whether to allow the appeal to go forward will be final and there shall be no right to any administrative appeals of this decision.

## Introduction
County of Orange (“County”) is soliciting proposals from qualified contractors (“Respondents”) to provide Construction Manager at Risk (“CM”) Services for 
Seed Amplification and Coordination Services
 Project ("Project"), which is located at 
TBD
. The awarded proposal (“Contract”) will provide a negotiated Guaranteed Maximum Price (“GMP”) for Pre-Construction Services between the County and the selected Respondent (“CMAR Entity” or “CMARE”). The County may, at its sole discretion, exercise its option to negotiate a GMP for the construction of the Project with the CMARE and will return to the Board of Supervisors for to execute a construction services contract.

OCLSB or DVBE Preference provides for the following
:
Invitation for Bid – IFB
A five percent (5%) deduction in the original bid price shall be applied to all confirmed OCLSB or DVBE bidders for evaluation purposes. If the lowest bidder is a certified OCLSB or DVBE bidder, the contract will be awarded at the certified OCLSB or DVBE’s original bid price. The maximum allowable preference deduction is $100,000.
Request for Proposal - RFP
No Cost - Any Request for Proposals that does not include cost as a scoring criteria shall instead apply the five percent (5%) or eight percent (8%) preference percentage pursuant to the eligibility requirements above to a scoring criteria in the RFP that makes up no more than twenty percent (20%) of the total RFP.
With Cost - An additional five percent (5%) shall be applied to the total cost of each certified OCLSB or DVBE to obtain their final score. 
If the final score of any OCLSB or DVBE matches the final score of a respondent who is not an OCLSB or DVBE, preference shall be given to the certified OCLSB or DVBE. If two or more OCLSBs and/or DVBEs have the same final score, the County shall determine the contract award based on the County’s best interests. Notwithstanding these preference procedures, the Orange County Board of Supervisors reserves the right to award contracts in any other permissible manner in consideration of the County’s best interests.

Business Certified as OCLSB and DVBE

Subcontractors
If bidder is submitting subcontractors to qualify for the OCLSB or DVBE preference, bidder must demonstrate through the Staffing Plan that 20% of the total bid amount is allocated to the OCLSB and/or DVBE subcontractor(s).

## Overview
The County is seeking a Contractor to facilitate seed amplification and provide coordination services to ensure a consistent and reliable supply of critical native plant materials for ecological restoration and enhancement in support of preserving and enhancing the County’s natural resources, aligned with the ecological approach and best practices developed by the Orange County Native Seed Partnership (Seed Partnership). Native seed amplification involves specialized expertise, long lead times, and coordination with seasonal growing cycles. A standing contract provides a dependable source and allows for flexibility to meet project-specific demands while protecting sensitive habitats and preserving genetic integrity of locally and regionally adapted seed stock.
The Seed Partnership includes Orange County land managers (e.g., OC Parks, California State Parks, University of California Irvine, and others). OC Parks, along with other County Agencies, participates in Seed Partnership coordination meetings aimed at developing best practices for native seed and enhancing the supply of native seeds with genetic origins in the Orange County Seed Collection Zone (Exhibit 1). Seed amplification is also known as “seed multiplication,” “seed increase,” “seed bulking,” or “seed farming.” The Contractor will address the County’s seed needs by subcontracting with qualified growers to fulfill seed orders and identify and recommend opportunities for regional collaboration, cost efficiency, quality improvement, and reliable supply development, supporting a consistent and reliable supply of genetically suitable native seed for County restoration and enhancement projects. Genetic suitability is determined by genetic provenance and protocols for collection and amplification of seed. The goal of genetic management within a native seed program is to maximize the success of restoration plantings while protecting the genetic diversity of natural populations.

## Seed Amplification and Coordination Services Scope
The Contractor shall amplify native seeds. The County will request seed amplification grow-outs by identifying the annual desired amount of pure live seed (PLS) pounds by species as a multi-year seed demand forecast. The Contractor will determine an appropriate plot size to yield the requested amount in coordination with the County. Standardized grow-out plots will include 50 square feet, 200 square feet, 500 square feet, 0.25-acre, 0.5-acre, and 1.0-acre sizes. There are hundreds of species of plants that grow on County property. Plants are organized into different groups by growth form and life history, including annuals, geophytes, perennial herbs, and perennial woody shrubs. Seed amplification shall occur in accordance with the County’s current best practices (Exhibit 2). Contractor shall maintain relevant knowledge as best practices adapt.
The Contractor shall utilize wild seed provided by the County to sow into container pots, planting beds, or farmland for custom amplification grow-outs. All equipment, materials, and labor needed to produce amplified seed are included in the Contractor’s pricing for the amplification services. All seed shall be grown in southern California under environmental conditions similar to Orange County (e.g., temperature range, rainfall, elevation). The Contractor shall provide supplemental watering (e.g., irrigation) as needed to support successful plant establishment and maturation. The plants that grow will mature and produce seed, and the resulting seed will be collected by the Contractor.
The Contractor shall clean, process, conduct initial seed testing at no extra charge on all amplified seed lots* (*A seed lot is defined as the harvested seed from a single year, representing a unique combination of species, year, and location.). All seed shall be cleaned using industry best practices, with all Stipa species de-awned. Very small lots, where seed testing would destroy an undesirable percentage of the available seed will be exempted from seed testing and labelled as such. The Contractor shall forgo seed testing on small lots only after consultation with the Manager. Seed testing shall be conducted by qualified labs familiar with testing seeds native and exotic to southern California and shall include a full evaluation of purity, germination, and a tetrazolium test. A tetrazolium test will be required for applicable species; otherwise, an alternative dormancy test will be conducted. Seed testing should include the type of seed, test date, the name of the supplier, live seed count per pound, results of a tetrazolium test, and percentage of the following: pure seed, crop seed, inert matter, weed seed, noxious weeds, and total germination content.
The Contractor shall deposit seed into refrigerated storage. Seed will be stored in a protected, refrigerated indoor location that is dark and cool. The seed will not be allowed to become damp.
County has first right of refusal on excess seed and focused coordination will occur as needed to make this determination. Discussion of excess seed between Contractor and County will occur as part of periodic coordination meetings.
The Contractor shall keep an inventory spreadsheet up to date and provide it to the County Project Manager when requested. For each seed lot, the inventory spreadsheet will include at a minimum the original wildland collection location, collection dates, number of bulk pounds of seed, number of PLS pounds of seed, purity, germination, live seed count per pound, date entered into storage, and the date of the most recent seed test.
The Contractor shall prepare (e.g., weighing, mixing, labeling, and bagging) and ship custom seed mixes and/or seed of individual species to County-designated destinations, including park facilities, nurseries, seed testing laboratories, etc. Upon County request, bran or sand may be added as a seed mix filler. The Contractor shall provide all materials needed for preparation and packaging/shipping, as applicable, including bags/containers, labels, and humidity/moisture control materials.
In addition to County-requested custom seed amplification grow-outs, the Contractor shall offer amplified seed from its general inventory for County purchase at a cost per PLS pound. The Contractor shall maintain an updated list of all available amplified seed, with pricing per PLS pound of each species, and provide it to the County Project Manager annually and upon request. “Off-the-shelf” purchases of amplified seed by PLS pound must be approved by the County Project Manager or designee.
The Contractor shall package and deliver seed to the County. Each seed bag must have a label that includes species name(s), Stock Keeping Unit (SKU) number(s), bulk pounds, PLS pounds, collection locations, and if the seed is an admixed ecotype the label shall include percent PLS from each collection location.
The Contractor shall create a Species Production Plan (Production Plan) for each species prior to amplification and provide it to the County Project Manager.
The Contractor shall perform restoration genetics due diligence by creating a concise (<1 page) Species Amplification Profile (Amplification Profile) for each ecotype, to be included with the Production Plan and used to guide County seed sourcing/collection and mixing strategies from natural populations. The purpose of the Amplification Profile is to ensure native seed amplification is ecologically appropriate and genetically sound. Each Amplification Profile will:
Summarize relevant species-specific knowledge, including key life history traits (e.g., dispersal syndromes), pollinator interactions, and population distributions.
Document the subwatershed and subregional origin of seed collections, including the percent PLS admixture in any composite ecotype.
Reference relevant scientific literature that informs the ecotype’s composition and restoration use.
 
The Contractor shall develop a Species Amplification Yield Estimation Table (SAYET) that identifies plant material types and quantities needed to establish bulking plots of various sizes and provides a method to estimate the plot size required to produce a target quantity of PLS pounds by species.
The Contractor shall coordinate proposed seed collection on County property and implement quality assurance protocols, including Calflora tracking, as follows:
Coordinate and review proposed seed collection activities on County property for County review and approval. Encroachment permits will be evaluated and processed by OC Parks.
Review seed collection documentation and deliverables as directed by the County. 
Review Calflora seed collection observation entries for accuracy and completeness.
Review historical Calflora records to help prevent overcollection, consistent with Exhibit 3 - Seed Collection Best Management Practices.
The Contractor shall provide once every two months a Bi-Monthly Progress Update and once every year an Annual Summary Report. Each Bi-Monthly Progress Update and Annual Summary Report shall be provided via a Microsoft Teams post. The Bi-Monthly Progress Update and the Annual Summary Report Progress will both be uploaded to a Microsoft Teams Channel that is created by the County Project Manager for the purposes of this Contract.
The Contractor shall attend six virtual meetings per year: one kickoff, four coordination meetings, and one closeout. At the beginning of each Contract Year, the County and Contractor will meet to allocate the annual budget across seed production and other Contract tasks and confirm the work plan.
The Contractor shall coordinate with regional subject-matter experts, as directed by the County, to develop and refine Best Management Practices (BMPs) for native seed collection, amplification, and storage. See Exhibit 2 – for amplification BMPs. 
The Contractor shall work with the County and, as directed by the County, regional practitioners to develop and maintain guidance documents for sowing native seed in wildlands.
The Annual Summary Report format will be developed in coordination with the County and shall be submitted in the last month of each Contract Year.  At minimum, the Annual Summary Report shall include:
Seed Needs
Summary of Seed Production for the Contract by grower
Summary of Calflora data related to seed collection
Species Production Plans for any species currently being amplified, including current status
Species Amplification Profiles for any species currently being amplified
Current Inventory Spreadsheet
The Contractor shall develop a Quality Assurance and Quality Control Protocol with Geospatial Tracking that is compatible with the Calflora Weed Manager application (https://www.calflora.org/entry/weed-mgr.html) and integrated with the seed inventory to meet the goals of OC Parks such as preventing over-collection and tracking collection provenance.
The Contractor shall develop a Seeding Rate Recommendations Table to track estimated and field-tested PLS lbs/acre seeding rates for species appropriate for direct seeding in restoration projects. The purpose of the Seeding Rate Recommendations Table is to guide the County to use the lowest effective seeding rate for successful establishment of species from seed to maximize cost efficiency and restoration project success. Seeding rate recommendations will be presented as a range for each species.
The Contractor shall develop a Plant Species Restoration Guide that summarizes species-specific best practices, including a Direct Seeding vs. Container Planting Recommendations Table indicating the preferred establishment method by species. The Guide shall be developed using input from subject-matter experts (e.g., ecologists, native plant propagators) and existing literature, as coordinated with the County, to support cost-effective restoration outcomes.
The Contractor shall develop a Seed Pricing Database in PLS pounds by compiling southern California industry pricing and documenting actual production costs for species amplified under this Contract.
The Contractor shall prepare a Provenancing Approach Guide, including a table of recommended sourcing scales (e.g., regional, subregional, watershed) for ecotype development by species.
The Contractor shall prepare a Plant Species Supply Optimization Guide (table format) identifying, by species, when to use wild-collected plant material (including seed and, where applicable, non-seed propagules such as bulbs/corms/tubers) versus amplified plant material for restoration projects. The Guide shall include suggested decision thresholds (if applicable) and a brief justification prioritizing minimizing impacts to natural populations and maintaining genetic suitability.
The Contractor shall prepare a Species Collection and Tribal Harvesting Guide (table format), by species, identifying recommended timing windows for wild seed collection. Any information on seasonal Tribal harvesting periods shall be included by species only when provided/approved by regionally appropriate Tribes and as directed by the County. The Guide shall include citations for referenced information, and each entry shall include the associated reference/source.
The Contractor shall prepare Standardized Plant Species Lists outlining planting and seeding palettes for restoration and enhancement project types as directed by the County. Each list shall include at least 15 species and identify no more than 4 core species. Project types may include the following:
Coastal CSS
Interior CSS
Native Grassland
Native Forbland
Post-fire Recovery
North-facing Slopes / Lemonade Scrub
Chaparral
Oak Woodland Understory
Elderberry Shrubland
Emergent Wetland
Transitional Riparian
Riparian Woodland Understory
Erosion Control Mix
Showy Wildflower Mix
Trailside for Restoration Projects (10-foot buffer)
Tribal Use/Tribal Priorities, as directed by the County and regionally appropriate Tribes
OCFA compatible Fuel Modification Mix
The Contractor shall develop and refine Best Management Practices Guidelines for Wild Seed Collection, Seed Amplification, and Seed Storage, as directed by the County.

## Prequalification Protest Hearing Procedure
Where the prospective bidder has made a timely and complete submittal of prequalification documents that result in a determination that the contractor is not qualified, the prospective bidder can contest the department’s decision via administrative hearing.
To petition for a hearing, the prospective bidder must deliver written notice of its desire to contest the department’s decision to County of Orange within seven (7) calendar days of the date of County’s notice of determination. Failure to file a timely notice shall result in the prospective bidder’s waiver of any and all rights to challenge the prequalification determination, whether by administrative process, judicial process, or any other legal process or proceeding.
The prospective bidder may request the County to advise it in writing of the basis for the prequalification determination and any supporting evidence that was received from others or adduced as a result of an investigation by the County.
A Hearing Panel shall be established and consist of three panelists from various County of Orange infrastructure departments, with a maximum of one (1) panelist from the procuring department.
The Hearing Panel shall render its decision based on all potentially relevant evidence submitted by either the County or the prospective bidder, including but not limited to, the administrative record and testimonial evidence. The prospective bidder may submit on the record, or provide other evidence, including testimony given under oath, to rebut the department’s determination of non-qualification. Such a hearing is conducted in an informal manner, and all relevant evidence is admissible. The department rendering the initial determination may rebut any evidence proffered by the prospective bidder in writing or through its own testimony. Finally, the Hearing Panel may ask questions of either the prospective bidder or department before making its decision.
If the prospective bidder requests to provide testimony, the hearing shall be conducted within five (5) business days after the County’s receipt on notice of appeal and no later than 20 business days prior to the last date of receipt of bids on the project. Within three (3) business days after the conclusion of the hearing, the Hearing Panel will render its decision in writing.
The decision of the Hearing Panel shall be the County’s final administrative decision and any judicial review thereof shall be instituted no later than the time period specified in Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

Description:
The County of Orange, 
County Executive Office - CPO
 (hereinafter referred to as “County”), is soliciting proposals from qualified firms (hereinafter referred to as “Respondents”) to establish a Regional Cooperative Agreement (RCA) for 
The County is soliciting proposals to establish a Countywide Regional Cooperative Agreement (RCA) for Janitorial Services to support multiple County departments and facilities. Services include routine, periodic, and emergency cleaning of interior and exterior areas such as offices, public spaces, restrooms, locker rooms, showers, gyms, kitchens, clinical and high-risk environments, detention or secured facilities (where applicable), and surrounding exterior areas. The scope of services includes, but is not limited to, trash and recycling removal, floor care (sweeping, mopping, stripping, sealing, waxing, and carpet extraction), restroom and shower sanitation, cleaning and disinfecting of high-touch and public-facing areas, glass and window cleaning, exterior waste collection, enhanced disinfecting services, and day porter services at designated locations. All services shall be provided as a full-service janitorial operation using commercial-grade equipment, supplies, and disinfectants, and performed in accordance with applicable health, safety, environmental, and regulatory requirements to maintain County facilities in a clean, safe, sanitary, and professional condition.

Attendance at all required job walks and compliance with the requirements contained in these documents is mandatory. Failure to comply with these requirements may result in a proposal being deemed non-responsive. Any parking fees incurred while attending the mandatory pre-proposal job walks shall be the sole responsibility of the Respondent.

The County of Orange operates a large and diverse portfolio of facilities that support essential public services, including public-facing offices, clinical and health service locations, libraries, detention and secure facilities, training centers, and administrative buildings. These facilities experience high daily usage, extended operating hours, and serve a wide range of users, including County staff, justice-involved individuals, vulnerable populations, and the general public. Maintaining clean, safe, and sanitary facilities is critical to supporting County operations, protecting public health, ensuring regulatory compliance, and maintaining public trust. Janitorial services play a direct role in risk reduction, infection prevention, facility longevity, and overall service delivery, particularly in high-traffic, high-risk, and continuously operating environments.
The County is seeking a contractor capable of delivering consistent, professional, and full-service janitorial operations across multiple facility types with varying usage patterns, security requirements, and sanitation needs. The work extends beyond routine cleaning and requires the ability to adapt to operational realities, including after-hours service, emergency response, enhanced disinfecting, exterior waste challenges, and day porter support at select locations.
Project Challenges:
Managing services across multiple departments and facility types, each with distinct operational needs
Maintaining sanitation standards in high-traffic and public-facing environments
Supporting facilities with 24-hour operations, secure areas, or restricted access
Addressing specialized cleaning requirements, including biohazard-sensitive areas and infection-control environments
Responding quickly to unplanned events, such as spills, public health concerns, or increased facility usage
Ensuring consistent service delivery while coordinating with County staff, facility managers, and security personnel
A successful contractor will demonstrate the ability to deliver reliable, consistent, and high-quality cleaning services across all assigned facilities; proactively manage staffing, supervision, and communication to prevent service gaps; and recognize that this is a full-service operation requiring more than surface-level or minimum-effort cleaning. The contractor must respond promptly to day-to-day needs, issues, and emergency situations while maintaining strong quality control, compliance, and accountability practices. Successful vendors will also demonstrate a clear understanding of the County’s operational complexity, show flexibility and responsiveness, and present a service approach that prioritizes health, safety, professionalism, and consistency in support of clean, safe, and professional County environments.

## General Information:
The County of Orange is comprised of 22 Departments and over 18,000 employees located throughout the County.  The County’s core businesses are public safety, public works, construction management, public health, environmental protection, regional planning, public assistance, social services, and aviation.

## PROTEST PROCEDURES
PROTEST PROCEDURES
All protests shall be typed under the protestor’s letterhead and submitted in accordance with the provisions stated herein. All protests shall include at a minimum the following information: 
The name, address, and telephone number of the protestor;
The signature of the protestor or the protestor’s representative;
The solicitation or contract number;
A detailed statement of the legal and/or factual grounds for the protest; and, 
The form of relief requested. 
Protest of Solicitation Specifications: 
All protests related to solicitation specifications must be submitted to the 
Deputy Procurement Agent (DPA), 
Jessica Cortez
 at 
jessica.cortez@ceo.oc.gov
, no later than five (5) business days prior to the Closing Date of the solicitation. Protests received after the five (5) business-day deadline will not be considered by the County.
In the event the protest of specifications is denied, and the protestor wishes to continue in the solicitation process, the protestor must still submit a bid/response prior to the close of the solicitation in accordance with the solicitation submittal procedures provided in this solicitation. 
Protest of Award of Contract: 
Protests related to the award of a contract must be submitted to the 
Deputy Procurement Agent, 
Jessica Cortez
 at 
jessica.cortez@ceo.oc.gov
, no later than five (5) business days after the Notice of Solicitation Ranking Results is provided by the DPA.
Protests relating to a proposed contract award received after the five (5) business day deadline 
will not
 be considered by the County. 
If the five (5) business day period expires without the receipt of a protest, the department may move forward with the contract award or if necessary, file the item for approval by the Board of Supervisors.
Protest Process 
In the event of a timely protest, the County shall not proceed with the solicitation or award of the contract until the DPA issues a decision on the protest. 
Upon receipt of a timely protest, the DPA will, within ten (10) business days of receipt of the protest, issue a decision in writing which shall state the reasons for the actions taken. 
The County may, after providing written justification, make the determination that an immediate award of the contract is necessary to protect the substantial interests of the County. The award of a contract shall in no way compromise the protester’s right to the protest procedures outlined herein. 
If the protestor disagrees with the decision of the DPA, the protestor may submit a written appeal to the County Procurement Officer requesting an appeal to the Procurement Appeals Board, in accordance with the process stated below. 
 
APPEALS PROCESS
If the protestor wishes to appeal the protest decision of the Deputy Procurement Agent, the protestor must submit, within three (3) business days from receipt of the Deputy Procurement Agent’s decision, a written appeal to the Office of the County Procurement Officer.

## Attachment A - Scope Of Work
General Information
Contractor shall provide comprehensive Countywide Janitorial Services to County departments and facilities throughout the County of Orange on a professional, systemic, and thorough basis. Services shall include, but are not limited to, routine and enhanced cleaning, chemical based disinfecting, emptying and transporting trash and waste to designated disposal locations, interior and exterior glass and window cleaning, vacuuming, sweeping, dusting, hard surface floor maintenance including buffing, stripping, sealing, and waxing, carpet vacuuming and deep extraction shampooing, restroom, kitchen, locker room, shower, gym, and high-risk are cleaning, exterior waste and debris collection, and emergency clean-ups. All 
services shall be performed in strict accordance with the frequencies, standards, and performance requirements set forth in this Scope of Work. Partial, surface only, or dry cleaning that fails to meet required disinfecting, sanitation, or appearance standards is unacceptable and shall constitute non-performance. 
Contractor acknowledges that this Scope of Work represents a full-service janitorial operation. Contractor shall provide, at its sole expense, all labor, supervision, equipment, tools, materials, chemicals, disinfectants, paper goods, consumables, dispensers, personal protective equipment (PPE), and incidentals necessary to fully and properly perform the required services. Failure to include these costs in pricing shall not relieve the Contractor of any performance obligation under this Contract. 
Each service period, as defined in this Scope of Work, shall  commence on the effective date of the Contract unless otherwise directed by the County’s Project Manager or designee. Within ten (10) calendar days of the effective date of the Contract, Contractor shall submit a mutually agreeable service calendar identifying all required daily, weekly, biweekly, monthly, quarterly, semi-annual and annual services. The service calendar shall be subject to County review and approval and shall not be implemented until approved. The Contractor shall notify the County’s Project Manager or designee of any proposed or actual deviation from the approved schedule and shall obtain approval prior to implementing any changes. Failure to submit, maintain, or adhere to the approved service calendar shall constitute non-performance under this Contract.
Definitions
County: The County of Orange, including all County departments, agencies, offices, boards, commissions, facilities, properties, and authorized representatives.
County Project Manager: The County employee designated by the County to administer, oversee, and enforce the Contract at a specific facility or for designated facilities. The County Project Manager is authorized to provide direction regarding scheduling, inspection, acceptance of work, performance standards, access coordination, reporting requirements, and day to day operational matters related to this Contract.
Biohazard: Biological substances or materials that pose a threat to human health. Biohazards include, but are not limited to, medical waste, blood and other bodily fluids, sharps and needles, laboratory specimens, and  microorganism, virus, bacteria, or toxins derived from biological source that may cause disease or adverse health effects.
Daily: Shall include the period of normal work week, i.e., Monday through Friday, including Saturdays and Sundays when necessary or so designated.
Weekly: Shall mean once per calendar week.
Bi-Weekly:  Shall mean once every two (2) calendar weeks. Bi-weekly service shall be scheduled at regular two-week intervals and are not tied to the  number of days in a calendar month. 
Monthly: Shall mean once per calendar month, regardless of the number of days in the month.  All monthly services shall be performed during the first full week of each calendar month unless otherwise approved in writing by the County Project Manager or designee.
Quarterly: Shall mean once every three (3) calendar months.  All quarterly services shall be performed during the second full week of the first month of each  quarter, unless otherwise approved in writing by the  County Project Manager or designee. The first quarterly service period shall commence on the effective date of the Contract, and each subsequent quarterly period shall commence at three (3) month intervals thereafter.
Semi-Annually: Shall mean once every six (6) calendar months.  All semi-annual services shall be performed during the third full week of the first month of each semi-annual period, unless otherwise approve in writing by the County Project Manager or designee. The first semi-annual service period shall commence on the effective date of the Contract, and each subsequent semi-annual period shall commence at six (6) months intervals thereafter.
Annual: Shall mean once (1) per calendar year.  All annual services shall be performed  during the fourth full week of the first month of each annual period, unless otherwise approved in writing by the County Project Manager or designee.   The first annual service period shall commence on the effective date of the Contract, and each subsequent annual period shall commence at one (1) year intervals thereafter.
Day Porter: A Contractor employee assigned  on-site during normal working hours for the purpose of providing immediate, ongoing support and response to Contract related services. Day Porter duties include, but are not limited to, removal of health and safety hazards such as spills, broken glass, and debris, response to emergency clean-ups, including plumbing and roof leaks, refilling and maintaining supplies or dispensers, enhanced disinfecting of high-touch and public areas, restroom, kitchens servicing, exterior waste collection, and general facility upkeep. Day Porter services are in addition to, and not a substitute for, regular custodial operations performed outside normal working hours.
Damp Mopping: A floor cleaning method performed after sweeping and/or  dust mopping to remove remaining dust, dirt, and debris. Damp mopping shall be performed using a clean mop, clean water, and an all purpose floor cleaner, with  a disinfectant added where required by the Scope of Work. Mop shall be properly wrung out so that floors are left clean without excess moisture, standing water, or reside.
Dirt: Foreign matter or debris including, but not limited to, sand, soil, grit, pebbles, mud, dust, lint, fuzz, tar, ashes, liquid spills, stains, residue, and other particulate or contaminating substances.
Disinfect: To apply a germicidal disinfectant in sufficient quantity to fully wet or saturate the surface, fixture, or floor so as to achieve complete contact coverage, and to allow the disinfectant to remain on the surface for the full manufacturer specific dwell time, followed by rinsing or wiping as required by the manufacturer’s instructions. Dry wiping, misting, surface-only application, or chemical application without achieving full coverage or required dwell time does not constitute disinfecting and is unacceptable.
Spray Buffing: A floor maintenance process used to remove heel marks, scuffs, and light soil in high traffic areas and to restore hard surface floors to a uniform appearance. Spray buffing shall be performed using an approved floor machine and soft buffing pad in accordance with manufacturer recommendations. Sweeping or dust mopping and damp mopping shall be completed prior to spray buffing.
Carpet Cleaning: The cleaning of carpets using the deep dirt extraction method (steam cleaning) performed in accordance with the carpet manufacturer’s recommendations. Carpet cleaning shall remove embedded soil, stains, residue, and contaminants. Bonnet buffing, surface shampooing, or other low-moisture methods that do not achieve deep extraction do not meet this definition unless expressly approved in writing by the County.
Dust Mopping:  The removal of loose dirt, dust, lint, and debris from floor surfaces using a dust mop prior to damp mopping, wet mopping, or other floor maintenance activities.
Easily Movable Items:  Furniture, equipment, waste receptacles, chairs, or other items  that weigh fifty (50) pounds or less or can be safely moved by one (1) person without the use of mechanical assistance.
Emergency Clean-ups:  Immediate response cleaning services required to address unplanned or hazardous conditions, including but not limited to water intrusion from  roof leaks, plumbing leaks, flooding, sewer backups, spills, broken fixtures, or other conditions that pose a risk to health, safety, property, or operations. Emergency clean-ups include containment, removal of water debris, disinfecting affected areas as required, placement of warning signage or barricades, and actions necessary to prevent further damage until permanent repairs are completed.
Floor Maintenance:  The performance of floor care activities required to maintain floors in a clean, orderly, uniform, and safe condition. Floor maintenance includes, but is not limited to, sweeping, dust mopping, damp mopping, wet mopping, scrubbing, stripping, sealing, waxing, dry buffing, and spray buffing, as applicable to the floor type and service frequency specified in this Scope of Work.
Glass:  All exposed interior or exterior glass or glass like surfaces that are not classified as windows, including but not limited to, mirrors, glass entrance doors, glass partitions, display cases, and transparent or translucent materials such as  Lucite, acrylic, plastic, or similar  materials.
Gyms/Fitness Rooms/Exercise Areas:  County facilities may include gyms, fitness rooms, exercise areas, or similar spaces. Contractor shall provide full janitorial cleaning and disinfecting services for such areas.
High Glass:  Glass surfaces, including but not limited to glass walls, elevator glass, partitions, similar glass elements, where the lower edge or any portion of the glass surface begins at or extends  six (6) feet or more above the finished floor or ground level.
Neat/Clean:  Orderly and well maintained, free from visible dirt, dust, stains, smudges, debris, residue and other foreign matter.
Cleaning: The physical removal of  dirt, dust, organic matter, and impurities from surfaces using appropriate cleaning agents and methods. Cleaning reduces the number  germs present but does not kill germs. Cleaning is a required preparatory step and does not replace disinfecting where disinfecting is specified in the Scope of Work.
Disinfecting: The application of  chemical agents, including EPA-registered disinfectants, to kill germs and microorganisms on surfaces. Disinfecting shall be performed after cleaning, in accordance with manufacturer instructions, and shall include full service coverage and required dwell time. Disinfecting does not replace  cleaning and shall not be considered complete unless surfaces have been properly cleaned prior to disinfectant application.
Professional:  Conforming to the technical, ethical, and performance standards of the janitorial and facilities maintenance profession; exhibiting appropriate conduct, appearance, skill, experience, and competence, and performing services in a matter consistent with industry best practices and the requirements of this Contract.
Scrubbing (hard surface floors):  The cleaning of hard surface floor areas performed  after sweeping or dust mopping by applying an appropriate all-purpose detergent,  agitating the surface using a floor scrubber or slow speed buffing machine, and thoroughly rinsing the area two (2) or more times with clean water. Residual water, soil, and detergent shall be removed using  a wet-vacuum or equivalent method, leaving the floor free of residue, film, and standing water.
Sealing (Hard Surface Floors):  The application of a protective floor sealant following  stripping and cleaning with a neutral cleaner. Sealing shall include the application of a minimum of two (2) uniform coats of sealant to protect and seal the floor surface, applied in accordance with manufacturer recommendations and allowed to properly cure prior to use.
Dressing Rooms: Rooms or areas designated for changing clothes or personal preparation, including but not limited to locker rooms, changing rooms, and adjacent or associated areas. Dressing rooms include all floors, walls, ceilings, lockers (interior and exterior where accessible), benches, seating, hooks, mirrors, doors, door hardware, vents, drains, mats, trash receptacles, and all other fixtures, furnishings, and surfaces within the space.  
Spray Buffing (Hard Surface Floors): A floor maintenance process used to clean hard surface floors, remove heal marks, scuffs, and light soil in high traffic areas, and restore a uniform appearance. Spray buffing shall be performed using an approved buffing pad, floor machine, and spray buffing chemical, resulting in a uniform, thin coat of non-skid floor finish. Sweeping or dust mopping and damp mopping shall be completed prior to spray buffing.
Stairways/Stairwell/Staircase:  One or more flights of stairs used to travel between levels, including steps, risers, treads, landings, handrails, guardrails, casings, supporting framework, and the vertical shaft or enclosure in which the stairs are located. Stairways, stairwells, and staircases include all associated floor surfaces, walls, and adjacent areas.  All stairways, stairwells, and staircases shall receive floor maintenance and cleaning services in accordance with this Scope of Work.
Stripping (Hard Surface Floors): The removal of existing floor finish or wax using an approved stripping solution (alkaline based), in combination with a stripping pad and floor scrubbing or stripping machine,  including edges and corners. Stripping shall be followed by neutralization using an appropriate neutralizing agent and area minimum of two (2) rinses with clean water. All stripper solution, residue, and rinse water shall be removed using a wet vacuum or equivalent method,  leaving the floor clean and free of  wax buildup, residue, and film.
Sweeping:  The removal of loose dirt, dust, debris, and foreign matter from floor surfaces using a broom, brush broom, or dust mop as preparatory step prior to damp mopping, wet mopping, or other floor maintenance activities.
Walk-Off Mats: Mats made of rubber, carpet, vinyl, polyester, or other materials, located inside and outside building entrances and in other designated interior areas, used to capture dirt, moisture, and debris tracked into County facilities. Walk-off mats include all entrance mats, runner mats, and floor mats placed for safety, cleanliness, or facility protection purposes.
Waxing: The application of manufacturer recommended thin coasts of non-skid floor finish to hard surface floors to protect the surface and enhance durability. Waxing shall be performed in accordance with manufacturer instructions and shall result in a uniform, glossy appearance that is non-slippery, free from streaks, buildup, or uneven coating, and safe for pedestrian traffic after proper cleaning.
Kitchen:  Any food preparation, food storage, breakroom, or kitchenette area, including but not limited to walls, floors, ceilings, countertops, cabinets, sinks, appliances such as but not limited to refrigerators, microwaves, and ventilation surfaces.
Showers: Any enclosed or unenclosed area designated for bathing or rinsing, including individual or group shower areas and adjacent wet zones. Showers include all walls, floors, ceilings, drains, grout, fixtures, valves, handles, shower heads, curtains, doors, frames, mats, benches, shelves, and all adjacent surfaces exposed to water, moisture, soap or bodily contract.
Wet Mopping: The thorough cleaning of hard floor surfaces performed after sweeping or dust mopping, using clean water and an appropriate all-purpose detergent solution, with a disinfectant added where required by the Contract specifications. Wet mopping shall remove soil, stains, and residue, and floors shall be left clean, uniform in appearance, and free of standing water, streaks, and slip hazards. 
Glass and Windows: Includes all interior glass and windows, including but not limited to glass partitions, glass lobby walls, trophy and display cases, directory boards, wall mirrors, door windows, doors and adjacent trim, including escalator glass (if applicable), and all associated interior and exterior frames, casings, sills, and adjacent trim. . Unless explicitly excluded in writing by the County, window and glass cleaning includes interior and exterior windows, glass lobby walls, glass partitions, and glass in reporting-writing rooms.
Commercial Grade: Equipment, tools, materials, supplies, and dispensers designed, manufactured, and marketed for continuous or frequent use in commercial, institutional, or industrial facilities. Commercial-grade items shall be durable, heavy-duty, suitable for high-traffic and high-use environments, and capable of meeting the performance, safety, and longevity requirements for this Contract. Residential, consumer, or household-grade items are not considered commercial-grade unless expressly approved in writing by the County.

Safety

Contractor shall provide notice to affected personnel by posting caution signs, barricades, or other warning devices where applicable. Contractor shall safely handle any biohazardous materials encountered during performance of services and shall immediately notify the Project Manager or designee upon discovery of needles, sharps, bodily fluids, or other hazardous or potentially infectious waste. Contractor shall take reasonable and appropriate measures to secure the area and prevent further exposure until proper response or disposal can be arranged. 
Personal Protective Equipment (PPE): Contractor shall provide, at its sole expense, and require all Contractor personnel to properly use appropriate Personnel Protective Equipment (PPE) necessary to safely perform services under this Contract. PPE requirements shall comply with all applicable, federal, state, and local laws, regulations, and directives, including but not limited to Cal/OSHA requirements and any applicable County Health Officer orders in effect at the time services are performed. Required PPE may include, but is not limited to, face coverings, gloves, eye protection, gowns, masks, or other protective equipment appropriate to the work being performed, the environment, and any identified health or safety risks. The County reserves the right to require additional or enhanced PPE based on site-specific conditions, public health guidance, regulatory requirements, or the nature of services being performed. Failure to comply with PPE requirements may result in immediate removal of affected personnel and shall constitute non-performance. Contractor shall promptly provide qualified replacement personnel at no additional cost to the County, and such removal shall not relieve Contractor of its obligation to continue performance under the Contract. 
Safe Practices: Contractor shall use all cleaning solutions, disinfectants, and chemicals strictly in accordance with the manufacturer’s instructions, applicable safety date sheets (SDS/MSDS), and all applicable federal, state, and local health and safety laws and regulations. Contractor shall ensure that appropriate PPE is used, that work areas are adequately ventilated, and that products are properly mixed, handled, stored, and disposed of in accordance with applicable requirements.  Contractor shall post appropriate caution signs, barricades, or warnings to alert County staff, visitors, and the public of wet floors, slippery surfaces, chemical use, or other temporary hazards created during cleaning operations. Contractor shall immediately correct any unsafe condition created by its operations and shall promptly report any safety incidents, chemical spills, exposures, or injuries to the Project Manager or designee. Failure to follow safe practices may result in immediate removal or Contractor personnel and shall constitute non-performance under this Contract. 
Conservation of Utilities 
Contractor shall ensure that all Contractor personnel practice conservation of utilities while performing services under this Contract. Contractor shall conduct operations in a manner that prevents unnecessary use or waste of electricity, water, gas, or other utilities within the County facilities. Utilities shall be used only as necessary to perform required services and in compliance with all applicable County directives related to utility conservation. Failure to comply with utility conservation requirements may be considered non-performance. 
Lighting: Lights shall be used only in the areas where work is actively being performed and shall be turned off immediately upon completion of cleaning activities in each area, except where lighting must remain on for safety or security purposes as directed by the County. Failure to comply with lighting conservation requirements may be considered non-performance. 
Mechanical Systems: Contractor personnel shall not adjust, tamper with, override, or otherwise manipulate mechanical equipment or controls for heating, ventilation or air condition (HVAC) systems, thermostats, or related controls under any circumstances, unless expressly authorized in writing by the County. Any unauthorized adjustment or interference with mechanical systems shall constitute non-performance. 
Contractor’s Office/Emergency 
Contractor shall maintain a staffed office located within Orange County and shall provide a reliable telephone communications system capable of receiving and responding to emergency calls twenty-four (24) hours per day, seven (7) days per week.  Contractor shall ensure that all emergency calls are acknowledged and returned within one (1) hour. Contractor shall provide emergency responses to the affected site within no more than two (2) hours of notification, unless otherwise directed by the County. Emergency response shall include the dispatch of appropriately trained and equipped personnel capable of addressing the reported condition. Contractor shall bear all costs associated with emergency response services required under this Contract. Failure to meet emergency communication or response requirements may be considered non-performance and subject to corrective action in accordance with the Contract. 
Protection and Restoration 
Contractor shall take all necessary precautions to protect County facilities, furnishings, fixtures, equipment, surfaces, and improvements from damage resulting from Contractor operations.  Any damage to County property caused by the Contractor, its employees, agents, or subcontractors shall be promptly reported to the Project Manager or designee. All such damage shall be repaired or replaced, at the option of the County, at the Contractor’s sole expense and within a timeframe acceptable to the County.  Repairs and replacements shall be equal to or better than the original condition in all respects, including quality, appearance, and functionality. If Contractor fails to complete required repairs or replacements within the timeframe specified by the County, the County may, at its option, perform or procure the necessary work and deduct the associated costs from payments due or become due to the Contractor. Damage caused by Contractor operations shall not be considered normal wear and tear and shall not constitute grounds for delay, non-performance, or additional compensation. 
Restrictions 
Use of County Property and Equipment: Contractor personnel shall not disturb, remove, or handle papers, files, or materials on desks or workstations; open drawers, cabinets, or storage areas; or access, use, or operate County or personal equipment or property, including but not limited to radios, computers, televisions, printers, copiers, coffee pots, stoves, microwaves, refrigerators, or other appliances, unless expressly authorized in writing by the County.  Contractor personnel shall not tamper with, alter, damage, misuse, or interfere with any County or personal property. Any violation of this provision may result in immediate removal of Contractor personnel and shall constitute non-performance under this Contract. 
Telephone and Communications Systems: Contractor personnel shall not use County telephones, communication systems, or devices for personal use or for business purposes unrelated to performance of this Contract, unless expressly authorized in writing by the County. Use of County telephones is permitted solely for emergency purposes, including reporting the need for medical assistance, fire response, or law enforcement by dialing 8-911 or other emergency numbers as directed by the County. 
Unauthorized use of County telephones or communication systems shall constitute non-performance and may result in immediate removal of Contractor personnel from County facilities. Repeated or serious violations may be grounds for further contractual remedies, up to and including termination, in accordance with the Contract Terms and Conditions. 
Radios: Contractor personnel shall not access, use, operate, or interfere with any County two-way radios, radio systems, intercoms, security communications systems,  or other specialized  telecommunications equipment under any circumstances.  No exceptions shall be made to this requirement. Any unauthorized use or interference with County radios or telecommunications equipment shall constitute non-performance and may result in immediate removal of Contractor personnel from County facilities. Repeated or serious violations may be grounds for further contractual remedies, up to and including termination, in accordance with the Contract Terms and Conditions.

Claims of financial hardship, cost increases, or inability to perform related to materials, supplies, equipment, or consumables shall not be accepted and shall not excuse performance or serve as a basis for price adjustments. Janitorial Cleaners & Products
Janitorial Cleaners and Products are divided into the following classifications: Hard surface/General-Purpose Cleaners; Biologically based Cleaning and Degreasing Compounds; Disinfectants and Disinfecting Cleaners; Carpet & Upholstery Cleaners; and Floor-Care Products. These classifications cover products ranging from bathroom, carpet and upholstery, general purpose, window/glass, disinfectant, and industrial cleaners.
Contractor must purchase products in compliance with the maximum allowable Volatile Organic Compound content, under the California Code of Regulations (Article 2 Section 94509, Title 17). The current level of VOC content for this product category is 30%. Products must, at a minimum, meet this VOC requirement. Product performance should meet industry acceptable performance standards. All products must be compliant with California OSHA requirements.
Improper use can affect the performance of green cleaning products; Contractor should provide training to maintenance staff on the proper use of the products. Training is considered essential for successful implementation.
