Services To Be Provided
The Contract specifications define the minimum level of service and frequency deemed acceptable.  Contractor shall schedule and perform its operations to meet or exceed these requirements. Contractor shall provide a thorough and comprehensive level of cleaning and maintenance and shall not perform surface-only or cosmetic cleaning. Services shall include, but are not limited to, thorough high and low dusting of all areas as described in the Scope of Work: sweeping, mopping, waxing, and buffing hard surfaces floors to maintain a clean, uniform, and glossy appearance; spot cleaning, complete vacuuming, and deep extraction shampooing of carpeted floors, leaving carpets free of dirt, gum, stains, residue, or other foreign matter; cleaning of interior and exterior glass and entrance doors so that all traces of film, dirt, smudges, streaks and water spots are removed; and spot cleaning of smudges, smears, grease marks, and residue from walls, doors, handles, push bars, kick plates, light switches and electrical outlet cover plates. Restroom facilities shall be thoroughly cleaned and sanitized, and fixtures polished to achieve a level of cleanliness consistent with institutional or healthcare grade environments. Where specified in this Contract, Contractor shall perform chemical-based disinfecting using appropriate disinfectants and required dwell times. Dry wiping or surface-only cleaning is unacceptable in high-touch, high-risk, clinical, laboratory, restroom, kitchen, gyms, shower, dressing rooms, and public areas. Services shall be performed in a manner that reflects actual facility usage, environmental conditions, surrounding population impacts, and operational realities, including increased waste generation, exterior debris accumulation, and the need for emergency or unscheduled cleaning services.
Contractor shall at all times provide adequate supervision of Contractor’s personnel to ensure complete, timely, and satisfactory performance of all services in full compliance with the terms, conditions, and requirements of this Contract.
The Contractor shall, perform the following services:
Trash: Contractor shall remove all trash daily from the entire facility and from any additional areas designated by the County’s Project Manager. Contractor shall empty all exterior trash receptacles located at entrances, exits, and other designated exterior areas. All trash shall be disposed of in the trash dumpsters and /or other trash containers provided for disposal of trash.
Contractor shall use containers on wheels, or other approved methods, to transport trash from one part of the building to another.  Under no circumstances shall trash containers, carts, or equipment dragged, slid, or otherwise moved in a manner that may damage floor surfaces.
Contractor shall not recycle trash or store recyclable materials, including bottles and cans,  on County premises unless expressly authorized in writing by the County.
Contractor shall install plastic trash liners for each trash receptacles, including those located in rooms, offices, common areas, hallways, break rooms, lunch areas, security offices, and all other areas where trash receptacles are present. Liners shall be appropriately sized for each receptacle and shall be replaced daily or more frequently as required by the County’s Project Manager.
Contractor shall install sanitary napkin receptacle liners in all women’s restrooms within the facility. Liners shall be replaced daily and more frequently as required by the County’s Project Manager to ensure receptacles remain clean, sanitary, and functional.
Building Entrance and Atriums shall be maintained on a daily basis in a clean condition and free of dust, debris, cobwebs bird droppings, and other visible contaminants.
Maintain Floors: All hard surface floors shall receive routine and periodic floor maintenance. Floor maintenance includes, but is not limited to, sweeping, dust mopping, damp mopping, wet mopping, dry buffing, spray buffing, stripping, scrubbing, sealing, and waxing as required to achieve the results specified in this Contract. After floor maintenance is performed, floor surfaces shall have a uniform coating of nonskid floor finish, a consistent and glossy appearance where applicable, and shall be free of scuff marks, heel marks, stains, residue, buildup, and discoloration.
All floor maintenance solutions, residue, and splatter shall be completely removed from baseboards, furniture, fixtures, trash receptacles, and adjacent surfaces.  Chairs, trash receptacles,  and other easily moveable items shall be moved as necessary to properly maintain floor surfaces and shall be returned to their original positions upon completion of floor maintenance.
All items moved  to facilitate floor maintenance shall be returned to their original and proper positions upon completion of all floor maintenance operations.  Wax or floor finish shall be applied only to floor surfaces that have been properly cleaned and prepared.
Sweep/Dust Mop Floors:  All accessible floor areas shall be swept or dust mopped daily.  After sweeping and/or dust mopping, the entire floor surface, including areas around stationary objects, corners, edges, and abutments, shall be free of litter, cobwebs, dust and debris. Chairs, trash receptacles, plants and any other easily movable object shall be moved or tilted as necessary to allow sweeping or dust mopping underneath.
Mop Floors: All accessible hard surface floor areas shall be damp and/or wet mopped daily, as appropriate to the floor type. Chairs, trash receptacles, and other easily moveable items shall be moved as necessary to allow mopping underneath.  After mopping, floors shall have a uniform appearance and be free of streaks, swirl marks, detergent residue, soil, stains, film, debris, and standing water.  There shall be no splash marks, mop streaks, or residue on furniture, walls, baseboards, or adjacent surfaces, and no mop strands shall remain in the area. Wood floors shall not be damp or wet mopped.
Sweep and Damp Mop Floors in Difficult to Reach Areas:  Contractor shall thoroughly sweep and damp mop floors in areas not fully addressed by routine daily cleaning. This includes, but is not limited to, wall edges, corners, areas around furniture and cabinets, and underneath desks and all moveable office furniture.
Dry/Spray Buff Floors:  All applicable floor surfaces shall be dry or spray buffed as required to eliminate heal marks, scuffs, and light surface oils suing appropriate buffing pad, floor machine, and approved spray buff solution. This process shall leave a uniform, thin coat of non-skid wax/floor finish. Sweeping and wet mopping shall be completed prior to performing dry or spray buffing.
Gyms/Fitness Rooms/Exercise Areas:  County facilities may include gyms, fitness rooms, exercise areas, or similar spaces. Contractor shall provide full janitorial cleaning and disinfecting services for such areas. Gyms and fitness areas services shall include, but not limited to, the following:
Cleaning and disinfecting of all exercise equipment, including but not limited to:
Cardio equipment (treadmills, stationary bikes, ellipticals, rowers, etc.)
Weight machines and selectorized equipment
Free weights, kettlebells, dumbbells, barbells, and racks
Benches, mats, platforms, resistance bands, and related accessories
Disinfecting all high-touch surfaces, including but not limited to:
Hand grips, handles, seats, pads, adjustment knobs, rails, touchscreen, and control panels
Mirrors, doors, door handles, light switches, lockers (exterior), and wall-mounted fixtures
Cleaning and disinfecting of gym floors, baseboards, walls (as needed), vents, and surrounding surfaces.
Cleaning and disinfecting of gym and exercise mats, including floor mats, stretching mats, and protective mats.
Removal and disposal of all trash within the gym and fitness areas, including trash located in receptacles, on floors, around equipment, and in common use areas. Trash liners shall be replaced as required, and receptacles shall be cleaned as needed.
Chemical-based disinfecting shall be performed using EPA-registered disinfectants with required manufacturer dwell time. Dry wiping or surface-only cleaning is unacceptable.
Services shall be performed at a frequency sufficient to maintain a sanitary condition, at a minimum daily, and more frequently when Day Porter services are assigned or when usage levels require.
Partial cleaning, exclusion of equipment, or limitation of services to floors or mats only is not acceptable. 
Dressing Rooms: Dressing rooms are located in some departments throughout the County of Orange. Where such facilities exist, Contract shall provide complete cleaning and disinfecting of all dressing room areas. Cleaning shall include all surfaces, including but not limited to floors, walls, benches, lockers, fixtures, mirrors, mats, doors and all adjacent surfaces. All dressing room cleaning shall be performed in a thorough and comprehensive manner. Partial, spot, or surface-only is not acceptable. Dressing rooms shall be left clean, disinfected, free of residue, odors, and visible soil, and maintained in a sanitary condition consistent with professional janitorial standards
Shower Cleaning:  Shower facilities are located in some departments throughout the County of Orange. Where such facilities exist, Contractor shall provide complete cleaning and disinfecting of all shower areas. Cleaning shall include all surfaces including but not limited to, walls, floors, drains, fixtures, curtains, doors, grout, and adjacent surfaces. drains, fixtures, grout, doors, curtains, mats, and adjacent surfaces. All shower cleaning shall be performed in a thorough and comprehensive manner. Partial, spot, or surface-only cleaning is unacceptable. Shower areas shall be left clean, disinfected, free of residue, buildup, mildew, odors, and visible soil, and maintained in a sanitary condition consistent with professional janitorial standards. 
Strip, Scrub, Seal, and Wax Floors: All hard floors shall be stripped, scrubbed, sealed, and waxed as necessary to maintain a clean uniform, and glossy appearance.  Contractor shall perform all tasks associated with stripping, scrubbing, sealing, and waxing floor surfaces, including proper surface preparation and finish application.  Non-skid wax shall be used. Upon completion,  floor surfaces shall have a uniform, glossy appearance and shall be free of scuff marks, heel marks, wax buildup, stains, and other discoloration. Contractor shall strip floors of existing wax, dirt, debris, buildup, and residue prior to scrubbing, sealing, and waxing operations. Where required by the County or appropriate to the floor type or operational environment, Contractor shall apply a minimum of two (2) coats of anti-static or non-skid floor finish as directed by the County Project Manager or designee. 
Remove Trash: All trash containers both interior and exterior, shall be emptied at the frequencies specified in this Contract and returned to their original locations.  Boxes, cans, papers, and other materials placed near a trash receptacle and clearly marked “TRASH” shall be removed.  Soiled,  torn or damaged plastic trash receptacle liners shall be replaced as needed.  All debris, liquids, or residue remaining inside trash receptacles shall be completely removed, and receptacles shall be cleaned as necessary. Trash shall be placed in plastic bags and secured with bag ties prior to disposal.  Contractor shall collect and remove any trash that falls onto facility floors,  grounds, or surrounding areas during the trash removal activities.  All trash shall be deposited in the nearest exterior trash collection point. Trash receptacles that are dirty or contaminated shall be washed inside and out and left clean and odor free.
Empty and Clean Public Ash Trays and Urns.  Contractor shall empty all public ashtrays and urns at the required frequencies.  Ashtrays shall be wiped,  washed with an appropriate cleaning solution and dried as necessary to remove odor, stains, residue, and debris.  All public urns shall be cleaned by removing debris, and the sand shall be replenished or replaced as needed to maintain a clean and sanitary condition.
Perform Low Dusting: All dust, lint, litter, cobwebs and dry soil shall be removed from horizontal surfaces, including but not limited to chairs, file cabinets, conference tables, furniture, equipment,  ledges, windowsills, handrails, baseboards, air conditioning vents, up to a height of seven (7) feet above the finished floor . 
Perform High Dusting:  Contractor shall provide high dusting to remove all dust, lint, litter, and dry soil from surfaces located higher than seven (7) feet above the finished floor . High dusting shall include, where installed, air conditioning grills, vents, ledges, and other elevated surfaces within the service areas.
Clean and Polish Interior Glass, Mirrors, and Glass/Mirrored Surfaces.  Contractor shall clean and polish all interior glass and mirrored surfaces, including glass partitions, glass walls, doors with glass components, mirrors, and adjacent trim where lower edge of the glass surface is below seven (7) feet above the finished floor.  Glass surfaces extending higher than seven (7) feet shall not be included under this subsection.  After cleaning, all glass and mirrored surfaces shall be free of film, dirt, smudges, water spots, and other foreign matter.  Both sides of applicable glass partitions, walls, and doors shall be cleaned.
Clean and Polish Other Interior Glass.  Contractor shall clean and polish all other interior glass surfaces not addressed above, including but not limited to trophy and display cases, directory boards, and similar glass features.  After cleaning, all such glass surfaces shall be free of film, dirt, smudges, streaks, water spots, and other foreign matter.
Clean Drinking Fountains: Contractor shall clean and sanitize all porcelain and polished metal surfaces of drinking fountains, including orifices, drains, and all exterior surfaces.  After cleaning, drinking fountain shall be free from streaks, stains, spots, smudges, scale buildup, and other visible soil or residue.
Clean Elevators: Contractor shall clean all public and freight elevators.  Cleaning shall include removal of all marks, writing, graffiti, dirt, smudges, scuffs, food residue, trash, and other foreign matter from the elevator floors, walls, doors, controls and ceiling.
Clean Stairways: All stairway floor surfaces shall be cleaned and all lint, dust, dirt, cobwebs, and debris removed. Grease, grime, and residue shall be removed from metal or rubber stair guards, handrails and baseboards. Contractor shall also remove all marks, dirt, smudges, scuffs, and other foreign matter from adjoining stairwell walls to maintain a clean, uniform appearance.
Vacuum Carpets, Rugs and Mats: All carpeted floors, including hallway carpets, area rugs, throw rugs and mats, shall be vacuumed daily using a HEPA-filter vacuum and shall be free of all visible litter and soil. Any spots and stains shall be removed as soon as identified using  carpet manufacturer approved cleaning methods. Chairs, trash receptacles, and other easily moveable items shall be moved as necessary to allow vacuuming  underneath carpets and rugs. All items moved for carpet and rug maintenance shall be returned to their original or proper positions upon completion of cleaning.  Any observed tears, burns,  raveling, or other damage to carpets or rugs shall be promptly reported  to the County’s Project Manager or designee.
Vacuum Carpets and Rugs and Difficult to Reach Areas: Contractor shall thoroughly vacuum carpets and rugs using  a HEPA filter vacuum in areas not fully addressed by routine daily vacuuming. This includes,  but is not limited to, wall edges, corners, areas around furniture and cabinets, and underneath desks and all moveable office furniture.
Spot Clean Carpets: Contractor shall promptly spot clean or shampoo carpeted areas with stains covering two (2) square feet or less upon identification to prevent setting or spreading of stains.
Carpet Cleaning:  Contractor shall clean all carpeted surfaces using the deep extraction method and carpet manufacturer recommended cleaning solution. All carpets shall be left clean and free of dirt, residue, and embedded soil. The bonnet buffing method of cleaning carpet is expressly prohibited and shall not be accepted. Carpet cleaning shall be performed at the frequencies specified in this Scope of Work, including the periodic cleaning requirements identified herein. Failure to perform scheduled carpet cleaning in accordance with Contract requirements shall constitute a material breach. Contractor shall maintain accurate logs and schedules documenting all carpet cleaning activities and shall provide such documentation to the County upon request.
Vacuum and Clean Walk-Off Mat:  Contractor shall vacuum and clean all interior and exterior walk-off mats using a HEPA filter vacuum or other appropriate cleaning method based on mat type. After cleaning, mats shall be free of all visible lint, litter, soil and debris.  Carpet style and entrance mats shall be vacuumed as necessary to remove soil and restore carpet pile resiliency. Rubber, vinyl, or polyester entrance mats shall be swept, vacuumed, or washed as appropriate and thoroughly dried to remove soil, grit, and moisture.  Soil and moisture beneath entrance mats shall be removed,  and mats shall be returned to their original and proper locations after cleaning. 
General Spot Cleaning:  Contractor shall perform spot cleaning on a continual basis to maintain a clean and sanitary environment. Spot cleaning includes, but is not limited to, the removal of smudges, fingerprints, marks, streaks, spills, and residue from washable surfaces, including walls, partitions, vents, grillwork, doors, door guards, door handles, push bars, kick plates and fixtures.  A germicidal detergent shall be used in restrooms, locker rooms, showers, break areas, and drinking fountains. After spot cleaning, all treated surfaces shall have a clean, uniform appearance and shall be free of streaks, spots, residue, and other evidence of  soil or contamination.
Kitchens:  Facility kitchens shall be thoroughly cleaned and disinfected. Cleaning shall include, but not be limited to, walls (including removal of grease buildup), floors, countertops, cabinets, sinks, and all appliances. Appliances shall include refrigerators (exterior and interior where accessible), microwaves, ovens, stoves, fryers (if applicable), and all related surfaces. Interior cleaning of refrigerators shall include removal of debris, wiping of shelves and compartments, and odor control; Contractor shall coordinate with County staff prior to disposal of any contents. Partial cleaning, dry wiping, or surface-only cleaning shall not be permitted. All kitchen areas shall be left in a clean, sanitary, and odor free condition.
Dust Blinds, Windowsills and Draperies:  All blinds, windowsills and draperies shall be dusted and cleaned as required to remove dust, lint, cobwebs, and debris and shall be left free of visible accumulation.
Clean Upholstered Furniture: Contractor shall vacuum, and spot clean all upholstered furniture as required so that, after cleaning, all dust, lint, dirt, debris, stains, gum and other foreign substances are removed. Spot cleaning shall be performed using cleaning products specifically designed, and manufacturer approved for use on upholstered furniture.
Toilets, Toilet Seats, and Urinals: Toilets, toilet seats, and  urinals shall be thoroughly cleaned, disinfected, and sanitized and shall  be free of dust, bacteria, soil, organic matter, cleaner residue scale, streaks, film and water spots. Cleaning shall be performed without causing damage to fixture or finishes. Upon completion, all fixtures shall appear visibly clean, uniformly disinfected, and polished dry.
Enhanced Disinfecting Services:  Chemical-based disinfecting shall be performed in all high-touch, high-traffic, and high-risk areas. Contractor shall disinfect work areas in building with non-bleach and non-aerosol disinfectant products that are on the EPA’s Registered Antimicrobial Products for use against Novel Coronavirus SARS-CoV-2, the Cause of COVID-19 list. Disinfect all public areas, including lobbies, interview rooms, conference rooms, and orientation rooms using non-bleach and non-aerosol disinfecting products:

Work surfaces

Dry dusting, dry wiping, or surface only cleaning without the use of an appropriate disinfectant is not acceptable in any areas where disinfecting is specified.
Hand Sanitizer and Soap Dispensers: Contractor shall fill, refill and replace batteries as necessary for all soap and antibacterial dispensers. Contractor shall ensure that all wall-mounted hand sanitizer dispensers are refilled, properly maintained, and kept in operable conditions at all times.
Exterior Waste:  Contractor shall perform routine and emergency waste collection outside County buildings, including the entire surrounding property. Services shall include, but not limited to, walkways, landscaped areas, courtyards, loading areas, parking lots, perimeter zones, and building exteriors. All exterior areas shall be maintained free of trash, debris, loose waste, and litter generated by normal use, environmental conditions, or emergency events.
Exterior waste collection shall also include the safe removal, containment, and disposal of human waste, bodily fluid, soiled materials, needles, sharps, and other biohazardous or unsanitary materials encountered in exterior areas, in accordance with applicable health, safety, and biohazard handling requirements. When such materials are present, Contractor shall implement appropriate safety measures, use required PPE, disinfect affected areas as necessary, and promptly notify the County Project Manager or designee. Failure to properly address exterior waste, including biohazardous or unsanitary conditions, shall constitute non-performance.
Glass and Windows:  Contractor shall provide complete cleaning and maintenance of all glass and window surfaces as defined herein, including but not limited to interior and exterior windows, glass partitions, glass walls, glass lobby areas, door glass, mirrors, trophy and display cases, directory boards, and all other interior and exterior glass surfaces. Services shall include cleaning and polishing of all glass so that, after cleaning, surfaces are free of film, dirt, smudges, streaks, water spots, residue, and other foreign matter. Interior and exterior window frames, casings, sills, and adjacent trim shall also be cleaned and left free of buildup and residue. High and difficult to reach glass surfaces shall be cleaned using appropriate equipment, access methods, and safety practices. Spot cleaning shall be performed as necessary to remove fingerprints, smudges, and visible marks between scheduled cleanings. Glass and window cleaning shall be performed at the frequencies specified in this Scope of Work and as necessary to maintain a clean, professional appearance. Any exclusions must be explicitly approved in writing by the County. Absent such written exclusion, all glass and window surfaces are included. Partial cleaning, dry wiping, or surface only cleaning that results in streaks, residue, or unclean frames or sills constitute non-performance.

Locations - Various County Buildings
Restrooms
Daily:
Clean and refill soap, paper towels, toilet tissue, sanitary napkins, sanitary disposal bags, and toilet seat cover dispensers. Contractor shall ensure restrooms are fully stocked at all times so that supplies do not run out between service periods. Deodorizing blocks shall be used in all urinals. Continuous air freshener dispensers shall be installed where missing and shall be refilled and serviced as needed. Contractor shall maintain sufficient on-site inventory of all restroom consumables, including soap, paper goods, hand sanitizer (if applicable), liners, and all required special towel rolls, to ensure uninterrupted availability.
Clean and polish all mirrors and faucets so they are free of streaks, spots, residue, and water marks.
Thoroughly damp clean and disinfect all surfaces of wash bowls, toilet bowls, urinals, sanitary napkin dispensers, showers, shower mats, soap dispensers, plumbing fixtures, partitions, dispensers, doors, walls, seating (if applicable), floors and all other restroom surfaces using an approved germicidal detergent. Shower cleaning shall include all surfaces, including walls, floors, fixtures, grout, drains, curtains, doors, and adjacent surfaces. Partial, dry, or surface only cleaning is not acceptable. After cleaning, all surfaces shall be free of deposits, dirt, streaks, residue, and odors. Contractor shall use approved germicidal, and acid based cleaners as necessary to remove mineral deposits and stains.
Thoroughly damp clean and disinfect all surfaces of partitions, stalls, stall doors, entry doors, door handles, kick plates, ventilation grates, metal guards, and wall areas adjacent to wall-mounted soap dispenser, urinals and toilets. All graffiti shall be removed. Surfaces shall be disinfected using approved germicidal and acid based cleaners to remove water deposits and stains.
De-scale showers, toilet bowls and urinals.  After de-scaling, all surfaces shall be free of streaks, stains, scale, scum, urine deposits, rust stains and rings. Shower curtains shall be sprayed with an approved mildew disinfectant to prevent mildew build.
Sweep and wet mop floors using approved germicidal cleaner, including corners, coves, and difficult to reach areas.  After cleaning, floors and grout shall be free from litter, dirt, dust, scum, mildew, residue, and foreign debris. Floors shall have a uniform appearance without streaks, swirl marks, detergent residue, stains, film, or standing water.  Easily moveable items shall be tilted or moved as necessary to clean underneath.
Remove all trash. Empty and clean wastepaper containers and wipe them down as needed using an approved all-purpose cleaner. Empty and replace waxed liners in sanitary napkin disposal receptacles.
Add water and approved disinfectant to all floor drains to maintain trap seals and control odors.
Unstop common toilet stoppages using a plunger. Issues beyond basic stoppages shall be reported immediately to the County’s Project Manager or designee.
Weekly:
Clean and wet wipe with an approved disinfectant all restroom walls, wall areas around plumbing fixtures, toilet compartment partitions, soap dispensers, partition doors, door hardware, and related surfaces. All graffiti shall be removed.
Clean all exposed plumbing and remove hard water deposits, scale, and buildup from all chrome and metal fixtures so that surfaces are free of residue and discoloration.
Clean and disinfect all grab bars and pull bars to remove soil, residue, and germs, leaving surfaces visibly clean and free of streaks.
Dust and clean the tops of partitions, windowsills, vents, and other horizontal surfaces to remove dust, lint, and cobwebs.
Clean toilets and urinals using an approved acid based cleaner to remove lime deposits and prevent alkaline buildup in traps. Wire-formed bowl brushes are prohibited due to damage to porcelain surfaces; pumice stones are acceptable. Toilet rings, scale, stains, and buildup are not acceptable and shall be fully removed.
Monthly:
Wipe down and disinfect all restroom walls using an approved disinfect. Machine scrub and disinfect restroom floors using an approved hospital grade cleaner. Ceramic floors shall be sealed with a minimum of two (2) coats of sealer, as applicable, to maintain sanitary and slip resistant conditions.
Clean restroom vents, including removal of vent plate and brushing and vacuuming around and into duct, when requested by the County or where access permits.
Dust and clean venetian blinds, where applicable, to remove dust, lint, and buildup.
Clean door jambs, frames, and surrounding areas, removing fingerprints, smudges, residue, and surface grime.
Various County Buildings:
Certain County facilities may be located in remote or difficult to access areas. Contractor shall be responsible for accessing and servicing all assigned locations, including locations accessible only by dirt, gravel, or unpaved roads.
Some sites may require extended travel times and may involve travel through mountainous terrain or remote areas. Road conditions at these locations may include dirt and graded gravel surfaces. Work will generally not be requested during inclement weather conditions; however, Contractor shall ensure personnel and vehicles are capable of safely accessing these locations when services are required. Use of four-wheel drive (4WD) vehicles is strongly recommended for applicable sites. 
Contractor acknowledges that all costs associated with accessing remove or difficult to access locations, including travel time, transportation, fuel, mobilization, and related operational expenses, shall be included in Contractor's pricing and shall not constitute grounds for additional compensation.

Custodial Closets:
The Contractor shall keep all tools, equipment, and supplies used in the performance of this Contract stored exclusively in designated janitorial or custodial  storage closets and not in any other part of the building.  Custodian closets shall be maintained in a clean, neat, and orderly condition at all times and shall be subject to regular inspection by the County. Disinfectants, cleaning chemicals, and any biohazard response supplies shall be stored in accordance with OSHA requirements, manufacturer instructions, and applicable safety regulations.
Flammable liquids are prohibited from being stored on County premises. Rags and other flammable solids shall be stored in State Fire Marshal approved containers. All containers shall be clearly and properly labeled as to contents. Any toxic material that must be stored shall be appropriately labeled with the product name and applicable hazard and antidote information.  All buckets, wringers, mop sinks, tools,  and equipment shall be kept clean and free of objectionable odors. Floors, walls,  sinks, whether porcelain or stainless steel, shall be kept clean and polished at all times. Bottles, cans, and unrelated materials shall not be stored in custodial closets. 
Day Porter:
Some County departments will require a Day Porter to be assigned to the facility. The Day Porter shall be an employee of the Contractor and shall be stationed on-site for the purpose of providing immediate attention during normal working hours to Contract related services. Duties shall include, but not be limited to, removal of hazards such as spills or broken glass; response to plumbing leaks or roof leaks; refilling supplies, enhanced disinfecting, restroom and kitchen servicing; exterior waste collection; and general facility upkeep. The Day Porter shall provide immediate response to health and safety hazards as they arise.
The Day Porter shall work in accordance with the schedule established by the requesting  department. Schedules may vary by location and operational needs.
Contractor shall provide full Day Porter services during all hours designated for performance of this work and shall provide qualified suitable personnel whenever the regular Day Porter is unavailable. All services performed by the Day Porter shall be in addition to, and not a substitute for, regular nighttime custodial operations. Substitute personnel shall possess the same qualifications, training, and responsibilities as the regular Day Porter.
Supervision:
The Day Porter shall report directly to and be supervised by the County’s Project Manager or designee. The Contractor shall inspect and review the Day Porter’s work at least weekly to ensure compliance with all Contract requirements and service standards.
The Day porter shall sign in and sign out with the designated Project Manager or designee at the beginning and end of each shift. Sign-in and sign-out records shall be maintained and made available to the County upon request.
The Project Manager may prepare a list of regular duties and a corresponding daily schedule based on anticipated work requirements. If such a list is not provided, the Contractor shall be responsible for establishing and following a daily work schedule that meets all Contract requirements. The schedule shall include designated times for the Day Porter to report back to the Project Manager to or designee to receive additional or special assignments that may arise during the workday.
Required Clothing and Identification:
The Day porter shall wear a clean, professional uniform furnished by the Contractor at all times while performing services under this Contract. The uniform shall include, at a minimum, closed toe shoes, long pants, and a polo style shirt. The Day Porter shall also wear a clearly visible, easy to read name badge identifying the individual as a Contractor employee.
To ensure immediate communication and responsiveness, Contractor shall furnish and maintain a dedicated cell phone exclusively assigned to the Day Porter. The cell phone shall have active and continuous service with a licensed carrier, be powered on, fully functional, and monitored at all times during assigned duties. Contractor shall ensure the Day Porter responds to communications from the County’s Project Manager or designee within no more than five (5) minutes, except during scheduled breaks approved by the County. Contractor shall be solely responsible for maintaining uninterrupted service, including timely payment of all carrier charges, monitoring account status, and promptly resolving any service interruption. Any loss of service due to non-payment, suspension, lapse in coverage, equipment failure, or failure to monitor service status shall constitute non-performance, regardless of whether the Contractor or Day Porter was aware of the issue at the time. Failure to maintain an active, operational cell phone or to meet response time requirements may result in corrective action, removal of personnel, or other remedies available under the Contract.
The Day Porter shall be knowledgeable in general custodial practices, including the proper and safe application of cleaning chemicals and the correct use of all cleaning machines, tools, and equipment provided by the Contractor. Day Porters shall be trained in bloodborne pathogens, tuberculosis awareness, biohazardous waste handling, sharps and needle exposure response, and other applicable health and safety protocols.
The Day Porter shall be able to speak, read, and write effectively and fluently in English to ensure clear communication with County staff and accurate performance of assigned duties.
The Day Porter shall possess general maintenance skills and shall be capable of working productively, independently, and with minimal supervision.
The Day Porter shall immediately respond to all requests from the County’s Project Manager or designee. For immediate health and safety hazards, the Day Porter shall take prompt corrective action, with or without prior direction, as necessary to mitigate risk and protect County staff, the public, and facilities.
Daily:
Inspect and services all restrooms and kitchen areas on fewer than three (3) times per day to ensure floors, counters, walls, and fixtures remain clean and free from debris; trash receptacles are emptied, and all dispensers are fully stocked. When mopping restroom floors during the day, wet floor signage shall be placed at restroom entrances in accordance with safety requirements.
Inspect and clean all public hallways, corridors, entrances and exits no fewer than two (2) times per day to remove accumulations of dirt, debris, and spills. Clean all public ashtrays and sand urns.
Clean interior and exterior glass doors in the main reception area to remove fingerprints, smudges, streaks and residue.
Maintain exterior building entrances in a clean condition, free of dust, debris, cobwebs, and bird droppings.
Notify Project Manager or designee of any repair needs that exceed minor maintenance or require specialized skills or tools. When appropriate, take immediate action to prevent further damage or mitigate hazards until repair personnel arrive, including shutting off water, power, or access, as necessary and authorized.
Report all building or equipment deficiencies to the County’s Project Manager or designee, providing a clear description of the issue, its location, and any relevant details to facilitate prompt and cost effective repair. Post warning signs, barricades, or other controls as necessary to restrict access and inform staff, clients, and the public of hazards. 
Lobby Day Porter Services:
The Contractor shall, at a minimum, perform the following services:
Disinfect and clean lobby and all other public areas within County buildings using  non-bleach, non-aerosol disinfectant products listed on the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency’s (EPA) Registered Antimicrobial Products approved for use against Novel Coronavirus SARS-CoV-2 (the virus that causes COVID- 19), or any successor list as applicable. Chemical-based disinfecting shall be performed in accordance with manufacturer required dwell times. Dry wiping, misting, or surface-only cleaning without disinfectant is unacceptable and shall constitute non-performance.
Contractor shall thoroughly disinfect and clean all public spaces no later than one (1) hour prior to the building opening to the public, including, but not limited to:
All public counters and transaction surfaces
Door handles, doorknobs, lobby doors, all doors in public areas, and ADA push buttons
Chairs and seating surfaces
Tables
Electronic equipment and frequently touched devices, including telephones, copiers, pamphlet holders, hand sanitizer dispensers, computer screens, keyboards, mice.
Interview room tables, work surfaces, and chairs
Public Restrooms, including doors and door handles, counters, faucets, sinks, partition doors  and locks, toilet flash handles, and toilet seats
Drinking fountains and bottle filling stations
Light switches
Stair rails and handrails, where applicable
Elevators, where applicable, including buttons, handrails, and interior touch surfaces
Contractor shall repeat the cleaning and disinfecting services specified above routinely throughout the day, multiple times per day, and between public use as feasible. At  a minimum, all identified high-touch public areas shall be cleaned and disinfected at least once every one (1) hour. Chemical based disinfecting shall include required dwell time. Failure to maintain the minimum hourly disinfecting frequency constitutes non-performance.
After the lobby is closed to the public, the Contractor shall perform a full detail cleaning and disinfecting of all areas specified in section B. This shall include comprehensive  disinfecting, cleaning, and restocking of all public restrooms. All public areas shall be left fully disinfected, stocked, and ready for the next day of operation.
Contractor shall provide a minimum of one (1) dedicated staff member to perform Lobby Day Porter services, Monday through Friday, from 8:00 am to 5:00 pm, and on Saturdays on an “as needed” basis, as determined by the County. Lobby Day Porter services shall not be provided on County observed holidays unless otherwise directed in writing by the County. The County Facility Manager or designee may adjust service hours based on operational needs. Failure to staff required lobby services during designated hours shall constitutes non-performance.

Best Management Practices (BMP)
Contractor shall conduct all operations under this Contract in a manner that prevents pollutants from entering municipal storm drain systems, including but not limited to, curbs, gutters, catch basins, and other components of the street and drainage infrastructure (collectively, the "Stormwater Drainage System"). The Contractor shall also ensure that operations do not directly or indirectly impact "Receiving Waters" which  include, but are not limited to, rivers, creeks, streams, estuaries, lakes, harbors, bays, and oceans. Contractor shall routinely inspect and clean debris from mop sink floor drains and shall ensure that no pollutants are discharged to the Stormwater Drainage System.
The Santa Ana and San Diego Regional Water Quality Control Boards have issued National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) permits ("Stormwater Permits") to the County of Orange, the Orange County Flood Control District, and cities within Orange County, as co-permittees (collectively, the "County Parties"). These permits regulate the discharge of urban runoff from areas within the County of Orange, including facilities and premises serviced under this Contract.  The County Parties have adopted water quality ordinances that prohibit activities and conditions that may result in polluted runoff being discharged into the Stormwater Drainage System. The Contractor shall comply with all applicable Stormwater Permits and water quality ordinances at all times.
To ensure compliance with Stormwater Permits and water quality ordinances, the County Parties have developed a Drainage Area Management Plan (DAMP) which includes a Local Implementation Plan (LIP) for each jurisdiction. The LIP contains required Best Management Practices (BMPs) applicable to activities performed under this Contract. As used herein, a BMP is defined as a technique, measure, or structural control implemented to manage stormwater runoff quantity and improve runoff quality in a cost effective manner. These BMPs are set forth in  Model Maintenance Procedures and BMP Fact Sheets contained within the DAMP/LIP (collectively, "BMP Fact Sheets"). Contractor shall comply with all applicable BMP Fact Sheets and shall   Ensure that waste, debris, biohazardous materials, cleaning chemicals, wash water, and other pollutants are properly contained, handled, and disposed of in accordance with BMP requirements. Non-stormwater discharges to the Stormwater Drainage System are prohibited. Failure to comply with BMP requirements shall constitute non-performance under this Contract.
BMP Fact Sheets shall include but shall not be limited to the following which may be viewed for municipal activities and downloaded at 
https://ocerws.ocpublicworks.com/service-areas/oc-environmental-resources/oc-watersheds/unincorporated-countywide-compliance/best-2
:
 
BMP Fact Sheets may be modified during the term of the Contract. The  County’s Project Manager or designee shall provide Contractor with any updated or revised BMP Fact Sheets applicable to the services performed under this Contract.  
Contractor shall, throughout the term of this Contract, comply with the BMP Fact Sheets as they exist at the time of Contract commencement and as they may be modified during the Contract term. The Contractor shall also comply with all applicable requirements of the Stormwater Permits, as in effect  at the commencement of the Contract and as permits may be amended or modified. The Contractor shall maintain current copies of all applicable BMP Fact Sheets at each job site and shall ensure that all BMPs applicable to activities authorized under this Contract are performed strictly in accordance with the requirements set forth in the applicable BMP Fact Sheets.
Contractor may propose alternative BMPs that meet or exceed the pollution prevention and control performance of the applicable BMP Fact Sheets. Any proposed alternative BMPs shall be submitted in writing to the County’s Project Manager or designee for review and shall not be implemented unless and until written approval is received from the County.
County’s Project Manager or designee may, at any time, visit job sites and/or review Contractor’s records to verify compliance with this section. The Contractor may be required, upon request, to implement and maintain a self-evaluation or monitoring program to demonstrate ongoing compliance with BMP requirements and Stormwater Permit obligations.
Failure to comply with BMP Fact Sheets requirements or Stormwater Permit obligations shall constitute a material breach of this Contract.

## OCLSB Subcontractor Participation - Construction
For the purpose of satisfying subcontracting participation requirements and/or being eligible for the preference, only 
1st-tier OCLSB subcontractors 
will be recognized as participants in the Contract according to the following criteria:
For credit to be allowed toward a respective participation level, all listed OCLSB firms shall have been certified by the Bid due date.
The Subcontractor shall perform a commercially useful function for credit to be allowed toward subcontractor participation levels. The Subcontractor shall be required by you to be responsible for the execution of a distinct element of the Work and shall carry out its responsibility by actually performing and supervising its own workforce.
If the Bidder is seeking the recognition of materials, supplies, or both towards achieving any mandatory subcontracting participation level, the Bidder shall indicate on the Subcontractor List with the Bid the following: 
(BUYER - Upload list)
If the materials or supplies are obtained from a OCLSB manufacturer, the Bidder will receive 100% of the cost of the materials or supplies toward OCLSB participation. For the purposes of counting OCLSB participation, a manufacturer is a firm that operates or maintains a factory or establishment that produces, on the premises, the materials, supplies, articles, or equipment required under the Contract and of the general character described by the specifications.
If the materials or supplies are obtained from a OCLSB supplier, the Bidder will receive 60% of the cost of the materials or supplies toward OCLSB participation. For the purposes of counting OCLSB participation a Supplier is a firm that owns, operates, or maintains a store, warehouse, or other establishment in which the materials, supplies, articles or equipment of the general character described by the specifications and required under the Contract are bought, kept in stock, and regularly sold or leased to the public in the usual course of business. To be a supplier, the firm shall be an established, regular business that engages, as its principal business and under its own name, in the purchase and sale or lease of the products in question. A person may be a supplier in such bulk items as petroleum products, steel, cement, gravel, stone, or asphalt without owning, operating, or maintaining a place of business if the person both owns and operates distribution equipment for the products. Any supplementing of the suppliers’ own distribution equipment shall be by a long-term lease agreement and shall not be on an ad hoc or contract-by-contract basis.
If the materials or supplies are obtained from an OCLSB, which is neither a manufacturer nor a supplier, the entire amount of fees or commissions charged for assistance in the procurement of the materials and supplies, fees or transportation charges for the delivery of materials or supplies required on a job site will be counted toward OCLSB participation, provided the fees are reasonable and not excessive as compared with fees customarily allowed for similar services. No portion of the cost of the materials and supplies themselves will be counted toward OCLSB participation.
If the Bidder is seeking the recognition of OCLSB Trucking towards achieving any mandatory subcontracting participation level, the Bidder shall indicate it on the List of Subcontractors with the Bid. The following factors will be evaluated in determining the credit to be allowed toward the respective participation level:
The OCLSB shall be responsible for the management and supervision of the entire trucking operation for which it is getting credit on a particular Contract and there shall not be a contrived arrangement for the purpose of counting OCLSB participation.
The OCLSB shall itself own and operate at least 1 fully licensed, insured, and operational truck used on the Contract.
The OCLSB receives credit for the total value of the transportation services it provides on the Contract using trucks it owns, insures, and operates using drivers it employs.
The OCLSB may lease trucks from another OCLSB firm including an owner-operator who is certified as an OCLSB. The OCLSB who leases trucks from another OCLSB receives credit for the total value of the transportation services the lessee OCLSB provides on the contract.
The OCLSB may also lease trucks from a non-OCLSB firm, including an owner-operator. The OCLSB who leases trucks from a non-OCLSB is entitled to credit for the total value of transportation services provided by non-OCLSB lessees not to exceed the value of transportation services provided by OCLSB owned trucks on the contract. Additional participation by non-OCLSB lessees receive credit only for the fee or commission it receives as a result of the lease arrangement.
A lease shall indicate that the OCLSB has exclusive use of and control over the truck. This does not preclude the leased truck from working for others during the term of the lease with the consent of the OCLSB so long as the lease gives the OCLSB absolute priority for use of the leased truck.

## Prequalification Protest Hearing Procedure
Where the prospective bidder has made a timely and complete submittal of prequalification documents that result in a determination that the contractor is not qualified, the prospective bidder can contest the department’s decision via administrative hearing.
To petition for a hearing, the prospective bidder must deliver written notice of its desire to contest the department’s decision to County of Orange within seven (7) calendar days of the date of County’s notice of determination. Failure to file a timely notice shall result in the prospective bidder’s waiver of any and all rights to challenge the prequalification determination, whether by administrative process, judicial process, or any other legal process or proceeding.
The prospective bidder may request the County to advise it in writing of the basis for the prequalification determination and any supporting evidence that was received from others or adduced as a result of an investigation by the County.
A Hearing Panel shall be established and consist of three panelists from various County of Orange infrastructure departments, with a maximum of one (1) panelist from the procuring department.
The Hearing Panel shall render its decision based on all potentially relevant evidence submitted by either the County or the prospective bidder, including but not limited to, the administrative record and testimonial evidence. The prospective bidder may submit on the record, or provide other evidence, including testimony given under oath, to rebut the department’s determination of non-qualification. Such a hearing is conducted in an informal manner, and all relevant evidence is admissible. The department rendering the initial determination may rebut any evidence proffered by the prospective bidder in writing or through its own testimony. Finally, the Hearing Panel may ask questions of either the prospective bidder or department before making its decision.
If the prospective bidder requests to provide testimony, the hearing shall be conducted within five (5) business days after the County’s receipt on notice of appeal and no later than 20 business days prior to the last date of receipt of bids on the project. Within three (3) business days after the conclusion of the hearing, the Hearing Panel will render its decision in writing.
The decision of the Hearing Panel shall be the County’s final administrative decision and any judicial review thereof shall be instituted no later than the time period specified in Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

PROTEST PROCEDURES
All protests shall be typed under the protestor’s letterhead and submitted in accordance with the provisions stated herein. All protests shall include at a minimum the following information: 
The name, address, and telephone number of the protestor;
The signature of the protestor or the protestor’s representative;
The solicitation or contract number;
A detailed statement of the legal and/or factual grounds for the protest; and, 
The form of relief requested. 
Protest of Solicitation Specifications: 
All protests related to solicitation specifications must be submitted to the 
Deputy Procurement Agent (DPA), 
Sheriff Procurement
 at 
ocsdpurchasing@ocsheriff.gov
, no later than five (5) business days prior to the Closing Date of the solicitation. Protests received after the five (5) business-day deadline will not be considered by the County.
In the event the protest of specifications is denied, and the protestor wishes to continue in the solicitation process, the protestor must still submit a bid/response prior to the close of the solicitation in accordance with the solicitation submittal procedures provided in this solicitation. 
Protest of Award of Contract: 
Protests related to the award of a contract must be submitted to the 
Deputy Procurement Agent, 
Sheriff Procurement
 at 
ocsdpurchasing@ocsheriff.gov
, no later than five (5) business days after the Notice of Solicitation Results is provided by the DPA.
Protests relating to a proposed contract award received after the five (5) business day deadline 
will not
 be considered by the County. 
If the five (5) business day period expires without the receipt of a protest, the department may move forward with the contract award or if necessary, file the item for approval by the Board of Supervisors.
Protest Process 
In the event of a timely protest, the County shall not proceed with the solicitation or award of the contract until the DPA issues a decision on the protest. 
Upon receipt of a timely protest, the DPA will, within ten (10) business days of receipt of the protest, issue a decision in writing which shall state the reasons for the actions taken. 
The County may, after providing written justification, make the determination that an immediate award of the contract is necessary to protect the substantial interests of the County. The award of a contract shall in no way compromise the protester’s right to the protest procedures outlined herein. 
If the protestor disagrees with the decision of the DPA, the protestor may submit a written appeal to the County Procurement Officer requesting an appeal to the Procurement Appeals Board, in accordance with the process stated below. 
 
 
APPEALS PROCESS
If the protestor wishes to appeal the protest decision of the Deputy Procurement Agent, the protestor must submit, within three (3) business days from receipt of the Deputy Procurement Agent’s decision, a written appeal to the Office of the County Procurement Officer. 
Written appeals must be sent by mail to the address below with a courtesy copy by email;
 
County of Orange/County Executive Office
County Procurement Office
400 W. Civic Center Drive, 5th Floor
Santa Ana, CA 92701
Attn: County Procurement Officer
CPOAppeals@ceo.oc.gov
 
Within fifteen (15) business days, the County Procurement Officer will review all materials in connection with the appeal, assess the merits of the protest and provide a written determination that shall contain his or her decision on whether the appeal shall be forwarded to the Procurement Appeals Board.
The decision of the County Procurement Officer on whether to allow the appeal to go forward will be final and there shall be no right to any administrative appeals of this decision.

Invitation for Bid – IFB

Request for Proposal - RFP
No Cost - Any Request for Proposals that does not include cost as a scoring criteria shall instead apply the five percent (5%) or eight percent (8%) preference percentage pursuant to the eligibility requirements above to a scoring criteria in the RFP that makes up no more than twenty percent (20%) of the total RFP.
With Cost - An additional five percent (5%) shall be applied to the total cost of each certified OCLSB or DVBE to obtain their final score. 
If the final score of any OCLSB or DVBE matches the final score of a respondent who is not an OCLSB or DVBE, preference shall be given to the certified OCLSB or DVBE. If two or more OCLSBs and/or DVBEs have the same final score, the County shall determine the contract award based on the County’s best interests. If the materials or supplies are obtained from a OCLSB manufacturer, the Bidder will receive 100% of the cost of the materials or supplies toward OCLSB participation. For the purposes of counting OCLSB participation, a manufacturer is a firm that operates or maintains a factory or establishment that produces, on the premises, the materials, supplies, articles, or equipment required under the Contract and of the general character described by the specifications.
If the materials or supplies are obtained from a OCLSB supplier, the Bidder will receive 60% of the cost of the materials or supplies toward OCLSB participation. For the purposes of counting OCLSB participation a Supplier is a firm that owns, operates, or maintains a store, warehouse, or other establishment in which the materials, supplies, articles or equipment of the general character described by the specifications and required under the Contract are bought, kept in stock, and regularly sold or leased to the public in the usual course of business. To be a supplier, the firm shall be an established, regular business that engages, as its principal business and under its own name, in the purchase and sale or lease of the products in question. A person may be a supplier in such bulk items as petroleum products, steel, cement, gravel, stone, or asphalt without owning, operating, or maintaining a place of business if the person both owns and operates distribution equipment for the products. Any supplementing of the suppliers’ own distribution equipment shall be by a long-term lease agreement and shall not be on an ad hoc or contract-by-contract basis.
If the materials or supplies are obtained from an OCLSB, which is neither a manufacturer nor a supplier, the entire amount of fees or commissions charged for assistance in the procurement of the materials and supplies, fees or transportation charges for the delivery of materials or supplies required on a job site will be counted toward OCLSB participation, provided the fees are reasonable and not excessive as compared with fees customarily allowed for similar services. No portion of the cost of the materials and supplies themselves will be counted toward OCLSB participation.
If the Bidder is seeking the recognition of OCLSB Trucking towards achieving any mandatory subcontracting participation level, the Bidder shall indicate it on the List of Subcontractors with the Bid. The following factors will be evaluated in determining the credit to be allowed toward the respective participation level:
The OCLSB shall be responsible for the management and supervision of the entire trucking operation for which it is getting credit on a particular Contract and there shall not be a contrived arrangement for the purpose of counting OCLSB participation.
The OCLSB shall itself own and operate at least 1 fully licensed, insured, and operational truck used on the Contract.
The OCLSB receives credit for the total value of the transportation services it provides on the Contract using trucks it owns, insures, and operates using drivers it employs.
The OCLSB may lease trucks from another OCLSB firm including an owner-operator who is certified as an OCLSB. The OCLSB who leases trucks from another OCLSB receives credit for the total value of the transportation services the lessee OCLSB provides on the contract.
The OCLSB may also lease trucks from a non-OCLSB firm, including an owner-operator. The OCLSB who leases trucks from a non-OCLSB is entitled to credit for the total value of transportation services provided by non-OCLSB lessees not to exceed the value of transportation services provided by OCLSB owned trucks on the contract. Additional participation by non-OCLSB lessees receive credit only for the fee or commission it receives as a result of the lease arrangement.
A lease shall indicate that the OCLSB has exclusive use of and control over the truck. This does not preclude the leased truck from working for others during the term of the lease with the consent of the OCLSB so long as the lease gives the OCLSB absolute priority for use of the leased truck.

## Protest Procedures
PROTEST PROCEDURES
All protests shall be typed under the protestor’s letterhead and submitted in accordance with the provisions stated herein. All protests shall include at a minimum the following information: 
The name, address, and telephone number of the protestor;
The signature of the protestor or the protestor’s representative;
The solicitation or contract number;
A detailed statement of the legal and/or factual grounds for the protest; and, 
The form of relief requested. 
Protest of Solicitation Specifications: 
All protests related to solicitation specifications must be submitted to the 
Deputy Procurement Agent (DPA), 
Mary Barreto
 at 
mbarreto@ocsheriff.gov
, no later than five (5) business days prior to the Closing Date of the solicitation. Protests received after the five (5) business-day deadline will not be considered by the County.
In the event the protest of specifications is denied, and the protestor wishes to continue in the solicitation process, the protestor must still submit a bid/response prior to the close of the solicitation in accordance with the solicitation submittal procedures provided in this solicitation. 
Protest of Solicitation Results: 
Protests related to solicitation results must be submitted to the 
Deputy Procurement Agent, 
Mary Barreto
 at 
mbarreto@ocsheriff.gov
, no later than five (5) business days after the Notice of Solicitation Results is provided by the DPA.
Protests relating to solicitation results received after the five (5) business day deadline 
will not
 be considered by the County. 
If the five (5) business day period expires without the receipt of a protest, the department may move forward with contract negotiation and award or if necessary, file the item for approval by the Board of Supervisors.
Protest Process 
In the event of a timely protest, the County shall not proceed with the solicitation or award of the contract until the DPA issues a decision on the protest. 
Upon receipt of a timely protest, the DPA will, within ten (10) business days of receipt of the protest, issue a decision in writing which shall state the reasons for the actions taken. 
The County may, after providing written justification, make the determination that an immediate award of the contract is necessary to protect the substantial interests of the County. The award of a contract shall in no way compromise the protester’s right to the protest procedures outlined herein. 
If the protestor disagrees with the decision of the DPA, the protestor may submit a written appeal to the County Procurement Officer requesting an appeal to the Procurement Appeals Board, in accordance with the process stated below. 
 
 
APPEALS PROCESS
If the protestor wishes to appeal the protest decision of the Deputy Procurement Agent, the protestor must submit, within three (3) business days from receipt of the Deputy Procurement Agent’s decision, a written appeal to the Office of the County Procurement Officer. 
Written appeals must be sent by mail to the address below with a courtesy copy by email;
 
County of Orange/County Executive Office
County Procurement Office
400 W. Civic Center Drive, 5th Floor
Santa Ana, CA 92701
Attn: County Procurement Officer
CPOAppeals@ceo.oc.gov
 
Within fifteen (15) business days, the County Procurement Officer will review all materials in connection with the appeal, assess the merits of the protest and provide a written determination that shall contain his or her decision on whether the appeal shall be forwarded to the Procurement Appeals Board.
The decision of the County Procurement Officer on whether to allow the appeal to go forward will be final and there shall be no right to any administrative appeals of this decision.

OCLSB or DVBE Preference provides for the following
:
Invitation for Bid – IFB
A five percent (5%) deduction in the original bid price shall be applied to all confirmed OCLSB or DVBE bidders for evaluation purposes. If the lowest bidder is a certified OCLSB or DVBE bidder, the contract will be awarded at the certified OCLSB or DVBE’s original bid price. The maximum allowable preference deduction is $100,000.
Request for Proposal - RFP
No Cost - Any Request for Proposals that does not include cost as a scoring criteria shall instead apply the five percent (5%) or eight percent (8%) preference percentage pursuant to the eligibility requirements above to a scoring criteria in the RFP that makes up no more than twenty percent (20%) of the total RFP.
With Cost - An additional five percent (5%) shall be applied to the total cost of each certified OCLSB or DVBE to obtain their final score. 
If the final score of any OCLSB or DVBE matches the final score of a respondent who is not an OCLSB or DVBE, preference shall be given to the certified OCLSB or DVBE. If two or more OCLSBs and/or DVBEs have the same final score, the County shall determine the contract award based on the County’s best interests. Notwithstanding these preference procedures, the Orange County Board of Supervisors reserves the right to award contracts in any other permissible manner in consideration of the County’s best interests.

Subcontractors

If the materials or supplies are obtained from a OCLSB manufacturer, the Bidder will receive 100% of the cost of the materials or supplies toward OCLSB participation. For the purposes of counting OCLSB participation, a manufacturer is a firm that operates or maintains a factory or establishment that produces, on the premises, the materials, supplies, articles, or equipment required under the Contract and of the general character described by the specifications.
If the materials or supplies are obtained from a OCLSB supplier, the Bidder will receive 60% of the cost of the materials or supplies toward OCLSB participation. For the purposes of counting OCLSB participation a Supplier is a firm that owns, operates, or maintains a store, warehouse, or other establishment in which the materials, supplies, articles or equipment of the general character described by the specifications and required under the Contract are bought, kept in stock, and regularly sold or leased to the public in the usual course of business. To be a supplier, the firm shall be an established, regular business that engages, as its principal business and under its own name, in the purchase and sale or lease of the products in question. A person may be a supplier in such bulk items as petroleum products, steel, cement, gravel, stone, or asphalt without owning, operating, or maintaining a place of business if the person both owns and operates distribution equipment for the products. Any supplementing of the suppliers’ own distribution equipment shall be by a long-term lease agreement and shall not be on an ad hoc or contract-by-contract basis.
If the materials or supplies are obtained from an OCLSB, which is neither a manufacturer nor a supplier, the entire amount of fees or commissions charged for assistance in the procurement of the materials and supplies, fees or transportation charges for the delivery of materials or supplies required on a job site will be counted toward OCLSB participation, provided the fees are reasonable and not excessive as compared with fees customarily allowed for similar services. No portion of the cost of the materials and supplies themselves will be counted toward OCLSB participation.
If the Bidder is seeking the recognition of OCLSB Trucking towards achieving any mandatory subcontracting participation level, the Bidder shall indicate it on the List of Subcontractors with the Bid. The following factors will be evaluated in determining the credit to be allowed toward the respective participation level:
The OCLSB shall be responsible for the management and supervision of the entire trucking operation for which it is getting credit on a particular Contract and there shall not be a contrived arrangement for the purpose of counting OCLSB participation.
The OCLSB shall itself own and operate at least 1 fully licensed, insured, and operational truck used on the Contract.
The OCLSB receives credit for the total value of the transportation services it provides on the Contract using trucks it owns, insures, and operates using drivers it employs.
The OCLSB may lease trucks from another OCLSB firm including an owner-operator who is certified as an OCLSB. The OCLSB who leases trucks from another OCLSB receives credit for the total value of the transportation services the lessee OCLSB provides on the contract.
The OCLSB may also lease trucks from a non-OCLSB firm, including an owner-operator. The OCLSB who leases trucks from a non-OCLSB is entitled to credit for the total value of transportation services provided by non-OCLSB lessees not to exceed the value of transportation services provided by OCLSB owned trucks on the contract. Additional participation by non-OCLSB lessees receive credit only for the fee or commission it receives as a result of the lease arrangement.
A lease shall indicate that the OCLSB has exclusive use of and control over the truck. This does not preclude the leased truck from working for others during the term of the lease with the consent of the OCLSB so long as the lease gives the OCLSB absolute priority for use of the leased truck.

All Contractor personnel shall be identified by a distinctive Contractor logo, emblem or patch attached prominently on an outer garment. In addition to Contractors’ ID all Contractors’ personnel shall be required to present 
an acceptable valid government or state identification card (i.e., driver’s license, passport, or identification card) prior to entering any secured facility.

Contractor personnel shall not smoke (including use of any form of electronic device), use profanity or inappropriate language while on County property or performing duties or tasks under the contract.

Contractor personnel shall have 
NO CONTACT
, either direct or indirect physical, verbal and/or written, with internees in any facility and immediately report any attempt by internee to contact Contractor.

## CMARE General Responsibilities:
The CMARE becomes a collaborative member of the County’s project team members.  The CMARE will support the County’s project team members during the Pre-Construction Services and Construction Services and will potentially hold the construction Contract for the project. Following completion of the project constructability review, but prior to construction, the CMARE will assume the risk of delivering the project through a Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) Contract. The CMARE will be responsible for construction means and methods, budgeting, cost estimating, scheduling, constructability review and valued engineering studies and may be required to solicit Proposals from subcontractors to perform the work (see Model Contract).
The classification of the CMARE’s license required in the performance of this Contract is 
TBD
.
Pre-Construction services by the CMARE may include but not limited to following:
Participation in design review process during the creation of the Design Development Phase documents. Provide design to comply with the project engineer’s prescribed specifications and select subcontractor that is experienced and qualified for performing the work.
Detailed cost estimating and knowledge of marketplace conditions; 
Project planning and scheduling; 
Provide for construction phasing and scheduling that will minimize interruption to operations;
Alternate systems evaluation and constructability studies; 
Advise County on ways to gain efficiencies in project delivery;
Advise and initiate procurement of long-lead items; 
Assist in the permitting processes;
Select subcontractors/suppliers for this project (see “Scope of Work” in Section II.) 
Protect the County’s sensitivity to quality, safety, and environmental factors;
Advise County on choosing green building materials; 
Provide CEQA and permitting data such as detailed description of contract work, hours of operation and identification of staging areas (if applicable); and
Constructability review of project design plans. 
Construction services by the CMARE may include: 
Coordinate with various County of Orange departments, other agencies, utility companies, etc.;
Comply with project Mitigated Negative Declaration (MND) CEQA document’s requirements of mitigation and monitoring of the site construction. 
Arrange for procurement of materials and equipment;
Schedule and manage site operations; 
Comply with County building & grading permits requirements for regular and special inspections;
Provide quality controls; 
Provide commissioning phase services;
Bond and insure the construction;
Address all federal, state and local permitting and reporting requirements; and
Maintain a safe work site for all project participants.

## OCLSB: 
Effective January 1, 2020, County of Orange Board of Supervisors adopted the OCLSB Preference policy.  Implementation of the OCLSB Preference policy supports local businesses, the local economy and the development of the County’s tax base.
To be certified as a Local Small Business by the County of Orange, a business shall meet (1) and (2) below:
Local Business Requirements:
Maintains their principal center of operations (i.e. headquarters) within Orange County, and:
Has:
A business address located in the County of Orange that is not a post office box, or
A valid business license or certificate of occupancy issued by the County of Orange or by an Orange County city, or other documentation acceptable to the County of Orange. 
Small Business Requirements:
Must be certified as a Small Business by the 
State of California Department of General Services (DGS)
; and,
Above requirements must be valid at the time of proposal submittal through the time of award of the contract. The terms and conditions of the contract shall additionally require the contractor to remain in compliance with the Local Business requirements (pursuant to subsection (a) above) through the term of the contract, including any extensions or renewals, and shall provide that contractor’s failure to comply may be construed by County as a material breach of the contract.

## Scope of Work 
The County of Orange is comprised of 22 Departments and over 18,000 employees located throughout the County.  The County’s core businesses are public safety, public works, construction management, public health, environmental protection, regional planning, public assistance, social services, and aviation.
Introduction
This Contract is a Regional Cooperative Agreement (RCA) for General Maintenance Services available to County departments and participating agencies. All work authorized under this Contract shall be limited to maintenance work that does not constitute a public project as defined in Public Contract Code Section 22002(c). Allowable use under this Contract is based on the nature and scope of the work, not solely on the trade discipline or contractor license held.
Allowable maintenance work includes routine, recurring, and usual work necessary to preserve, protect, keep, operate, or maintain an existing County facility, system, or component for its intended purpose. This Contract may include incidental removal, repair, replacement, or reinstallation of existing components when necessary to complete allowable maintenance work. This Contract shall not be used for new construction, reconstruction, renovation, expansion, capital improvement work, new installation of a facility or system, standalone demolition, or work that materially changes the function, capacity, layout, or intended use of an existing facility or system.
Contractor shall provide all staffing, labor, equipment, materials, and incidentals required to provide General Maintenance Services on an as-needed basis as requested by County departments.
 
Definitions
All trade classifications identified herein are limited solely to maintenance, repair, troubleshooting, servicing, and replacement-in-kind of existing County facilities, systems, and equipment. No trade classification may be used to perform new construction, facility expansion, structural alterations, renovations, tenant improvements, or capital improvement projects.
Contractor Performance Evaluation: 
Evaluation to be completed by County department after each project completed by Contractor.  Evaluations will be sent to the assigned buyer at County and be utilized to monitor performance issues.
Maintenance Work: 
Routine, recurring, and usual work necessary to preserve, protect, keep, operate, or maintain an existing County facility, system, or component for its intended purpose, as further defined by Public Contract Code §22002(c). For purposes of this Contract, Maintenance Work includes the trade classifications and services described in this Section 3.1.B. Maintenance Work does not include new construction, renovation, expansion, capital improvement, standalone demolition, or any work that materially changes the function, capacity, layout, or intended use of an existing facility or system.
Work Authorization: 
All maintenance work must be reviewed and approved by the County Project Manager or designee prior to commencement. Work Authorizations shall include Contractor information, description of maintenance work to be performed, materials, equipment rentals, applicable trade classifications, and required approval.
ASB – Asbestos Certification – 
No contractor shall engage in asbestos-related work, as defined in Section 6501.8 of the Labor Code, which involved 100 square feet or more of surface area of asbestos containing materials, unless the qualifier for the license passes an asbestos certification examination.  Additional updated certification examination shall be made by Contractors’ State License Board, in consultation with the Division of Occupational Safety and Health in the Department of Industrial Relations and the State Department of Health Services. No asbestos certification examination shall be required for contractors involved with the installation, maintenance, and repair of asbestos cement pipe or sheets, vinyl asbestos floor materials, or asbestos bituminous or resinous materials.
