## Protest Procedures
PROTEST PROCEDURES
All protests shall be typed under the protestor’s letterhead and submitted in accordance with the provisions stated herein. All protests shall include at a minimum the following information: 
The name, address, and telephone number of the protestor;
The signature of the protestor or the protestor’s representative;
The solicitation or contract number;
A detailed statement of the legal and/or factual grounds for the protest; and, 
The form of relief requested. 
Protest of Solicitation Specifications: 
All protests related to solicitation specifications must be submitted to the 
Deputy Procurement Agent (DPA), 
Mary Barreto
 at 
mbarreto@ocsheriff.gov
, no later than five (5) business days prior to the Closing Date of the solicitation. Protests received after the five (5) business-day deadline will not be considered by the County.
In the event the protest of specifications is denied, and the protestor wishes to continue in the solicitation process, the protestor must still submit a bid/response prior to the close of the solicitation in accordance with the solicitation submittal procedures provided in this solicitation. 
Protest of Award of Contract: 
Protests related to the award of a contract must be submitted to the 
Deputy Procurement Agent, 
Mary Barreto
 at 
mbarreto@ocsheriff.gov
, no later than five (5) business days after the Notice of Solicitation Results is provided by the DPA.
Protests relating to a proposed contract award received after the five (5) business day deadline 
will not
 be considered by the County. 
If the five (5) business day period expires without the receipt of a protest, the department may move forward with the contract award or if necessary, file the item for approval by the Board of Supervisors.
Protest Process 
In the event of a timely protest, the County shall not proceed with the solicitation or award of the contract until the DPA issues a decision on the protest. 
Upon receipt of a timely protest, the DPA will, within ten (10) business days of receipt of the protest, issue a decision in writing which shall state the reasons for the actions taken. 
The County may, after providing written justification, make the determination that an immediate award of the contract is necessary to protect the substantial interests of the County. The award of a contract shall in no way compromise the protester’s right to the protest procedures outlined herein. 
If the protestor disagrees with the decision of the DPA, the protestor may submit a written appeal to the County Procurement Officer requesting an appeal to the Procurement Appeals Board, in accordance with the process stated below. 
 
 
APPEALS PROCESS
If the protestor wishes to appeal the protest decision of the Deputy Procurement Agent, the protestor must submit, within three (3) business days from receipt of the Deputy Procurement Agent’s decision, a written appeal to the Office of the County Procurement Officer. 
Written appeals must be sent by mail to the address below with a courtesy copy by email;
 
County of Orange/County Executive Office
County Procurement Office
400 W. Civic Center Drive, 5th Floor
Santa Ana, CA 92701
Attn: County Procurement Officer
CPOAppeals@ceo.oc.gov
 
Within fifteen (15) business days, the County Procurement Officer will review all materials in connection with the appeal, assess the merits of the protest and provide a written determination that shall contain his or her decision on whether the appeal shall be forwarded to the Procurement Appeals Board.
The decision of the County Procurement Officer on whether to allow the appeal to go forward will be final and there shall be no right to any administrative appeals of this decision.

For the purposes of counting OCLSB participation, a manufacturer is a firm that operates or maintains a factory or establishment that produces, on the premises, the materials, supplies, articles, or equipment required under the Contract and of the general character described by the specifications.
If the materials or supplies are obtained from a OCLSB supplier, the Bidder will receive 60% of the cost of the materials or supplies toward OCLSB participation. For the purposes of counting OCLSB participation a Supplier is a firm that owns, operates, or maintains a store, warehouse, or other establishment in which the materials, supplies, articles or equipment of the general character described by the specifications and required under the Contract are bought, kept in stock, and regularly sold or leased to the public in the usual course of business. To be a supplier, the firm shall be an established, regular business that engages, as its principal business and under its own name, in the purchase and sale or lease of the products in question. A person may be a supplier in such bulk items as petroleum products, steel, cement, gravel, stone, or asphalt without owning, operating, or maintaining a place of business if the person both owns and operates distribution equipment for the products. Any supplementing of the suppliers’ own distribution equipment shall be by a long-term lease agreement and shall not be on an ad hoc or contract-by-contract basis.
If the materials or supplies are obtained from an OCLSB, which is neither a manufacturer nor a supplier, the entire amount of fees or commissions charged for assistance in the procurement of the materials and supplies, fees or transportation charges for the delivery of materials or supplies required on a job site will be counted toward OCLSB participation, provided the fees are reasonable and not excessive as compared with fees customarily allowed for similar services. The OCLSB shall be responsible for the management and supervision of the entire trucking operation for which it is getting credit on a particular Contract and there shall not be a contrived arrangement for the purpose of counting OCLSB participation.
The OCLSB shall itself own and operate at least 1 fully licensed, insured, and operational truck used on the Contract.
The OCLSB receives credit for the total value of the transportation services it provides on the Contract using trucks it owns, insures, and operates using drivers it employs.
The OCLSB may lease trucks from another OCLSB firm including an owner-operator who is certified as an OCLSB. The OCLSB who leases trucks from another OCLSB receives credit for the total value of the transportation services the lessee OCLSB provides on the contract.
The OCLSB may also lease trucks from a non-OCLSB firm, including an owner-operator. The OCLSB who leases trucks from a non-OCLSB is entitled to credit for the total value of transportation services provided by non-OCLSB lessees not to exceed the value of transportation services provided by OCLSB owned trucks on the contract. Additional participation by non-OCLSB lessees receive credit only for the fee or commission it receives as a result of the lease arrangement.
A lease shall indicate that the OCLSB has exclusive use of and control over the truck. This does not preclude the leased truck from working for others during the term of the lease with the consent of the OCLSB so long as the lease gives the OCLSB absolute priority for use of the leased truck.

## Protest Procedures
PROTEST PROCEDURES
All protests shall be typed under the protestor’s letterhead and submitted in accordance with the provisions stated herein. All protests shall include at a minimum the following information: 
The name, address, and telephone number of the protestor;
The signature of the protestor or the protestor’s representative;
The solicitation or contract number;
A detailed statement of the legal and/or factual grounds for the protest; and, 
The form of relief requested. 
Protest of Solicitation Specifications: 
All protests related to solicitation specifications must be submitted to the 
Deputy Procurement Agent (DPA), 
Erin Barnes
 at 
erin.barnes@occr.oc.gov
, no later than five (5) business days prior to the Closing Date of the solicitation. Protests received after the five (5) business-day deadline will not be considered by the County.
In the event the protest of specifications is denied, and the protestor wishes to continue in the solicitation process, the protestor must still submit a bid/response prior to the close of the solicitation in accordance with the solicitation submittal procedures provided in this solicitation. 
Protest of Award of Contract: 
Protests related to the award of a contract must be submitted to the 
Deputy Procurement Agent, 
Erin Barnes
 at 
erin.barnes@occr.oc.gov
, no later than five (5) business days after the Notice of Solicitation Results is provided by the DPA.
Protests relating to a proposed contract award received after the five (5) business day deadline 
will not
 be considered by the County. 
If the five (5) business day period expires without the receipt of a protest, the department may move forward with the contract award or if necessary, file the item for approval by the Board of Supervisors.
Protest Process 
In the event of a timely protest, the County shall not proceed with the solicitation or award of the contract until the DPA issues a decision on the protest. 
Upon receipt of a timely protest, the DPA will, within ten (10) business days of receipt of the protest, issue a decision in writing which shall state the reasons for the actions taken. 
The County may, after providing written justification, make the determination that an immediate award of the contract is necessary to protect the substantial interests of the County. The award of a contract shall in no way compromise the protester’s right to the protest procedures outlined herein. 
If the protestor disagrees with the decision of the DPA, the protestor may submit a written appeal to the County Procurement Officer requesting an appeal to the Procurement Appeals Board, in accordance with the process stated below. 
 
 
APPEALS PROCESS
If the protestor wishes to appeal the protest decision of the Deputy Procurement Agent, the protestor must submit, within three (3) business days from receipt of the Deputy Procurement Agent’s decision, a written appeal to the Office of the County Procurement Officer. 
Written appeals must be sent by mail to the address below with a courtesy copy by email;
 
County of Orange/County Executive Office
County Procurement Office
400 W. Civic Center Drive, 5th Floor
Santa Ana, CA 92701
Attn: County Procurement Officer
CPOAppeals@ceo.oc.gov
 
Within fifteen (15) business days, the County Procurement Officer will review all materials in connection with the appeal, assess the merits of the protest and provide a written determination that shall contain his or her decision on whether the appeal shall be forwarded to the Procurement Appeals Board.
The decision of the County Procurement Officer on whether to allow the appeal to go forward will be final and there shall be no right to any administrative appeals of this decision.

## OCLSB Subcontractor Participation - Construction
For the purpose of satisfying subcontracting participation requirements and/or being eligible for the preference, only 
1st-tier OCLSB subcontractors 
will be recognized as participants in the Contract according to the following criteria:
For credit to be allowed toward a respective participation level, all listed OCLSB firms shall have been certified by the Bid due date.
The Subcontractor shall perform a commercially useful function for credit to be allowed toward subcontractor participation levels. The Subcontractor shall be required by you to be responsible for the execution of a distinct element of the Work and shall carry out its responsibility by actually performing and supervising its own workforce.
If the Bidder is seeking the recognition of materials, supplies, or both towards achieving any mandatory subcontracting participation level, the Bidder shall indicate on the Subcontractor List with the Bid the following: 
(BUYER - Upload list)
If the materials or supplies are obtained from a OCLSB manufacturer, the Bidder will receive 100% of the cost of the materials or supplies toward OCLSB participation. For the purposes of counting OCLSB participation, a manufacturer is a firm that operates or maintains a factory or establishment that produces, on the premises, the materials, supplies, articles, or equipment required under the Contract and of the general character described by the specifications.
If the materials or supplies are obtained from a OCLSB supplier, the Bidder will receive 60% of the cost of the materials or supplies toward OCLSB participation. For the purposes of counting OCLSB participation a Supplier is a firm that owns, operates, or maintains a store, warehouse, or other establishment in which the materials, supplies, articles or equipment of the general character described by the specifications and required under the Contract are bought, kept in stock, and regularly sold or leased to the public in the usual course of business. To be a supplier, the firm shall be an established, regular business that engages, as its principal business and under its own name, in the purchase and sale or lease of the products in question. A person may be a supplier in such bulk items as petroleum products, steel, cement, gravel, stone, or asphalt without owning, operating, or maintaining a place of business if the person both owns and operates distribution equipment for the products. Any supplementing of the suppliers’ own distribution equipment shall be by a long-term lease agreement and shall not be on an ad hoc or contract-by-contract basis.
If the materials or supplies are obtained from an OCLSB, which is neither a manufacturer nor a supplier, the entire amount of fees or commissions charged for assistance in the procurement of the materials and supplies, fees or transportation charges for the delivery of materials or supplies required on a job site will be counted toward OCLSB participation, provided the fees are reasonable and not excessive as compared with fees customarily allowed for similar services. No portion of the cost of the materials and supplies themselves will be counted toward OCLSB participation.
If the Bidder is seeking the recognition of OCLSB Trucking towards achieving any mandatory subcontracting participation level, the Bidder shall indicate it on the List of Subcontractors with the Bid. The following factors will be evaluated in determining the credit to be allowed toward the respective participation level:
The OCLSB shall be responsible for the management and supervision of the entire trucking operation for which it is getting credit on a particular Contract and there shall not be a contrived arrangement for the purpose of counting OCLSB participation.
The OCLSB shall itself own and operate at least 1 fully licensed, insured, and operational truck used on the Contract.
The OCLSB receives credit for the total value of the transportation services it provides on the Contract using trucks it owns, insures, and operates using drivers it employs.
The OCLSB may lease trucks from another OCLSB firm including an owner-operator who is certified as an OCLSB. The OCLSB who leases trucks from another OCLSB receives credit for the total value of the transportation services the lessee OCLSB provides on the contract.
The OCLSB may also lease trucks from a non-OCLSB firm, including an owner-operator. The OCLSB who leases trucks from a non-OCLSB is entitled to credit for the total value of transportation services provided by non-OCLSB lessees not to exceed the value of transportation services provided by OCLSB owned trucks on the contract. Additional participation by non-OCLSB lessees receive credit only for the fee or commission it receives as a result of the lease arrangement.
A lease shall indicate that the OCLSB has exclusive use of and control over the truck. This does not preclude the leased truck from working for others during the term of the lease with the consent of the OCLSB so long as the lease gives the OCLSB absolute priority for use of the leased truck.

## Traffic Control
Contractor shall conduct its operations in a manner which will minimize traffic congestion during A.M. and P.M. peak-hour traffic.  This may require beginning work after the A. M. peak-hour traffic and ending work before the 
P. M. peak-hour traffic.
 
Contractor shall maintain access to schools and commercial areas at all times during project operation.
 
Spillage resulting from hauling operations along or across any public traveled way will be removed immediately by Contractor, at his expense.
 
When entering or leaving roadways carrying public traffic, Contractor’s equipment, whether empty or loaded, shall in all cases yield to public traffic.
 
Special emphasis will be placed on the use of construction zone ahead (C18R) signs at the beginning, end and all access and/or intersecting streets with roads under construction.  In addition to construction zone signs, rough road signs (W33) will be used on all roads with a posted or marked bicycle trail.
 
Contractor shall provide and maintain all signs, barricades, pedestals, flashers, delineators and other necessary facilities for the protection of the motoring public within the limits of the construction area and all its approaches, including advanced signing and barricades. Contractor shall also post proper signs to notify public regarding condition of roadway, all in accordance with provisions of the Vehicle Code and "Manual of Traffic Controls", as published by the State of California, Department of Transportation, latest edition.
 
Flashing arrow signs, of the appropriate type per the "Manual of Traffic of Traffic Controls", latest edition, shall be provided for all lane closures on all arterial highways and collector street.
 
Portable delineators, either conical (traffic cone) or tubular shaped plastic devices, with a minimum height of 28 inches will be used for delineation of the travel way.  
 
If the traffic cones or portable delineators are damaged, displaced or unacceptable for any reason by County staff or are not in an upright position from any cause, said cones or portable delineators will immediately be replaced or restored to their original location, in an upright position, by Contractor.
 
Contractor shall maintain 11’ lanes of traffic in each direction at all times.
 
Contractor shall furnish such flagmen as are necessary to give adequate warning to traffic or to the public of any dangerous conditions to be encountered.  Flagmen, while on duty and assigned to give warning to the public that the street is under construction and of any dangerous conditions to be encountered as a result thereof, will perform their duties and will be provided with the necessary equipment in accordance with the current "Instructions to Flaggers", by the State of California, Department of Transportation.  The equipment shall be furnished and kept clean and in good repair by the Contractor, at its expense.
 
Should Contractor appear to be neglectful or negligent in furnishing warning and protective measures as provided, County staff may direct attention to the existence of a hazard and necessary warning and protective measures will be furnished and installed by Contractor, at its expense. Should County staff point out the inadequacy of warning and protective measures, such action on the part of County staff will not relieve Contractor from responsibility for public safety or abrogate its obligation to furnish and pay for these devices.
 
Contractor shall maintain safe working conditions at each work location.
 
At the end of each day, all equipment and other obstructions will be removed from the roadway.
 
Full compensation for conforming to requirements of traffic control will be considered as included in the various items of work involved and no additional compensation will be allowed thereafter.

PROTEST PROCEDURES

 at 
beatriz.castellon@ssa.ocgov.com

In the event the protest of specifications is denied, and the protestor wishes to continue in the solicitation process, the protestor must still submit a bid/response prior to the close of the solicitation in accordance with the solicitation submittal procedures provided in this solicitation. 
Protest of Award of Contract:

Deputy Procurement Agent, 
Beatriz Castellon
 at 
beatriz.castellon@ssa.ocgov.com
, no later than five (5) business days after the Notice of Solicitation Results is provided by the DPA.
Protests relating to a proposed contract award received after the five (5) business day deadline 
will not
 be considered by the County. 
If the five (5) business day period expires without the receipt of a protest, the department may move forward with the contract award or if necessary, file the item for approval by the Board of Supervisors.
Protest Process 
In the event of a timely protest, the County shall not proceed with the solicitation or award of the contract until the DPA issues a decision on the protest. 
Upon receipt of a timely protest, the DPA will, within ten (10) business days of receipt of the protest, issue a decision in writing which shall state the reasons for the actions taken. 
The County may, after providing written justification, make the determination that an immediate award of the contract is necessary to protect the substantial interests of the County. The award of a contract shall in no way compromise the protester’s right to the protest procedures outlined herein. 
If the protestor disagrees with the decision of the DPA, the protestor may submit a written appeal to the County Procurement Officer requesting an appeal to the Procurement Appeals Board, in accordance with the process stated below. 
 
 
APPEALS PROCESS
If the protestor wishes to appeal the protest decision of the Deputy Procurement Agent, the protestor must submit, within three (3) business days from receipt of the Deputy Procurement Agent’s decision, a written appeal to the Office of the County Procurement Officer.

Title VI Solicitation Notice: The (Title of Recipient), in accordance with the provisions of Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 (78 Stat. 252, 42 U.S.C. §§ 2000d to 2000d-4), 28 CFR § 50.3, and 49 CFR Part 21, hereby notifies all bidders that it will affirmatively ensure that any contract entered into pursuant to this advertisement, all contractors will be afforded full opportunity to submit bids in response to this invitation and will not be discriminated against on the grounds of the owner’s race, color, national origin, sex, creed, age, or disability in consideration for an award.

## Protest Procedures
PROTEST PROCEDURES
All protests shall be typed under the protestor’s letterhead and submitted in accordance with the provisions stated herein. All protests shall include at a minimum the following information: 
The name, address, and telephone number of the protestor;
The signature of the protestor or the protestor’s representative;
The solicitation or contract number;
A detailed statement of the legal and/or factual grounds for the protest; and, 
The form of relief requested. 
Protest of Solicitation Specifications: 
All protests related to solicitation specifications must be submitted to the 
Deputy Procurement Agent (DPA), 
Julian Garcia
 at 
jugarcia@ocsheriff.gov
, no later than five (5) business days prior to the Closing Date of the solicitation. Protests received after the five (5) business-day deadline will not be considered by the County.
In the event the protest of specifications is denied, and the protestor wishes to continue in the solicitation process, the protestor must still submit a bid/response prior to the close of the solicitation in accordance with the solicitation submittal procedures provided in this solicitation. 
Protest of Award of Contract: 
Protests related to the award of a contract must be submitted to the 
Deputy Procurement Agent, 
Julian Garcia
 at 
jugarcia@ocsheriff.gov
, no later than five (5) business days after the Notice of Solicitation Results is provided by the DPA.
Protests relating to a proposed contract award received after the five (5) business day deadline 
will not
 be considered by the County. 
If the five (5) business day period expires without the receipt of a protest, the department may move forward with the contract award or if necessary, file the item for approval by the Board of Supervisors.
Protest Process 
In the event of a timely protest, the County shall not proceed with the solicitation or award of the contract until the DPA issues a decision on the protest. 
Upon receipt of a timely protest, the DPA will, within ten (10) business days of receipt of the protest, issue a decision in writing which shall state the reasons for the actions taken. 
The County may, after providing written justification, make the determination that an immediate award of the contract is necessary to protect the substantial interests of the County. The award of a contract shall in no way compromise the protester’s right to the protest procedures outlined herein. 
If the protestor disagrees with the decision of the DPA, the protestor may submit a written appeal to the County Procurement Officer requesting an appeal to the Procurement Appeals Board, in accordance with the process stated below. 
 
 
APPEALS PROCESS
If the protestor wishes to appeal the protest decision of the Deputy Procurement Agent, the protestor must submit, within three (3) business days from receipt of the Deputy Procurement Agent’s decision, a written appeal to the Office of the County Procurement Officer. 
Written appeals must be sent by mail to the address below with a courtesy copy by email;
 
County of Orange/County Executive Office
County Procurement Office
400 W. Civic Center Drive, 5th Floor
Santa Ana, CA 92701
Attn: County Procurement Officer
CPOAppeals@ceo.oc.gov
 
Within fifteen (15) business days, the County Procurement Officer will review all materials in connection with the appeal, assess the merits of the protest and provide a written determination that shall contain his or her decision on whether the appeal shall be forwarded to the Procurement Appeals Board.
The decision of the County Procurement Officer on whether to allow the appeal to go forward will be final and there shall be no right to any administrative appeals of this decision.

## OCLSB Subcontractor Participation - Construction
For the purpose of satisfying subcontracting participation requirements and/or being eligible for the preference, only 
1st-tier OCLSB subcontractors 
will be recognized as participants in the Contract according to the following criteria:
For credit to be allowed toward a respective participation level, all listed OCLSB firms shall have been certified by the Bid due date.
The Subcontractor shall perform a commercially useful function for credit to be allowed toward subcontractor participation levels. The Subcontractor shall be required by you to be responsible for the execution of a distinct element of the Work and shall carry out its responsibility by actually performing and supervising its own workforce.
If the Bidder is seeking the recognition of materials, supplies, or both towards achieving any mandatory subcontracting participation level, the Bidder shall indicate on the Subcontractor List with the Bid the following: 
(BUYER - Upload list)
If the materials or supplies are obtained from a OCLSB manufacturer, the Bidder will receive 100% of the cost of the materials or supplies toward OCLSB participation. For the purposes of counting OCLSB participation, a manufacturer is a firm that operates or maintains a factory or establishment that produces, on the premises, the materials, supplies, articles, or equipment required under the Contract and of the general character described by the specifications.
If the materials or supplies are obtained from a OCLSB supplier, the Bidder will receive 60% of the cost of the materials or supplies toward OCLSB participation. For the purposes of counting OCLSB participation a Supplier is a firm that owns, operates, or maintains a store, warehouse, or other establishment in which the materials, supplies, articles or equipment of the general character described by the specifications and required under the Contract are bought, kept in stock, and regularly sold or leased to the public in the usual course of business. To be a supplier, the firm shall be an established, regular business that engages, as its principal business and under its own name, in the purchase and sale or lease of the products in question. A person may be a supplier in such bulk items as petroleum products, steel, cement, gravel, stone, or asphalt without owning, operating, or maintaining a place of business if the person both owns and operates distribution equipment for the products. Any supplementing of the suppliers’ own distribution equipment shall be by a long-term lease agreement and shall not be on an ad hoc or contract-by-contract basis.
If the materials or supplies are obtained from an OCLSB, which is neither a manufacturer nor a supplier, the entire amount of fees or commissions charged for assistance in the procurement of the materials and supplies, fees or transportation charges for the delivery of materials or supplies required on a job site will be counted toward OCLSB participation, provided the fees are reasonable and not excessive as compared with fees customarily allowed for similar services. No portion of the cost of the materials and supplies themselves will be counted toward OCLSB participation.
If the Bidder is seeking the recognition of OCLSB Trucking towards achieving any mandatory subcontracting participation level, the Bidder shall indicate it on the List of Subcontractors with the Bid. The following factors will be evaluated in determining the credit to be allowed toward the respective participation level:
The OCLSB shall be responsible for the management and supervision of the entire trucking operation for which it is getting credit on a particular Contract and there shall not be a contrived arrangement for the purpose of counting OCLSB participation.
The OCLSB shall itself own and operate at least 1 fully licensed, insured, and operational truck used on the Contract.
The OCLSB receives credit for the total value of the transportation services it provides on the Contract using trucks it owns, insures, and operates using drivers it employs.
The OCLSB may lease trucks from another OCLSB firm including an owner-operator who is certified as an OCLSB. The OCLSB who leases trucks from another OCLSB receives credit for the total value of the transportation services the lessee OCLSB provides on the contract.
The OCLSB may also lease trucks from a non-OCLSB firm, including an owner-operator. The OCLSB who leases trucks from a non-OCLSB is entitled to credit for the total value of transportation services provided by non-OCLSB lessees not to exceed the value of transportation services provided by OCLSB owned trucks on the contract. Additional participation by non-OCLSB lessees receive credit only for the fee or commission it receives as a result of the lease arrangement.
A lease shall indicate that the OCLSB has exclusive use of and control over the truck. This does not preclude the leased truck from working for others during the term of the lease with the consent of the OCLSB so long as the lease gives the OCLSB absolute priority for use of the leased truck.

Bidder must be capable of and plan to employ such means and methods as will allow performance of the work in accordance with the Contract Documents, and will not cause any interruption or interference with any other contractor working at the site.

## Joint Bids

## Unfair Practices and Other Laws

## Delivery of Bids
Bids and modifications to the Bids, if any, must be submitted electronically via the OpenGov at County's online bidding system before the time and date set for the electronic Bid submittal in the Notice of Inviting Bids. Only electronic bids will be accepted, no exceptions. Bidders shall use the Pricing section of the electronic submittal to prepare and submit their Base Bid Amounts in response to this solicitation. Submission of the Bid before the time specified above shall be the sole responsibility of the Bidder. Late Bids will not be accepted under any circumstances.

## Modification After Bid Opening
A modification received from the lowest responsive, responsible Bidder after Bids have been opened that makes the terms of the Bid more favorable to County may be considered at any time and the Contract may be awarded based on such modification.

## Independence of Bid
By submitting a bid, Bidder swears under penalty of perjury that it did not conspire with any other supplier to set prices in violation of anti-trust laws.

## Withdrawal of Bids
A Bidder may withdraw their bid at any point prior to the due date and time of bids and any bid not in a "Submitted" status as of the deadline shall not be considered. The successful Bidder shall submit the bonds in duplicate, all of which shall bear original signatures. The signature of the surety representative must be notarized.

The Contractor is required to provide a completed Safety Data Sheet (SDS) for each hazardous substance provided to the County under the Contractor’s Contract with the County. The provision of the SDSs must be in accordance with the requirements of California Labor Code Sections 6380 through 6399, General Industry Safety Order Section 5194, and Title 8, California Code of Regulations. The SDSs for each substance must be sent to the place of shipment or provision of goods/service.

Contractor will notify County Project Manager of any revisions to the Safety-Activity Checklist and will provide a new Safety-Activity Checklist upon County request. The IIPP shall comply with California Code of Regulations, Title 8, Section 1509 or 3203(whichever applies). Contractor shall submit other safety programs that pertain to the type of job that will be performed on site. County reserves the right to conduct inspections and audits as necessary for the purpose of evaluating any aspect of safety performance under this Contract.

County will not execute the Agreement or issue a Notice to Proceed with the work until Bidder has submitted and County has approved Bidder’s Faithful Performance and Labor and Material Payment Bonds, proof of insurance, and initial job progress schedule. Any claims by Contractor for adjustments in time and/or cost for delays in issuing the Notice to Proceed due to Contractor’s failure to deliver bonds, insurance, and initial job progress schedule acceptable to County will not be considered.

Pursuant to Business & Professions Code Section 7028.15, County will not consider any Bid submitted by a Bidder that does not hold a valid contractor’s license at the time of submitting its Bid. This requirement is not a mere formality, and it will not be waived by the Board of Supervisors. The classification of contractor's license required for the performance of this Contract is specified in the Notice Inviting Bids.

## Contractor's License
Pursuant to Business & Professions Code Section 7028.15, a Bidder that does not hold a valid contractor’s license by the time of scheduled public meeting of Board of Supervisors for consideration of award this project shall not be considered or awarded. This requirement is not a mere formality, and it will not be waived by the Board of Supervisors. The classification of contractor's license required for the performance of this Contract is specified in the Notice Inviting Bids.

## Compliance with Laws and Regulations
Contractor represents and warrants that services to be provided under this Contract shall fully comply, at Contractor’s expense, with all standards, laws, statutes, restrictions, ordinances, requirements, and regulations (collectively “laws”), including, but not limited to those issued by County in its governmental capacity and all other laws applicable to the services at the time services are provided to and accepted by County. Contractor acknowledges that County is relying on Contractor to ensure such compliance, and pursuant to the requirements of the Insurance and Indemnification section, Contractor agrees that it shall defend, indemnify and hold County and County Indemnitees harmless from all liability, damages, costs and expenses arising from or related to a violation of such laws.
Contractor shall remain in compliance and in good standing, maintaining current and active business entity and/or nonprofit registration status, with all applicable federal, state and local registration requirements at the time of execution of the contract through the duration of the term of the Contract, and shall provide annual confirmation of current and active status to County through the term of the Contract.

## Time is of the Essence
Time is of the essence to the contract.  Contractor shall complete the project within the contract time as defined in the “contract price and time” section of the agreement.  Failure to meet this requirement will subject contractor to liability for liquidated damages pursuant to the “liquidated damages” section of the agreement.

Allowances, where included, are listed in the Bid as lump-sum estimates. The tasks, conditions, standards, and schedules for performance of Allowances shall be subject to prior written approval of County.  Payment for Allowances shall be in accordance with the “Allowances” subsection of the “Payments” Section of the General Conditions. Any costs exceeding the maximum amount of any Allowance shall be addressed in accordance with the “Changes” Section of the General Conditions.  Upon completion of the Project, each Allowance estimate will be corrected for unused balances by Change Order to reflect the actual amount authorized for that Allowance.

## PROTEST PROCEDURES
Any Broker-Dealer that participated in the application process may submit a written protest regarding the County’s selection decision. The protests must be submitted on the Broker-Dealer’s letterhead and must include the Broker-Dealer’s contact information, the specific grounds for the protest, the relief requested, and the signature of the Broker-Dealer’s authorized representative.
Protests must be received within five (5) business days following the Broker-Dealer’s receipt of notice of the County’s selection decision. The County reviews the protest and issues a written decision within ten (10) business days of receipt of the protest.
All protests must be submitted electronically to 
ocinvestments@ceo.oc.gov
.

## Introduction Summary
The County of Orange (County) periodically evaluates and establishes a slate of Broker-Dealers authorized to provide investment-related services to the County. Through this application process, the County will evaluate Broker-Dealers (BDs) submitting applications for potential inclusion on the County’s “Approved Broker-Dealers List.” All applicants will be evaluated based upon the County’s requirements and other relevant factors; prior inclusion on the County’s “Approved Broker-Dealers List” does not confer preference or guarantee continued inclusion.

## REQUIRED DOCUMENTATION
The County must 
receive
 the following documents from each existing and prospective Broker-Dealer:
A completed Broker-Dealer Application
A copy of the firm’s most recent audited Annual Report
A copy of the firm’s current Form BD Status Report
A copy of the firm’s most recent SEC Form X-17 A-5 “Focus Report” or most recent Consolidated Reports of Condition and Income for A Bank with Domestic and Foreign Offices – FFIEC 031 (in the case of a bank)
A copy of the firm’s service level agreement or scope of service agreement that outlines trade execution, settlement, coverage/support staff and escalation paths.
MSRB Rule G-37 filing for the past 12 months (if not applicable, please provide reason)
Levine Act Campaign Contribution Disclosure Form (Government Code § 84308), completed and signed by the applicant, including disclosure of any reportable contributions, as applicable.
 
All currently authorized Broker-Dealers that wish to continue conducting business with the County must submit a complete application packet by the specified deadline for consideration. Submission of a 
complete
 application is required to be eligible for inclusion on the County’s new slate of authorized Broker-Dealers, which will be established through this application and evaluation process. Current authorization does not guarantee continued approval or inclusion on the new slate of Broker-Dealers.

## Non‑Binding Disclaimer
Responses and documents submitted as part of this Broker‑Dealer Application are informational only and do not constitute an offer. Submission cannot be accepted by the County to form a binding agreement or commit the County to any business relationship.
The County reserves the right, in its sole discretion and subject to applicable law and County policy, to accept or reject any application, request additional information, waive immaterial deficiencies, modify or discontinue this application process, determine the number of Broker-Dealers to be approved, and add or remove Broker-Dealers from the Approved Broker-Dealers List as the County determines appropriate.

## Change of Ownership/Name and Litigation Status
Applicant agrees that if there is a change or transfer in ownership of applicant’s firm, and the County agrees to continue conducting business with the applicant, the new owners shall be required to assume Broker‑Dealer’s duties and obligations and complete them to the satisfaction of the County.
The County reserves the right to immediately terminate conducting business with the firm in the event the County determines that the assignee is not qualified or is otherwise unacceptable to the County for the provision of services.

## Conflict of Interest
Applicant shall exercise reasonable care and diligence to prevent any actions or conditions that could result in a conflict with County interests. In addition to the applicant, this obligation shall apply to the applicant’s employees, agents, and subcontractors associated with the provision of services provided. The applicant’s efforts shall include, but not be limited to establishing rules and procedures preventing its employees, agents, and subcontractors from providing or offering gifts, entertainment, payments, loans or other considerations which could be deemed to influence or appear to influence County staff or elected officers in the performance of their duties.
The County reserves the right to disqualify any applicant on the basis of any real or apparent conflict of interest that is disclosed in the application submitted or any other information available to the County. This disqualification is at the sole discretion of the County. Any applicant submitting an application herein waives any right to object to the County’s exercise of this right, now or at any future time, before anybody or agency including, but not limited to, the County Board of Supervisors or any court of competent jurisdiction.

## Confidentiality
California Public Records Act
Pursuant to California law, all information contained in an application may be public record, subject to disclosure to any member of the public who requests it through the California Public Records Act (CPRA). If it is necessary to include proprietary/trade secret information in a response, the County recommends that the applicant clearly and prominently marks the information believed to fall within such categories.
Applicant will include a written statement as to the basis for considering the marked pages confidential including the specific harm or prejudice if disclosed and the County will review the material, applicant’s concerns and make an independent determination.

## Modifications of the BDA
The County reserves the sole right to interpret or change any provision of the solicitation at any time prior to the application submission date. Any and all interpretations or changes will be in the form of a written addendum, which will be furnished to all applicants through the County’s online bidding system. All addendums issued will become part of the solicitation and resultant expected services provided. ## Vehicle Window Tinting Services
I.    SCOPE OF WORK
Contractor shall provide all labor, supervision, materials, automotive window film, tools, equipment, transportation, cleanup, disposal, and incidentals necessary to furnish, install, remove, replace, and repair vehicle window film on County-owned or County-operated passenger vehicles, sport utility vehicles, pickup trucks, vans, buses, and other fleet vehicles of various makes, models, and sizes, as requested by OC Public Works/Fleet Services.
II.    SERVICE DESCRIPTION - MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS
A.    Contractor shall:
1.    Be located within five (5) road miles of 1102 E. Fruit Street, Santa Ana, CA 92701, unless otherwise approved in writing by the County.
2.    Perform rush tinting services with a four (4) hour turnaround for standard tinting, removal, or replacement work when requested and scheduled by the County. Contractor shall immediately notify the County Project Manager or designee if the requested turnaround cannot be met.
3.    Comply with Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard No. 205 (49 CFR 571.205), California Vehicle Code section 26708, and all other applicable federal, state, and local requirements. Contractor shall not install film that would place a County vehicle out of legal compliance.
4.    Have a minimum of five (5) years of demonstrated experience performing professional automotive window tinting services.
5.    Furnish professional-grade, current-generation automotive window film from an established manufacturer. Standard County installations shall use non-metalized/electrically non-conductive, signal-safe nano-ceramic, multilayer optical/polyester, or County-approved equivalent high-performance technology. Film shall be color-stable, non-reflective, suitable for fleet use, and shall not interfere with AM/FM radio, GPS, cellular/5G, satellite radio, emergency radio, toll-transponder, telematics, keyless-entry, antennas, or other RF/electronic communication systems. Conventional dyed-only or metalized/electrically conductive film shall not be used unless specifically approved in writing by the County.
6.    Provide legal film options in a range of visible-light-transmission (VLT) levels. All proposed film shall meet the technology, performance, technical-data, and substitution requirements in Section II.B.
7.    Perform film installation in a clean, controlled indoor work area at the Contractor's place of business. Vehicles shall be kept clean and protected from overspray, adhesive, tools, and other materials during service.
8.    Install film backed by a manufacturer's warranty that expressly applies to government/commercial fleet use for not less than five (5) years from the installation date. When the manufacturer offers a lifetime warranty applicable to government/commercial fleet vehicles, that lifetime warranty shall apply. Warranty coverage shall include bubbling, peeling, delamination, cracking, discoloration or fading, adhesive failure, and defects in material or workmanship. Warranty correction shall include removal, replacement materials, and labor at no additional cost to the County.
9.    Before beginning work, inspect the vehicle and document pre-existing damage or conditions relevant to the service. Contractor shall also complete the glazing-compatibility review required by Section II.B.4 and notify the County before proceeding when a condition may affect the installation or removal.
10.    Use manufacturer-approved installation and removal methods and comply with the glazing, liquid-protection, and ADAS/electronics requirements in Sections II.B.4 through II.B.6.
11.    Perform only work authorized by the OC Public Works/Fleet Services Project Manager or designee. Contractor shall verify the County Equipment ID and the applicable work authorization, work order/repair order, when provided, before starting work.
12.    Upon completion, provide warranty/service documentation identifying the service date, County Equipment ID, vehicle VIN (full VIN or at least the last eight characters), film manufacturer, exact product line/series and product code or SKU when available, nominal/published VLT or shade, windows serviced, installer or installing location, roll/lot number when available, total charge, and manufacturer cure/cleaning instructions. For clear front-side solar/UV-control film, include the records required by Section II.B.3.
13.    Correct any installation that fails the acceptance requirements in Section II.B.7 at no additional cost to the County within a reasonable timeframe after notification.
14.    Be responsible for damage caused by the Contractor. Any such damage shall be repaired to the County's satisfaction at the Contractor's expense and at no additional cost to the County.
15.    Store any County vehicle or equipment kept overnight in a secure building or secured storage area. The vehicle/equipment shall be locked whenever it is not being serviced. If Contractor cannot meet this requirement for a particular vehicle, Contractor shall notify the County Project Manager or designee immediately so other arrangements can be made.
16.    Accept work originating from the County locations listed below and from other County locations designated in writing by the County Project Manager or designee.

B.    FILM TECHNOLOGY AND PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS
1.    Minimum Solar and Optical Performance. Except where a different legal VLT requirement applies, each proposed standard film series shall reject/block at least ninety-nine percent (99%) of ultraviolet radiation and have exterior visible-light reflectance (VLR) of ten percent (10%) or less. Published film-on-glass TSER shall meet or exceed the minimum applicable to its published installed VLT range shown below. Performance shall be based on manufacturer data tested in accordance with ANSI/NFRC 200 procedures or another nationally recognized equivalent method, and the manufacturer shall identify the glass type and thickness used for the reported values.

2.    Technical Data and Product Substitution. Contractor shall maintain a current manufacturer technical data sheet for each film supplied under the Contract showing published VLT, exterior VLR, UV rejection/blocking, TSER, IRER over approximately 780-2500 nm when reported, the applicable test method and glass substrate, and warranty terms. Narrow-band IR rejection values may be shown only as supplemental information and shall not substitute for TSER or full-range IRER. No film series or product may be substituted after award without prior written County approval. Any substitute shall meet or exceed the awarded product 's VLT, TSER, UV, reflectance, warranty, signal-compatibility, and other Contract requirements.
3.    Clear Front-Side Solar/UV-Control Film. When specifically ordered for the immediate left and right front-seat side windows, Contractor shall use only clear, colorless, transparent material compliant with California Vehicle Code section 26708(d). The film material shall have a minimum VLT of eighty-eight percent (88%), and the complete glazing with film applied shall retain at least seventy percent (70%) VLT and comply with Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard No. 205, including applicable AS-14 abrasion-resistance requirements. Contractor shall verify each completed window using a calibrated VLT meter, record the measured reading, and provide the County the signed installer certificate identifying the installing company and film manufacturer as required by law. Dark or colored film shall not be supplied under this line item.
4.    Glass and Glazing Compatibility. Before installation, Contractor shall identify whether the affected glazing is tempered, laminated/acoustic, OEM privacy glass, solar-control or coated glass, panoramic/sunroof glass, plastic/polycarbonate glazing, or contains embedded heating elements, antennas, cameras, sensors, or other components. Film shall not be applied to plastic or polycarbonate glazing, panoramic/sunroof glazing, specially coated glazing, or unusual laminated constructions unless the film manufacturer confirms the application is compatible and the County approves the installation in writing. Manufacturer glass-compatibility limitations shall be followed.
5.    Protection From Installation Liquids. Contractor shall use absorbent barriers, towels, protective covers, or equivalent methods to prevent application solution, cleaning liquid, adhesive remover, or moisture from entering door panels, dashboards, headliners, switches, connectors, speakers, electronic modules, cameras, sensors, lighting assemblies, wiring, or other vehicle components.
6.    ADAS, Camera, Sensor, HUD, and Antenna Keep-Clear Areas. Contractor shall not cover, obstruct, cut through, heat-damage, or otherwise affect any OEM-designated keep-clear or functional area for forward-facing cameras, rain/light sensors, infrared or optical sensors, HUD projection, embedded antennas, defrosters, or related systems. No film shall be installed on the windshield except a specifically authorized legal sun strip or other application expressly authorized by law and the County. When the vehicle manufacturer or film manufacturer specifies a restricted area or installation procedure, that requirement shall be followed.
7.    Optical and Workmanship Acceptance. After the normal manufacturer cure period, installed film shall provide a uniform, professional appearance and shall be free of objectionable haze, optical distortion, iridescence, moiré, scratches, creases, fingers, edge lifting, peeling, adhesive defects, excessive contamination, trapped debris clusters, or other conditions that impair driver visibility, camera/sensor function, or HUD performance. Necessary borders and cutouts shall be neat, consistent, and within manufacturer installation tolerances.
8.    Warranty Traceability and Fleet Ownership. Warranty coverage shall remain with the County vehicle and shall not depend on an individual driver or employee. Contractor shall retain the installation records required by Section II.A.12 for the entire warranty period and provide duplicate records to the County upon request.
9.    Dynamic or Powered Smart Film. Electrochromic, photochromic, thermochromic, liquid-crystal/switchable, electrically powered privacy film, or other dynamic glazing technology is not required under the standard pricing schedule and shall not be installed unless specifically approved as Additional Work after County review of legal compliance, electrical integration, failure mode, warranty, and vehicle compatibility.

PROTEST PROCEDURES
All protests shall be typed under the protestor’s letterhead and submitted in accordance with the provisions stated herein. All protests shall include at a minimum the following information: 
The name, address, and telephone number of the protestor;
The signature of the protestor or the protestor’s representative;
The solicitation or contract number;
A detailed statement of the legal and/or factual grounds for the protest; and, 
The form of relief requested. 
Protest of Solicitation Specifications: 
All protests related to solicitation specifications must be submitted to the 
Deputy Procurement Agent (DPA), 
Alan Araujo
 at 
tbd@pw.oc.gov
, no later than five (5) business days prior to the Closing Date of the solicitation. Protests received after the five (5) business-day deadline will not be considered by the County.
In the event the protest of specifications is denied, and the protestor wishes to continue in the solicitation process, the protestor must still submit a bid/response prior to the close of the solicitation in accordance with the solicitation submittal procedures provided in this solicitation. 
Protest of Award of Contract: 
Protests related to the award of a contract must be submitted to the 
Deputy Procurement Agent, 
Alan Araujo
 at 
tbd@pw.oc.gov
, no later than five (5) business days after the Notice of Solicitation Results is provided by the DPA.
Protests relating to a proposed contract award received after the five (5) business day deadline 
will not
 be considered by the County. 
If the five (5) business day period expires without the receipt of a protest, the department may move forward with the contract award or if necessary, file the item for approval by the Board of Supervisors.
Protest Process 
In the event of a timely protest, the County shall not proceed with the solicitation or award of the contract until the DPA issues a decision on the protest. 
Upon receipt of a timely protest, the DPA will, within ten (10) business days of receipt of the protest, issue a decision in writing which shall state the reasons for the actions taken. 
The County may, after providing written justification, make the determination that an immediate award of the contract is necessary to protect the substantial interests of the County. The award of a contract shall in no way compromise the protester’s right to the protest procedures outlined herein. 
If the protestor disagrees with the decision of the DPA, the protestor may submit a written appeal to the County Procurement Officer requesting an appeal to the Procurement Appeals Board, in accordance with the process stated below. 
 
 
APPEALS PROCESS
If the protestor wishes to appeal the protest decision of the Deputy Procurement Agent, the protestor must submit, within three (3) business days from receipt of the Deputy Procurement Agent’s decision, a written appeal to the Office of the County Procurement Officer. 
Written appeals must be sent by mail to the address below with a courtesy copy by email;
 
County of Orange/County Executive Office
County Procurement Office
400 W. Civic Center Drive, 5th Floor
Santa Ana, CA 92701
Attn: County Procurement Officer
CPOAppeals@ceo.oc.gov
 
Within fifteen (15) business days, the County Procurement Officer will review all materials in connection with the appeal, assess the merits of the protest and provide a written determination that shall contain his or her decision on whether the appeal shall be forwarded to the Procurement Appeals Board.
The decision of the County Procurement Officer on whether to allow the appeal to go forward will be final and there shall be no right to any administrative appeals of this decision.

This provision is in addition to that required by Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964.
The above provision binds the Contractor and subcontractors from the bid solicitation period through the completion of the contract.
Nondiscrimination:

Compliance with Regulations:

## OCLSB Subcontractor Participation - Construction
For the purpose of satisfying subcontracting participation requirements and/or being eligible for the preference, only 
1st-tier OCLSB subcontractors 
will be recognized as participants in the Contract according to the following criteria:
For credit to be allowed toward a respective participation level, all listed OCLSB firms shall have been certified by the Bid due date.
The Subcontractor shall perform a commercially useful function for credit to be allowed toward subcontractor participation levels. The Subcontractor shall be required by you to be responsible for the execution of a distinct element of the Work and shall carry out its responsibility by actually performing and supervising its own workforce.
If the Bidder is seeking the recognition of materials, supplies, or both towards achieving any mandatory subcontracting participation level, the Bidder shall indicate on the Subcontractor List with the Bid the following: 
(BUYER - Upload list)
If the materials or supplies are obtained from a OCLSB manufacturer, the Bidder will receive 100% of the cost of the materials or supplies toward OCLSB participation. For the purposes of counting OCLSB participation, a manufacturer is a firm that operates or maintains a factory or establishment that produces, on the premises, the materials, supplies, articles, or equipment required under the Contract and of the general character described by the specifications.
If the materials or supplies are obtained from a OCLSB supplier, the Bidder will receive 60% of the cost of the materials or supplies toward OCLSB participation. For the purposes of counting OCLSB participation a Supplier is a firm that owns, operates, or maintains a store, warehouse, or other establishment in which the materials, supplies, articles or equipment of the general character described by the specifications and required under the Contract are bought, kept in stock, and regularly sold or leased to the public in the usual course of business. To be a supplier, the firm shall be an established, regular business that engages, as its principal business and under its own name, in the purchase and sale or lease of the products in question. A person may be a supplier in such bulk items as petroleum products, steel, cement, gravel, stone, or asphalt without owning, operating, or maintaining a place of business if the person both owns and operates distribution equipment for the products. Any supplementing of the suppliers’ own distribution equipment shall be by a long-term lease agreement and shall not be on an ad hoc or contract-by-contract basis.
If the materials or supplies are obtained from an OCLSB, which is neither a manufacturer nor a supplier, the entire amount of fees or commissions charged for assistance in the procurement of the materials and supplies, fees or transportation charges for the delivery of materials or supplies required on a job site will be counted toward OCLSB participation, provided the fees are reasonable and not excessive as compared with fees customarily allowed for similar services. No portion of the cost of the materials and supplies themselves will be counted toward OCLSB participation.
If the Bidder is seeking the recognition of OCLSB Trucking towards achieving any mandatory subcontracting participation level, the Bidder shall indicate it on the List of Subcontractors with the Bid. The following factors will be evaluated in determining the credit to be allowed toward the respective participation level:
The OCLSB shall be responsible for the management and supervision of the entire trucking operation for which it is getting credit on a particular Contract and there shall not be a contrived arrangement for the purpose of counting OCLSB participation.
The OCLSB shall itself own and operate at least 1 fully licensed, insured, and operational truck used on the Contract.
The OCLSB receives credit for the total value of the transportation services it provides on the Contract using trucks it owns, insures, and operates using drivers it employs.
The OCLSB may lease trucks from another OCLSB firm including an owner-operator who is certified as an OCLSB. The OCLSB who leases trucks from another OCLSB receives credit for the total value of the transportation services the lessee OCLSB provides on the contract.
The OCLSB may also lease trucks from a non-OCLSB firm, including an owner-operator. The OCLSB who leases trucks from a non-OCLSB is entitled to credit for the total value of transportation services provided by non-OCLSB lessees not to exceed the value of transportation services provided by OCLSB owned trucks on the contract. Additional participation by non-OCLSB lessees receive credit only for the fee or commission it receives as a result of the lease arrangement.
A lease shall indicate that the OCLSB has exclusive use of and control over the truck. This does not preclude the leased truck from working for others during the term of the lease with the consent of the OCLSB so long as the lease gives the OCLSB absolute priority for use of the leased truck.

## Protest Procedures
PROTEST PROCEDURES
All protests shall be typed under the protestor’s letterhead and submitted in accordance with the provisions stated herein. All protests shall include at a minimum the following information: 
The name, address, and telephone number of the protestor;
The signature of the protestor or the protestor’s representative;
The solicitation or contract number;
A detailed statement of the legal and/or factual grounds for the protest; and, 
The form of relief requested. 
Protest of Solicitation Specifications: 
All protests related to solicitation specifications must be submitted to the 
Deputy Procurement Agent (DPA), 
Wayne Hsiao
 at 
wayne.hsiao@pw.oc.gov
, no later than five (5) business days prior to the Closing Date of the solicitation. Protests received after the five (5) business-day deadline will not be considered by the County.
In the event the protest of specifications is denied, and the protestor wishes to continue in the solicitation process, the protestor must still submit a bid/response prior to the close of the solicitation in accordance with the solicitation submittal procedures provided in this solicitation. 
Protest of Award of Contract: 
Protests related to the award of a contract must be submitted to the 
Deputy Procurement Agent, 
Wayne Hsiao
 at 
wayne.hsiao@pw.oc.gov
, no later than five (5) business days after the Notice of Solicitation Results is provided by the DPA.
Protests relating to a proposed contract award received after the five (5) business day deadline 
will not
 be considered by the County. 
If the five (5) business day period expires without the receipt of a protest, the department may move forward with the contract award or if necessary, file the item for approval by the Board of Supervisors.
Protest Process 
In the event of a timely protest, the County shall not proceed with the solicitation or award of the contract until the DPA issues a decision on the protest. 
Upon receipt of a timely protest, the DPA will, within ten (10) business days of receipt of the protest, issue a decision in writing which shall state the reasons for the actions taken. 
The County may, after providing written justification, make the determination that an immediate award of the contract is necessary to protect the substantial interests of the County. The award of a contract shall in no way compromise the protester’s right to the protest procedures outlined herein. 
If the protestor disagrees with the decision of the DPA, the protestor may submit a written appeal to the County Procurement Officer requesting an appeal to the Procurement Appeals Board, in accordance with the process stated below. 
 
 
APPEALS PROCESS
If the protestor wishes to appeal the protest decision of the Deputy Procurement Agent, the protestor must submit, within three (3) business days from receipt of the Deputy Procurement Agent’s decision, a written appeal to the Office of the County Procurement Officer. 
Written appeals must be sent by mail to the address below with a courtesy copy by email;
 
County of Orange/County Executive Office
County Procurement Office
400 W. Civic Center Drive, 5th Floor
Santa Ana, CA 92701
Attn: County Procurement Officer
CPOAppeals@ceo.oc.gov
 
Within fifteen (15) business days, the County Procurement Officer will review all materials in connection with the appeal, assess the merits of the protest and provide a written determination that shall contain his or her decision on whether the appeal shall be forwarded to the Procurement Appeals Board.
The decision of the County Procurement Officer on whether to allow the appeal to go forward will be final and there shall be no right to any administrative appeals of this decision.

## Scope of Work
Scope of Work:  
This Contract is for Construction Materials (Sand, Gravel, DG, & Class II aggregate Base) Contractor shall furnish all labor, equipment, tools and incidentals required for Construction Materials (Sand, Gravel, DG & Class II aggregate Base) on an as needed basis as required by County and District. 
Construction materials to be purchased off this contract shall consists of but not be limited to Sand, Gravel, Class 2 Aggregate Road Base, and Decomposed Granite.
All Construction Materials supplied by Contractor shall conform to the requirements of the most current edition of the “Greenbook” Standard Specifications for Public Works Construction (Sections 200 and 400) and OC Public Works Standard Plans (most current issue and supplements).
Materials shall be delivered to various locations throughout County as requested by the Project Manager.
Normal delivery times shall be between 7:00 AM and 3:00 PM Monday through Friday.  Special deliveries may be required at other times due to emergency operations conducted by this department.
Deliveries will usually be accepted in truck and transfers or semi-end dumps, but at times bottom dumps may be requested.
Contractor Requirements
Contractor shall have office staff available to take orders and respond to request via telephone and/or email Monday through Friday during the hours of 7:00am and 4:30pm.
Contractor shall be available and respond to requests on a 24-hour a day, 7-day a week basis.  No award will be made to a vendor not available 24/7.
 
County may need Construction Materials during inclement weather due to emergency operations and deliveries could be in periods of severe rain and to locations where access can be difficult.
 
A primary delivery location is identified in Section “E” below.  However, Contractor shall deliver materials to various County locations as specified at the time of ordering.  Deliveries may be needed at any of the Supervisorial Districts as defined in Attachment “C” Supervisorial District Map.
Contractor must have materials delivered to the job site within 3 hours of the order being placed when items are requested in an emergency situation.
 
Contractor’s response time to County’s requests for materials in an emergency situation is critical.  Contractor is advised that delivery times need to be precise when given to County’s Project Manager at time of ordering.  Failure to provide accurate response times under emergency requests shall be grounds for immediate termination of this Contract.
 
Contractor shall allow County to pick up material at Contractor’s facility using County’s vehicles upon request by County.
 
Contractor is required to provide the names and telephone numbers of personnel available 24-hours at the beginning of this Contract and on September 1
st
 of each succeeding year.
 
Contractor shall provide a standard form delivery ticket stating material type, weight in tons, delivery location, supervisorial district, and the signature of County representative on site.  A copy of the delivery ticket shall be given to the onsite representative.  The number of the delivery ticket shall be referenced on the invoice.
 
Contractor shall provide annual usage report to County upon request.
 
Contractor is required to provide County with the location(s) from which materials for this Contract will be provided.
 
Contractor shall supply all pertinent licenses, permits, and fees necessary to perform the work under this Contract. Contractor’s delivery drivers shall possess a valid California driver's license at all times during the performance of this work and maintain good safety and driving records and use extreme caution during delivery operations.
 
Contractor shall be responsible for any damages sustained to County equipment or facilities as a result of Contractor's operations.  All damage will be repaired or replaced, at the option of County, at Contractor’s expense within three (3) days after notification of such damage by Project Manager.  Repairs and/or replacements will be equal to original in all aspects.
 
Contractor shall perform all work outlined in this Contract in such a manner as to meet all accepted standards for safe practices during operations and to maintain safe conditions or premises and ways at all times, including safely stored equipment, machines and materials.  This includes compliance with Local County, State or other legal intents and terms of the applicable OSHA and CAL/OSHA Safety orders at all times so as to protect all persons, including Contractor’s employees and Agency against injury or damage to their property.
County’s Requirements:
 
      County’s Project Manager or designee will be responsible for ordering materials off this Contract and shall provide Contractor with the material type needed, quantities required, delivery address/location, and delivery time.
 
County personnel shall be allowed to inspect Contractor’s location(s) and materials and perform all necessary testing to confirm compliance with the specifications prior to award of bid and anytime throughout the Contract term.
 
County shall allow Contractor twenty (20) minutes for unloading.  Unloading time shall commence at the time the truck arrives at the delivery site and is ready to unload 
after
 the pre-set delivery time.
 
County shall allow for unloading charges beyond twenty (20) minutes, if delays are a result of County staff.  County shall not be charged unloading charges as a result of delays by Contractor’s staff.  Unloading charges shall be billed at the rate provided for in Attachment B “Contractor’s pricing.”
 
County acknowledges that during emergency operations Contractor may acquire additional fees for opening up the plant after normal business hours.  Therefore, if County request materials after normal plant operational hours, County agrees to pay Contractor an emergency plant opening fee at the rate provided for in Attachment B “Contractor’s pricing”.
 
County may Contract with other vendors to provide the materials if Contractor doesn’t supply materials as specified in this Contract.  Such action does not constitute an acceptable alternative to performance of the work by Contractor.
General Conditions:
Additional like items not listed in Attachment B “Contractor’s pricing” may be purchased off this Contract at a price agreed upon by County and Contractor.  Contractor shall provide a written quote to County for items not listed in Attachment B “Contractor’s pricing” at the request of the Project Manager.
 
No guarantee is given by County to Contractor regarding usage of this Contract.  Usage figures, if provided, are approximate, based upon the last usage.  Contractor agrees to supply materials requested, as needed by County, at prices listed in Attachment B “Contractor’s pricing”, regardless of quantity requested. Orders may be placed against this contract at the convenience of the using agency/department.

Bidders shall include in their bid response a monetary sum to cover the cost of all items included in the Contract.  The Model Contract contained in this solicitation is the Contract proposed for execution.  Upon award, awarded Bidder will be required to sign and submit Contract for execution.

## Electronic Fund Transfer (EFT)
If awarded, the County offers Bidder the option of receiving payment directly to its bank account via an Electronic Fund Transfer (EFT) process in lieu of a check payment. Payment made via EFT shall also receive an Electronic Remittance Advice with the payment details via e-mail. An e-mail address shall need to be provided to County via an EFT Authorization Form. A copy of the EFT form is attached as an Exhibit to this solicitation.

OCLSB or DVBE Preference provides for the following
:
Invitation for Bid – IFB
A five percent (5%) deduction in the original bid price shall be applied to all confirmed OCLSB or DVBE bidders for evaluation purposes. If the lowest bidder is a certified OCLSB or DVBE bidder, the contract will be awarded at the certified OCLSB or DVBE’s original bid price. The maximum allowable preference deduction is $100,000.
Request for Proposal - RFP
No Cost - Any Request for Proposals that does not include cost as a scoring criteria shall instead apply the five percent (5%) or eight percent (8%) preference percentage pursuant to the eligibility requirements above to a scoring criteria in the RFP that makes up no more than twenty percent (20%) of the total RFP.
With Cost - An additional five percent (5%) shall be applied to the total cost of each certified OCLSB or DVBE to obtain their final score. 
If the final score of any OCLSB or DVBE matches the final score of a respondent who is not an OCLSB or DVBE, preference shall be given to the certified OCLSB or DVBE. If two or more OCLSBs and/or DVBEs have the same final score, the County shall determine the contract award based on the County’s best interests. Notwithstanding these preference procedures, the Orange County Board of Supervisors reserves the right to award contracts in any other permissible manner in consideration of the County’s best interests.
Dual OCLSB and DVBE Preference provides for the following
:
Business Certified as OCLSB and DVBE
If a State-certified OCLSB is also a State-certified DVBE, the preference given to that business shall be 8% instead of 5%.
Subcontractors
If bidder is submitting subcontractors to qualify for the OCLSB or DVBE preference, bidder must demonstrate through the Staffing Plan that 20% of the total bid amount is allocated to the OCLSB and/or DVBE subcontractor(s).

Only electronic bids will be accepted, no exceptions. Once the Bid Due Date and Time has lapsed, bidders, the public and County staff are able to immediately see the results on OpenGov Procurement.

A person, firm or corporation who has submitted a sub-bid to a Bidder, or who has quoted prices on materials to a Bidder, is not hereby disqualified from submitting a sub-bid or quoting prices to other Bidders.
Bidders shall take all responsibility for any errors or omissions in their bids. Any discrepancies in numbers or calculations shall be interpreted to reflect the lowest price to the County.
The County shall not be liable for any expenses incurred by potential Bidders in the preparation or submission of their bids. Pre-contractual expenses are not to be included in the Contractor’s Pricing Sheet. Pre-contractual expenses are defined as, including but not limited to, expenses incurred by Bidder in:
Preparing its bid in response to this IFB;
Submitting that bid to the County;
Negotiating with the County any matter related to the bid; and,
Any other expenses incurred by the Bidder prior to the date of the award and execution, if any, of the Contract.

## OCLSB and DVBE Subcontractor Requirement - Construction:
This project is estimated to exceed five million dollars ($5,000,000). As a result, at least 3% of the total contract value must be subcontracted to an Orange County Local Small Business (OCLSB) or Disabled Veteran Business Enterprise (DVBE). 
Under the Public Contract Code, no DVBE preference can be applied to Public Works projects.
The Bid may be declared non-responsive if the Bidder fails to include at least 3% of the total contract value subcontracted to certified OCLSB or DVBE subcontractors.
