Solicitation Text:
## Best Qualified Person Or Firm
The award, if any, will be made to the best qualified person or firm(s). In evaluating whether a proposer(s) is (are) the best qualified person or firm(s) pursuant to the Santa Monica Municipal Code, City staff may utilize some or all of the following criteria:
The training, credentials and experience of the person or firm;
The demonstrated competence, ability, capacity and skill of the person or firm to perform the contract or provide the services;
The capacity of the person or firm to perform the contract or provide the service promptly, within the time specified, and without delay;
The sufficiency of the person’s or firm’s financial and other resources;
The character, integrity, reputation and judgment of the person or firm;
The ability of the person or firm to provide such future service as may be needed;
The price which the person or firm proposes to charge, including whether the price is fair, reasonable and competitive; and
Any other factor which will further the intent set forth in Section 608 of the City Charter.
The City shall have absolute discretion in determining the applicability and weight or relative weight of some or all of the criteria listed above and is not required to select the lowest monetary proposer.

## Term
The City is inviting proposals from qualified persons or firms for a firm-fixed contract for a term of four (4) years.

## Questions and Answers
Vendor Queries Due
Questions must be submitted online in the “Q&A” tab. The City will only accept or respond to questions submitted through the online vendor portal. 
One question per submittal. (This does not mean one question per vendor.) Submittals containing multiple questions will not be answered.

## Applicant Eligibility Requirements
In order to be considered for funding through the City’s Human Services Grants Program (HSGP), applicants must meet the following Council-approved minimum eligibility requirements:
Be:
A nonprofit organization with tax exempt status under Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Service Code and Section 23701(d) of the California State Franchise Tax Code; AND registered with the office of the Attorney General of the State of California Department of Justice with a current registration status; AND have a Board of Directors; OR
 
A hospital, health care, or educational institution with a governing board.
 
Certify that they are and will remain in compliance with any law which prohibits discrimination based on race, gender, sexual preference, sexual orientation, ethnic background, nationality, religion, age, parenthood, marriage, pregnancy, disability, HIV/AIDS status, immigration status, source of income, gender identity, gender expression, or any other class expressly protected by a local, state, or federal law. Including, but not limited to:
 
Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964;
 
Title VIII of the Civil Rights Act of 1968 (as amended);
 
Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 (as amended);
 
Age Discrimination Act of 1974;
 
Title I of the Housing and Community Development Act of 1974 (as amended); and
 
The Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990.
 
Agree that no City funds shall be expended for any political purpose, defined as participation or intervention in any political campaign on behalf of or in opposition to any candidate for public office, any initiative, referenda, ballot measure, recall, or any partisan or non-partisan electoral activity.
 
Agree that no City funds shall be used to teach, advance, advocate or promote any religion or religious belief or practices, including any irreligious belief or practice.
 
Document the ability to provide services accessible to SMPP, including services that are located or co-located in Santa Monica. Agencies not currently providing services in Santa Monica must describe a plan to deliver services to SMPP, including how services will be brought to SMPP, how SMPP will access physical service locations, and/or how programs will remove barriers to virtual services.
 
Be in Good Standing with the State of California Office of the Secretary of State.

## Eligible Services
Proposals must be for programs that provide one or more of the following Council-approved services. Programs that do not provide at least one of the services below will not be eligible for HSGP funding.

## Eligible Santa Monica Program Participants (SMPP)
The HSGP relies on Council-adopted criteria for program participants/clients to ensure that local resources serve local needs. Applicants have flexibility in determining the population(s) they propose to serve, so long as program participants comply with the following SMPP eligibility criteria:
General Eligibility Criteria
An individual or household with a permanent address in Santa Monica; or
A student currently enrolled in a Santa Monica public school (for school-based services).
Eligibility Criteria for People Experiencing Homelessness
An individual/household experiencing homelessness whose last permanent address at which they resided was in Santa Monica; or
An individual/adult-only household experiencing homelessness who has been in Santa Monica for at least three years; or
A family with at least one minor child experiencing homelessness who has been in Santa Monica for at least one year; or
An individual/household experiencing homelessness referred by City staff as a high utilizer of City services; or
An individual experiencing homelessness who currently works in Santa Monica a minimum of thirty (30) hours per week for at least six (6) continuous months; or
An individual experiencing homelessness who, within the past year, was terminated or laid off from a job in Santa Monica after having worked there a minimum of thirty (30) hours per week for at least six (6) continuous months.

## Receiving Time / Late Proposals
It is the responsibility of proposer to see that their proposal is submitted with sufficient time to be received by the City prior to the proposal closing time. The receiving time in the City Office will be the governing time for acceptability of proposals.
Late proposals are not accepted.

## Cash Match or Living Wage Options
The City is offering greater funding flexibility to HSGP grantees, potentially making it more feasible for programs to increase compensation for front-line workers such as case managers, care coordinators, outreach workers, and counselors. Applying agencies must select one of the following options and meet all relevant conditions:
Option 1: 30% Cash Match
Use City funds to cover up to 70% of the cost of services to eligible Santa Monica Program Participants and secure non-City funding for the balance of those costs (30% minimum).
No minimum threshold for staff salaries.
Option 2: Living Wage
Use City funds to cover up to 100% of the cost of services to eligible Santa Monica Program Participants. Non-city funding/cash match is not required.
Agree to meet the City’s 
Minimum Wage
 ($25.00 per hour for Fiscal Year 2026-27), adjusted annually, for all staff billed 90% or more to the HSGP program.
Complete the attached Living Wage Certification.
Conditions
Only programs that bill staff salaries to the HSGP grant will be eligible to apply for Option 2. Programs that do not bill staff salaries to the HSGP grant must apply for Option 1 and provide 30% cash match.
Agencies that receive HSGP funding will be required to work closely with City staff to ensure their program budget accurately reflects the true staffing structure of the program. Programs choosing Option 2 are subject to review and approval by City staff.

## Acceptance of Conditions Governing this RFP
Submission of a proposal constitutes acceptance of the Evaluation Factors contained in this RFP.

## Reporting Requirements
HSGP programs are intended to be data-driven and have lasting positive impacts on the lives of participants. 
Quantitative data, contextualized with qualitative program descriptions, are a key tool for understanding a program’s performance and can help identify what is working and where adjustments are needed. HSGP-funded programs are required to report on performance twice during the fiscal year, at mid-year and at year-end. They must submit a program report that includes a qualitative performance description and report on quantitative performance indicators, including outputs and outcomes.  
Proposals must
 define a minimum of two (2) and a maximum of five (5) performance indicators to assess the impact of their program. An indicator is a pair of one output and one outcome. Outputs describe the result of an activity and can include the number of people served or number of services performed, while outcomes focus on measurable impacts to participants’ lives and assess improvements that result from the program. Indicators should be specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound (SMART) and assess progress made during the program year.  The following table provides example performance indicators:
As part of the proposal, programs applying for HSGP funding must submit proposed performance indicators on the 
Performance Indicators
 tab of the 
Program Budget Demographics and Performance Workbook
.

## Incurring Cost
Any cost incurred by the proposer in preparation, transmittal, presentation of any proposal or material submitted in response to this RFP shall be borne solely by the proposer.

## Prime Consultant Responsibility
Any agreement that may result from the RFP shall specify that the prime consultant is solely responsible for fulfillment of the agreement with the City. The City will make agreement payments only to the prime consultant.

## Sub-consultants
Use of sub-consultants must be clearly explained in the proposal, and major sub-consultants must be identified by name. Prime consultants shall be wholly responsible for the entire performance whether or not sub-consultants are used.

## Amended Proposals
A proposer may submit an amended proposal before the deadline for receipt of proposals. Such amended proposals must be complete replacements for a previously submitted proposal and must be clearly identified as such in the transmittal letter. City personnel will not merge, collate, or assemble proposal materials.

## Proposer’s Rights to Withdraw Proposal
Proposers will be allowed to withdraw their proposals at any time prior to the deadline for receipt of proposals. The proposer must submit a written withdrawal request signed by the proposer’s duly authorized representative addressed to the City Contact.

## Proposal Offer Firm
Responses to this RFP, including proposal prices, will be considered firm for one hundred eighty (180) days after the due date for receipt of proposals or sixty (60) days after receipt of a best and final offer, if one is requested.

## Selection
The City of Santa Monica, through either the City Council or the City Manager (or his designee) has the sole authority to select the consulting firm and reserves the right to reject any and all proposals. The City reserves the right to approve or reject all sub-consultants and engineers proposed to be retained by the prime consultant. Upon signing of the agreement, no change in proposed personnel or sub-consultants can be made without the City’s review and written authorization.
By submitting a response to this RFP, prospective consultants waive the right to protest after award or seek any legal remedies whatsoever regarding any aspect of this RFP. The City reserves the right to select any number of finalists. In addition, the City reserves the right to issue written notice to all prospective consultants of any changes in the RFP terms or proposal submission schedule, should the City determine in its sole and absolute discretion that such changes are necessary.
The City reserves the right to request additional information from any proposing consultant and to reject any and all proposals. All original work products, including computer files, shall remain the property of the City.
The City reserves the right to retain an expert to evaluate the proposing consultant’s work or qualifications at all stages in the selection process. Additionally, any contract entered into will be subject to termination at any stage if in the judgment of the City, such termination is in the best interest of the City. In the event such decision is made, appropriate written notice would be given before any termination and the consultant would be compensated on a pro-rata basis for work performed.
The responsible proposer whose proposal is the most advantageous to the City, taking to consideration all the evaluation factors will be recommended for the contract award. Notwithstanding the Evaluation Team’s selection, the City reserves the right to award this RFP and the resultant Contract in any manner it deems to be in the best interest of the City and make the selection based on its sole discretion. The City is the sole and exclusive judge of quality and compliance with proposal specifications in any of the matters pertaining to this RFP.

## Best and Final Offer
The City reserves the right to request Best and Final Offers from any or all proposers. This will be the only opportunity to amend or modify proposals based on feedback from the City. Information from competing proposals will not be disclosed to other proposers prior to submission of a Best and Final Offer.

## Living Wage Requirement
Any agreement issued as a result of this Request for Proposal may be subject to the City’s Living Wage Ordinance, Santa Monica Municipal Code Chapter 4.65 (LWO), and its implementing regulations.

##   Disclosure of Proposal Contents
All proposals are subject to the provisions of the California Public Records Act, California Government Code section 6250 et seq., and any information submitted with a response is a public record subject to disclosure, unless a specific exemption applies.

## Notice Regarding Disclosure of Contents of Documents
All responses to this Request for Proposal (RFP) accepted by the City of Santa Monica (City) shall become the exclusive property of the City. All proposals accepted by the City shall become a matter of public record and shall be regarded as public, with the exception of those elements of each proposal which are defined by the contractor as business or trade secrets and plainly marked as "Trade Secret", "Confidential" or "Proprietary". Each element of a proposal which a contractor desires not to be considered a public record must be clearly marked as set forth above, and any blanket statement (i.e. regarding entire pages, documents or other non-specific designations) shall not be sufficient and shall not bind the City in any way whatsoever. ## Best Qualified Person Or Firm
The award, if any, will be made to the best qualified person or firm(s). In evaluating whether a proposer(s) is (are) the best qualified person or firm(s) pursuant to the Santa Monica Municipal Code, City staff may utilize some or all of the following criteria:
The training, credentials and experience of the person or firm;

## Scope of Work
The consultant must:
Meet with the Safety Administrator to develop an agreed upon annual training schedule.  The schedule will identify the safety training sessions to be provided each department/division, along with a timeframe for when the sessions will be carried out.
Work with department/division representatives designated by the Safety Administrator to make arrangements to deliver the training sessions identified in the annual training schedule.  The training will be provided on City premises during periods that ensure the greatest employee participation and are most convenient to departmental operations. This may require the consultant to provide training sessions as early as 6am and as late as 9pm.
Provide approximately 100 one hour, “general” safety training sessions annually on topics selected by the Safety Administrator (see list in section B below).  The training sessions will include an instructor presentation, interactive learning, post-training retention quiz, and where applicable, video and on-site practical demonstration. Class sizes will generally range from 10 to 40 participants.
Provide approximately 25 advanced/specialized safety training sessions on topics selected by the Safety Administrator (see list in section C below). The training sessions will include an instructor presentation, interactive learning, post training retention quiz, and where applicable, video and on-site practical demonstration.  Further, the training sessions must satisfy the time required for certification or recommended by the Consultant.  Class size will vary by topic, but, generally should not exceed 25 participants per session.
Provide additional miscellaneous safety training sessions that arise during the year as directed by the Safety Administrator.
Supply all course materials, teaching aides (e.g., video presentations, power-point presentations, etc.), and certification paperwork (as applicable) for all training sessions.  Further, the consultant will ensure all training session presentations and course materials meet the requirements stipulated by CCR Title 8 for the specific topic being presented.
Document training session attendance and provide a copy to the appropriate department/division supervisor and Safety Administrator.
Assist the Safety Administrator as a consultant on safety specific areas of need where a subject matter expert or specialist is needed. 
Assist the Safety Administrator with safety plan/program development, Job Safety Analysis, Job Hazard Assessment, or Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) where needed.

## Acceptance of Conditions Governing this RFP
Submission of a proposal constitutes acceptance of the Evaluation Factors contained in this RFP.

## Incurring Cost
Any cost incurred by the proposer in preparation, transmittal, presentation of any proposal or material submitted in response to this RFP shall be borne solely by the proposer.

## Prime Consultant Responsibility
Any agreement that may result from the RFP shall specify that the prime consultant is solely responsible for fulfillment of the agreement with the City. The City will make agreement payments only to the prime consultant.

## Sub-consultants
Use of sub-consultants must be clearly explained in the proposal, and major sub-consultants must be identified by name. Prime consultants shall be wholly responsible for the entire performance whether or not sub-consultants are used.

## Amended Proposals
A proposer may submit an amended proposal before the deadline for receipt of proposals. Such amended proposals must be complete replacements for a previously submitted proposal and must be clearly identified as such in the transmittal letter. City personnel will not merge, collate, or assemble proposal materials.

## Proposer’s Rights to Withdraw Proposal
Proposers will be allowed to withdraw their proposals at any time prior to the deadline for receipt of proposals. The proposer must submit a written withdrawal request signed by the proposer’s duly authorized representative addressed to the City Contact.

## Proposal Offer Firm
Responses to this RFP, including proposal prices, will be considered firm for one hundred eighty (180) days after the due date for receipt of proposals or sixty (60) days after receipt of a best and final offer, if one is requested.

## Selection
The City of Santa Monica, through either the City Council or the City Manager (or his designee) has the sole authority to select the consulting firm and reserves the right to reject any and all proposals. The City reserves the right to approve or reject all sub-consultants and engineers proposed to be retained by the prime consultant. Upon signing of the agreement, no change in proposed personnel or sub-consultants can be made without the City’s review and written authorization.
By submitting a response to this RFP, prospective consultants waive the right to protest after award or seek any legal remedies whatsoever regarding any aspect of this RFP. The City reserves the right to select any number of finalists. In addition, the City reserves the right to issue written notice to all prospective consultants of any changes in the RFP terms or proposal submission schedule, should the City determine in its sole and absolute discretion that such changes are necessary.
The City reserves the right to request additional information from any proposing consultant and to reject any and all proposals. All original work products, including computer files, shall remain the property of the City.
The City reserves the right to retain an expert to evaluate the proposing consultant’s work or qualifications at all stages in the selection process. Additionally, any contract entered into will be subject to termination at any stage if in the judgment of the City, such termination is in the best interest of the City. In the event such decision is made, appropriate written notice would be given before any termination and the consultant would be compensated on a pro-rata basis for work performed.
The responsible proposer whose proposal is the most advantageous to the City, taking to consideration all the evaluation factors will be recommended for the contract award. Notwithstanding the Evaluation Team’s selection, the City reserves the right to award this RFP and the resultant Contract in any manner it deems to be in the best interest of the City and make the selection based on its sole discretion. The City is the sole and exclusive judge of quality and compliance with proposal specifications in any of the matters pertaining to this RFP.

## Best and Final Offer
The City reserves the right to request Best and Final Offers from any or all proposers. This will be the only opportunity to amend or modify proposals based on feedback from the City. Information from competing proposals will not be disclosed to other proposers prior to submission of a Best and Final Offer.

## Living Wage Requirement
Any agreement issued as a result of this Request for Proposal may be subject to the City’s Living Wage Ordinance, Santa Monica Municipal Code Chapter 4.65 (LWO), and its implementing regulations.

##   Disclosure of Proposal Contents
All proposals are subject to the provisions of the California Public Records Act, California Government Code section 6250 et seq., and any information submitted with a response is a public record subject to disclosure, unless a specific exemption applies.

## Notice Regarding Disclosure of Contents of Documents
All responses to this Request for Proposal (RFP) accepted by the City of Santa Monica (City) shall become the exclusive property of the City. All proposals accepted by the City shall become a matter of public record and shall be regarded as public, with the exception of those elements of each proposal which are defined by the contractor as business or trade secrets and plainly marked as "Trade Secret", "Confidential" or "Proprietary". Each element of a proposal which a contractor desires not to be considered a public record must be clearly marked as set forth above, and any blanket statement (i.e. regarding entire pages, documents or other non-specific designations) shall not be sufficient and shall not bind the City in any way whatsoever. If disclosure is required or permitted under the California Public Records Act, or otherwise by law, the City shall not in any way be liable or responsible for the disclosure of any such records or part thereof.

## No Obligation
This RFP in no manner obligates the City to the eventual rental, lease, purchase, etc., of any goods or services offered until a valid written agreement is executed by the City and the selected proposer.

## Termination
This RFP may be canceled at any time and any and all proposals may be rejected in whole or in part when the City determines such action to be in the best interest of the City of Santa Monica.

## Sufficient Appropriation
Any agreement awarded for multiple years as a result of this RFP may be terminated if sufficient appropriations or authorizations do not exist. Such termination will be effected by sending written notice to the selected proposer. The City’s decision as to whether sufficient appropriations and authorizations are available will be accepted by the selected proposer as final.

## Errors and Restrictive Specifications
If a proposer discovers any ambiguity, conflict, discrepancy, omission, or other error in the RFP, the proposer should immediately notify the City Contact designated in Section I, B. Without disclosing the source of the request, the City may issue a written addendum to clarify the ambiguity, or to correct the problem, omission, or other error.
If prior to the submission date, a proposer knows of or should have known of an error in the RFP but fails to notify the City Contact of the error, the proposer shall submit their proposal at his, her or its own risk, and, if awarded an agreement, shall not be entitled to additional compensation or time by reason of error or its later correction.

## Legal Review
The City requires that all proposers agree to be bound by the General Requirements contained in this RFP.

## Contract Award and Execution
Selection of a proposer with whom the City enters into contract negotiations with, or a recommendation of an award by the Evaluation Committee or any other party, does not constitute an award of Contract. Once the City formally awards the contract, the successful consultant will be notified to enter into an agreement. If the selected consultant does not enter into the agreement, the City will begin negotiations with the second highest ranking proposing consultant.
Please review all contract forms prior to submitting a proposal. The City of Santa Monica intends to use these forms as the baseline agreements with the successful consultant. The City will not entertain proposals to make material changes to the contract form once the project has been awarded. If you wish to request changes to the contracting forms, you must do so during the proposal process. In addition, the City requires compliance with several other policies and ordinances, proposing consultants will need to complete these Exhibits and submit with their Proposal.
The RFP document and the successful proposal response, as amended by agreement between the City of Santa Monica and the successful consultant, will become part of the contract documents. Additionally, the City of Santa Monica may verify the successful consultant’s representations that appear in the proposal. Failure of the successful consultant to perform as represented may result in elimination of the successful consultant from further negotiation or in contract cancellation or termination.
No oral explanation or instruction of any kind or nature whatsoever given before the award of a contract to a consultant shall be binding. The City of Santa Monica shall not be bound, or in any way obligated, until the City has awarded the contract and all documents have been executed. The proposing consultant may not incur any chargeable costs prior to final contract execution.

## Governing Law
This RFP, and any agreement entered into pursuant to this RFP, are governed by the laws of the State of California.

## Oral Changes and Basis for Proposal
Proposers may not rely upon oral explanations. All changes and addenda will be issued in writing. Only information supplied by the City in writing through the City’s Contact, or in this RFP should be used as the basis for the preparation of proposals.

## Agreement Terms and Conditions
The agreement between the City and the selected proposer(s) will follow the format specified by the City and contain the terms and conditions set forth in Attachment B, Professional Services Agreement. However, 
the City reserves the right to negotiate with a successful proposer the final provisions or provisions in addition to those contained in this RFP.
 The contents of this RFP, as revised and/or supplemented, and the successful proposal will be incorporated into and become part of the agreement.
Should a proposer object to any of the City’s terms and conditions, as contained in this Section or in Attachment B, that proposer must propose specific alternative language in his, her, or its proposal. The City may or may not accept the alternative language. General references to the proposer’s terms and conditions or attempts at complete substitutions are not acceptable to the City and may result in disqualification of the proposer.

## Proposer’s Terms and Conditions
Proposers must submit with the proposal a complete set of any additional terms and conditions that they expect to have included in an agreement negotiated with the City.

## Proposer Qualifications
The City may make such investigations as necessary to determine the ability of the proposer to adhere to the requirements specified within this RFP.

## Right to Waive Minor Irregularities
The City reserves the right to waive minor irregularities and the right to waive mandatory requirements, provided that all of the otherwise responsive proposals fail to meet the same mandatory requirements and/or doing so does not otherwise materially affect the procurement. This right is at the sole discretion of the City.

## Change in Agreement or Representatives
The City reserves the right to require a change in the selected proposer or representatives if the assigned representatives are not, in the opinion of the City, meeting its needs adequately.

## City Rights
The City reserves the right to award the proposal to separate proposers on any of the services as set forth in the proposer’s proposal. It is further understood that if the proposer to whom any recommended award is made fails to enter into an agreement with the City, award may be made to the next best qualified person or firm, who shall be bound to perform as if she, he or it received the award in the first instance.

## Right to Publish
Throughout the duration of this procurement process and agreement term, potential proposers, and proposers, must secure from the City written approval prior to the release of any information that pertains to the potential work or activities covered by this procurement or the subsequent agreement. Failure to adhere to this requirement may result in disqualification of the proposer or termination of the agreement.

## Ownership of Proposals
All documents submitted in response to the RFP shall be become the property of the City of Santa Monica and are subject to the provisions of the California Public Records Act, as described in Section II. A. 11. herein.

Proposal will be evaluated by a committee comprised of City staff and may include outside consultants (the “Evaluation Committee”). The Evaluation Committee will make an award recommendation to City staff. City Council may give approval of the agreement and/or direct staff to negotiate the final terms and execute the agreement.
This agreement shall be awarded to the proposer or proposers whose proposal is best qualified, taking into consideration the evaluation factors set forth in the RFP. here
. Proposer may file a written protest with the Purchasing Agent no more than seven calendar days following the posting of award recommendation on the City’s online vendor portal website.

A party's failure to require strict performance of any provision of this Agreement shall not waive or diminish that party's right thereafter to demand strict compliance with that or any other provision. No waiver by a party of any of its rights under this Agreement shall be effective unless expressed in writing and signed by the party alleged to have granted the waiver. State of California Office of Industrial Relations
. The contractor shall post a copy of these prevailing wage rates at the site of the project. It is the duty of the contractor and subcontractors to employ registered apprentices and to comply with all aspects of Labor Code Section 1777.5.
There are penalties required for contractor’s/subcontractor’s failure to pay prevailing wages and for failure to employ apprentices, including forfeitures and debarment under Labor Code Sections 1775, 1776, 1777.1, 1777.7 and 1813.

The prime contractor is responsible for submittal of their payrolls and those of their subcontractors as one package. The contractor, and any work performed under this CSA, shall, at all times comply and be in accordance with, and subject to the provisions of Articles 2 and 3, Division 2, Part 7, Chapter 1 of the Labor Code, State of California.

## Specifications
The primary objectives of this procurement are to obtain a modern, reliable, and fully integrated Onboard Video Surveillance System (OBVSS) solution that supports the operational, safety, security, evidentiary, and maintenance needs of the Big Blue Bus fleet.
Primary Objectives
The selected Proposer shall provide a turnkey solution that includes, at a minimum, the following primary objectives:
3.1.1 System Replacement and Modernization
Replace the existing onboard video surveillance equipment across the entire fixed-route fleet with a modern, transit-grade IP-based surveillance system including onboard recording hardware, cameras, communications equipment, and centralized video management software.
 
3.1.2 Safety, Security, and Evidentiary Support
Provide high-quality video and audio coverage to support incident investigation, operator and passenger safety, claims management, liability review, law enforcement coordination, and public records requests.
 
3.1.3 Integrated Vehicle Systems Compatibility
Provide a solution that integrates with existing vehicle systems and display infrastructure, including multiplex controls, rear-view monitors, Multi-Function Displays (MFDs), passenger-facing entry monitors, and communications systems, as applicable.
 
3.1.4 Wireless Communications and Remote Access
Support reliable wireless video offload, live video access, health monitoring, remote configuration, and communications through vendor-provided cellular and Wi-Fi solutions.
 
3.1.5 Scalable and Future-Ready Platform
Provide a scalable platform capable of supporting future fleet needs, expanded camera coverage, optional advanced analytics, and evolving cloud or on-premises hosting requirements.
 
3.1.6 Installation, Training, and Support
Provide pilot deployment, fleet-wide installation, training, documentation, warranty, and ongoing technical support services necessary for successful long-term system operation.

3.3 Technical Specifications
 
3.3.1 System Capabilities – Network Video Recorder and Onboard Storage
3.3.1.1 Each vehicle shall be equipped with a high-definition network video recorder (NVR) or similar product (analog devices not accepted).
3.3.1.2 The NVR shall be capable of withstanding vibration consistent with public transit, temperature ranging from -10 degrees F to 120 degrees F, and humidity ranging from 5% - 95% non-condensing.
3.3.1.3 NVR Scalability: The NVR shall support all cameras for the initial vehicle configuration and provide capacity for future expansion. The proposed architecture shall support up to thirty-two (32) IP camera channels. SMDOT does not currently anticipate installation of 32 cameras per vehicle; this capacity is required to provide flexibility for future fleet and camera expansion.
3.3.1.4 Camera/Resolution Capacity: The NVR shall support IP cameras meeting the resolution and camera-type requirements of this RFP, including fixed cameras, 360°/fisheye IP cameras, and 4K/UHD cameras.
The system shall support up to thirty-two (32) IP camera channels at a minimum resolution of 1920x1080, Full HD or FHD, and up to eight (8) cameras with a resolution of 3840x2160 (4K/UHD).
3.3.1.5 Discrete Inputs: The NVR shall support a minimum of six (6) discrete inputs. Inputs shall support association of vehicle events, including brake application, turn signals, hazard lights, kneeling, wheelchair ramp deployment, or other available vehicle states, with the corresponding video.
3.3.1.6 The NVR shall be able to support both battery and ignition power configurations.
3.3.1.7 The NVR shall capture GPS data, speed, and other telemetry.
3.3.1.8 G-Force/Event Detection: The OBVSS shall incorporate a 3-axis accelerometer or equivalent sensing capability capable of detecting vehicle acceleration/deceleration and G-force events. The system shall automatically create time-synchronized event tags within the associated recorded video.
3.3.1.9 Post-Ignition Operation: The NVR shall provide a user configurable automatic shutdown timer following vehicle ignition-off and shall be capable of continuing video and audio recording during that period. The Proposer shall identify the supported post-ignition recording duration.
3.3.1.10 Post-Ignition Video Download: The OBVSS shall be configurable so that the NVR can continue downloading video footage over Wi-Fi using onboard routers (either existing or installed by Proposer) even after the vehicle’s ignition is turned off, drawing on battery power for a pre-determined amount of time or until the download is completed, whichever amount of time is lesser.
3.3.1.11 The NVR shall be compatible with the electrical power characteristics of SMDOT’s fleet and have the ability to operate on 9-32 VDC.
3.3.1.12 Time Synchronization: The NVR shall maintain accurate, synchronized date and time across onboard recording, video, audio, metadata, event markers, and system logs. The system shall support automatic network time synchronization using Network Time Protocol (NTP) and shall be configurable to use the City’s designated NTP source. The Proposer shall describe how accurate time is maintained during temporary loss of network connectivity or vehicle power.
3.3.1.13 Vehicle Data Integration: The NVR shall support the vehicle-system and metadata integration requirements specified in Sections 3.3.6.2 through 3.3.6.4.
3.3.1.14 The NVR shall store and manage video data from interior and exterior cameras within the vehicle.
3.3.1.15 Removable Storage and Manual Retrieval: The NVR shall utilize removable and interchangeable storage media housed in a removable drive caddy or equivalent configuration. The storage media shall be capable of being physically removed from the vehicle and accessed using a compatible review station or docking solution for manual video retrieval without reliance on vehicle communications.
The system shall allow a removed storage unit to be replaced with another compatible storage unit so that the vehicle may be returned to service without waiting for video retrieval to be completed.
Proposers shall identify the storage media type (e.g., SSD, HDD, or equivalent).
 
3.3.1.16 Retention and Storage Sizing
: The proposed onboard storage configuration shall provide a minimum of 600 hours of usable recorded-video retention per vehicle, representing approximately 30 days of typical vehicle operation, after accounting for redundancy, mirroring, formatting, and other storage overhead.
3.3.1.17 Storage calculations shall be based on continuous recording using the camera quantities, resolutions, frame rates, compression technology, bitrates, and other recording parameters proposed for each vehicle configuration. Calculations shall include the required 4K/UHD forward roadway camera and all other required camera coverage.
3.3.1.18 Proposers shall provide the storage-sizing calculations used for each proposed vehicle configuration, including camera quantity, resolution, frame rate, codec/compression technology, assumed average and/or maximum bitrate per stream, total installed storage, usable storage after redundancy and other overhead, and estimated hours of retained video.
3.3.1.19 Evidentiary Video Quality: Proposed recording, compression, and bitrate settings shall maintain evidentiary-quality video appropriate for incident investigation, safety, security, and liability review. Recording parameters shall not be reduced solely for purposes of satisfying the retention requirement.
3.3.1.20 Storage Redundancy: The onboard storage solution shall support redundant mirrored storage or equivalent fault-tolerant architecture.
3.3.1.21 Spare Parts Requirements: The Proposer shall include pricing for spare components to support ongoing maintenance and minimize system downtime.
Spare components shall be provided at a minimum ratio of 10–15% of deployed quantities, unless otherwise specified.
Proposers shall provide a detailed list of recommended spare components based on the proposed system architecture and shall identify any components considered critical for maintaining system uptime.
3.3.1.22 Optional Spare Parts: The Proposer shall include pricing for optional spare parts, such as antennas, SIM cards/modems, spare LED status indicators, and event marker buttons.
3.3.1.23 PoE Connectivity: The proposed system shall provide standards-based Power over Ethernet (PoE) connectivity sufficient to power and communicate with all required IP cameras under normal operating conditions (standard 802.3af; supporting a full 15.4W per port). The Proposer shall identify the applicable PoE standards, per-port capability, and any external PoE equipment required by the system.
Externally mounted PoE switches are permitted if installed within a secured electronics compartment of the bus.
Alternative connection methods to PoE are not desired.
3.3.1.24 The NVR shall provide sufficient aggregate PoE power to support all required onboard cameras, including 4K, 360°, and IR-enabled cameras, operating simultaneously at full load (minimum 120w aggregate PoE budget).
3.3.1.25 The NVR shall not impose unreasonable PoE port-assignment restrictions that limit SMDOT’s ability to replace, relocate, or reconfigure compatible cameras. The Proposer shall identify any camera-to-port restrictions or special power/connectivity requirements applicable to the proposed system. 
3.3.1.26 Onboard Communications: The OBVSS shall provide onboard communication capability to enable wireless data download and remote configuration of on-board camera system via router devices and Wi-Fi when the vehicle is in the yard.
3.3.1.27 Health Indicator: The OBVSS shall provide an operator-accessible visual indication of basic system operating status (LED status display or equivalent) without requiring the operator to access the NVR or equipment compartment.
3.3.1.28 Operator Event Marker: The OBVSS shall include a driver-accessible event marker button or equivalent operator-initiated trigger that allows the operator to manually flag and preserve video associated with an incident or noteworthy event.
Activation of the event marker shall create a time-stamped event tag within the system and preserve a configurable pre-event and post-event video segment from all relevant camera views for expedited retrieval and evidentiary review.
The event marker shall be easily accessible to the operator from the driver compartment and shall not interfere with safe vehicle operation.
The Proposer shall identify whether the event marker function is integrated with existing vehicle controls, multiplex inputs, or requires dedicated hardware.
 
3.3.2 Video Management System, Client /Server Software
3.3.2.1 The Proposer shall provide a unified software suite or integrated platform capable of managing all system functions (video requests, video review, system configuration, fleet health status monitoring, etc.).
3.3.2.2 The VMS shall not require a specialized PC or other PC equipment to view, download, or access recorded content beyond a hard drive dock.
3.3.2.3 Licensing shall support all required SMDOT operational, maintenance, supervisory and administrative users without additional per-user charges during the warranty/support term.
3.3.2.4 VMS Architecture: The Proposer shall describe the architecture of the proposed VMS, including client, browser-based, server, cloud, database, and other components required to provide the functionality specified in this RFP.
3.3.2.5 The VMS shall support integration with the City’s identity management environment.
3.3.2.6 Scheduled Retrieval: Authorized users shall be able to create video/data retrieval requests for immediate or scheduled processing and track the status of those requests through completion.
3.3.2.7 The VMS shall allow for the video to be:
Exported to common, widely compatible formats like MP4, AVI or MOV.
Downloaded and distributed without requiring additional proprietary software.
Provide options for downloading video at different quality/resolutions as needed.
3.3.2.8 Automated Retrieval: The VMS shall support automated workflows for retrieving requested video/audio and collecting system-health and diagnostic information from fleet vehicles.
3.3.2.9 Date/Time Retrieval: VMS users shall be able to search for archived video by date and time.
3.3.2.10 Location-Based Retrieval: Authorized users shall be able to identify and retrieve recorded video using vehicle location as a search criterion in addition to date, time, vehicle, and other available metadata.
3.3.2.11 Database Language: The VMS shall maintain the information necessary to efficiently catalog, search, retrieve, manage, and associate video, audio, metadata, system-health information, and other required records. The Proposer shall describe the underlying data-management architecture or database.
3.3.2.12 Single-File Delivery: The VMS shall provide an efficient means of exporting the requested video files as a continuous reviewable file. Segmented video, or “blocks” are not acceptable.
3.3.2.13 Download Resumption: The VMS shall be able to pause and resume downloading requested video. For example, if a large file does not download completely because the vehicle leaves the Wi-Fi coverage area, it should be able to resume downloading once the vehicle returns to the coverage area without restarting the download.
3.3.2.14 Partial Downloads: Authorized users shall be able to begin reviewing available portions of requested video before the entire requested transfer has completed, where supported by the selected retrieval method, without compromising completion or integrity of the remaining download.
3.3.2.15 Live Video Monitoring: The system shall be capable of real-time video monitoring to enable users to view video from the on-board system in real-time over cellular or Wi-Fi data including live look-in capabilities.
3.3.2.16 Adaptive Video Streaming: The system shall support configurable primary and secondary video streams, or equivalent adaptive-streaming functionality, to optimize bandwidth utilization for live viewing and remote video access over cellular and Wi-Fi networks without reducing the quality of locally recorded evidentiary video.
3.3.2.17 Mapping: The VMS shall provide map-based visualization of available vehicle-location data in conjunction with live and/or recorded video, allowing authorized users to correlate vehicle movement and location with the associated video timeline.
3.3.2.18 Metadata Display: During video review, authorized users shall be able to view applicable time-synchronized vehicle and event metadata required by this RFP in conjunction with the associated video.
3.3.2.19 Privacy Redaction: The VMS shall have the capability to blur or block out identifying features during video retrieval or in post-video download.
3.3.2.20 Health Alerts: The VMS shall automatically identify reportable system-health conditions and notify designated SMDOT personnel. Notification methods shall include email and may include additional configurable notification methods.
3.3.2.21 System Health Monitoring: The VMS shall provide fleet-level and individual-vehicle health information sufficient to identify, diagnose, and troubleshoot failures involving NVRs, cameras, storage, communications, and other monitored OBVSS components, as well as historical logs for maintenance diagnosis.
3.3.2.22 Hosting: The proposed VMS shall be capable of deployment using either the City-provided on-premises environment or a Proposer-provided cloud-hosted environment.
 
3.3.2.23 Pricing Alternatives – Hosting Options
Proposers shall provide separate pricing in the Cost Proposal Schedule for both of the following hosting alternatives:
Utilization of the City of Santa Monica’s existing on-prem server environment (identify pricing separately using Category I of the Cost Proposal), and
A Proposer-provided cloud-hosted VMS solution (Use Category H-Recurring Costs in Cost Proposal).
Proposers shall identify any additional hardware, software, storage licensing, or implementation costs required for each hosting option.
 
3.3.3 IP Cameras
3.3.3.1 IP Cameras/PoE: The base camera solution shall utilize digital IP cameras that receive power and data connectivity through PoE or an equivalent standards-based architecture. Analog HD/AHD are not acceptable for new camera installations.
3.3.3.2 Resolution: Except where a higher resolution is expressly required in Section 3.3.4, newly provided cameras shall record at a minimum native resolution of 1920x1080.
3.3.3.3 Low Light / IR Cameras: Cameras shall provide usable evidentiary video throughout the anticipated lighting conditions of the vehicle environment. Interior cameras and exterior cameras requiring nighttime coverage shall incorporate infrared illumination or equivalent low-light technology appropriate to the proposed camera location.
3.3.3.4 Microphones: Interior camera coverage shall support synchronized audio recording. The Proposer shall identify the microphone configuration and whether microphones are integral to the cameras or provided through another component of the proposed solution.
3.3.3.5 Exterior Environmental Protection: Exterior-mounted cameras and associated exposed components shall be designed for transit-vehicle exterior service and shall have an environmental rating of IP67 or greater.
3.3.3.6 All cameras shall provide an image that is stable and free from vibration.
 
3.3.4 Camera Views and Coverage
3.3.4.1 This defines the minimum required camera coverage views for all fixed-route vehicles included in this procurement. Proposed camera layouts shall provide full coverage of the locations identified in the tables below.
Attachment I shows current camera placement for most models, however, diagrams for each bus model are not available. Proposers should defer to the requested minimum coverage requirements described in this scope rather than existing camera placement.
3.3.4.2 The Proposer shall ensure that the proposed camera layout provides continuous evidentiary coverage of all passenger boarding, alighting, operator interaction, ADA securement, articulation, stairwell, and exterior hazard zones. Blind spots shall be minimized through the use of additional fixed, 360°, or fisheye cameras where necessary.
3.3.4.3 The Proposer may recommend additional cameras or alternative camera types (including 360° / fisheye cameras) where necessary to eliminate blind spots and improve evidentiary quality, provided that all required coverage zones identified in this attachment are fully met or exceeded.
3.3.4.4 The City encourages Proposers to recommend optimized camera layouts utilizing 360°, fisheye, or other equivalent advanced camera technologies that reduce total device count while maintaining or improving evidentiary coverage and video quality. Where such cameras are proposed, the system should support digital de-warping, post-event pan/zoom review, and export of evidentiary-quality video.

3.3.4.7 Pricing Alternatives – Camera Replacement Options
Proposers shall provide separate pricing for the following camera deployment alternatives:
Full Camera Replacement: Complete replacement of all onboard cameras with Proposer-provided equipment.
Existing Camera Reuse: SMDOT will consider the continued use of existing serviceable IP cameras currently installed on fleet vehicles where such cameras are compatible with the proposed OBVSS and satisfy applicable system performance and coverage requirements.
Proposers shall provide separate unit pricing for replacement cameras by applicable camera type as part of the Cost Proposal in Category G.
Following award and prior to installation on each vehicle, the Contractor shall inspect and evaluate existing IP cameras to determine their condition, compatibility with the proposed OBVSS, and suitability for continued service. The Contractor shall identify cameras recommended for reuse and cameras recommended for replacement and shall provide the basis for each replacement recommendation.
Replacement of existing cameras shall be subject to SMDOT approval. Existing cameras approved for reuse shall be fully integrated into the proposed OBVSS and shall meet applicable functional, video-quality, coverage, and system-integration requirements of this specification.
 
3.3.5 Audio
3.3.5.1 The OBVSS shall provide synchronized audio recording sufficient to support incident and evidentiary review within the passenger compartment. Audio shall remain time-synchronized with the associated video and shall be attributable to the applicable recording source or vehicle area. Authorized users shall be able to select and review available audio independently as necessary during video review. The proposed solution shall provide intelligible audio under typical transit operating conditions, recognizing normal vehicle and passenger background noise.
 
3.3.6 Multiplex / Multi-Function Display Integration
3.3.6.1 The proposed OBVSS shall be fully compatible with the existing multiplex control system currently installed on the SMDOT fleet, including the Dinex / I/O Controls multiplex architecture and associated display logic used to activate rear-view camera displays and driver Multi-Function Displays (MFDs).
3.3.6.2 The system shall support integration with the vehicle trigger states and logic outputs, including but not limited to:
Reverse gear engagement
Turn signal activation
Hazard lights
Door open / close status
Kneel and ramp deployment
Other available multiplex discrete inputs and J1939 / CAN signals
3.3.6.3 The primary purpose of vehicle-system metadata integration is to support accident, incident, and evidentiary video review. At a minimum, SMDOT expects the proposed system to capture and associate with the corresponding video, where available from the vehicle's J1939, CAN/multiplex, discrete-input, GPS, or OBVSS interfaces, the following information: date/time, vehicle identification, GPS location, vehicle speed, brake application/status, left and right turn-signal status, hazard-light status, reverse-gear status, door open/closed status, kneel activation, wheelchair-ramp deployment, G-force/event data, and operator event-marker activation.
3.3.6.4 The metadata shall be time-synchronized with the associated video and available for display during video review and evidentiary retrieval.
3.3.6.5 The OBVSS shall be capable of automatically routing the designated rear-facing camera feed to the existing MFD or rear-view monitor with minimal latency and without degradation of image quality. Proposer shall identify whether the proposed video-output/interface method is HDMI (digital output) or BNC (analog output).
3.3.6.6 The Proposer shall be responsible for identifying all interface requirements, signal conversion devices, software configuration, multiplex programming coordination, and integration modules necessary to ensure compatibility with the existing multiplex environment.
3.3.6.7 Replacement of existing MFD displays, rear-view monitors, or multiplex control hardware shall not be assumed unless specifically proposed as an approved alternate.
3.3.6.8 The Proposer shall provide a written description and schematic of how the proposed system will integrate with the existing multiplex and Dinex control logic.
 
3.3.7 Passenger Entry Monitor Integration and Replacement
3.3.7.1 The proposed OBVSS shall provide the cost to replace the existing passenger-facing monitors currently installed above the operator compartment that display live video of the front entrance door area for deterrence and passenger awareness purposes whenever the vehicle is powered on.
3.3.7.2 The Proposer shall identify all required hardware, cabling, signal converters, mounting brackets, and software configuration necessary for installation.
3.3.7.3 Replacement monitors shall, at a minimum:
Be a minimum of 10 inches diagonal display size
Support HDMI digital video input
Provide continuous live display of the entrance-door camera feed
Be industrial / transit-grade and designed for vibration, temperature, and transit vehicle environments
Be securely mounted in a vandal-resistant enclosure
Provide brightness and contrast sufficient for daylight passenger visibility
3.3.7.4 Pricing for this optional alternate shall be provided separately in the Cost Proposal Schedule under Category I and shall not be considered part of the base proposal.
 
3.3.8 Wireless and Cellular Communications
3.3.8.1 SMDOT currently utilizes existing onboard communications equipment associated with other vehicle systems, including Clever Devices and CradlePoint router infrastructure.
3.3.8.2 For purposes of this procurement, Proposers shall provide and recommend their own dedicated onboard router, modem, gateway, or equivalent communications solution required to support the proposed OBVSS, including live view, wireless offload, remote configuration, and health monitoring functions.
3.3.8.3 Proposers shall not assume use of the City’s existing Clever Devices / CradlePoint communications environment as the primary OBVSS communications path.
3.3.8.4 Wireless Performance and Remote Configuration: Through the Proposer's selected communications solution, the system shall support live video streaming over yard Wi-Fi and cellular connectivity and facilitate remote configuration of the onboard camera system.
3.3.8.5 The Proposer shall describe the capabilities of the OBVSS when utilizing both a 5G cellular network and BBB’s current Wi-Fi infrastructure.
3.3.8.6 Wi-Fi/Cellular Retrieval: The system shall support remote retrieval and transfer of requested video, audio, metadata, and system information through both SMDOT yard Wi-Fi and the proposed cellular communications solution.
3.3.8.7 Communications Standards: The proposed onboard communications solution shall support current commercial 4G LTE and 5G cellular service and shall be compatible with SMDOT's wireless environment. Wi-Fi connectivity shall support the standards necessary to operate with the City's existing yard infrastructure, including 802.11ax, and shall support 5 GHz operation for high-volume video offload. Proposers shall identify all supported wireless standards and frequency bands.
3.3.8.8 Cellular Service and Ongoing Communication Costs
Proposers shall separately identify all required recurring cellular service, data plans, SIM management, cloud connectivity, and communications licensing costs associated with the proposed OBVSS communications solution.
Costs shall be clearly separated between:
One-time hardware and installation costs
Recurring monthly / annual cellular service costs
Optional managed service costs
 
3.3.9 Cloud Hosting, Redundancy, and Cybersecurity Requirements 
3.3.9.1 The Proposer shall complete and submit the City's required Vendor Information Security Assessment (VISA) Questionnaire and Technology/Architecture Questionnaire. The questionnaires shall be considered part of the Proposer's technical response and shall provide the requested information regarding system architecture, cloud hosting, cybersecurity, data protection, access management, backup/disaster recovery, integrations, and related technology requirements.
 
3.4 Installation
3.4.1 All installations of new OBVSS equipment will be performed at the following locations:
Big Blue Bus: 1660 7th Street, Santa Monica, CA 90401
SMDOT can provide two (2) buses per day and two (2) maintenance bays to conduct the work.
Installation may take place between 5:00 AM and 1:00 PM, seven (7) days a week.
3.4.2 SMDOT will provide space for OBVSS equipment to be stored during the project at the following lockable and secure location:
Big Blue Bus Maintenance Facility: 1660 7th Street, Santa Monica, CA 90401
3.4.3 Installer will be responsible for removing existing OBVSS.
3.4.4 Disposal of Sensitive Data: Items containing sensitive data such as hard drives shall be done through a certified disposal process.
3.4.5 Installation will be handled by the vendor or the vendor’s selected sub-contractor.
3.4.6 Pilot Installation and Approval
3.4.6.1 Prior to fleet-wide installation, the Proposer shall complete pilot installations on at least one (1) standard 40-foot bus and one (1) 60-foot articulated bus, if applicable.
3.4.6.2 Pilots shall be reviewed and approved by SMDOT prior to the commencement of full fleet deployment.
 
3.4.7 Installation Work Plan and Schedule
3.4.7.1 The Proposer shall provide a detailed fleet installation schedule, including projected daily/weekly vehicle quantities, installation sequence, milestone dates, and estimated total project duration.
 
3.4.8 Maximum Vehicle Downtime
3.4.8.1 Installation activities shall be coordinated to minimize vehicle downtime. SMDOT can provide two (2) buses per day.
3.4.8.2 No vehicle shall be out of service for installation for more than one (1) service day without written approval from SMDOT.
 
3.4.9 Post-Installation Functional Verification
3.4.9.1 Following installation on each vehicle, the Proposer shall perform functional verification testing including, at a minimum:
All camera views
Audio recording
Live view functionality
Wireless offload
Rear-view monitor / MFD integration
Reverse trigger activation
Passenger entry monitor display
GPS and metadata capture
 
3.4.10 Operational Acceptance Period
3.4.10.1 Following completion of fleet installation, the system shall undergo a thirty (30) day operational acceptance test period during which system functionality, wireless downloads, live viewing, storage, and alerting functions shall be verified prior to final project sign-off.
 
3.4.11 Restoration of Vehicle Interiors and Equipment Compartments
3.4.11.1 The Proposer shall restore all vehicle panels, equipment compartments, wireways, mounting surfaces, and interior finishes to original condition following installation activities.
 
3.4.12 As-Built Documentation
3.4.12.1 The Proposer shall provide as-built documentation for each vehicle type, including wiring diagrams, camera locations, monitor connections, NVR locations, and multiplex integration points.
 
3.5 Warranty
3.5.1 The Proposer’s solution shall provide the City with a warranty for the system for a minimum of one (1) year warranty on all provided hardware and maintenance support.
3.5.2 The one (1) year warranty period shall begin at completion and sign off of the project.
3.5.3 The Proposer shall provide the City the option of purchasing extended warranties for the system for an additional four (4) years, exercised at the City’s sole discretion.
3.5.4 Warranty Support and Updates: During the base warranty and maintenance support term, the Proposer shall provide technical support for all hardware and software and shall provide, license, install, and integrate all applicable software updates, security patches, firmware updates, bug fixes, and manufacturer-released upgrades for the VMS, mobile applications, onboard NVRs, and associated system components at no additional cost to the City.
 
3.6 Training
3.6.1 Initial training for operations and maintenance staff shall be conducted in person at BBB’s Maintenance Facility at 1660 7
th
 Street, Santa Monica, CA 90401
3.6.2 Proposers shall provide a detailed training plan including topics to be covered, and quantity of training hours, for maintenance and operational users.
3.6.3 Technical training for maintenance shall include, at a minimum:
All aspects of maintaining the OBVSS including, but not limited to, repair, replacement, installation, troubleshooting, diagnostics, and preventative maintenance activities of all OBVSS components.
All aspects of using the VMS system including, but not limited to, video retrieval, reporting, alert management, troubleshooting, and advanced user-functions, including system configuration, user access, and asset management.
3.6.4 User guides, troubleshooting manuals, preventative maintenance instructions, equipment material lists, wiring diagrams, or other documented materials for the use and maintenance of system and associated hardware are required.
These materials should be provided in digital form.
 
3.7 Customer Support
3.7.1 Return Merchandise Authorization (RMA) Process
Proposer to provide a thorough explanation of the RMA process including but not limited to:
Steps required to initiate RMA
Method of submitting an RMA request
Average turnaround time for repair, replacement or refund
Whether expedited RMA processing is available for critical failures
Communication channels for tracking updates on RMAs
Any costs to the customer related to the RMA process (e.g. shipping)
 
3.7.2 Preventative Maintenance
3.7.2.1 Proposer shall provide documented instructions for recommended preventative maintenance (PM) activities, including recommended PM frequency, and PM inspection checklist of onboard equipment, including NVR units, cameras, power supplies, and connectivity modules.
 
3.8 Optional Emerging Technology / AI Capabilities (Non-Mandatory)
3.8.1 The City is interested in understanding currently available or emerging artificial intelligence (AI), computer vision, analytics, or pilot-stage capabilities that may enhance onboard safety monitoring, operational awareness, risk mitigation, or liability management.
3.8.2 This section is optional and is provided for informational purposes only. Responses to this section shall not be scored as part of the base proposal evaluation and shall not affect Proposer responsiveness.
3.8.3 Examples of such capabilities may include, but are not limited to:
Automated passenger counting and occupancy analytics
Operator distraction or inattentive driving detection
Passenger fall event detection
Door-area incident analytics
Mobility device / wheelchair securement monitoring concepts
Passenger behavior analytics related to boarding and alighting
Hazard-zone awareness and passenger movement analytics
3.8.4 Proposers currently developing, piloting, testing, or commercially offering such capabilities may provide a separate narrative description of:
Current maturity level
Existing deployments
Active pilot programs
Known limitations
Required hardware or cloud dependencies
Expected implementation timeline
3.8.5 Any optional AI or advanced analytics capability shall be submitted as a separately priced optional alternate, clearly segregated from the base proposal cost. Use Category I-Optional Equipment & Services of the Cost Proposal attachment.
3.8.6 The City makes no representation that any optional AI capability will be purchased, evaluated, or implemented as part of this procurement.
 
3.9 Optional Non-Revenue Vehicle Camera System (Non-Mandatory)
3.9.1 In addition to the fixed-route fleet, the City operates approximately fifteen (15) non-revenue service support vehicles. As an optional alternate, the Proposer may provide forward-facing vehicle camera recording solutions for these vehicles. The desired coverage is forward-facing camera coverage only.
3.9.2 This optional alternate is requested for informational and pricing purposes only and shall not be considered a mandatory requirement of this procurement. The pricing for the optional non-revenue vehicle camera solution may be provided on a cost-per-vehicle basis. Proposals that do not include this optional capability shall not be deemed non-responsive.                                                   
3.9.3 If proposing this option, the Proposer shall describe:
The recommended camera hardware and recording platform.
Whether the solution integrates with the proposed OBVSS Video Management System.
Storage methodology (onboard, cloud, or hybrid).
Video retrieval process.
GPS, date/time, and event metadata capabilities.
Cellular connectivity requirements, if applicable.
Warranty and support provisions.
3.9.4 The Proposer shall identify any differences between the proposed vehicle solution and the transit bus OBVSS, including any limitations related to integration, software functionality, or video management.
3.9.5 Pricing for this optional alternate shall be provided separately in the Cost Proposal under Category F and shall include, at a minimum:
Camera hardware
Recording device (if required)
Installation
Mounting hardware
Software licensing
Cellular equipment and service (if applicable)
Warranty
Any recurring subscription or cloud-hosting fees
 
3.10 Optional Ridership / APC Validation Capability
SMDOT is interested in VMS functionality that facilitates manual validation of ridership and/or Automatic Passenger Counter (APC) data using onboard video.
 
3.10.1 Proposers shall describe any available functionality that allows authorized users to efficiently review passenger boarding and alighting activity for a selected vehicle, route/trip, date, and time period. Such functionality may include identification of door-open/door-close events, navigation between passenger boarding events, generation of consolidated boarding/alighting video, or other methods that reduce the need to review continuous trip video.
 
3.10.2 Proposers shall describe the proposed method for identifying passenger boarding/alighting or door events, any required integration with existing vehicle systems or APC/CAD-AVL data, and any additional hardware, software, licensing, or integration required.
The functionality is desirable, but it is not a mandatory requirement. Pricing shall be identified under Category I of the Cost Proposal. 
 
3.11 Project Deliverables
The Proposer shall deliver the following:
3.11.1 OBVSS Solution:
 A fully functional, turnkey Onboard Video Surveillance System (OBVSS) solution for the Big Blue Bus fleet that meets all technical, operational, installation, integration, and performance requirements outlined in this RFP, including onboard hardware, cameras, network video recorders (NVRs), communication devices, and Video Management System (VMS) software.
3.11.2 Implementation Services
: Complete project implementation services including pilot installation, fleet-wide installation, removal and disposal of existing OBVSS equipment, configuration, integration with existing vehicle systems and displays, testing, acceptance support, and final system commissioning.
 
3.11.3 System Integration Services:
 Complete integration with existing and/or Proposer-provided onboard communications equipment, vehicle multiplex systems, Multi-Function Displays (MFDs), passenger entry monitors, Wi-Fi and cellular communications infrastructure, and City identity management systems, as applicable.
3.11.4 Documentation
: Complete system documentation including user manuals, maintenance guides, administrator guides, wiring diagrams, as-built drawings, camera layout schematics, training materials, and technical support documentation.
3.11.5 Support and Warranty Services:
 Ongoing warranty coverage, software and firmware updates, maintenance support, Return Merchandise Authorization (RMA) procedures, and technical support services for the duration of the warranty and maintenance term.
3.11.6 Future Fleet Compatibility and Replacement Standard:
Any hardware, software, cameras, NVRs, monitors, communications equipment, or associated components installed after the initial fleet deployment, whether as part of future vehicle procurements, warranty replacements, spare part use, lifecycle refresh, or repair activities, shall be fully compatible with the deployed OBVSS platform and shall be of equal or better quality, performance, and durability than the originally installed components.
Where originally specified components are discontinued, obsolete, or no longer commercially available, replacement equipment shall be the current manufacturer-supported equivalent or newer generation technology, provided that such replacement maintains full compatibility with the City’s existing OBVSS architecture, VMS software, camera layouts, and vehicle integration requirements.
Any replacement or future-installed components shall not reduce system functionality, video quality, retention capability, interoperability, or operational performance.
3.11.7 Project Management
: Comprehensive project management including project schedule, installation sequencing plan, pilot deployment plan, communication methods, quality assurance plan, testing plan, acceptance plan, and final project closeout documentation.
3.11.8 Training Services:
 Initial and follow-up training for operations, maintenance, safety, and administrative users, including system use, video retrieval, diagnostics, troubleshooting, preventive maintenance, and system administration.

## Scope of Work
City Hall UPS Replacement
The vendor must provide a turnkey, fully functional replacement of the existing UPS system at City Hall that meets manufacturer specifications. Work includes:
Removal and proper disposal of the existing UPS equipment, including batteries, cabinets, and related components in accordance with all applicable federal, state, and local requirements.
Provision and installation of a new UPS system with equal or greater capacity than the existing system, including battery systems, cabinets, maintenance bypass panels, and all required components. 
Installation of all electrical connections, conduits, wiring, and supporting infrastructure needed for the new system.
Coordination and completion of required permits, inspections, and compliance with applicable codes and standards.
Replacement equipment must include network management capabilities that allow City staff to remotely monitor equipment status and receive alerts and notifications.
Startup and testing of the new system, including verification that it operates correctly and integrates properly with City systems in accordance with manufacturer requirements, including verification of UPS operation, battery operation, bypass functionality, alarms, and monitoring and communication functions, as applicable.
City Hall In Row Cooling Replacement
The vendor must replace the seven existing APC ACRC100 chilled water in row cooling units serving the City Hall data center with a fully operational cooling system that maintains reliable environmental conditions within the data center. Work includes:
Removal and proper disposal of existing in row cooling units and related components in accordance with all applicable federal, state, and local requirements.
Furnishing and installation of seven new chilled water in row cooling units that fit within the existing physical configuration and meet or exceed the manufacture's rated performance specifications of the existing APC ACRC100 unites.
All required mechanical, electrical, and controls work, including electrical connections, signal connections, drain connections, chilled water supply and return connections, control wiring, and environmental sensor integration, as applicable.
Verification of proper airflow, temperature control, and compatibility with the existing rack configurations.
Replacement equipment must include network management capabilities that allow City staff to remotely monitor equipment status and receive alerts and notifications.
Testing to confirm proper operation and communication with any existing APC monitoring and management environment.
Temporary Power, Cooling, and Phased Implementation
Continuous operation of critical systems must be maintained throughout the UPS and cooling replacement work. The vendor must develop and implement a phased approach that maintains continuous operation and prevents disruptions to critical City systems. This includes:
Providing and installing temporary UPS, cooling, or other systems as needed.
Sequencing the work to maintain continuous operation and avoid downtime to critical systems.
Coordinating scheduling and transition activities with City staff.
Citywide Maintenance, Support, and As-Needed Services
The vendor must provide ongoing maintenance and support services for the new City Hall equipment and existing UPS and related equipment across City facilities. Services must include, but are not limited to:
Preventive maintenance, inspections, testing, and system diagnostics at the intervals recommended by the equipment manufacturer, but no less than annually.
On site repair services, troubleshooting, and corrective actions, in accordance with the services levels and response times specified in this RFP.
Replacement of batteries, consumables, components, UPS systems, cooling equipment, environmental monitoring equipment, and other related equipment, as needed.
Emergency repair and response services. 
Technical support and coordination with OEMs or certified partners, as applicable. 
Inspection of existing equipment and identification of equipment conditions for deficiencies requiring maintenance or repair.
