Event Name: Request for Proposal - Environmental Impact Report (EIR) for Santa Monica Airport Conversion Project
Description:
The City of Santa Monica is requesting proposals from qualified consulting firms to prepare an Environmental Impact Report meeting the requirements of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) for the Santa Monica Airport Conversion Project.

Measure LC is a ballot measure that was passed by Santa Monica voters on November 6, 2014.  Measure LC states, as follows:
Subject only to limitations imposed by law, the City Council shall have full authority, without voter approval, to regulate use of the Santa Monica Airport, manage Airport leaseholds, condition leases, and permanently close all or part of the Airport to aviation use.
If all or part of the Airport land is permanently closed to aviation use, no new development of that land shall be allowed until the voters have approved limits on the uses and development that may occur on the land. However, this section shall not prohibit the City Council from approving the following on Airport land that has been permanently closed to aviation use: the development of parks, public open spaces, and public recreational facilities; and the maintenance and replacement of existing cultural, arts and education uses.  (Emphasis added.)
In 2017, the City and FAA entered into a consent decree, which allows (but does not mandate) that the City can close the Santa Monica Airport after December 31, 2028.
Following the consent decree, on February 28, 2017, the City Council adopted Resolution No. 11026 which (1) “authoriz[es] all actions necessary to ensure the closure of Santa Monica airport effective as of midnight on December 31, 2028,” and (2) provides that the City “shall take all actions necessary and proper to ensure that SMO will cease to operate as an airport and shall be closed to all aeronautical use forever effective as of midnight on December 31, 2028.”
In light of the foregoing actions, but subject to future policy considerations, the City has commenced preliminary planning and community engagement efforts to consider future land uses at the Airport, as further described, below.  These efforts have culminated in what is referenced hereinafter as the “Santa Monica Conversion Project”.
The Santa Monica Airport Conversion Project (the Proposed Project) is a comprehensive multi-phase initiative to reimagine 192 acres of public land following the planned closure of the Santa Monica Airport on December 31, 2028, as afforded by the Consent Decree signed in 2017. The effort establishes a long-term land use vision centered on a future, Measure LC compliant, Great Park that reflects community aspirations while balancing legal, environmental, economic, and social considerations along with funding realities and feasibility. Community engagement over the past two years has generated a substantial foundation of feedback that will inform development of a Preferred Scenario Framework Plan for the site, anticipated before the end of 2026. This Preferred Scenario, which includes the anticipated closure of the airport, will become the basis for environmental review under the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA).
The planning work builds on the five Guiding Principles unanimously adopted by the City Council in January 2025: Start with Nature, Inspire Wonder, Balance Economics, Amplify Versatility, and Celebrate Place. It also reflects more than 16,100 survey responses, 102 public meetings, and extensive input from boards, commissions, task forces, and the broader community. Phase 3b resulted in the creation of a Framework Diagram that organizes the site into eight flexible districts informed by the engagement to date: Immersive Nature, Active Sports, Urban Edge, Arts & Culture, The Stroll, The Meadow, The Lawn, and The Heart. These districts identify general locations, approximate sizes, and potential activities that can evolve over time and support a multi-year buildout while remaining adaptable to future conditions and community needs. As the City progresses into Phase 4, each district from the Framework Diagram will be carefully evaluated and illustrated to show its purpose and anticipated uses.
Once the City Council formally selects a Preferred Scenario Framework Plan, the City intends to begin preparation of a program level EIR. This EIR will evaluate environmental impacts, feasible mitigation measures, and a full range of alternatives, including the required No Project option. The program level EIR will also support future regulatory work such as creation of a Specific Plan, General Plan amendments, zoning updates, and phased implementation strategies.
The City also received $10,000,000 in Proposition 4 funds (Climate Bond) to plan and develop a portion of what is anticipated to be the Great Park.    Following voter approval of Proposition 4, the California legislature enacted Public Resources Code Section 21080.57, as follows:
This division does not apply to any activity or approval necessary for or incidental to planning, design, site acquisition, construction, operation, or maintenance of public park or nonmotorized recreational trail facilities funded in whole or in part by the Safe Drinking Water, Wildfire Prevention, Drought Preparedness, and Clean Air Bond Act of 2024 (Division 50 (commencing with Section 90000)).  (Emphasis added.)
The program EIR should take into consideration Public Resources Code Section 21080.57. For more information please go to the project website 
www.smacproject.com

The award, if any, will be made to the best qualified person or firm(s). In evaluating whether a proposer(s) is (are) the best qualified person or firm(s) pursuant to the Santa Monica Municipal Code, City staff may utilize some or all of the following criteria:
The training, credentials and experience of the person or firm;
The demonstrated competence, ability, capacity and skill of the person or firm to perform the contract or provide the services;
The capacity of the person or firm to perform the contract or provide the service promptly, within the time specified, and without delay;
The sufficiency of the person’s or firm’s financial and other resources;
The character, integrity, reputation and judgment of the person or firm;
The ability of the person or firm to provide such future service as may be needed;
The price which the person or firm proposes to charge, including whether the price is fair, reasonable and competitive; and
Any other factor which will further the intent set forth in Section 608 of the City Charter.
The City shall have absolute discretion in determining the applicability and weight or relative weight of some or all of the criteria listed above and is not required to select the lowest monetary proposer.

## Questions and Answers
Vendor Queries Due
Questions must be submitted online in the “Q&A” tab. The City will only accept or respond to questions submitted through the online vendor portal. 
One question per submittal. (This does not mean one question per vendor.) Submittals containing multiple questions will not be answered.

## Scope of Work 
Consultant will prepare a program-level Environmental Impact Report (EIR) for the proposed Project in close coordination with City staff. The EIR must be prepared in accordance with the criteria, standards, and provisions of the CEQA, Section 21000 et seq. of the Public Resources Code and the State CEQA Guidelines (California Code of Regulations Section 15000 et seq.), and relevant CEQA case law.
 Task A. Initial Study/Project Description
The selected consultant will prepare an EIR Project Description that meets CEQA requirements. Selected consultant must work with the City on drafting a schedule and an information needs list to the City, as necessary, to begin EIR work. Additionally, the Consultant must prepare an Initial Study and Notice of Preparation to be reviewed by the City. The Initial Study must scope out the environmental issues that the project is anticipated to have "No Impacts" or "Less Than Significant Impact".
Deliverables
Information Needs List
Project Description (electronic format)
Initial Study
Notice of Preparation
EIR schedule
Task B. Notice of Preparation/Scoping Meeting
In accordance with the requirements of CEQA, selected consultant must prepare a Notice of Preparation (NOP) of a Draft EIR/Notice of Scoping Meeting and circulate to the State Clearinghouse; Responsible Agencies; Trustee Agencies; other interested and affected State, County, and local governmental agencies; local Native American tribal representatives; and other groups and individuals that may have interest in the proposed project.
Selected consultant must also conduct a public scoping meeting in coordination with City staff and consultants, and prepare relevant scoping materials for the proposed project.
Deliverables
Notice of Preparation 
Scoping Meeting (CEQA boards, CEQA/Project presentation on Powerpoint)
Task C. Preparation of the Draft EIR
A CEQA-compliant EIR that analyzes the potential environmental impacts of the project, including closure of the Santa Monica Airport (SMO), will be required. In accordance with CEQA, the EIR must include a thorough explanation/analysis of the project’s construction and operational impacts for each environmental issue area, feasible mitigation measures, an analysis of impacts following mitigation, identification of impacts that cannot be mitigated to a less than significant level, and an assessment of cumulative effects. An alternatives analysis and preparation of a mitigation monitoring program are also required.
The scope and format of the EIR will follow the outline below and include the following:
Introduction
Executive Summary
Project Description
Analysis of Environmental Impacts
Alternatives (Up to five alternatives)
Other CEQA Considerations/Mandatory Findings of Significance
List of Preparers/References
For each environmental issue area to be analyzed, the EIR must include a description of existing conditions (environmental and regulatory setting), identification of the methodology and significance thresholds used based on Appendix G of CEQA Guidelines and CEQA caselaw, a thorough analysis of the project’s potential for significant impacts, a discussion of cumulative impacts, feasible mitigation measures, and level of significance after mitigation. At minimum, it is anticipated that the Draft EIR will analyze the following environmental issues:
Aesthetics/Visual Resources
 - The project site is located in an urbanized area and developed with an existing airport. There are no designated scenic highways adjacent to the project site, and the City is not aware of any scenic resources in the project area. However, the existing site topography is such that scenic vistas such as westward ocean views and northward views of the Santa Monica Mountains, are available from the project site.  Development of the project would change the existing visual character and quality of views and would also introduce new sources of light and glare.  As such, the EIR will include an analysis of project impacts on scenic vistas, scenic resources, visual character, and light/glare.
Air Quality
 - The EIR will include an analysis of the operational air emissions and construction air emissions that would be generated using the most recent version of CalEEMod. Project emissions will be compared against relevant and applicable significance criteria to determine if the project would conflict with or obstruct an air quality plan or exceed an established standard for a criteria pollutant, or result in other emissions adversely affecting a number of people.  In addition to the analysis of the air emissions that would be generated by operation and construction of the project, the EIR will analyze operational air emissions that would be generated/re-distributed as a result of the closure of SMO.  A human health risk assessment is also required to address potential public health impacts and should be based on updated guidance to determine if project-related toxic air contaminants or hazards pose significant risks to nearby communities. 
Cultural Resources - 
The City's consultant for the Proposed Project previously commissioned a preliminary Cultural Resources Report in March 2025 to identify potential archaeological and historic resources on the project site.  The report includes background research on the history of SMO and provides an inventory of potential historic resources that warrant further review and analysis. The airport has two City Landmarks, the Beacon and Compass Rose, which could be incorporated into the design and planning of the project.  The EIR will include a detailed full analysis of the identified potential historic resources on the project site and whether each of these resources are considered significant at the local, state, or regional level.  
Energy - 
Based on the Proposed Project's anticipated operations and construction details, the EIR will include an analysis of the project's energy impacts (including a quantification of energy demands accounting for proposed sustainable and/or renewable energy features) and determine whether the project would result in potentially wasteful, inefficient consumption of energy resources and whether the project would conflict with a state or local plan for renewable energy/energy efficiency.
Geology/Soils
 - While the project site is not located on any known fault or fault zones, the project site is susceptible to seismic risks similar to other developments in the Los Angeles region. The project would include substantial excavation and grading during project construction, which could potentially create on-site geologic risks such as erosion and soil stability issues. The consultant or subconsultant will prepare a Preliminary Geological Investigation Report to assess existing geological conditions and determine potential geological and soil impacts based on the project's components. Results of the report will be summarized and incorporated in the EIR.
Greenhouse Gas Emissions - 
The EIR will include an analysis of the operational greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and construction air emissions that would be generated using the most recent version of CalEEMod. Similar to the air quality analysis, GHG emissions will be compared against relevant significance criteria and/or adopted climate action plans to determine if the project would result in a significant GHG impact.  In addition to the analysis of the GHG emissions that would be generated by operation and construction of the project, the EIR will analyze operational GHG emissions that would be generated/re-distributed as a result of the closure of SMO.  
Hazards and Hazardous Materials 
- Airport operations have existed on the project site since the 1910s. These operations have included the use and handling of various hazards and hazardous materials, which have resulted in potential subsurface contamination. A Phase I Environmental Site Assessment (Phase I ESA) was prepared for the City for the project site, which identified a number of recognized environmental conditions (RECs). Subsequently, a Phase II ESA was prepared. As part of the EIR, consultant will provide review of the Phase II ESA and develop appropriate mitigation measures. 
 
Hydrology and Water Quality - 
The project site lies within the Santa Monica Bay Watershed which encompasses 414 square miles from the Santa Monica Mountains to the north and downtown LA to the east, to the Bay.  Primary pollutant concerns for the Bay include DDT (dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane), PCB (polychlorinated biphenyls), and sediment contamination.  The EIR will analyze surface runoff flows from the project site including potential for contaminants to be discharged into the City's storm drain system and ultimately the Bay. The analysis will also include a technical analysis of whether existing and planned storm drain capacity can accommodate project flows.
Land Use and Planning  - 
The existing SMO has long been recognized by the City as a site that can offer unique land use opportunities. The project would result in the closure of the airport, and conversion of the property into a public park with supportive land uses.  Although the project site is not zoned, it does have a General Plan land use designation of Institutional/Public Lands. The EIR will analyze the project's consistency with applicable regional and local plans and regulations. The analysis will also consider the project's relationship with surrounding land uses.
Noise 
- The project has the potential to generate new sources of noise and vibration due to increased visitation to the project site and project construction equipment. The EIR must include a quantitative estimate of the operational and construction noise levels that would be generated by the project.  Existing noise measurements will be taken to establish ambient noise levels at nearby sensitive receptors and on roadways.  The project's increase in noise levels must be compared against relevant criteria and/or the City's Noise Ordinance to determine if the project would result in a significant noise impact.  In addition to the analysis of the noise levels that would be generated by operation and construction of the project, the EIR will analyze noise impacts as a result of the closure of SMO.  
 
Public Services/Recreation
 - The project could potentially increase demand for public services such as police protection, park, and fire protection services due to increased visitation levels to the project site. The EIR will include an analysis of whether such increased demand would result in substantial adverse physical impacts associated with the provision of new or expanded facilities. Additionally, as the Proposed Project provides significant park and recreational facilities, the EIR will analyze the impacts associated with the construction of such facilities.
Transportation
 - The project will include the construction of a number of circulation improvements, including new street segments, bicycle lanes, and pedestrian facilities. An analysis of the project's potential impacts relative to vehicle miles traveled (VMT), and potential conflict with a plan, policy or regulation addressing the circulation system must be addressed. The analysis will be based on the City's adopted VMT significance criteria. Additionally, an assessment of whether the project would result in a hazardous design feature or inadequate emergency access must be conducted.
Tribal Cultural Resources - 
The project site is located on the ancestral land of the Gabrieleno/Tongva tribe.  In addition to a records search for tribal resources, the consultant will assist the City with tribal consultation consistent with AB 52. Results of the tribal consultation will be included as part of the EIR.
Utilities and Service Systems - 
The project is anticipated to result in increased water consumption, wastewater generation, and solid waste generation. The project would include utility system improvements that may include the replacement, relocation, modification or construction of new infrastructure or facilities. The EIR will include preparation of technical reports on project utility demands and anticipated capacity, determine whether current and planned water supplies, sewer capacity, and solid waste facilities are sufficient to accommodate the project. 
Selected consultant will assume three rounds of review for each completed section of the EIR and two final rounds of review of the full completed Draft EIR prior to publication.
Deliverables
Transportation Study
Air Quality/Greenhouse Gas Emissions Analysis Report
Construction and Operational Health Risk Assessment
Preliminary Geotechnical Investigation Report
Noise Technical Report
Phase II ESA
AB 52 Tribal Consultation Letters
Utility Technical Reports
Completed Draft EIR
On-line Submittal of Draft EIR on State Clearinghouse website 
Notice of Completion/Notice of Availability for Draft EIR
Task D.  Preparation of the Final EIR
Following the end of the public review period for the Draft EIR, consultant must prepare a Final EIR consisting of written responses to public comments, revisions to the Draft EIR, and a Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Program.
Deliverables
Completed Final EIR
Notice of Completion for Final EIR
Statement of Overriding Considerations
EIR Findings
Task E. CEQA Exemption for portion of the Great Park funded with Proposition 4 funds. 
Concurrent analysis and preparation of a CEQA exemption relating to use of Proposition 4 grant funds per Public Resources Code section 21080.57.
Task F. Meetings/Public Hearings/Management
The consultant will anticipate attendance at up to 10 meetings (NOP scoping meeting, Planning Commission hearings, City council hearings, and any other meetings as necessary).  In addition, biweekly conference calls during preparation of the Draft EIR and Final EIR should be anticipated.

## Term
The City is inviting proposals from qualified persons or firms for a firm-fixed contract for an initial term of 
One (1) 
, with 
Four (4)
 for renewal of 
One (1)
 each, to be exercised at the City’s sole discretion.

## Other Requirements
Consultant should have a minimum of 10 years of experience in preparing CEQA related documents.

## Prevailing Wage
Proposers are hereby notified that pursuant to provisions of Section 1770, et seq., of the Labor Code of the State of California, the Contractor shall pay its employees the general prevailing rate of wages as determined by the Director of Department of Industrial Relations. In addition, the Contractor shall be responsible for compliance with the requirements of Section 1777.5 of the California Labor Code relating to apprentice public works contracts.
No consultant or sub-consultant may be listed on a bid proposal for a public works project (submitted on or after March 1, 2015) unless registered with the Department of Industrial Relations pursuant to Labor Code section 1725.5 [with limited exceptions from this requirement for bid purposes only under Labor Code section 1771.1(a)].
No consultant or sub-consultant may be awarded a contract for public work on a public works project (awarded on or after April 1, 2015) unless registered with the Department of Industrial Relations pursuant to Labor Code section 1725.5.
This project is subject to compliance monitoring and enforcement by the Department of Industrial Relations.

## Minimum Vendor Requirements 
The City hopes to achieve completion of the Final EIR by June 2028 or sooner.  A summary of the consultant's qualifications with the firm’s relevant expertise and experience in preparing environmental documentation, particularly in the City of Santa Monica and/or similar cities. Provide an appropriately detailed description of at least five (5) projects that firm has worked on, which demonstrates firm’s relevant experience and successes. Each project description should include the date(s) that the relevant work was performed, project work plan/timeline, and project start/completion date as well as the name, title, address and telephone number of a contact person who can be contacted for verification of information provided by the firm. An electronic link to the project’s environmental documentation should also be provided. 
Please indicate in-house technical capabilities (e.g., historical, utilities, air quality, noise, etc.).

## Receiving Time / Late Proposals
It is the responsibility of proposer to see that their proposal is submitted with sufficient time to be received by the City prior to the proposal closing time. The receiving time in the City Office will be the governing time for acceptability of proposals.
Late proposals are not accepted.

## Acceptance of Conditions Governing this RFP
Submission of a proposal constitutes acceptance of the Evaluation Factors contained in this RFP.

## Incurring Cost
Any cost incurred by the proposer in preparation, transmittal, presentation of any proposal or material submitted in response to this RFP shall be borne solely by the proposer.

## Prime Consultant Responsibility
Any agreement that may result from the RFP shall specify that the prime consultant is solely responsible for fulfillment of the agreement with the City. The City will make agreement payments only to the prime consultant.

## Sub-consultants
Use of sub-consultants must be clearly explained in the proposal, and major sub-consultants must be identified by name. Prime consultants shall be wholly responsible for the entire performance whether or not sub-consultants are used.

## Amended Proposals
A proposer may submit an amended proposal before the deadline for receipt of proposals. Such amended proposals must be complete replacements for a previously submitted proposal and must be clearly identified as such in the transmittal letter. City personnel will not merge, collate, or assemble proposal materials.

## Proposer’s Rights to Withdraw Proposal
Proposers will be allowed to withdraw their proposals at any time prior to the deadline for receipt of proposals. The proposer must submit a written withdrawal request signed by the proposer’s duly authorized representative addressed to the City Contact.

## Proposal Offer Firm
Responses to this RFP, including proposal prices, will be considered firm for one hundred eighty (180) days after the due date for receipt of proposals or sixty (60) days after receipt of a best and final offer, if one is requested.

## Selection
The City of Santa Monica, through either the City Council or the City Manager (or his designee) has the sole authority to select the consulting firm and reserves the right to reject any and all proposals. The City reserves the right to approve or reject all sub-consultants and engineers proposed to be retained by the prime consultant. Upon signing of the agreement, no change in proposed personnel or sub-consultants can be made without the City’s review and written authorization.
By submitting a response to this RFP, prospective consultants waive the right to protest after award or seek any legal remedies whatsoever regarding any aspect of this RFP. The City reserves the right to select any number of finalists. In addition, the City reserves the right to issue written notice to all prospective consultants of any changes in the RFP terms or proposal submission schedule, should the City determine in its sole and absolute discretion that such changes are necessary.
The City reserves the right to request additional information from any proposing consultant and to reject any and all proposals. All original work products, including computer files, shall remain the property of the City.
The City reserves the right to retain an expert to evaluate the proposing consultant’s work or qualifications at all stages in the selection process. Additionally, any contract entered into will be subject to termination at any stage if in the judgment of the City, such termination is in the best interest of the City. In the event such decision is made, appropriate written notice would be given before any termination and the consultant would be compensated on a pro-rata basis for work performed.
The responsible proposer whose proposal is the most advantageous to the City, taking to consideration all the evaluation factors will be recommended for the contract award. Notwithstanding the Evaluation Team’s selection, the City reserves the right to award this RFP and the resultant Contract in any manner it deems to be in the best interest of the City and make the selection based on its sole discretion. The City is the sole and exclusive judge of quality and compliance with proposal specifications in any of the matters pertaining to this RFP.

## Best and Final Offer
The City reserves the right to request Best and Final Offers from any or all proposers. This will be the only opportunity to amend or modify proposals based on feedback from the City. Information from competing proposals will not be disclosed to other proposers prior to submission of a Best and Final Offer.

## Living Wage Requirement
Any agreement issued as a result of this Request for Proposal may be subject to the City’s Living Wage Ordinance, Santa Monica Municipal Code Chapter 4.65 (LWO), and its implementing regulations.

##   Disclosure of Proposal Contents
All proposals are subject to the provisions of the California Public Records Act, California Government Code section 6250 et seq., and any information submitted with a response is a public record subject to disclosure, unless a specific exemption applies.

## Notice Regarding Disclosure of Contents of Documents
All responses to this Request for Proposal (RFP) accepted by the City of Santa Monica (City) shall become the exclusive property of the City. All proposals accepted by the City shall become a matter of public record and shall be regarded as public, with the exception of those elements of each proposal which are defined by the contractor as business or trade secrets and plainly marked as "Trade Secret", "Confidential" or "Proprietary". Each element of a proposal which a contractor desires not to be considered a public record must be clearly marked as set forth above, and any blanket statement (i.e. regarding entire pages, documents or other non-specific designations) shall not be sufficient and shall not bind the City in any way whatsoever. If disclosure is required or permitted under the California Public Records Act, or otherwise by law, the City shall not in any way be liable or responsible for the disclosure of any such records or part thereof.

## No Obligation
This RFP in no manner obligates the City to the eventual rental, lease, purchase, etc., of any goods or services offered until a valid written agreement is executed by the City and the selected proposer.

## Termination
This RFP may be canceled at any time and any and all proposals may be rejected in whole or in part when the City determines such action to be in the best interest of the City of Santa Monica.

## Sufficient Appropriation
Any agreement awarded for multiple years as a result of this RFP may be terminated if sufficient appropriations or authorizations do not exist. Such termination will be effected by sending written notice to the selected proposer. The City’s decision as to whether sufficient appropriations and authorizations are available will be accepted by the selected proposer as final.

## Errors and Restrictive Specifications
If a proposer discovers any ambiguity, conflict, discrepancy, omission, or other error in the RFP, the proposer should immediately notify the City Contact designated in Section I, B. Without disclosing the source of the request, the City may issue a written addendum to clarify the ambiguity, or to correct the problem, omission, or other error.
If prior to the submission date, a proposer knows of or should have known of an error in the RFP but fails to notify the City Contact of the error, the proposer shall submit their proposal at his, her or its own risk, and, if awarded an agreement, shall not be entitled to additional compensation or time by reason of error or its later correction.

## Legal Review
The City requires that all proposers agree to be bound by the General Requirements contained in this RFP.

## Contract Award and Execution
Selection of a proposer with whom the City enters into contract negotiations with, or a recommendation of an award by the Evaluation Committee or any other party, does not constitute an award of Contract. Once the City formally awards the contract, the successful consultant will be notified to enter into an agreement. If the selected consultant does not enter into the agreement, the City will begin negotiations with the second highest ranking proposing consultant.
Please review all contract forms prior to submitting a proposal. The City of Santa Monica intends to use these forms as the baseline agreements with the successful consultant. The City will not entertain proposals to make material changes to the contract form once the project has been awarded. If you wish to request changes to the contracting forms, you must do so during the proposal process. In addition, the City requires compliance with several other policies and ordinances, proposing consultants will need to complete these Exhibits and submit with their Proposal.
The RFP document and the successful proposal response, as amended by agreement between the City of Santa Monica and the successful consultant, will become part of the contract documents. Additionally, the City of Santa Monica may verify the successful consultant’s representations that appear in the proposal. Failure of the successful consultant to perform as represented may result in elimination of the successful consultant from further negotiation or in contract cancellation or termination.
No oral explanation or instruction of any kind or nature whatsoever given before the award of a contract to a consultant shall be binding. The City of Santa Monica shall not be bound, or in any way obligated, until the City has awarded the contract and all documents have been executed. The proposing consultant may not incur any chargeable costs prior to final contract execution.

## Governing Law
This RFP, and any agreement entered into pursuant to this RFP, are governed by the laws of the State of California.

## Oral Changes and Basis for Proposal
Proposers may not rely upon oral explanations. All changes and addenda will be issued in writing. Only information supplied by the City in writing through the City’s Contact, or in this RFP should be used as the basis for the preparation of proposals.

## Agreement Terms and Conditions
The agreement between the City and the selected proposer(s) will follow the format specified by the City and contain the terms and conditions set forth in Attachment , Services Agreement. However, 
the City reserves the right to negotiate with a successful proposer the final provisions or provisions in addition to those contained in this RFP.
 The contents of this RFP, as revised and/or supplemented, and the successful proposal will be incorporated into and become part of the agreement.
Should a proposer object to any of the City’s terms and conditions, as contained in this Section or in Attachment , that proposer must propose specific alternative language in his, her, or its proposal. Proposer must provide a brief discussion of the purpose and impact, if any, of each proposed changed followed by the specific proposed alternate wording. The City may or may not accept the alternative language. General references to the proposer’s terms and conditions or attempts at complete substitutions are not acceptable to the City and may result in disqualification of the proposer.

## Proposer’s Terms and Conditions
Proposers must submit with the proposal a complete set of any additional terms and conditions that they expect to have included in an agreement negotiated with the City.

## Proposer Qualifications
The City may make such investigations as necessary to determine the ability of the proposer to adhere to the requirements specified within this RFP.

## Right to Waive Minor Irregularities
The City reserves the right to waive minor irregularities and the right to waive mandatory requirements, provided that all of the otherwise responsive proposals fail to meet the same mandatory requirements and/or doing so does not otherwise materially affect the procurement. This right is at the sole discretion of the City.

## Change in Agreement or Representatives
The City reserves the right to require a change in the selected proposer or representatives if the assigned representatives are not, in the opinion of the City, meeting its needs adequately.

## City Rights
The City reserves the right to award the proposal to separate proposers on any of the services as set forth in the proposer’s proposal. It is further understood that if the proposer to whom any recommended award is made fails to enter into an agreement with the City, award may be made to the next best qualified person or firm, who shall be bound to perform as if she, he or it received the award in the first instance.

## Right to Publish
Throughout the duration of this procurement process and agreement term, potential proposers, and proposers, must secure from the City written approval prior to the release of any information that pertains to the potential work or activities covered by this procurement or the subsequent agreement. Failure to adhere to this requirement may result in disqualification of the proposer or termination of the agreement.

## Ownership of Proposals
All documents submitted in response to the RFP shall be become the property of the City of Santa Monica and are subject to the provisions of the California Public Records Act, as described in Section II. A. 11. herein.

## Agreement Award
Proposal will be evaluated by a committee comprised of City staff and may include outside consultants (the “Evaluation Committee”). The Evaluation Committee will make an award recommendation to City staff. City Council may give approval of the agreement and/or direct staff to negotiate the final terms and execute the agreement.
This agreement shall be awarded to the proposer or proposers whose proposal is best qualified, taking into consideration the evaluation factors set forth in the RFP. The most qualified proposal may or may not have received the most points or be the lowest cost proposal. Proposers will be notified when the award is being made or an award recommendation goes to the City Council for approval.

## Protest Deadline
All parties wishing to file a protest shall comply with the procedures set forth in Santa Monica Municipal Code section 2.24.110 found 
here
. Proposer may file a written protest with the Purchasing Agent no more than seven calendar days following the posting of award recommendation on the City’s online vendor portal website.
Protests received after the deadline will not be accepted.

## Records and Audits
The Consultant shall maintain such detailed records as may be necessary to demonstrate its performance of the duties required by this Agreement, including the date, time and nature of services rendered. These records shall be maintained for a period of three years from the date of the final payment under this Agreement and shall be subject to inspection by City. The City shall have the right to audit any billings or examine any records maintained pursuant to this Agreement both before and after payment. Payment under this Agreement shall not foreclose the right of City to recover excessive and/or illegal payments.

## Enforcement of Agreement/Waiver
A party's failure to require strict performance of any provision of this Agreement shall not waive or diminish that party's right thereafter to demand strict compliance with that or any other provision. No waiver by a party of any of its rights under this Agreement shall be effective unless expressed in writing and signed by the party alleged to have granted the waiver. A waiver by a party of any of its rights shall not be effective to waive any other rights.

## Prevailing Wage, Apprentices, Penalties & Certified Payroll
In accordance with the provisions of Labor Code Section 1773.2, the Director of Industrial Relations has determined the general prevailing rates of wages and employer payments for health, welfare, vacation, pensions and similar purposes applicable, which is on file in the 
State of California Office of Industrial Relations
. The contractor shall post a copy of these prevailing wage rates at the site of the project. It shall be mandatory upon the contractor to whom the contract is awarded and its subcontractors hired to pay not less than the said prevailing rates of wages to all workers employed by him in the execution of the contract as required under Articles 2 and 3, Division 2, Part 7, Chapter 1 of the Labor Code, State of California, including, but not limited to, Sections 1771, 1774 and 1815.
It is the duty of the contractor and subcontractors to employ registered apprentices and to comply with all aspects of Labor Code Section 1777.5.
There are penalties required for contractor’s/subcontractor’s failure to pay prevailing wages and for failure to employ apprentices, including forfeitures and debarment under Labor Code Sections 1775, 1776, 1777.1, 1777.7 and 1813.
Under Labor Code Section 1776, contractors and subcontractors are required to keep accurate payroll records. The prime contractor is responsible for submittal of their payrolls and those of their subcontractors as one package. Payroll records shall be certified and made available for inspection at all reasonable hours at the principal office of the contractor/subcontractor pursuant to Labor Code Section 1776.
The contractor, and any work performed under this CSA, shall, at all times comply and be in accordance with, and subject to the provisions of Articles 2 and 3, Division 2, Part 7, Chapter 1 of the Labor Code, State of California.

## Evaluation criteria
- Experience / Technical Competence: 30
- Cost: 20
- Stability / References: 10
- Ability to Meet Work Plan / Timelines: 20
- Value Add / Breadth of Service: 20

Event Name: CODE ENFORCEMENT SERVICES
Description:
The City of Santa Monica is inviting proposals from qualified firms to provide professional Code Enforcement Services to support the City's Code Enforcement Division in enforcing the Santa Monica Municipal Code. The City of Santa Monica has a need to contract with a qualified firm to provide Code Enforcement Officers with experience for on-call code enforcement services to augment the Division's staff during periods of high workloads, subject to funding availability and proper delegation of authority by the City. The City is seeking assistance to ensure compliance with the Santa Monica Municipal Code as it relates to the following: Building and Safety, Property Maintenance, Nuisances, Regulatory, and Zoning.

Located in coastal Los Angeles County, the City of Santa Monica has a population of 93,000 residents and is known for its beaches, vibrant economy and scenic pier.
The Code Enforcement Division is budgeted for fourteen Code Enforcement Officers, two Code Enforcement Supervisors, one Senior Administrative Analyst, one Administrative Staff Assistant, two Code Enforcement Specialists, and one Neighborhood Preservation Coordinator. We are currently in the process of filling four positions.

The training, credentials and experience of the person or firm;

The ability of the person or firm to provide such future service as may be needed;
The price which the person or firm proposes to charge, including whether the price is fair, reasonable and competitive; and
Any other factor which will further the intent set forth in Section 608 of the City Charter.
The City shall have absolute discretion in determining the applicability and weight or relative weight of some or all of the criteria listed above and is not required to select the lowest monetary proposer.

## Acceptance of Conditions Governing this RFP
Submission of a proposal constitutes acceptance of the Evaluation Factors contained in this RFP.

## Incurring Cost
Any cost incurred by the proposer in preparation, transmittal, presentation of any proposal or material submitted in response to this RFP shall be borne solely by the proposer.

## Prime Consultant Responsibility
Any agreement that may result from the RFP shall specify that the prime consultant is solely responsible for fulfillment of the agreement with the City. The City will make agreement payments only to the prime consultant.

## Sub-consultants
Use of sub-consultants must be clearly explained in the proposal, and major sub-consultants must be identified by name. Prime consultants shall be wholly responsible for the entire performance whether or not sub-consultants are used.

## Amended Proposals
A proposer may submit an amended proposal before the deadline for receipt of proposals. Such amended proposals must be complete replacements for a previously submitted proposal and must be clearly identified as such in the transmittal letter. City personnel will not merge, collate, or assemble proposal materials.

## Proposer’s Rights to Withdraw Proposal
Proposers will be allowed to withdraw their proposals at any time prior to the deadline for receipt of proposals. The proposer must submit a written withdrawal request signed by the proposer’s duly authorized representative addressed to the City Contact.

## Proposal Offer Firm
Responses to this RFP, including proposal prices, will be considered firm for one hundred eighty (180) days after the due date for receipt of proposals or sixty (60) days after receipt of a best and final offer, if one is requested.

## Selection
The City of Santa Monica, through either the City Council or the City Manager (or his designee) has the sole authority to select the consulting firm and reserves the right to reject any and all proposals. The City reserves the right to approve or reject all sub-consultants and engineers proposed to be retained by the prime consultant. Upon signing of the agreement, no change in proposed personnel or sub-consultants can be made without the City’s review and written authorization.
By submitting a response to this RFP, prospective consultants waive the right to protest after award or seek any legal remedies whatsoever regarding any aspect of this RFP. The City reserves the right to select any number of finalists. In addition, the City reserves the right to issue written notice to all prospective consultants of any changes in the RFP terms or proposal submission schedule, should the City determine in its sole and absolute discretion that such changes are necessary.
The City reserves the right to request additional information from any proposing consultant and to reject any and all proposals. All original work products, including computer files, shall remain the property of the City.
The City reserves the right to retain an expert to evaluate the proposing consultant’s work or qualifications at all stages in the selection process. Additionally, any contract entered into will be subject to termination at any stage if in the judgment of the City, such termination is in the best interest of the City. In the event such decision is made, appropriate written notice would be given before any termination and the consultant would be compensated on a pro-rata basis for work performed.
The responsible proposer whose proposal is the most advantageous to the City, taking to consideration all the evaluation factors will be recommended for the contract award. Notwithstanding the Evaluation Team’s selection, the City reserves the right to award this RFP and the resultant Contract in any manner it deems to be in the best interest of the City and make the selection based on its sole discretion. The City is the sole and exclusive judge of quality and compliance with proposal specifications in any of the matters pertaining to this RFP.

## Best and Final Offer
The City reserves the right to request Best and Final Offers from any or all proposers. This will be the only opportunity to amend or modify proposals based on feedback from the City. Information from competing proposals will not be disclosed to other proposers prior to submission of a Best and Final Offer.

## Living Wage Requirement
Any agreement issued as a result of this Request for Proposal may be subject to the City’s Living Wage Ordinance, Santa Monica Municipal Code Chapter 4.65 (LWO), and its implementing regulations.

##   Disclosure of Proposal Contents
All proposals are subject to the provisions of the California Public Records Act, California Government Code section 6250 et seq., and any information submitted with a response is a public record subject to disclosure, unless a specific exemption applies.

## Notice Regarding Disclosure of Contents of Documents
All responses to this Request for Proposal (RFP) accepted by the City of Santa Monica (City) shall become the exclusive property of the City. All proposals accepted by the City shall become a matter of public record and shall be regarded as public, with the exception of those elements of each proposal which are defined by the contractor as business or trade secrets and plainly marked as "Trade Secret", "Confidential" or "Proprietary". Each element of a proposal which a contractor desires not to be considered a public record must be clearly marked as set forth above, and any blanket statement (i.e. regarding entire pages, documents or other non-specific designations) shall not be sufficient and shall not bind the City in any way whatsoever. If disclosure is required or permitted under the California Public Records Act, or otherwise by law, the City shall not in any way be liable or responsible for the disclosure of any such records or part thereof.

## No Obligation
This RFP in no manner obligates the City to the eventual rental, lease, purchase, etc., of any goods or services offered until a valid written agreement is executed by the City and the selected proposer.

## Termination
This RFP may be canceled at any time and any and all proposals may be rejected in whole or in part when the City determines such action to be in the best interest of the City of Santa Monica.

## Sufficient Appropriation
Any agreement awarded for multiple years as a result of this RFP may be terminated if sufficient appropriations or authorizations do not exist. Such termination will be effected by sending written notice to the selected proposer. The City’s decision as to whether sufficient appropriations and authorizations are available will be accepted by the selected proposer as final.

## Errors and Restrictive Specifications
If a proposer discovers any ambiguity, conflict, discrepancy, omission, or other error in the RFP, the proposer should immediately notify the City Contact designated in Section I, B. Without disclosing the source of the request, the City may issue a written addendum to clarify the ambiguity, or to correct the problem, omission, or other error.
If prior to the submission date, a proposer knows of or should have known of an error in the RFP but fails to notify the City Contact of the error, the proposer shall submit their proposal at his, her or its own risk, and, if awarded an agreement, shall not be entitled to additional compensation or time by reason of error or its later correction.

## Legal Review
The City requires that all proposers agree to be bound by the General Requirements contained in this RFP.

## Governing Law
This RFP, and any agreement entered into pursuant to this RFP, are governed by the laws of the State of California.

## Contract Award and Execution
Selection of a proposer with whom the City enters into contract negotiations with, or a recommendation of an award by the Evaluation Committee or any other party, does not constitute an award of Contract. Once the City formally awards the contract, the successful consultant will be notified to enter into an agreement. If the selected consultant does not enter into the agreement, the City will begin negotiations with the second highest ranking proposing consultant.
Please review all contract forms prior to submitting a proposal. The City of Santa Monica intends to use these forms as the baseline agreements with the successful consultant. The City will not entertain proposals to make material changes to the contract form once the project has been awarded. If you wish to request changes to the contracting forms, you must do so during the proposal process. In addition, the City requires compliance with several other policies and ordinances, proposing consultants will need to complete these Exhibits and submit with their Proposal.
The RFP document and the successful proposal response, as amended by agreement between the City of Santa Monica and the successful consultant, will become part of the contract documents. Additionally, the City of Santa Monica may verify the successful consultant’s representations that appear in the proposal. Failure of the successful consultant to perform as represented may result in elimination of the successful consultant from further negotiation or in contract cancellation or termination.
No oral explanation or instruction of any kind or nature whatsoever given before the award of a contract to a consultant shall be binding. The City of Santa Monica shall not be bound, or in any way obligated, until the City has awarded the contract and all documents have been executed. The proposing consultant may not incur any chargeable costs prior to final contract execution.

## Oral Changes and Basis for Proposal
Proposers may not rely upon oral explanations. All changes and addenda will be issued in writing. Only information supplied by the City in writing through the City’s Contact, or in this RFP should be used as the basis for the preparation of proposals.

## Agreement Terms and Conditions
The agreement between the City and the selected proposer(s) will follow the format specified by the City and contain the terms and conditions set forth in Attachment , Services Agreement. However, 
the City reserves the right to negotiate with a successful proposer the final provisions or provisions in addition to those contained in this RFP.
 The contents of this RFP, as revised and/or supplemented, and the successful proposal will be incorporated into and become part of the agreement.
Should a proposer object to any of the City’s terms and conditions, as contained in this Section or in Attachment , that proposer must propose specific alternative language in his, her, or its proposal. Proposer must provide a brief discussion of the purpose and impact, if any, of each proposed changed followed by the specific proposed alternate wording. The City may or may not accept the alternative language. General references to the proposer’s terms and conditions or attempts at complete substitutions are not acceptable to the City and may result in disqualification of the proposer.

## Proposer’s Terms and Conditions
Proposers must submit with the proposal a complete set of any additional terms and conditions that they expect to have included in an agreement negotiated with the City.

## Proposer Qualifications
The City may make such investigations as necessary to determine the ability of the proposer to adhere to the requirements specified within this RFP.

## Right to Waive Minor Irregularities
The City reserves the right to waive minor irregularities and the right to waive mandatory requirements, provided that all of the otherwise responsive proposals fail to meet the same mandatory requirements and/or doing so does not otherwise materially affect the procurement. This right is at the sole discretion of the City.

## Change in Agreement or Representatives
The City reserves the right to require a change in the selected proposer or representatives if the assigned representatives are not, in the opinion of the City, meeting its needs adequately.

## City Rights
The City reserves the right to award the proposal to separate proposers on any of the services as set forth in the proposer’s proposal. It is further understood that if the proposer to whom any recommended award is made fails to enter into an agreement with the City, award may be made to the next best qualified person or firm, who shall be bound to perform as if she, he or it received the award in the first instance.

## Right to Publish
Throughout the duration of this procurement process and agreement term, potential proposers, and proposers, must secure from the City written approval prior to the release of any information that pertains to the potential work or activities covered by this procurement or the subsequent agreement. Failure to adhere to this requirement may result in disqualification of the proposer or termination of the agreement.

## Ownership of Proposals
All documents submitted in response to the RFP shall be become the property of the City of Santa Monica and are subject to the provisions of the California Public Records Act, as described in Section II. A. 11. herein.

## Agreement Award
Proposal will be evaluated by a committee comprised of City staff and may include outside consultants (the “Evaluation Committee”). The Evaluation Committee will make an award recommendation to City staff. City Council may give approval of the agreement and/or direct staff to negotiate the final terms and execute the agreement.
This agreement shall be awarded to the proposer or proposers whose proposal is best qualified, taking into consideration the evaluation factors set forth in the RFP. The most qualified proposal may or may not have received the most points or be the lowest cost proposal. Proposers will be notified when the award is being made or an award recommendation goes to the City Council for approval.

## Protest Deadline
All parties wishing to file a protest shall comply with the procedures set forth in Santa Monica Municipal Code section 2.24.110 found 
here
. Proposer may file a written protest with the Purchasing Agent no more than seven calendar days following the posting of award recommendation on the City’s online vendor portal website.
Protests received after the deadline will not be accepted.

## Records and Audits
The Consultant shall maintain such detailed records as may be necessary to demonstrate its performance of the duties required by this Agreement, including the date, time and nature of services rendered. These records shall be maintained for a period of three years from the date of the final payment under this Agreement and shall be subject to inspection by City. The City shall have the right to audit any billings or examine any records maintained pursuant to this Agreement both before and after payment. Payment under this Agreement shall not foreclose the right of City to recover excessive and/or illegal payments.

## Enforcement of Agreement/Waiver
A party's failure to require strict performance of any provision of this Agreement shall not waive or diminish that party's right thereafter to demand strict compliance with that or any other provision. No waiver by a party of any of its rights under this Agreement shall be effective unless expressed in writing and signed by the party alleged to have granted the waiver. A waiver by a party of any of its rights shall not be effective to waive any other rights.

In accordance with the provisions of Labor Code Section 1773.2, the Director of Industrial Relations has determined the general prevailing rates of wages and employer payments for health, welfare, vacation, pensions and similar purposes applicable, which is on file in the 
State of California Office of Industrial Relations
. The contractor shall post a copy of these prevailing wage rates at the site of the project. It shall be mandatory upon the contractor to whom the contract is awarded and its subcontractors hired to pay not less than the said prevailing rates of wages to all workers employed by him in the execution of the contract as required under Articles 2 and 3, Division 2, Part 7, Chapter 1 of the Labor Code, State of California, including, but not limited to, Sections 1771, 1774 and 1815.
It is the duty of the contractor and subcontractors to employ registered apprentices and to comply with all aspects of Labor Code Section 1777.5.
There are penalties required for contractor’s/subcontractor’s failure to pay prevailing wages and for failure to employ apprentices, including forfeitures and debarment under Labor Code Sections 1775, 1776, 1777.1, 1777.7 and 1813.
Under Labor Code Section 1776, contractors and subcontractors are required to keep accurate payroll records. The prime contractor is responsible for submittal of their payrolls and those of their subcontractors as one package. Payroll records shall be certified and made available for inspection at all reasonable hours at the principal office of the contractor/subcontractor pursuant to Labor Code Section 1776.
The contractor, and any work performed under this CSA, shall, at all times comply and be in accordance with, and subject to the provisions of Articles 2 and 3, Division 2, Part 7, Chapter 1 of the Labor Code, State of California.

## Oaks Initiative
Santa Monica’s voters adopted a City Charter amendment commonly known as the Oaks Initiative. The Oaks Initiative requires the City to provide this notice and information about the Initiative’s requirements. You may obtain a full copy of the Initiative’s text from the City Clerk.
This information is required by City Charter Article XXII—Taxpayer Protection. It prohibits a public official from receiving, and a person or entity from conferring, specified personal benefits or campaign advantages from a person or entity after the official votes, or otherwise takes official action, to award a “public benefit” to that person or entity. The prohibition applies within and outside of the geographical boundaries of Santa Monica.
All persons or entities applying or receiving public benefits from the City of Santa Monica shall provide the names of trustees, directors, partners, and officers, and names of persons with more than a 10% equity, participation or revenue interest. An exception exists for persons serving in those capacities as volunteers, without compensation, for organizations exempt from income taxes under Section 501(c)(3), (4), or (6), of the Internal Revenue Code. However, this exception does not apply if the organization is a political committee or controls political committees. Examples of a “public benefit” include public contracts to provide goods or services worth more than $25,000 or a land use approval worth more than $25,000 over a 12-month period.
In order to facilitate compliance with the requirements of the Oaks Initiative, the City compiles and maintains certain information. That information includes the name of any person or persons who is seeking a “public benefit.” If the “public benefit” is sought by an entity, rather than an individual person, the information includes the name of every person who is: (a) trustee, (b) director, (c) partner, (d) officer, or has (e) more than a ten percent interest in the entity. Therefore, if you are seeking a “public benefit” covered by the Oaks Initiative, you must supply that information on the Oaks Initiative Disclosure Form. This information must be updated and supplied every 12 months.

## Specifications
The prop will support high‑volume hose‑stream training, fire engine pump testing, standpipe operations, and pressure‑reducing valve instruction. The system must be engineered for long‑term durability, mobility, and safe operation while meeting realistic fire‑ground training requirements.
2.1.1 Pump Recirculation Tank
The prop is designed to safely capture water from fire‑hose streams, store it within an integrated tank, and recirculate that water for continuous, repeatable training use. The system should be engineered for long‑term durability and dependable performance, offering easy operation and maintenance while withstanding the rigorous demands of repeated fire‑service training.
The completed prop should substantially reduce overall water consumption and limit excess water discharge from the training area.
Physical components and engineering expectations or capabilities the bidder must provide, build, fabricate, or deliver:
Portable hydrant for testing in remote locations.
- Wet barrell, have 4" and 2.5" outlets, yellow in color.
- 4" female connection at the base of the hydrant to connect a supply hose to.
- Mounted on a stable base wide and heavy enough so the hydrant does not tip over when it is pressurized.
Have mounting location for at least six (6) nozzles/hose lines that can mount nozzles to. These nozzles then direct their streams into the tank for realistic flows and water recapturing.
Contain functional FDC (fire department connection) and standpipe system.
- Minimum of three 2.5" inlets.
- Exterior FDC with piping leading into the tank so that pumped water is recaptured in the tank for reuse.
Can receive master streams from aerial devices into the roof of the unit at flows of at least 1000 GPM (gallons per minute)
- Roof must have an opening to receive a "dynamic flow" of at least 1000 GPM.
- Roof opening must be a minimum of 25 square feet.
- "Dynamic flow" refers to a hose stream that can be moved, typically used during ladder pipe training where water is sprayed from approximately 80 feet in the air and directed downward into the prop.
Can receive horizontal hose streams delivered from master stream devices that are not physically attached to the prop.
- Ensures realistic fire-ground training and allow firefighters to position and operate master stream devices at typical field distances.
- Must be able to handle dynamic, moving water streams directed from various angles. This capability supports effective water recapture, expanding training realism and improving water-saving outcomes compared to props with fixed nozzles.
Provide a sufficiently large target area to receive water streams delivered at ground level.
- Must be capable of capturing handline streams operated by personnel, including dynamic (moving) flows. This requirement ensures realistic training conditions, allowing firefighters to move and reposition handlines as they would during actual fire-ground operations.
- Captured water must be suitable for recirculation and reuse, supporting water-saving objectives.
Storage for 6" hard suction drafting hose.
Contain a storage box for miscellaneous equipment such as hose, nozzles and fittings.
Have water capacity between 2000 and 3000 gallons.
Must be made of steel construction, 10 gauge minimum, lined by a durable water protecting product.
Prop should be fixed to a trailer so that it can be towed to offsite locations for realistic training in the field while recapturing water and reduce the impact of flooding.
- Steel construction.
- 10 gauge minimum.
- Lined by a durable water protecting product.
- DOT (department of transportation) compliant trailer manufactured in the USA.
2.1.2 Standpipe Training Prop
Physical components and engineering expectations or capabilities the bidder must provide, build, fabricate, or deliver:
Standpipe and manifold
- All hose and valve threads shall be National Standard Thread (NST) unless otherwise specified.
- 4" galvanized Schedule‑40 manifold.
- Clappered 2.5" Siamese Fire Department Connection (NST).
- Six (6) 2.5" Class I standpipe valves (Male NST).
- One (1) additional 2.5" capped outlet for optional seventh hose valve.
Pressure-Reducing and Pressure Restricting Valves (PRV)
- Three (3) types of pressure‑reducing valves, representing the common valve types found in buildings:
   1. Firefighter-adjustable PRV
   2. Field-adjustable PRV
   3. Factory-set, non-adjustable PRV
- Pressure‑restricting devices that help reduce outlet pressure so hose lines can be operated safely during training.
- Compatibility with Zurn ZW4000‑series PRVs or equivalent products.
- If the Fire Department supplies any PRVs, the vendor shall install the necessary adapter (for example, converting National Pipe Thread to grooved pipe) at no additional charge. Vendor warranties do not apply to customer‑supplied components.
Globe Valves
- Three (3) standard globe valves, consisting of:
   1. One (1) standard globe valve with an installed pressure‑restricting device
   2. Two (2) standard globe valves with no pressure‑restricting device
Physical Frame, Mounting, and Mobility Requirements
- Prop must be mounted on a sturdy base and designed to prevent water damage.
- Mobile configuration using heavy‑duty casters to allow the prop to be easily moved around the training site.
- Powder-coated steel frame construction for durability.
- Manifold, elbows, and frame shall be powder-coated red.
- Heavy-duty locking swivel casters and fixed casters, where appropriate.
- Integrated expanded‑steel shelving to store hose, valves, tools, and training appliances.
- Approximate accessory weight of up to 350 lbs, depending on configuration.
Durability and Finish
- All structural components shall be designed for long‑term, repeated fire‑training use.
- Powder‑coated components to improve corrosion resistance and visibility.

Event Name: 24x7 Service Desk
Description:
The City of Santa Monica (the City) is seeking qualified firms to provide 24x7 Service Desk services.

City of Santa Monica Overview: 
The City’s network connects 44 city facilities, 5 hub sites, a primary datacenter, and two supporting datacenters located within an 8.3 square mile area in Santa Monica, CA. All of these sites are connected via city-owned fiber network. The City also leverages several cloud-hosted applications and services including Microsoft 365 Office productivity apps. The City uses Cisco equipment as its standard for core, access layer, edge switching, and routing devices.  Most of city’s on-premises hosted applications run on Windows and SQL database systems.
The City also operates and supports the CityNet network and Community Broadband program. The CityNet network supports external customers, connecting over 140 locations in the City of Santa Monica, including City facilities, commercial sites, and residential buildings. A number of enterprise business customers, hospitals, and university customers are provided with dark fiber and lit services.
The Service Desk environment supports a diverse technology landscape, including Microsoft, Cisco, and multi-cloud platforms. Service request and incident intake is currently conducted through the ServiceNow portal and telephone, with a desire to expand intake and communication channels to include email, instant messaging, chatbots, and other emerging technologies.
The City’s highest-priority incidents include outages impacting 9-1-1 Emergency Dispatch, Public Safety/Security, Santa Monica Department of Transportation (SMDoT), and Water Utility (SCADA) systems where time-sensitive intervention is required. In addition, there are a list of “VIP” departments which includes the City Manager’s Office, City Attorney’s Office and City Council that require Priority 1 support and escalation. All other incidents and service requests are prioritized automatically within the Service Management system based on City-defined impact and urgency criteria.

Event Name: Santa Monica Groundwater Basin Monitoring Program
Description:
The City of Santa Monica, (the "City”) is soliciting proposals from qualified consultants or firms to implement a groundwater monitoring, modeling, and technical support program for the Santa Monica Groundwater Basin (SMGB).

The Santa Monica Groundwater Monitoring Program (Program) aims to unite all State-mandated groundwater monitoring requirements under one contract to manage the basin sustainably and in full regulatory compliance. Specific State orders for the Charnock and the Olympic Well Fields will be implemented in full compliance with orders/permits. In addition to remediation activities to restore the groundwater basin water quality, the City is also currently operating under the Division of Drinking Water’s 97-005 Policy Memo requirements to produce drinking water from the Charnock and Olympic Well Fields. The selected consultant will also work with current City engineering consultants to meet regulatory reporting requirements for the Santa Monica Subbasin Groundwater Sustainability Plan (GSP) and the City’s groundwater recharge permit for its Sustainable Water Infrastructure Project (SWIP). 
The City of Santa Monica is the only municipal agency that currently produces groundwater from the SMGB. The City has been producing groundwater from the basin since the 1920’s and has been actively managing groundwater since the 1950’s. The City owns and operates three groundwater production well fields in the SMGB: Arcadia, Charnock, and Olympic well fields. The Santa Monica Groundwater Monitoring Program (Program) includes the following regulatory efforts:
Coordination with the State Water Resources Control Board (SWRCB), the Division of Drinking Water (DDW), the Los Angeles Regional Water Quality Control Board (LARWQCB), and other stakeholders to remove industrial pollutants that have contaminated the groundwater of the basin.
Coordination with the Department of Water Resources (DWR) and the Santa Monica Basin Groundwater Sustainability Agency (SMBGSA) to support implementation of the Santa Monica Basin Groundwater Sustainability Plan (GSP).  The SMBGSA members include the City of Santa Monica, City of Los Angeles (via Los Angeles Department of Water and Power), Los Angeles County (via Planning Department), Culver City, and Beverly Hills.
Support regulatory compliance efforts for monitoring and reporting related to groundwater recharge operations for the City’s Sustainable Water Infrastructure Project (SWIP), an advanced water treatment facility that treats a blend of wastewater and stormwater/urban runoff for non-potable reuse and indirect potable (i.e., groundwater recharge via direct injection).
Multiple State regulatory agencies require groundwater monitoring in accordance with approved compliance schedules, including field sampling, laboratory analysis, and interpretation of groundwater quality and hydrogeologic data, as well as preparation and submittal of regulatory reports. These requirements exhibit substantial overlap in monitoring locations, analytical parameters, frequency, and reporting deliverables. To increase efficiency, ensure data consistency, and maintain regulatory compliance, the City proposes to implement an integrated groundwater monitoring program encompassing standardized sampling protocols, data validation and quality assurance/quality control (QA/QC), hydrogeologic and geochemical evaluation, numerical modeling, and consolidated reporting.

## Scope of Work 
The selected consultant shall be responsible for the full implementation of the Program, including, but not limited to, the following tasks:
Task 1 – Program Management
Review and ensure City compliance with all regulatory rules, regulations, and requirements related to the Program.
Conduct monthly virtual progress meetings with the City’s designated Project Manager to review progress and budget.
Conduct quarterly project status meetings with City Staff to provide updates and review of recent water quality data.
The consultant must schedule the meetings and prepare a draft agenda one week prior for City review.  The consultant shall prepare meeting minutes from the meeting and submit it to the City within one week after the meeting.
Please budget for two in-person meetings and two virtual meetings per year for the quarterly project status meetings.
Maintain communication with the City regarding monitoring program schedules, site access, and regulatory coordination.
Coordinate monitoring activities to ensure consistency with LARWQCB and DDW regulatory standards.
Task 2 - Charnock Well Field Early Warning Groundwater Quality Monitoring
The Charnock Well Field is the City’s largest drinking water aquifer. The City has received a No Further Action letter from the LARWQCB for the Charnock Subbasin in November 2023 and is currently working on destroying regional groundwater monitoring wells to comply with the conditions outlined in the No Further Action approval from the LARWQCB. The lead agency for contaminant monitoring and permitting for the Charnock Well Field is currently the DDW that provide regulatory oversight of the City’s Drinking Water Permit, under the guidance of the 97-005 Policy Memo, for the Charnock Treatment Plant and Arcadia Water Treatment Plant. At a minimum, the consultant shall be responsible for:
Fulfilling all DDW requirements set forth in their approved Early Warning Monitoring Program
 (Attachment D – August 2024 memo to DDW and Table 5 Summary Sheet)
.  
Monitoring groundwater elevation and collecting groundwater samples from twelve (12) wells at frequencies set by DDW.

The City has entered into Settlement and Release Agreements (SRAs) with two companies that formerly conducted business in the Olympic Well Field area.  Pursuant to a modified Clean-up and Abatement Order (CAO) issued to the City, the City has agreed to perform certain activities to demonstrate that the dissolved-phase VOCs in the B- and C- water-bearing zones are captured by the pumping of nearby City groundwater production wells.

Task 4.0 - GSP Groundwater Elevation Monitoring
The SMBGSA was formed in 2017 to manage the SMBG under California State Sustainable Groundwater Management Act (SGMA) regulations. The SMBGSA is comprised of five member agencies: Cities of Santa Monica, Los Angeles (via the LADWP), Culver City, Beverly Hills and Los Angeles County (via Planning Department). The GSA conducts quarterly Board Meetings open to the public. DWR approved the GSA’s Groundwater Sustainability Plan (GSP) in January 2022.  Annual reports are due every April and a 5-year GSP Update is due in January 2027. The GSA has a consulting firm on contract for GSP-related professional services.  SGMA defines sustainable groundwater management as the management and use of groundwater in a manner that can be maintained over a 50-year planning and implementation horizon without causing undesirable results. Groundwater levels obtained during the monitoring programs of the Charnock and Olympic Well Fields must be provided by the Consultant to the GSA Consulting firm so that they can be reported to DWR through the SGMA portal.
