## Term
The City is inviting proposals from qualified persons or firms for a firm-fixed contract for a term of 
five (5) years
.

## Scope of Work
The Consultant will work collaboratively with the City's Office of Sustainability and the Environment to develop, implement, and evaluate community-facing programs that increase awareness and adoption of sustainable practices among residents, businesses, community organizations, and other stakeholders.
The Consultant will be expected to build upon existing City programs while identifying and implementing innovative approaches to community engagement. The City welcomes proposals that incorporate new engagement strategies, partnerships, technologies, communication methods, behavioral approaches, and program models that may further advance the City's sustainability goals.
1. Community Engagement & Outreach
Consultant shall develop, coordinate, and implement free community sustainability engagement events in Santa Monica to promote the goals of Attachment D - Sustainable City Plan. This may include, but is not limited to:
Film screenings,
Resource fairs or expos,
Other innovative community engagement events
The Consultant shall coordinate the City’s annual Student Sustainability Poster Contest, which engages K-12 students in creative expression and learning related to sustainability topics. Responsibilities shall include:
Collaborating with City staff to develop a contest theme,
Conducting outreach,
Tracking submissions,
Coordinating judging,
Planning an awards ceremony for students
2. Green Business Program & Business Engagement
Recruit and engage businesses to participate in the City’s Green Business Certification Program, including providing guidance/technical assistance to fulfill the state-level California Green Business Network certification process.
Develop and implement the annual Sustainable Quality Awards in conjunction with the Office of Sustainability and the Environment. Consultant will support recruitment, nomination, applications, judging, outreach and promotion, event coordination, serve as event emcee (as needed), and develop post-event summary.
Participate in the development and implementation of the annual Most Loved Santa Monica Businesses Contest.
Utilize social media to raise awareness of the importance of buying local and to spotlight local businesses and best practices in sustainability (e.g. green business program achievements, Sustainable Quality Award Winners, Most Loved Santa Monica Winners).
Develop and maintain a monthly Buy Local SM e-newsletter to spotlight local businesses and showcase sustainable business practices, events and resources.
3. Communications, Data, & Program Support
Consultant will serve as a key point of contact for community sustainability and green business programs and will represent the Office of Sustainability and the Environment. Consultant will be expected to:
Develop and maintain Santa Monica-specific outreach materials.
Maintain a public webpage, email, phone line, and social media account.
Collaborate with local, regional, state and national organizations to provide resources to green businesses and Santa Monica residents.
Collect and maintain participation and engagement data for applicable programs. For green businesses, collect data regarding resource-use reductions, behavioral changes, and other measurable outcomes where feasible.
Provide presentations, briefings, or other technical assistance to City staff, community groups, businesses, or stakeholders. This includes periodic report-outs on outcomes to the Commission on Sustainability, Environmental Justice and the Environment as requested by the City.
Support special projects identified by the Office of Sustainability and the Environment that are consistent with the general scope of services, such as policy advancement or presence at city-sponsored events.
Specific City and Consultant responsibilities, including responsibility for venues, City staff participation, City communication channels, event costs, permits, materials, and other resources, shall be identified in the final agreement.

The price which the person or firm proposes to charge, including whether the price is fair, reasonable and competitive; and
Any other factor which will further the intent set forth in Section 608 of the City Charter.

## Oaks Initiative
Santa Monica’s voters adopted a City Charter amendment commonly known as the Oaks Initiative. The Oaks Initiative requires the City to provide this notice and information about the Initiative’s requirements. You may obtain a full copy of the Initiative’s text from the City Clerk.
This information is required by City Charter Article XXII—Taxpayer Protection. It prohibits a public official from receiving, and a person or entity from conferring, specified personal benefits or campaign advantages from a person or entity after the official votes, or otherwise takes official action, to award a “public benefit” to that person or entity. The prohibition applies within and outside of the geographical boundaries of Santa Monica.
All persons or entities applying or receiving public benefits from the City of Santa Monica shall provide the names of trustees, directors, partners, and officers, and names of persons with more than a 10% equity, participation or revenue interest. An exception exists for persons serving in those capacities as volunteers, without compensation, for organizations exempt from income taxes under Section 501(c)(3), (4), or (6), of the Internal Revenue Code. However, this exception does not apply if the organization is a political committee or controls political committees. Examples of a “public benefit” include public contracts to provide goods or services worth more than $25,000 or a land use approval worth more than $25,000 over a 12-month period.
In order to facilitate compliance with the requirements of the Oaks Initiative, the City compiles and maintains certain information. That information includes the name of any person or persons who is seeking a “public benefit.” If the “public benefit” is sought by an entity, rather than an individual person, the information includes the name of every person who is: (a) trustee, (b) director, (c) partner, (d) officer, or has (e) more than a ten percent interest in the entity. Therefore, if you are seeking a “public benefit” covered by the Oaks Initiative, you must supply that information on the Oaks Initiative Disclosure Form. This information must be updated and supplied every 12 months.

## Scope of Work
The City of Santa Monica (City) Water Resources Division is seeking laboratory services for the analysis of water, wastewater, storm water, and recycled water samples. 
Sample sources include:
Water
Treated Drinking Water
Raw Groundwater
Brackish Groundwater
Seawater
Wastewater
Raw Wasteawater
Pretreatment Device Effluent (e.g. Grease Interceptors, Clarifiers, Etc.)
Wastewater Treatment Plant Process Flow
Storm Water
Wet Weather Urban Runoff
Dry Weather Urban Runoff
Stormwater
Recycled Water
Advanced Treated Recycled Water
Treated Urban Runoff
The contracted vendor(s) shall provide laboratory services that comply with regulatory requirements for the handling and analysis of drinking water, wastewater, storm water, and Title 22 advanced treated recycled water. Services shall include sample testing/reporting that comply with Title 22 Recycled Water regulations, Unregulated Contaminant Monitoring Rule, and other testing as required by federal and state regulations and guidelines. Analysis shall also include Level 2 Quality Control (lab spikes, matrix spikes, blanks, surrogates) in compliance with U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Standard Methods, or other industry standard/accepted methods approved by the City. Specific requirements for laboratory results are provided in #4 of this Scope of Services.
Sample Kit Delivery and Pickup
The Lab Contractor shall provide sample kit delivery and pickup. Sampling kits shall include:
Coolers
Pre-labeled containers with site names
Pre-filled chain of custody forms with site names/tests
Gel packs
Packing slips
Sample kit delivery and pickup locations include: 
Water Resources Division
2500 Michigan Avenue, Bldg 1
Santa Monica, CA 90404
Arcadia Water Treatment Plant
1228 S. Bundy Drive
Los Angeles, CA 90025
Sustainable Water Infrastructure Project (SWIP)
1771 Main Street
Santa Monica, CA 90401
Santa Monica Urban Runoff Recycling Facility (SMURRF)
1623 Appian Way
Santa Monica, CA 9040
 
Upon pickup, the contracted vendor(s) shall comply with federal and state regulations related to sample handling, including but not limited to temperature, hold time, and chain-of-custody requirements. It is anticipated that deliveries and pickups will occur weekly, however, the City shall have the option to schedule additional deliveries and pickups with a minimum of three (3) days advance notice.
Reporting Requirements
Lab analysis reports shall include the following:
Electronic reports (via .pdf)
 Electronic data deliverables in .csv
Web access and online data management hosted by Lab Contractor. Web access shall be granted to City’s Project Manager and Water Resources Division (water.resources@santamonica.gov)
For low level analyte concentrations, such as 1,2,3-TCP, the Lab Contractor shall provide any J value above the Lab’s method detection limit (MDL) if below the reporting limit.
Test results shall be transmitted to the Project Manager identified on the chain-of-custody via email (specific email address to be determined based on sampling site) and to the City’s Water Resources Division via email (water.resources@santamoncia.gov) within 15 working days with the exception of analysis that require long hold times (e.g. pharmaceuticals and per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances [PFAS]).
Samples from Arcadia and SWIP
Test results shall be transmitted as required to the EPA’s Central Data Exchange (CDX) and/or State of California Division of Drinking Water Electronic Data Transfer (EDT) database. Results for samples submitted during last week of the month shall be uploaded to the required State database by the 10th of the following month with the exception of analysis that require long hold times (e.g. pharmaceuticals and PFAS). Test equivalents may be acceptable if reporting levels for the proposed test are the same or lower than the reporting levels required by the State Water Resources Control Board Division of Drinking Water.
Training
If requested by the City, the contract laboratory shall also provide the following:
Field sampler training (contact hours credit)
Regulatory training (contact hours credit)
Permit Documentation Support
If requested by the City, the contracted vendor(s) shall provide documentation supporting City permit requirements like Quality Assurance Project Plans, including, but not limited to, Quality Assurance / Quality Control plans, standard operating procedures, and operations manuals. Documents provided to the City may be redacted to preserve proprietary information.

Santa Cruz is part of the National Marine Sanctuary and is a popular tourist destination owing to its beaches, surf culture, and historical landmarks.
The City provides a full range of municipal services and facilities including a recreational wharf, public golf course, over thirteen hundred acres of open space, full beach services, refuse management, law enforcement, fire protection, and water and wastewater utilities. The County of Santa Cruz invites sealed proposals from fully licensed, insured, bonded, and certified vendors to furnish all labor, tools, equipment, and incidentals required to provide 
First Tier Conflict Indigent Defense Services
.
Established in 1850 as one of the state’s original 27 counties, the County of Santa Cruz was originally called Branciforte.  The name was later changed to Santa Cruz, which is “holy cross” in Spanish.  The County of Santa Cruz geographically is the second smallest county within the State of California yet it has one of the largest unincorporated area populations.  The 2020 estimated population for the County of Santa Cruz by the U.S. Census Bureau was 270,861.  The County encompasses an urban service area of 440 square miles.

1.1.  Introduction
The County seeks to procure indigent defense services for cases in which the Office of the Public Defender (PDO) is prevented from providing representation due to ethical conflicts or conflicts of interest (first-tier conflicts). The County seeks proposals that are independent, effective, transparent and fiscally responsible; and consistent with both Constitutional mandates as well as nationally recognized and California-specific standards for indigent defense. First-tier conflict indigent defense services are currently delivered by a contracted conflicts firm, and the contract will expire on June 30, 2027. The provider is anticipated to begin accepting cases on July 1, 2027. There is the potential of some administrative work beginning March 2027, for any cases that may need to be transferred from the current vendor to a new vendor.
Conflicts will be determined and appropriately resolved in accordance with California Rules of Professional Conduct, as interpreted by the California Bar Association and /or opinions of the state judiciary, and according to the American Bar Association Standards for Criminal Justice, as linked under “Philosophy and Program Goal.”
1.2.  The Existing Model
The existing contract for first-tier conflict legal services will expire on June 30, 2027. Pursuant to the County’s Purchasing Policy, a formal solicitation for a new agreement is being issued to ensure transparency, fiscal responsibility, and optimal service delivery.
The current model described above represents approximately 850 cases per year that the Public Defender’s Office (PDO) cannot represent due to a conflict of interest.
1.3.  Anticipated Caseloads based on 4-Year Averages
Based on historical caseloads from the last four years, the average annual caseload for first-tier conflicts is estimated at 800 - 850 cases per year. The following breakdown is for planning purposes only, and not a guaranteed volume of assignments.

1.4.  Philosophy and Program Goal
The County intends to provide representation that is independent, client-centered, and effective – as required by the Constitution. Effective defense – especially for clients experiencing mental and behavioral health symptoms - requires an interdisciplinary approach to pursue deflection and diversion, present social histories and other mitigation to advocate for fair outcomes and allow clients to participate in their defense as constitutionally required. An ideal provider will be able to provide this community-based, whole-person representation that addresses legal and related social needs, with the goal of improving client outcomes, reducing unnecessary system involvement, and promoting community safety.
The successful public defense provider will have clearly established policies, procedures, and experience with addressing barriers to facilitating access to necessary client services.
Respondent must provide clear examples of how they practice good stewardship and fiscal responsibility by leveraging available revenue, actively seeking additional funding opportunities, and providing transparent documentation.
Services must be delivered in alignment with the following relevant standards and best practices:
California Rules of Professional Conduct
 
California Standards for Contract & Panel Systems
State Bar of California: Guidelines on Indigent Defense Services Delivery Systems
American Bar Association Ten Principles of a Public Defense Delivery System
Working knowledge of the 
National Public Defense Workload Study
, case weighting and the 
National Association of Public Defense
 (NAPD) benchmarks for interdisciplinary defense teams.
Public defense provider shall ensure representation remains independent and free from improper judicial, political, or administrative influence consistent with professional obligations. To that end, the proposal should include a budget for any costs incurred in the course of performing services under this contract. Respondents must include itemized costs for contracted experts, social workers or similarly appropriately qualified staff, or investigators. The public defense provider will only be paid for services at set negotiated rates, as provided, and appropriately itemized per the County’s requirements.
Public defense provider will attend stakeholder meetings regularly – including but not limited to Criminal Justice Partner meetings, Incompetent to Stand Trial (IST) workgroup, Release to Program Workgroup, and other groups at the request of the County - as the conflict representative to enact changes in practice in response to new rulings and any other changes or trainings.

1.4.  Philosophy and Program Goal
The County intends to provide representation that is independent, client-centered, and effective – as required by the Constitution. Effective defense – especially for clients experiencing mental and behavioral health symptoms - requires an interdisciplinary approach to pursue deflection and diversion, present social histories and other mitigation to advocate for fair outcomes and allow clients to participate in their defense as constitutionally required. An ideal provider will be able to provide this community-based, whole-person representation that addresses legal and related social needs, with the goal of improving client outcomes, reducing unnecessary system involvement, and promoting community safety.
The successful public defense provider will have clearly established policies, procedures, and experience with addressing barriers to facilitating access to necessary client services.
Respondent must provide clear examples of how they practice good stewardship and fiscal responsibility by leveraging available revenue, actively seeking additional funding opportunities, and providing transparent documentation.
Services must be delivered in alignment with the following relevant standards and best practices:
California Rules of Professional Conduct
 
California Standards for Contract & Panel Systems
State Bar of California: Guidelines on Indigent Defense Services Delivery Systems
American Bar Association Ten Principles of a Public Defense Delivery System
Working knowledge of the 
National Public Defense Workload Study
, case weighting and the 
National Association of Public Defense
 (NAPD) benchmarks for interdisciplinary defense teams.
Public defense provider shall ensure representation remains independent and free from improper judicial, political, or administrative influence consistent with professional obligations. To that end, the proposal should include a budget for any costs incurred in the course of performing services under this contract. Respondents must include itemized costs for contracted experts, social workers or similarly appropriately qualified staff, or investigators. The public defense provider will only be paid for services at set negotiated rates, as provided, and appropriately itemized per the County’s requirements.
Public defense provider will attend stakeholder meetings regularly – including but not limited to Criminal Justice Partner meetings, Incompetent to Stand Trial (IST) workgroup, Release to Program Workgroup, and other groups at the request of the County - as the conflict representative to enact changes in practice in response to new rulings and any other changes or trainings.

It is recognized that it is not necessary that all secondary factors support creation of an independent contractor relationship, but rather that overall there are significant secondary factors that indicate that Contractor is an independent contractor.
Principal Test
:
Contractor rather than County has the right to control the manner and means of accomplishing the result contracted for.
Secondary Factors
:
(1) The extent of control which, by agreement, County may exercise over the details of the work is slight rather than substantial; (2) Contractor is engaged in a distinct occupation or business; (3) In the locality, the work to be done by Contractor is usually done by a specialist without supervision, rather than under the direction of an employer; (4) The skill required in the particular occupation is substantial rather than slight; (5) Contractor rather than the County supplies the instrumentalities, tools and work place; (6) The length of time for which Contractor is engaged is of limited duration rather than indefinite; (7) The method of payment of Contractor is by the job rather than by the time; (8) The work is part of a special or permissive activity, program, or project, rather than part of the regular business of County; (9) Contractor and County believe they are creating an independent contractor relationship not an employer-employee relationship; and (10) County conducts public business.

## Vendor Expectation of Services
Vendor will identify individuals who are living with or have a risk for Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) and provide linkage and navigation to care with the goal of achieving HCV cure.  The County of Santa Cruz (below referred to as County) expects the following services to be provided by the vendor:
Vendor is expected to implement a Hepatitis C virus (HCV) linkage and navigation workflow including client screening, follow-up with lab-based confirmatory HCV testing, medical visit(s), HCV treatment initiation, prescription pick-up and medication adherence to support treatment completion. 
Conduct HCV screenings for priority populations during Fiscal Year (FY) 2026-2027 in accordance with the recommendations for testing, managing and treating Hepatitis C from the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases and the Infectious Diseases Society of American (AASLD) HCV Guidance (2025).  Priority populations include people who use/inject drugs, people experiencing homelessness, Black, indigenous and other people of color, people with HIV, people who become pregnant, and trans/non-binary persons.
Link clients with a positive HCV screen to their assigned medical home for lab-based confirmatory HCV testing. Clients without an assigned medical home will receive medical benefits navigation and support to apply for medical insurance and/or identify a medical clinic and schedule an initial appointment to receive HCV care. Vendor will provide nutritional supplements for clients receiving HCV treatment to take with medications when necessary and appropriate.
Complete data collection per the HCV Care Continuum Report to assess outcomes for those engaging in HCV linkage and navigation services. Vendor's staff will complete an HCV assessment and will prioritize collecting a signed release of information (ROI) form as part of the assessment process.  If client signs an ROI form, Vendor's staff will share relevant HCV care information with client’s assigned clinic and lab personnel, medical providers and the County's Public Health HCV program staff to ensure successful linkage to care and care coordination.  If client declines to sign an ROI, vendor will assist clients in managing their HCV treatment and not share information with the County. 
Distribute client incentives according to the County's Behavior Modification Plan (BMP).  This includes completing the Client Incentive Receipt Form documenting distribution of the appropriate incentive as client advances through the HCV care cascade (rapid testing, confirmatory lab-based HCV testing, PCP visit/treatment initiation, and clearing of HCV virus).
Provide care coordination with the County's Public Health  HCV program while client is engaged in the vendor's program. Vendor will share exited client’s contact information with the County's Public Health HCV program and/or communicate to the client’s HCV treating provider.  In the absence of an ROI, Vendor's staff will document client’s care notes accordingly in compliance with the vendor's policy.     
Identify and advocate to address barriers to HCV treatment that clients report to achieve the best possible HCV linkage and navigation outcomes for the individual.
Meet monthly with the Senior Health Educator from County HCV program to discuss testing, linkage and navigation successes and challenges.

Details.Pre-Bid Meeting: 09/22/2026 09:00AM PDT | 461 Soquel San Jose Road, Soquel, CA 95073 | Mandatory

Description:
The project involves preparing a site for installation of a new water service line, abandoning an existing water service line in place, installation of new water service line, connection of the new water service line to existing park water system, and post-installation site work. This project is located at 461 Soquel San Jose Road, Soquel, CA 95073. The engineer's estimate for this project is $277,000. There are 75 working days in this contract.

The park’s existing main water line was installed beneath the entrance drive and has experienced recurring leaks at locations corresponding with the individual pipe sections. Repairs require Parks maintenance staff to excavate to a considerable depth within or adjacent to the entrance drive, resulting in disruptive and labor-intensive maintenance work.
To address these recurring leaks, Parks staff evaluated abandoning the existing water line in place and relocating the replacement line into the landscaped area adjacent to the entrance drive. Parks maintenance staff reviewed the proposed alignment and determined that the design is operationally feasible and will improve access for future maintenance.
Bowman & Williams prepared the plans and specifications for the project. The proposed work includes installation of approximately 925 linear feet of new water line, abandonment of the existing water line, connections to the existing park water system and utility infrastructure, installation of valves and related appurtenances, limited removal and replacement of concrete paving, testing and disinfection, erosion control, and restoration of disturbed areas. No tree removal is anticipated.

Information Technology Department

SBCUSD encompasses 105 square miles in the center of San Bernardino County, consisting of small schools in rural mountain and foothill communities and larger suburban schools in valley flatland areas. INFRASTRUCTURE EQUIPMENT, CABLING AND SERVICES
 SPECIFICATIONS AND SUPPLEMENTAL INFORMATION
 
San Bernardino City Unified School District (the District) is seeking proposals from qualified bidders to provide infrastructure cabling, equipment, materials, set-up, and services (public works) on an as needed basis at multiple school sites. 
The District reserves the right to extend the Bid on a year to year basis, not to exceed five (5) years (including the first year) at the discretion of the District, if it is in the best interest of the District. Bidders are to fill out all Bid forms and required documents including all Bid pricing sheets. Prices given on the Bid Price Sheets will be used to build proposals for any work and services throughout the term of the award. Prices given by Bidder on the Bid Price Sheets for equipment, materials and labor for any given “type of site work” may be used in conjunction or in any combination to build a scope for work after award at the same unit price provided in the awarded Bidder’s proposal. 
Introduction 
The District has standardized on particular products. In accordance with California Public Contract Code Section 3400, whenever in the Specifications any equipment, material, process or article is indicated or specified by grade, patent proprietary name or by name of manufacture, such specification shall be deemed to be used for the purpose of facilitating description of equipment, material, process or article desired and shall be deemed to be followed by the words “or equal”. The Bidder may offer any equipment, material, process or article which shall be substantially equal or better in every respect to that indicated. 
The District’s project encompasses the following main areas
: 
The Scope of Work applies to all of the District’s approximately 74 schools and 10 administrative non-instructional facilities (NIF).
Installation of cabling and pathways to support wired and wireless data network systems for classrooms, offices, gymnasiums, libraries, multipurpose rooms, outdoor spaces, high-density wireless environments, and other educational facilities throughout the District, including infrastructure supporting Wi‑Fi 6E, Wi‑Fi 7, multigigabit connectivity, and future standards‑based wireless technologies.
New installation of the MDF (Main Distribution Frame) to IDF (Intermediate Distribution Frame) and IDF to LDF (Local Distribution Frame) backbone cabling using laser-optimized OM4 multi-mode fiber optic cabling, or single mode fiber optic cabling (due to distance).
Installation, removal, and relocation of MDF and IDF cabinets in some instances.
Installation, repair, and relocation of wired connectivity drops at most sites.
Installation, repair, and rewiring of electrical circuits, electrical wiring, outlets, breakers, panels, UPS systems, and other electrical equipment in some instances.
Redressing of patch cording and repositioning of equipment in some existing cabinets.
Replacing cabinet locks to meet district key standards.
Re-securing existing cabinets to the current wall.
Installing of new pathways as well as enhancement of existing pathways, and in numerous cases the upgrading of existing pathways to meet codes and standards requirements, including outside plant trenching and concrete wall coring at some sites, and repair of existing penetration sleeves.
Installation, removal, relocation, and physical infrastructure support of District‑provided network equipment, wireless access point infrastructure, antenna infrastructure, cabinets, racks, patch panels, and related passive communications systems.
Connectivity upgrade of existing Network Equipment.
 
E-RATE ELIGIBILITY, COORDINATION, AND SERVICE DELINEATION 
The primary purpose of this contract is to provide the District with infrastructure cabling, pathway systems, emergency response services, physical layer support, infrastructure modernization, and related operational technology services for work that is not E-Rate eligible or not being funded through the E-Rate program.
The District maintains separate contracts and procurement processes for E-Rate eligible infrastructure services and telecommunications work.
The District reserves the sole and exclusive right to determine:
Whether the requested work is E-Rate eligible
Whether work shall be performed under this contract or another District contract
Whether work qualifies as emergency work
Which funding source shall be utilized for any requested service or project
Work determined by the District to be E-Rate eligible will generally be assigned to the District’s separately awarded E-Rate vendor or other District procurement vehicle.
However, the District reserves the right to authorize work under this contract when:
The work is determined by the District to be operationally necessary
Emergency restoration or rapid response services are required
Project conditions require coordination between multiple vendors
Portions of the work are non-E-Rate eligible
District operational continuity would otherwise be adversely impacted
In circumstances where requested work includes both E-Rate eligible and non-E-Rate eligible components, or where project scope boundaries overlap, the awarded contractor under this contract shall:
Coordinate and collaborate with the District and the District’s E-Rate vendor as directed
Cooperate in project scheduling and implementation activities
Provide separate quotations, invoices, and supporting documentation as requested
Assist the District in maintaining proper segregation of eligible and non-eligible work
Nothing in this contract shall prohibit the District from assigning portions of a project to multiple vendors when the District deems necessary.
Emergency infrastructure restoration work may be authorized under this contract at the District’s discretion, including work that may otherwise contain E-Rate eligible components, when necessary to restore operational continuity, protect District property, maintain instructional operations, or address immediate health and safety concerns.
The District’s determination regarding E-Rate eligibility, emergency status, vendor assignment, project segmentation, and procurement routing shall be final.
A.        
General Guidelines
 
The contractor shall coordinate all staging, scheduling, delivery, deployment, and implementation activities with the District’s Information Technology Department. Work may be required during evenings, weekends, holidays, instructional breaks, or other non‑standard hours in order to minimize disruption to District operations and instructional activities.
Development of Bid Response 
I.1        A general identification of the items to be installed and the tasks to be completed has been established by the District on the pricing sheets. These items and tasks encompass the greatest majority of what is anticipated to be required. 
I.2        The District has utilized information from past projects and site preliminary engineering to further the District’s Technology Plan and to be in line with the District’s Data System Specification. 
For the purposes of developing a bid for this project
, the bidder will utilize the Pricing Sheets by entering the costs to the district, excluding sales tax, of each item and the labor cost to install the item. Some items presented may include a number of steps or components. The bidder is to provide a full 
kit 
cost for these items. Other items are purely labor (tasks). The bidder is to provide a unit cost as identified by the item. 
I.2.A     Cabling & Pathways RFP Package includes: 
The San Bernardino City Unified School District Data System Specifications 
Cabling and Pathways 
A final pricing sheet to serve as the total bid summation. It is critical to realize that the unit pricing submitted for bidding purposes is to be utilized throughout the complete bid award. Bidders are cautioned to carefully calculate all extensions and totals as a material error (even a rounding error) will result in rejection of the bid. 
 
I.3        
Equivalent Products
I.3.A     There is no intent to eliminate any manufacturer’s proposal with any statement made by the District throughout this Bid Package. The District will consider items proposed as equivalent to those identified in the specifications and listed on the pricing sheets. The District requires a solution that is 100% compatible with the existing network infrastructure. The current network is standards-based and provides additional features to these standards. The District is open to any Bidder solution. However, The District does not want to lose the additional features currently utilized. The District will evaluate the proposed offerings based on their ability to provide the features currently installed in the existing network and based on proposed new features and functionality to upgrade the existing infrastructure. 
I.3.B     Respondents are expected to use their professional discretion when submitting an alternative proposal. However, one of the goals of this project is to expand the network. The District is looking for a smooth expansion rather than adding complexity to the network by introducing alternate specifications. When quoting equivalent products: 
The bidder is to identify the manufacturer and part number on the pricing sheets, where applicable, for each site. 
The bidder shall also provide statistical performance, warranty information, and cut sheets for all items considered equivalent. 
The bidder shall provide a narrative describing how the item meets or exceeds the District’s identified item in utility.
 
I.4        
Basic Design and Engineering
I.4.A     The District also requires a Basic Design and Engineering hourly rate from the bidders. The District has established a maximum number of hours to be utilized as a “not to exceed without prior consent of the District” through the construction process. They are: up to 10 hours per Elementary School site, up to 15 hours per Middle School site and up to 25 hours per High School site. Work done at Administrative NIFs will be up to 25 hours per site. The actual hours utilized may be less than the maximum, but cannot be more than the maximum without prior consent from the District.
I.4.B     Bidder is to use as much of the hour value given per site as needed to develop their own Final Engineered Design that is construction ready, and which will be used for project completion verification as well. This work includes, but is not limited to, starting with the information given herein, thoroughly surveying the site and making note of any and all observed differences from any starting documentation provided later, asking questions to the District IT Department and incorporating the responses given, and making any changes that the District IT Department chooses to make to the project design for budgetary needs or changes in scope or technology.
I.4.C    The contractor is to develop a site-specific price for any work to be completed. The District’s Information Technology (IT) Representative will be available, on site if needed, to answer questions. The same Pricing Sheet utilized for the bid process shall be utilized for any site-specific work. The District IT Representative will review the statement of work and pricing with the contractor, who may make suggestions in an effort to enhance efficiencies. These suggestions can be utilized only if approved by an IT Representative. It is conceivable that the District was not able to confirm some pathways. In this rare event, the specific pathway will be identified as non-confirmed on the Construction Drawings. 
I.4.D    Once the District’s IT Representative and the contractor agree on the specific work to be completed, and the pricing is reviewed to ensure its accuracy and consistency with the pricing submitted in the contractor’s bid package, both parties will sign and date the documents. IT or the requesting site will provide the District’s Purchasing Department with approved quotations for issuance of site-specific purchase orders for work to be performed in accordance with the Terms and Conditions of the Bid documents. The Purchase Order/Contract Price may not be changed, altered or otherwise modified except by a Change Order in accordance with the terms and provisions. 
I.4.E     In the unlikely event that an item or task is required and not included on the Master Bid Pricing Sheets, the contractor is to identify the item or task and notify the District’s IT Representative for further direction. At no time will the Basic Engineering and Design hours exceed the not-to-exceed hours stipulated herein. 
II.1       
Construction
 
II.1.A   When the site-specific purchase order has been issued, all Basic Engineering and Design tasks are considered complete and no such hours in excess of those quoted can be billed. In the event the conditions on a specific site have changed from the time quotation and/or Site-Specific Purchase Order/Contract Price was signed to the time the work commences, it is the responsibility of the contractor to advise the District Representative immediately upon discovery of the condition for an additional site visit and determination if additional Basic Design and Engineering hours are appropriate.
II.1.B   All new or enhanced pathways are to be inspected and signed off by the District’s IT Representative. This includes existing sleeve pathways where an upgrade or repair is identified in the site-specific Statement of Work. The contractor is to request the District’s IT Representative inspection of all new pathways prior to the installation of any cabling. The District IT Representative will sign and date the specific pathway on a contractor provided copy of signed site-specific Construction Drawings. The drawings are to be considered the Master Set of Work Drawings and are to be available any time the District Representative visits a site. 
II.1.C   Site visitations by the District Representative can occur throughout the construction process, sometimes announced, sometimes not. These are good times for the contractor to request completed pathway inspections and answer any questions. 
II.1.D   Any Network Equipment installation to be done under separate project(s) is to be coordinated with the cabling and pathways work. There are instances where this is critical due to the need to remove and replace cabling and equipment at the same site. 
II.1.E  Awarded contractor shall coordinate all infrastructure activities with District operational schedules and any separately awarded vendors performing related work. The contractor shall cooperate with the District, other District‑authorized vendors and service providers to minimize outages, maintain operational continuity, and support coordinated project implementation.
II.1.F   The District’s Information Technology, Maintenance and Operations (M&O), and Facilities Departments have worked together to assist the contractor in a number of ways: 
All outside penetration locations will be approved by the M&O Department prior to the commencement of construction and identified on the Construction Drawings. 
All underground trenching locations shall be approved by the M&O Department prior to the commencement of construction and identified on the Construction Drawings. 
All new or relocation of existing wall-mounted and/or floor-mounted cabinet locations will be approved by the IT Department prior to the commencement of construction and identified on the Construction Drawings. 
If the review of an as-built construction/modernization drawing set could prove helpful to the contractor for a specific site, for a specific reason, the Facilities Department will assist at the request of the District IT Representative. 
Master key sets for each site are available at the District’s M&O. Appointments to obtain master key sets must be made in advance. Each master key set requires a cash deposit of $200.00. These Key sets are Site Master key-sets for only the specific sites for which they are checked out.
A number of the District sites possess asbestos. The District’s M&O Department has established the following policy: 
Please note that no destructive bulk sampling was conducted in the original inspection. Therefore, if any technician uncovers suspect materials, the technician must immediately stop work and contact the District’s IT Representative who will contact the M&O Department for direction.
If approved to work in an asbestos environment, the contractor shall take proper measures to avoid disturbing asbestos containing materials. Before the Basic Design and Engineering process can begin, the District’s IT Representative will provide the contractor with a sample form to be signed by the contractor and a copy filed with the M&O Department.
The District has a list of sites with known asbestos, but there can still be situations where one can encounter unknown asbestos. Contractors are to immediately stop work, clear that area, and report it to M&O (per the Bid).
The District’s Safety Office/Asbestos Information Officer will identify areas at any particular site where the asbestos policy applies.
The cabling contractor is not required to be Asbestos Containment Certified to work in affected areas.
 
II.2       
Final Inspection
II.2.A   Upon completion of all work, the contractor is to provide a complete AutoCAD set of drawings and a complete list of all Items Installed and Tasks Completed. The Cabling and Pathways items shall be presented on separate lists from the Network Equipment.
Specific inspections shall include and not be limited to:

: the contractor shall be prepared to facilitate a 100% inspection if requested by the District’s IT Representative.

SCOPE OF WORK AND SPECIFICATIONS
 
Cabling Specification
 
II.A       
Supporting Codes and Standards Documents
 
It is not possible to list all of the applicable Codes and Standards documents. A non-inclusive list of key documents is presented below as a minimum:
 
ANSI/EIA/TIA-568-B: Commercial Building Telecommunications Cabling Standard
ANSI/EIA/TIA-569-A: Commercial Building Standard for Telecom Pathways and Spaces
ANSI/EIA/TIA-606: Administration Standard for the Telecommunications Infrastructure of Commercial Buildings
ANSI/EIA/TIA-607: Commercial Building Grounding/Bonding Requirements
NFPA 70: National Electrical Code

BICSI: Telecommunications Distribution Methods Manual (TDDM)

The latest revision of each document, and other related documents, is to be considered the one in force at the time of system construction and delivery to SBCUSD. The vendor is required to comply with the applicable documents in content and intent as well.
 
If any applicable documents are in conflict, then the more stringent requirement shall apply. The Contractor is required to advise the SBCUSD Information Technology (IT) Representative of any conflict that could result in work deficiencies.
 
 
II.B       
Cabling System
 
All copper and fiber optic components of the cabling system are either to be of a single manufacturer, or of a manufacturer partnership under a system trade name offering a single point of contact for SBCUSD in the event of a warranty claim. The SBCUSD has chosen the Panduit TX6A 10 Gig UTP Copper Cabling solution as the baseline for all equivalents to be measured. Vendors submitting other manufacturer systems for consideration must meet this system in physical and electronic performance as well as utility. 
 
II.B.1    Copper System
