All newly installed horizontal cabling systems shall support multigigabit Ethernet applications, IEEE 802.3bt Power over Ethernet standards, Wi‑Fi 6E, Wi‑Fi 7, and future standards‑based network technologies operating over Category 6A infrastructure.
 
II.B.2    Copper Cable Color Standards for Horizontal Cabling, Jack Inserts and Patch Cords
 
SBCUSD has standardized on specific colors identified below for horizontal cabling and jack inserts and patch cables on both ends of the horizontal cabling must be the same color. The following colors are the District Standards for the specific network devices and services listed below:
 
Yellow
: The Default color to be utilized when the project to install cabling has no specific device/service usage already determined, or will be used for general data services (i.e. Internet access for wired classroom drops) or is not specified to be one of the other color definitions. Otherwise, at any point prior to the installation of the cabling, inserts or patch cables, if the device types and services become known, the color is to be switched to the identified color standard in support of those now identified devices and services listed below.
 
Red
: To be utilized for devices and services that are in support of Alarms, Energy Management Systems (EMS), and Environmental monitoring.
 
Orange
: To be utilized for devices and services that are in support of Wireless Access Points (internal and external).
 
Green
: To be utilized for devices and services that are in support of IP cameras for Video Surveillance.
 
Blue
: To be utilized for devices and services that are in support of audio/visual displays and devices that connect clients to those projectors/TVs. This includes all Wi-Fi devices, Projectors and Apple TVs.
 
Purple
: To be utilized for devices and services that are in support of VoIP.
 
Black
: To be utilized for devices and services that are in support of IP-based Bells and Paging.
 
II.B.3    Cable
 
SBCUSD requires all cabling being installed within a building to be plenum rated in all environments. Even though quite desirable, SBCUSD is not aware of a Category 6A indoor/outdoor plenum-rated cable. As a result, SBCUSD is willing to accept an indoor/outdoor CM rated cable as long as the NEC termination and pathway requirements are met. Regardless of environment, the cabling shall be of the same electrical performance as Category 6A and be warranted by the same cabling system manufacturer, as Panduit or equivalent.
Ethernet patch cords must be made of 100% pure bare copper wire, as opposed to copper clad aluminum (CCA) wire, to be fully compliant with UL Code 444 and National Electrical Code TIA-568-C.2 fire and safety standards, which require pure bare copper wire in communications cable.
Installation of cabling shall be of continuous length from each termination point.
No length of cable shall exceed 285 feet (tested length).
The bend radius of any cable shall not exceed 4 times the diameter of the cable.
Should the cable become 
kinked
 while being installed, the contractor shall 
not
 attempt to repair the cable, but shall remove and replace the entire run. All cable runs are potential inspection items for the SBCUSD IT Representative.
The cable jacket shall be maintained as close to the point of termination as possible.
The cable pairs shall not be untwisted more than 1/2” from the termination point.
All cabling is to be installed in its own pathway and fully supported.
Cabling shall be installed with no more than a 4-foot space between supports.
Cabling can be installed in pathways such as cable tray and ladder racking, as long as the pathway is low-voltage cabling only, the pathway is appropriately bonded to the building grounding system, and the Data System cables are bundled separately from other low voltage cabling.
Underground cabling can be installed inside buildings to the ultimate termination point without transition as long as the cabling is rated for such applications.
Industry Standard cable waste varies between 7% and 10% per project and the District will not accept final invoices for cabling where cable waste exceeds 10%.
 
II.B.4    Terminations
 
Jack modules shall be of insulation-displacement termination construction, and may offer mass termination of all four pairs simultaneously. In addition, a jack module must be available as part of the cabling system, and facilitate the same system performance and warranties, that can be utilized in existing workstation outlet faceplates from other manufacturers. The most common situation is the Avaya (Lucent) system. Another common situation is Wiremold 5400 raceway.
In an effort to maximize space, SBCUSD has standardized on a discrete 
modular
 patch panel system. The system must allow the following:
Presentation of 48 individual module ports in a 1U (1.75”) rack height, preferred.
Presentation of 24 individual module ports in a 1U (1.75”) rack height.
Presentation of 12 individual module ports to be mounted in an 89B type wall bracket.
Offer Category 6A connectivity, preferred.
Offer Category 5e connectivity if required.
Cabling shall be dressed cleanly and fully supported via hook & loop straps and cabinet/rack supports. All cabling bundles are to be loosely secured with hook & loop straps only. Cable ties are not to be utilized. In addition, hook & loop straps must not be spaced at regular intervals but must vary between 4-6 inches at random over the length of the secured cable section.
Cabling slack can be placed in the cabinet/rack area as well as the ceiling areas if fully supported by the proper pathway device. No more than 4 feet per horizontal run shall be stored.
It is preferred that horizontal cabling does not bypass a patch panel and be terminated and directly plugged into a switch. Any cases would need to be signed off by SBCUSD IT Representative(s).
No particular order is required between workstation cabling terminations or Access Point cabling terminations, though there are instances where AP cabling must be on a specific patch panel associated with an AP supporting edge switch and other existing AP cabling.
The patch panel ports are to be populated beginning with port one in sequence (left to right), leaving no open ports. The only exception will be with 24-port switches that have their ports only on the right side of the faceplate and will require patch panel ports to be populated from right to left to allow for the desired patch cord lengths to work.
It is not a requirement to fill the unused ports with blanks.
Any new copper cabling to patch panels should be patched into an open switchport if available. If no ports are available, do not unplug any existing connectivity. Notify SBCUSD IT Representative(s) that a new switch is needed.
Fiber optic cabling shall be terminated in a fiber enclosure of appropriate size for the cabling being terminated. Unused adaptor panel ports shall be filled with blank panels.
 
II.B.5    Workstation Outlets
 
Faceplates are to be in two-port and four-port, and occasionally 6-port or larger, single gang configurations. The faceplates must include labels and label covers. SBCUSD has standardized on white color faceplates.
The outlet faceplate shall be affixed to the wall or surface mount termination box with two color-matching screws.
SBCUSD has installed a great deal of Wiremold 5400 raceway. Therefore, the raceway adaptors must accommodate the same manufacturer jack module as for all other termination needs, and must match the Wiremold 5400 color.
All empty ports shall be filled with a color matching blank module.
Cabling shall be coiled in the wall or surface mount boxes with no less than 4” and no more than 6” of slack cable. 
 
II.B.6    Access Point Cabling
 
A single-port surface mount termination box shall be utilized to house a single jack module for Access Point connectivity. The termination box shall be white.
Alternatively, a “field termination plug” will also be acceptable for Access Point connectivity as long as the correct cabling and jack color is maintained (even with a colored flag label should the field termination plugs not come in specific colors).
All AP drops installed above drop ceilings must be identified by a red dot affixed to the T-bar in the approximate location as the AP patch cable (not the biscuit box) so that the network electronics vendor can find it. Additionally, AP patch cords should be left dangling (no more than 6 inches) from the drop ceiling into the room to make locating the new drop simple.
Wireless access point infrastructure shall support current and future Wi‑Fi standards including Wi‑Fi 6E and Wi‑Fi 7 deployments. The contractor shall coordinate with the District regarding access point placement, mounting orientation, pathway routing, and high‑density wireless support requirements.
 
II.B.7    Patch Cords
 
Small diameter Category 6A patch cords, as manufactured by Panduit (or approved equivalent) shall be provided by the contractor for the outlet or Access Point termination end as well as the patch panel termination end. The contractor may be asked to install the MDF/IDF/LDF patch cords in instances where the existing Edge switches are not being replaced, as part of the SBCUSD cabinet redressing requirement. These patch cords for the most part shall be either 8” in length or 12” in length as required with preference given to the 8” length where it can be used without strain.
Small diameter Category 6A patch cords, as manufactured by Panduit (or approved equivalent), utilized for all patching shall be of appropriate length and engaged into the associated terminated jack, then coiled and left to be engaged into the Access Point at the appropriate time.
The patch cords shall be yellow in color for workstation drops and orange in color for AP drops, and follow the other color standards listed herein, and be of the same manufacturer as the cabling system.
As a space saving effort, SBCUSD requires the diameter of the patch cable shall not exceed .150” as manufactured by Panduit (or approved equivalent).
The connector end of the patch cord shall provide a 
tangle-free latch
 design as manufactured by Panduit (or approved equivalent).
A Category 6A small diameter, tangle-free latch design patch cord for workstations in lengths appropriate for the specific workstation shall be delivered to SBCUSD. The SBCUSD IT Representative(s) will confirm the quantities and lengths required per site. At no time shall a patch cord exceeding 5 meters be required.
 
II.B.8    Cable Management
 
As part of SBCUSD’s efforts to maximize cabinet/rack space utilization, no new horizontal cable management devices shall be installed. Further, any existing horizontal cable management shall be removed and the cabinet re-organized, re-patched and redressed. See Cabinets/Racks Redressing Requirements.
Rear cable management devices to support cables to the point of termination are to be utilized. A towel bar style bracket is acceptable as long as the cables are neatly and securely attached via hook and loop straps.
Vertical wire management may be utilized when appropriate.
 
II.B.9    Copper System Labeling
 
All workstation outlets, Access Points, and patch panel termination ports are to be labeled with the SBCUSD standard labeling system.
The standard labeling system is as follows:
The patch panel termination location followed by the Room and port number
                        Example: IDF-A1 to Room A1 port 07                     A1-07 (workstation cable)
                        Example: IDF-A1 to Room A1 port 07                     A1-W07 (Access Point cable)
A wrap around label shall be installed at each end of the cable no more than 4 inches from the point of termination presenting the same alphanumeric scheme.
Labeling shall be adopted that is a match and continuation of the accepted labeling already existing at any site(s), and with approval of SBCUSD IT Representative(s).
 
II.B.10  Fiber Optic System
 
SBCUSD has standardized on 12-strand fiber cabling for all backbone requirements. SBCUSD may require a 24-strand fiber cabling for some large IDFs. This includes cabling from the site MDF to each IDF location, and in the rare instance from an IDF to an LDF. In the rare instances from IDF to LDF, SBCUSD may elect to utilize a 6-strand fiber cable. The cabling shall be of indoor/outdoor construction and meet all requirements for plenum environments. 
For cost reasons, SBCUSD would like to utilize no less than Laser Optimized OM4-rated (defined in TIA-492-AAAD) graded-index Multi-Mode Fiber with 850 nm VCSELs (vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers) for all backbone cabling where the distance run is 400m or less which is capable of 10Gb/s connectivity from end-to-end. For all distances exceeding 400m, then Single Mode Fiber is to be utilized to achieve 10Gb/s connectivity end-to-end.
Single Mode Fiber installations will be limited due to the high cost of the transceivers. Some existing Single Mode Fiber runs at various sites which are under 400m in length may remain in place, at the District’s discretion, and be utilized if it is cheaper to do so than replacing it with new multi-mode fiber and new multi-mode transceivers.
There shall always be a minimum of 10’ of jacketed cable slack at each end of the cable.
Connectivity shall be of the LC duplex type. Both field polish and pre-polish termination methods are acceptable.
An appropriately sized fiber optic enclosure shall be utilized for all fiber optic cabling terminations.
Fiber cable slack shall be neatly coiled within the enclosure. No unjacketed slack loops shall be allowed external to the enclosure.
The cable jacket shall enter the enclosure at minimum of 6 inches, and its strength member shall be secured to the enclosure by mechanical means.
The general SBCUSD approach is to install the new fiber cabling alongside the existing OM1/OM2 multi-mode cabling. There will be instances where existing cabling must be removed to allow pathway space for the new cabling. In these instances, the cabling/pathway contractor shall coordinate with the SBCUSD IT Representative, who shall coordinate with the Active Equipment contractor, to ensure the required components are available and ready to be engaged simultaneously with the new fiber cabling.
Some MDF to IDF cabling is already single mode. In these instances, the current termination connector, if not LC, shall be removed. The cable shall be re-terminated with the required LC duplex connector, and the cabling link to be retested and warranted.
In the event the existing termination is already LC (simplex or duplex) the cable does not need to be re-terminated, but must be retested and warranted if disengaged and reengaged for any reason.
SBCUSD may elect to use Armored fiber optic options where/if needed due to known rodent issues, or where rodent issues present themselves at a later date if the fiber run must be replaced due to rodent chewing.
Fiber optic infrastructure shall support current and future high‑speed backbone applications including 10Gb, 25Gb, 40Gb, and 100Gb standards‑based connectivity where applicable. The District may request MPO/MTP backbone assemblies, higher‑density fiber enclosures, or pre‑terminated fiber systems for specific projects.
 
II.B.11  Fiber System Labeling
 
A wrap-around label shall be installed on the jacket of the cable no less than 4” and no more than 6” outside the enclosure at each end of the cables. The cables must be easily identifiable by visual mean the specific IDF or LDF cabinet.
Each MDF enclosure shall display a clearly identifiable labeling chart that easily accessible and legible on the front of the enclosure connector panels. Various methods are acceptable, as long as any specific IDF or LDF connector panel is easily identified and is consistent throughout the project.
IDF cabinets and racks shall identify on the front of the panel the IDF for the IDF to MDF cabling, and the LDF for the IDF to LDF cabling.
The labeling shall match the IDF/LDF nomenclature exactly.
Fiber Cabling Schedule Document that covers type and location of fiber runs from MDF to IDFs and IDFs to LDFs in a graphical format, and include a graphical picture of the cabling connectors in the fiber tray.
 
 
II.B.12  Cabinets Installation
 
New cabinets shall be installed at the location identified by the SBCUSD construction drawing documentation. The exact location shall be approved by the SBCUSD Maintenance and Operations (M&O) Department. The SBCUSD IT Representative will have already met with the M&O Department prior to commencement of construction.
Cabinets shall be manufactured by Southwest Data Products (or approved equivalent).
Wall cabinets shall be mounted on a 1” plywood 48” x 48” backboard, anchored sufficiently to support the maximum allowable weight of the cabinet being installed.
The backboard shall be painted white with two coats of fire-retardant paint on all sides.
In the unlikely event a backboard cannot be installed at the chosen cabinet location, the cabinet shall be installed on solid strut.
The strut shall be securely fastened to the wall and inspected by the SBCUSD IT Representative prior to cabinet mounting.
Two runs of strut extending at least 1” beyond the dimensions of the cabinet and fastened to at least two wall studs shall be utilized for cabinets no larger than 24” in height.
Three runs of strut extending fastened to at least three wall studs shall be utilized for cabinets greater than 24” height.
No wall cabinet greater than 48” in height shall be installed.
Wall cabinets shall be installed to where the bottom of the cabinet is a minimum of 15” AFF (above finished floor) or the top a maximum of 27” AFF. If a situation arises where this is not possible, the vendor is to contact the SBCUSD IT Representative. Existing cabinet locations do not apply.
Wall cabinets shall be of a double-swing, three-piece, design with care taken to the direction of the door swing.
Wall cabinet hinges shall not be of 
piano hinge 
type. All piano hinge type cabinets are to be removed and replaced.
Wall cabinets shall provide a lock for the front door and a lock for the mid-section, both keyed for #CH751 key. Any lock not utilizing a #CH751 key shall be removed and replaced.
Floor mounted cabinets or standing open frames shall be mounted with at least 3 feet of clearance from the front door and from the rear door.
Floor mounted cabinets or standing open frames shall be appropriately seismic braced to the floor.
All cabinets shall be a minimum of 30” depth.
Cabling electronics vendor to notify SBCUSD IT Representative of any existing hanging cabinet issues with the cabinet being securely fastened/attached to the wall/backboard as soon as they are noticed so that IT Representatives can visit the site with the SBCUSD Safety Office representative and determine severity and get Cabling vendor to quote repairs.
Cabinet and rack infrastructure shall support modern high‑density switching environments, high‑capacity wireless aggregation, multigigabit network infrastructure, and future standards‑based network growth.
The District may request additional cabinet environmental support systems including intelligent cooling systems, environmental monitoring, brush panels, vertical power distribution units (PDUs), cable gland systems, or other cabinet modernization components.
II.B.13  Cabinets/Racks Redressing Requirements
 
To maximize space, equipment shall be placed as follows:
Incoming IDF/LDF Fiber Tray at the top.
The 1U 48-port discrete modular patch panel to be positioned below the fiber tray(s).
The first switch to be positioned next.
The second 1U 48-port modular patch panel follows the first switch.
The second switch next.
And alternating so forth.
Patch cords shall be of 8” and 12” lengths as required.
These are Category 6A, yellow (or other color as required), tangle-free latch as manufactured by Panduit (or approved equivalent).
SBCUSD IT Representative may request the contractor to remove existing Category 5e patch panels, and replace with new 1U 48-port discrete modular patch panels as manufactured by Panduit (or equivalent).
A wrap around drop ID label is to be installed on all cables approximately 6” from the point of termination
The cables are to be removed from the patch panel.
The new patch panels are to be installed.
The existing cables are to be re-terminated, tested, and warranted.
The warranty shall meet or exceed minimum Category 5e standards, and be provided by a single manufacturer even though multiple manufactures’ products are utilized within the link. 
The warranty shall be through the same manufacturer as the Category 6A systems utilized elsewhere in the project.
Existing old patch cords are to be replaced with new 8” or 12” Cat6A lengths as required, and in the proper color standard (TBD on a case by case basis).
All cabinets/racks are to be labeled as indicated on the Construction Drawings even if it requires removing an existing label and replacing it with the new one.
All cabinets, new and existing, shall be equipped with a working cooling fan. If the cooling fan does not operate correctly, then it is to be replaced with a new fan as manufactured by Southwest Data Products (or approved equivalent).
All cabinet redress work must be completed in such a manner as all connections are operational for school days, even if the work requires more than one evening. In the event work requires school day down time, the contractor is to advise the SBCUSD IT Representative.
Ensure cabinet locks are operating properly and are keyed to CH751.
In the instances of removal of an existing cabinet and replacement with a new cabinet, all preceding items in this specification section shall apply.
 
II.B.14  Cabinets Labeling
 
All cabinets/racks, new and existing are to be labeled consistent with the Construction Drawings.
 
II.B.15  Hinged wall brackets
 
Brackets shall be utilized in the same U space as the patch panel--1U panel, 1U bracket, as manufactured by Panduit (or approved equivalent).
Brackets shall be utilized only when identified by the SBCUSD Construction Documents as required for a specific application.
 
II.B.16  System Testing and Certification
 
All components shall be inspected before installation to ensure the correct item is being installed and the component appears to be without flaws.
Any defect or system failure shall be corrected by the vendor prior to request for final inspection.
Testing equipment shall be calibrated no less than twelve months prior to the date of testing. Proof of certification is to be available to the SBCUSD IT Representative upon request.
Test results shall automatically be calculated and evaluated by the testing equipment, utilizing the most current performance and testing standards and the manufacturer’s system performance published statistics. Test results shall be provided within three calendar weeks of final inspection completion in an electronic format that does not require special software to review.
All site wide cabling project sign-offs must include testing results for all horizontal fiber runs and all horizontal copper runs performed per site, and that testing documentation must be attached to project sign off requests.
Copper system
Testing shall be compliant with the most recent Level III requirement for Category 6 testing. Level IIe requirements shall be met for all Category 5e testing.
Testing shall be directional, swept-frequency for the following:
Attenuation
Wire map
Attention to Crosstalk Ratio
Pair-to-Pair NEXT loss
PSNEXT loss
Return loss
Pair-to-pair ELFEXT
PSELFEXT
ANEXT
Propagation delay
Delay skew
Cable length
Contractor shall provide documentation to the SBCUSD IT Representative identifying the cable manufacturer’s published Nominal Velocity of Propagation (NVP).
Fiber system
All fiber optic cable testing shall be performed on all multi-mode and single mode fibers, newly installed, re-terminated, or relocated. 
Power meter testing shall provide system loss measurements at 850nm for MMF and both the SMF 1310 nm and 1550 nm windows in one direction.
Maximum system insertion loss shall not exceed 6dB.
OTDR testing is only required in the event an existing multi-mode or single mode fiber optic cable fails the power meter tests and troubleshooting is required to determine the cause.
Cleanup
All work areas should be cleaned of construction debris and left as found. Any ceiling tiles removed must be reinstalled and any damaged ceiling tiles must be repaired or replaced. Any moved furniture needs to be returned to the original locations.
 
II.C      
Warranty
 
Vendor shall warrant all workmanship for a minimum of one year after date of final inspection.
Vendor shall also facilitate a manufacturer’s system warranty certificate for the copper cabling system and fiber optic cabling system for a minimum of 25 years as offered by Panduit (or approved equivalent), and provide documentation in support thereof.
The warranty shall be applied to all current and future applications designed to run on the designated link or channel classification as defined in the Commercial Building Telecommunications Cabling Standards.
The warranty shall include all individual components and the performance thereof to meet the manufacturer’s requirements as a component of the warranted system.
The warranty shall guarantee Category 6A system performance including previously identified headroom, Category 6 where applicable, or Category 5e performance where applicable.
It is quite possible that circumstances will arise within the SBCUSD which will require termination of a new Category 6A cable to an existing patch panel from another manufacturer. The contractor is to consultant with the SBCUSD IT Representative prior to installation of any components or termination of cabling. It is a requirement of the contractor to facilitate a full manufacturer’s 25-year system warranty, at the lowest component performance level, as offered by Panduit (or approved equivalent) when such instances occur.
It is also quite possible that circumstances will arise within the SBCUSD which will require the relocation of existing cabling. It is a requirement of the contractor to facilitate a full manufacturer’s 25-year system warranty, at the lowest component performance level, as offered by Panduit (or approved equivalent) when such circumstances occur.
SBCUSD understands that manufacturers cabling system warranties may not include patch cords of lengths less than one meter. In these instances, SBCUSD will accept a 
link
 warranty in lieu of a 
channel
 warranty.
SBCUSD remedy of any warranty claim shall be through a single point of contact.
 
II.D      
Documentation
 
Cabling contractor must provide AutoCAD diagrams also attached to project sign off requests showing the entire site layout (top down) and all known conduit (whether they used it or not), with notes stating what fiber and/or copper runs are in what conduit pathways, where the building entrance point is for each run, and where each building network concentration point is (MDF or IDF) and where all the horizontal copper cabling runs are in the buildings to each AP location (classrooms, etc.).
All final AutoCAD drawings must be completed and presented to the District within 5 business days after cabling is done for a site walk prior.
The District may request additional cabinet environmental support systems including intelligent cooling systems, environmental monitoring, brush panels, vertical power distribution units (PDUs), cable gland systems, or other cabinet modernization components.
 
II.E       
Drop Requests by Sites
Cabling specifications and requirements for installation and other deliverables in this document are to be followed for network drop Adds and Repairs.
Drop Requests (Adds)
Site makes Drop Request for (1) or more new network drops to the SBCUSD IT Department.
Site fills out the Drop Request Form (e-form or paper) and submits it to the SBCUSD IT Department.
SBCUSD IT Department will submit the filled request form and supporting documents it receives to the Cabling Vendor.
See timelines for expectations of deliverables.
Drop Requests (Repairs of Existing)
Site makes a Drop Repair Request for (1) or more existing network drops to the SBCUSD IT department.
Site fills out the Drop Repair Request Form (e-form or paper) and submits it to the SBCUSD IT Department.
SBCUSD IT Department will submit the filled request form and supporting documents it receives to the Cabling Vendor.
See timelines for expectations of deliverables.
Timelines
From receipt of the filled request form from SBCUSD IT, Vendor must produce and send to SBCUSD IT a quote within (7) business days. Timeline Extensions can be granted on an as-needed basis for schedule availability.
Vendor will schedule site walk(s) with SBCUSD IT Representative if desired during that (7) day time period to review the request in person. This is optional and up to the Vendor depending on the complexity of the request.
Quote from Vendor must be submitted to SBCUSD IT Representative (or in some cases the Representative of another department that makes the request, like the Facilities Department).
Site will turn the Quote into a Purchase Request at whatever speed works for them.
Once Purchase Request becomes a Purchase Order, SBCUSD will submit the Purchase Order to the Vendor. Vendor then has (15) business days to perform the work requested.
If materials are on backorder, or labor cannot be scheduled (or both) within the expected time frame, Vendor must notify SBCUSD IT Representative (or other) immediately, and provide a new timeline Vendor expects they can meet for project completion.
Closeout Documents for Drop Requests by Sites
Vendor must provide link testing to SBCUSD IT Representative for all new or repaired network drops. For Fiber, OTDR or equivalent, for Copper, Fluke test results or equivalent. It should be in a searchable PDF format emailed to District IT Representative or a Cloud Service option accessible to SBCUSD to retrieve the documentation.
For new drop installs, it is desired that Vendor also provide a drawing showing the new pathway(s) and drop locations in the room or rooms for SBCUSD records. AutoCAD preferred. It should be emailed to District IT Representative or a Cloud Service option accessible to SBCUSD to retrieve the documentation.
Invoice must include the information on Requesting Person, and the Site or Department, and the Person who signs off on the job for that Requested Work.
 
Pathway Specification
 
III.A      
Conduits
 
Metallic conduit and tubing shall be manufactured under the supervision of an U.L. or another such factory inspection and label service program, as manufactured by Western Tube (or approved equivalent). Each 10-foot length of conduit and tubing shall bear the U.L. or other such label and the manufacturer’s name.
Conduits shall consist of GRC (galvanized rigid conduit) and EMT (electrical metallic tubing). GRC is to be utilized in any outside or 
wet 
areas, and areas where the conduit is exposed and less than 6’ AFF.
All GRC shall be rigid steel, heavy wall, zinc coated, with an inside and outside protective coating manufactured in accordance with ANSI C80.1.
All GRC fittings shall be threaded type, as manufactured by RACO (or approved equivalent). No die cast or screw-type fittings shall be allowed.
All EMT conduit fittings shall be compression type and manufactured in accordance with ANSI C80.3, as by RACO (or approved equivalent). No screw-type fittings shall be allowed.
LB-type, 90̊ covered fittings, are not allowed.
Liquid-tight flexible metal conduit shall be galvanized heavy wall, flexible locked steel strip construction, UV rated, with smooth moisture and oil-proof, abrasion-resistant, extruded plastic jacket, as manufactured by OZ Gozney (or approved equivalent). 
Conduits shall be supported at a minimum of two points per 10’ piece. 
Supports may be strut hardware, as manufactured by Unistrut (or equivalent), or conduit straps, as manufactured by Western Tube (or approved equivalent). In instances where a trapeze support system is required, the system shall be supported by ceiling mounted threaded steel rods shall be utilized--3/8” rod required for conduits 2” and smaller, and 1/2” for conduits over 2”.
Conduits shall not include more than two (2) aggregate 90̊ sweeps between pull boxes, or other such pathway device.
Bend radius of any conduit shall not exceed 6 times the inside diameter of the conduit for trade sizes under 2”, and 10 times the inside diameter of the conduit for trade sizes 2” and greater.
Conduit fill rates shall not exceed 40% for new construction and 50% for existing pathways. 
A fill rate of 80% is allowed for straight sleeves (with no bends) under 24” in length if approved by the SBCUSD IT Representative.
Conduits shall extend a minimum of 4” above floor level when entering from underground.
Any conduit exposed, shall be installed parallel or perpendicular to the building. The location of such conduit shall be approved by the SBCUSD Maintenance and Operations Department. The SBCUSD IT Department will meet with the Maintenance and Operations Department in advance of construction commencement to obtain approval.
Conduits shall not be installed underneath breezeways or eves areas between buildings without specific approval by the SBCUSD Maintenance and Operations Department.
All metallic pathways shall be appropriately bonded to building ground.
Underground pathways shall be of a minimum Schedule 40 PVC, as manufactured by Carlon (or approved equivalent) and adhere to the same bend radii and fill ratio requirements as GRC and EMT.
A GRC riser to underground transition shall occur at the same depth as the underground conduit installation.
Manufactured bend/elbow fittings shall be utilized. No attempt to bend underground conduit in the field shall be allowed.
Innerduct pathway, as manufactured by Carlon (or approved equivalent) shall be utilized as specifically located on the construction drawings. Plenum rated innerduct for exclusive indoor use shall be required. OSP rated innerduct for exclusive outdoor use shall be required and for instances where the innerduct enters a building for no more than 50’. Indoor/outdoor rated innerduct shall be required for instances where the innerduct will enter a building for more than 50’.
The innerduct pathway can be supported in various methods, but never by string, cable ties, etc.
No sharp edges shall exist at ends of the innerduct. All factory and/or field cut ends shall be smooth.
 
III.B      
Basket Trays/Wire Ways
 
      A. The District does not anticipate the requirement to install any basket tray or wire ways.
 
III.C     
J-hooks/Cradles
 
The vast majority of ceilings within the SBCUSD are of drop-type construction. A Cradle pathway, as manufactured by Tomarco (or approved equivalent) is the most economic choice in most instances.
J-hook/Cradle hardware shall be installed via wall mounting, beam brackets, ceiling mounted stringers. At no time shall j-hooks/cradles be attached to drop-type ceiling structures, supports, or suspension wiring.
The number of cables installed in a particular j-hook/cradle device shall not exceed manufacturer’s maximum fill ratio. The pathway contractor shall coordinate with the SBCUSD IT Representative to confirm the correct j-hook/cradle size to be utilized.
The maximum distance between j-hook/cradle devices shall not exceed 4’.
J-hook/cradle hanger cable surfaces must have rounded edges that will not damage or deform the cable sheath(s).
 
III.D     
Trenching
 
All contractors must obtain an authorized dig permit from the SBCUSD Maintenance and Operations Department prior to commencing 
any excavation.
 The SBCUSD IT Representative will have already met with the Maintenance and Operations Department prior to commencement of construction.
All surfaces shall be returned to their original state prior to the trenching work.
All patching of asphalt or concrete shall be made using the same materials, workmanship, and finish, and shall accurately match all surrounding areas.
All underground conduits shall have a minimum of 24" of trench back fill coverage.
All back filled trenches shall have a minimum of 95% compaction.
Within two weeks, the contractor shall coordinate with the SBCUSD IT Representative as-built drawings to be delivered to the Maintenance and Operations Department.
SBUCSD does not anticipate the need to install underground vaults within the scope of this project.
 
III.E      
Penetrations
 
All outside building penetrations shall be approved by the SBCUSD Maintenance and Operations Department. The SBCUSD IT Representative will have already met with the Maintenance and Operations Department prior to commencement of construction.
The specific sleeve pathway device, GRC, EMT, liquid-tight, shall be identified on the construction drawings and in the site-specific statement of work for all new penetrations.
All penetration sleeves, new or existing, shall be appropriately supported on each end.
All penetration sleeves shall be firestopped in accordance with NFPA 70 to obtain a 2 hour rating. At a minimum, an intumescent seal shall be installed between the sleeve and the penetration opening and an intumescent duct-seal material shall be installed in the sleeve’s annular space after all cabling has been installed. Technicians installing the firestopping materials shall be certified by the manufacturer whose products are being installed. SBCUSD has not standardized on a particular manufacturer of firestopping materials. Proof of such certification must be made available to the SBCUSD IT Representative upon request.
All conduit entries into a building from the outside must be through a correctly NEMA rated pull box. A myers hub fitting, as manufactured by Thomas & Betts (or approved equivalent) shall be installed in the pull box as a method of sealing the penetration.
 
III.F      
Pull Boxes
 
Pull boxes shall be installed at the locations identified on the construction drawings.
NEMA 1 rated pull boxes, as manufactured by Hoffman (or approved equivalent) shall be installed inside the buildings.
NEMA 3R rated pull boxes, as manufactured by Hoffman (or approved equivalent) shall be installed outside the buildings or in 
wet 
areas.
Pull boxes can be mounted via screws, bolts, or on strut supports.
Pull boxes sizes shall be a depth no less than twice the diameter of the largest conduit to be installed, a width and height to be six times the diameter of the largest conduit.
The specific size and NEMA rating will be identified on the construction drawings.
 
III.G     
Surface Mount Raceway
 
Wiremold 5400 (or approved equivalent plastic raceway) divided raceway shall be installed for all computer labs and will also be utilized for workstation drops where no there is no current presence of sufficient electrical power. Equivalency shall be determined by the SBCUSD Maintenance and Operations Department.
SBCUSD has standardized on Panduit LP3 plastic raceway for single cable, non-electrical installations. SBCUSD will consider equivalents.
The surface mount raceway shall be installed in accordance will manufacturer’s requirements.
Fill ratios shall be in accordance with manufacturer’s published information.
The divided raceway electrical channel shall be located closest to the floor when installed horizontally.
The specific locations of the raceway shall be identified on the construction drawings.
In the case of cabling entering from outside, the surface mount raceway shall be of metal construction and appropriately bonded. Therefore, Wiremold 5400 and Panduit LP3 do not qualify. In these cases, Wiremold 2400 (or equivalent metallic raceway) shall be installed.
 
III.H     
Bushings
 
Plastic insulation bushings, as manufactured by Crouse-Hinds (or equivalent) shall be installed at all connecting points of fittings, conduits, sleeves, etc. 
At no point shall a sharp or unprotected pathway edge be left uncovered with an insulation bushing.
Some repair or upgrade of existing sleeves/pathways will require installation of a split bushing since cables are already installed.
 
III.I       
Access Points and Outside Antennas
 
The vast majority of the Access Points shall be installed on drop ceilings via an application specific clip. In these cases, the terminated jack, surface mount box, and patch cord shall be placed on the same ceiling tile immediately above the installed Access Point. There are environments at some sites where the areas above the drop ceilings are not conducive to placing the connectivity items directly on the ceiling tile. In these instances, a mounting bracket such as manufactured
by TerraWave (or approved equivalent such as Oberon) shall be used for connectivity item mounting.
A number of Access Points shall be installed on hard surface walls. In these instances, a wall mount Access Point bracket or “doghouse”, such as manufactured by Precision Enclosure Solutions (PES) (or approved equivalent such as Oberon) shall be utilized. Indoor APs with built-in antennas shall always be mounted horizontally and never vertically.
The appropriate pathway (conduit or surface mount raceway) shall be identified on the construction drawings. A machined chase nipple with locking rings and plastic bushings shall act as a transition from the pathway to the bracket.
At a number of sites, an outside plant antenna is to be utilized. 
In these cases, an outside plant antenna enclosure, as manufactured by TerraWave (or approved equivalent), shall be utilized.
The enclosure is to be treated in all respects like a pull box and painted (with non-metallic paint) to match the outside wall color for theft and/or vandalism reduction purposes.
 
III.J      
Painting
 
Any exposed conduit, pull boxes, and associated hardware shall be painted to match the décor of the wall(s) the pathway is mounted on. Surface mount raceways are not to be painted.

## INTRODUCTION AND SOLICITATION SCHEDULE
A. Introduction
1. General
The San Francisco International Airport (the “Airport” or “SFO”) is operated by the City and County of San Francisco (the “City”) acting by and through its Airport Commission (the “Commission”).
  
This Request for Qualifications (hereinafter “RFQ” or “Solicitation”) is being issued by the Airport.  The Airport is looking for interested catering service providers (“Respondents”) to send in their information (“Submittals”) for as-needed catering services.
From time to time, the Airport hosts events that need food and beverage support. These events vary in size and happen only when needed. To make things easier going forward, SFO is creating a Prequalified Pool of catering partners that offer a wide mix of cuisines. Having this pool in place will help the Airport quickly line up catering services whenever an event comes up.
SFO connects the world to the San Francisco Bay Area. Register and provide basic information about your business today for the opportunity to provide catering, dining, and food services to staff and employees. SFO encourages all interested food businesses to register and begin the qualification process. Respondents meeting the minimum qualifications will be added to the Prequalified Pool and will be used by SFO, and potentially by other City departments, on an as-needed basis.
Registration is easy and takes less than 5 minutes.
Next, fill out the intake form (
https://cater.sfoprocure.com/
) with your basic business information: How we can reach you and what types of food you serve. The intake form asks for more detail, such as how many people you can serve and whether you are already a City-approved supplier. However, just having your contact information and the types of food you serve is enough for SFO to place you on its caterers contact list immediately. There will be an opportunity later to complete the intake form if you do not have the documents right now.
If you are interested, please visit the Airport’s OpenGov e‑procurement portal at 
https://procurement.opengov.com/portal/sfo/projects/247719
 and follow these steps:
Step one
 – Register with OpenGov. (It’s easy and takes less than 5 minutes.)
Step two
 – Start the intake form by filling in your contact information and cuisine types. It’s quick and easy. You will be added to the SFO caterers contact list. (Suppliers 
do not need to meet the MQs
 to start the intake form and be added to SFO’s caterers contact list.)
Step three
 – Show that you meet the MQs by filling in all required parts of the intake form and uploading your Minimum Qualification (MQ) documents for consideration for the Prequalified Pool.
A Respondent that completes and submits the information and documentation required in steps 1 through 3 has completed a “Submittal” under this RFQ. The Airport will evaluate the Submittals and create a Prequalified Pool of Respondents that meet the MQs (“Prequalified Pool”). Respondents must meet the MQs to be added to the Prequalified Pool. Only those in the Prequalified Pool may be selected to provide catering services.
Step four
 – Selection from the Prequalified Pool by the Airport or another City Department. The selection process is described below in Section I.C, entitled “Resulting Contracts Awarded to Contractors Selected from the Prequalified Pool.”
Respondents prequalified under this RFQ (“Prequalified Suppliers”) are not guaranteed a contract or catering work. The City may use the Prequalified Pool on an as-needed basis in City’s sole and absolute discretion.
Below is an overview of how Respondents will be evaluated and added to the Prequalified Pool.
When applicable and practical, Respondents are encouraged to engage contracting teams that reflect the diversity of the City and include participation of businesses and residents from the City’s most disadvantaged communities including, but not limited to the Bayview/Hunters Point, Chinatown, Mission, South of Market, Tenderloin, Visitacion Valley and Western Addition neighborhoods.
Respondents should not submit, and the City will not consider, any demographic data about the racial, ethnic, gender, sexual orientation, or national origin make up of Respondent’s staff, leadership, and/or board of directors.
B. Creation and Duration of the Prequalified Pool
Respondents meeting the Minimum Qualifications will be added to the Prequalified Pool and eligible for potential award and negotiation of a contract or purchase order (“Resulting Contract”) with the City, on an as-needed basis. The Prequalified Pool list is valid for 2 years but may be extended for up to 2 additional years if re-opened by City in accordance with Section 21.4 of the San Francisco Administrative Code.
Submittals may be accepted and evaluated on a rolling basis throughout the life of the Prequalified Pool. However, to maximize eligibility for upcoming opportunities, Respondents are strongly encouraged to respond by the initial deadline indicated in 
Section I. G. Solicitation Schedule
. Submittals after the initial deadline must still be approved by the Airport before a Respondent can be added to the Prequalified Pool and Respondents submitting after the initial deadline may experience delays that limit their ability to participate in time-sensitive opportunities.
This is an ongoing solicitation, and new Submittals will continue to be reviewed and added to the Prequalified Pool until its expiration. This RFQ will continue to be posted on the Airport e-Procurement Portal.
C. Resulting Contracts Awarded to Contractors Selected From the Prequalified Pool
1. Selection of Contractors from the Prequalified Pool 
Pursuant to Section 21.4 of the San Francisco Administrative Code, City shall select contractors from the Prequalified Pool for Resulting Contracts pursuant to three options, as described below. Selections must be made prior to the expiration of the Prequalified Pool.  
a.    City may select the highest available ranked contractor from the Prequalified Pool (if a ranking was done when the pool was created); OR 
b.    City may request quotes or Submittals from the Prequalified Pool from which to select. Where applicable, the Department shall apply Chapter 14B LBE Rating Bonuses or Bid Discounts when evaluating quotes or Submittals received from the Prequalified Pool. The request for quotes or Submittals may also include an LBE Participation Requirement.   
c.    For Resulting Contracts that are less than the Minimum Competitive Amount in effect when the selection is being made, City may select a contractor from the Prequalified Pool without any further solicitation. In choosing this option, City shall notify the Prequalified Pool of its selection. The Notice shall specify the commodities and/or services awarded; their cost; and the selected Contractor’s unique qualifications for having been selected without a further solicitation.
2. Notice of Intent to Award a Resulting Contract to the Prequalified Pool
Except where a contractor is selected without a further solicitation for a Resulting Contract amount equal to or less than the Minimum Competitive Amount, City shall not issue a Notice of Intent to Award when awarding a Resulting Contract to a contractor from the Prequalified Pool. The City’s award of a Resulting Contract to a contractor from the Prequalified Pool is final and not subject to further review.
3. Anticipated Term of Resulting Contracts
A Resulting Contract awarded to a Prequalified Supplier shall be non-exclusive, with an original term to be determined at the time of Resulting Contract award based on the awarding Department’s business needs but in no case shall the term exceed ten (10) years.
4. Anticipated Contract Not to Exceed Amount
The not to exceed (“NTE”) amount for a Resulting Contract awarded under this Solicitation cannot be anticipated at the time of this Solicitation but shall be determined at the time of Resulting Contract award based on the awarding Department’s needs.

Any other City department, public entity or non-profit made up of multiple public entities, may use the results of this Solicitation to obtain some or all of the commodities or services to be provided by Respondent under the same terms and conditions of any contract awarded under this Solicitation.

## SERVICES REQUESTED
A. Services Requested
Airport is issuing this Solicitation to identify and prequalify Respondents qualified to provide as‑needed catering services in support of Airport events. Respondents who are successfully added to the Airport’s Prequalified Pool may be contacted on an as‑needed basis to provide catering services that align with the specific requirements of each event as detailed in this RFQ. Other City Departments may also use the Prequalified Pool as described in this RFQ.
Catering needs will vary by event and will be communicated to Prequalified Suppliers at the time services are being planned. Events may differ in size, format, and culinary style. Prequalified Suppliers may be asked to provide catering services that align with the Airport’s/other City Department’s specific event requirements. These needs may include, but are not limited to, the following:
Cuisine Options:
A variety of culinary styles, including but not limited to: American, international, specialty, dietary‑restricted, or themed menus.
Ability to accommodate vegetarian, vegan, gluten‑free, allergen‑sensitive, or other dietary requirements.
Event Size and Format:
Catering for events of various sizes, including small meetings, employee gatherings, community events, or large‑scale functions hosted on Airport/other City Department property.
Support for multi‑shift events, including daytime and nighttime service to accommodate Airport/other City Department employee schedules.
Presentation and Types
Packaged meals for pickup or delivery.
Buffet or plated service, including setup and breakdown.
Food truck or mobile food service on Airport/other City Department grounds.

Title:
 
 
11211.52 San Francisco International Resource Management System/ Airport Operations Database Implementation, Maintenance and Support Services
 
 
 
 
Summary of Scope of Work:
 
 
The San Francisco International Airport is seeking to procure Resource Management System (RMS)/ Airport Operations Database (AODB) Implementation, Maintenance and Support Services.  

San Francisco International Airport (“SFO” or “the Airport”) served 52 Million Annual Passengers (“MAP”) in 2025 and is on track to reach 70MAP in the next decade. Serving as a major gateway to Europe and Asia across four terminals (1, 2, 3 and International) and seven concourses (A to G). SFO utilizes a shared use terminal strategy. The Airport’s capacity and flight schedule are facilitated as a Level 2 airport by the FAA Slot Administration Office within the Air Traffic Organization in accordance with the Worldwide Airport Slot Guidelines. 

Common Use Passenger Technology (CUP-T) is the umbrella term for three separate procurements that when completed will encompass the technologies needed to support common use at the Airport. 

The three separate CUP-T procurements include: (1) the Resource Management System (RMS) – Airport Operations Database (AODB); (2) Passenger Processing Systems (PPS) which includes Common Use Passenger Processing (CUPPS), Common Use Self Service (CUSS), Self Service Bag Drop (SSBD), Biometric (such as facial scans) for Passenger Boarding; and (3) Information Display Systems (IDS).
The intent of these separate procurements is to achieve best-of-breed solutions.

This Scope of Work (also referred to as the “Scope of Services”) covers the procurement, implementation, integration, and ongoing maintenance of the first CUP-T procurement identified above, which includes two core Airport operations and capacity management technology platforms: the RMS and AODB, as further detailed below:

1.1.1	Airport Operational Database. The AODB is the authoritative, real-time operational data platform for the Airport. It provides integrated capabilities for real-time messaging, storage and retrieval of operational information, and serves as the master source of flight data. ## Introduction / Project Summary
The San Francisco International Airport is seeking to procure Resource Management System (RMS)/ Airport Operations Database (AODB) Implementation, Maintenance and Support Services.  

San Francisco International Airport (“SFO” or “the Airport”) served 52 Million Annual Passengers (“MAP”) in 2025 and is on track to reach 70MAP in the next decade. Serving as a major gateway to Europe and Asia across four terminals (1, 2, 3 and International) and seven concourses (A to G). SFO utilizes a shared use terminal strategy. The Airport’s capacity and flight schedule are facilitated as a Level 2 airport by the FAA Slot Administration Office within the Air Traffic Organization in accordance with the Worldwide Airport Slot Guidelines. 

Common Use Passenger Technology (CUP-T) is the umbrella term for three separate procurements that when completed will encompass the technologies needed to support common use at the Airport. 

The three separate CUP-T procurements include: (1) the Resource Management System (RMS) – Airport Operations Database (AODB); (2) Passenger Processing Systems (PPS) which includes Common Use Passenger Processing (CUPPS), Common Use Self Service (CUSS), Self Service Bag Drop (SSBD), Biometric (such as facial scans) for Passenger Boarding; and (3) Information Display Systems (IDS).
The intent of these separate procurements is to achieve best-of-breed solutions.

This Scope of Work (also referred to as the “Scope of Services”) covers the procurement, implementation, integration, and ongoing maintenance of the first CUP-T procurement identified above, which includes two core Airport operations and capacity management technology platforms: the RMS and AODB, as further detailed below:

1.1.1	Airport Operational Database. The AODB is the authoritative, real-time operational data platform for the Airport. It provides integrated capabilities for real-time messaging, storage and retrieval of operational information, and serves as the master source of flight data. The AODB shall expose Representational State Transfer (REST) and event-based Application Programming Interfaces (APIs), for data and service integration with the Airport’s enterprise data platform and data-domain structure and shall make operational data available to downstream systems such as the IDS.
1.1.2	Resource Management System. The RMS supports SFO Operations in the planning and real-time assignment of physical Airport resources, including gates, check-in counters, baggage claim carousels, baggage makeup conveyors, and remote aircraft parking positions including fixed-base operation and cargo stands. The RMS shall provide planning functions, “best-fit” assignment recommendations, and real-time conflict detection and warnings.
Contractor shall ensure the RMS/AODB will interoperate cleanly with the separately-procured passenger processing platform and with the third-party IDS through documented, standards-based interfaces.
Software licenses provided under this Agreement shall be enterprise-wide and shall support all potential authorized users as designated by the Airport.

Description:
Sacramento Housing & Redevelopment Agency (SHRA) seeks actuarial services to support the ongoing measurement, funding, and financial reporting of its Other Post-Employment Benefits (OPEB) program. The project is centered on helping SHRA maintain a disciplined, sustainable approach to retiree healthcare obligations while producing clear, defensible actuarial information for both funding and accounting purposes. SHRA has historically prefunded its OPEB obligations through the California Employers’ Retiree Benefit Trust (CERBT) and has consistently contributed at or above the actuarially determined contribution, reflecting a strong commitment to long-term sustainability and sound fiscal management.
The selected vendor will be expected to provide actuarial valuation and advisory services that support several interconnected objectives: development of actuarially determined contributions, preparation of GASB 75 reporting, analysis of funded status and long-term liability trends, and evaluation of the Agency’s prefunding strategy.
The work is expected to require technical rigor, responsiveness, and the ability to communicate complex actuarial concepts to management and stakeholders in a practical way. SHRA values a partner who can do more than deliver compliant reports: the Agency is looking for actuarial expertise that can help leadership understand emerging risks, evaluate funding options, explain key drivers of change, and support informed decision-making over time. This engagement should be attractive to high-quality vendors with public-sector OPEB experience, particularly those who can combine strong actuarial credentials with thoughtful strategic advice, reliable project execution, and clear presentation of results.

SHRA sponsors an Other Post-Employment Benefits (OPEB) program for eligible retirees that includes retiree medical and dental benefits. In connection with these benefits, SHRA requires ongoing actuarial services to measure liabilities, support funding decisions, and provide information necessary for financial reporting and long-term planning. The Agency’s OPEB program includes both explicit employer-paid subsidies and implicit subsidy liabilities associated with blended active and retiree healthcare premiums, requiring specialized actuarial analysis and periodic review.
SHRA has historically taken a proactive approach to OPEB funding and administration. The Agency participates in the California Employers’ Retiree Benefit Trust (CERBT) and has used actuarial valuations to establish contribution levels and evaluate the funded status of the plan. Recent actuarial reports have supported development of Actuarially Determined Contributions (ADCs), measurement of total OPEB liability, and preparation of GASB 75 financial reporting disclosures. These services have been an important part of SHRA’s broader effort to manage retiree benefit obligations in a fiscally responsible and sustainable manner.
SHRA’s OPEB program contains multiple plan design features that require careful actuarial evaluation. The Agency maintains different contribution structures for employees based on hire date, including a medical allowance structure for certain retirees and a PEMHCA vesting-based subsidy structure for others. The actuarial work therefore requires not only technical valuation expertise, but also a clear understanding of public-sector retiree healthcare programs, applicable accounting standards, demographic and healthcare trend assumptions, and the funding implications of plan design and experience changes over time.
Through this solicitation, SHRA seeks to retain a qualified actuarial services firm with demonstrated experience in public-sector OPEB valuations, funding analysis, and GASB 75 reporting. The Agency is interested in obtaining professional services that are accurate, timely, and clearly communicated, and that will support SHRA in continuing its prudent management of retiree healthcare obligations.

## Scope of Work
Sacramento Housing and Redevelopment Agency (“SHRA” or “Agency”) seeks proposals from qualified actuarial firms to provide actuarial services for the Agency’s Other Post-Employment Benefits (“OPEB”) program, including actuarial valuation services and GASB Statement No. 75 reporting support for retiree healthcare benefits.
This Scope of Work is intended to serve as a general guide to the work SHRA expects to be performed and is not intended to be a complete listing of all services that may be required. The selected consultant shall furnish all professional actuarial services, labor, supervision, calculations, consultation, reports, and related support reasonably necessary to complete the work in accordance with applicable professional standards and SHRA requirements.
The selected consultant shall provide actuarial services in accordance with applicable Actuarial Standards of Practice and in a manner that allows SHRA to report in compliance with Governmental Accounting Standards Board Statement No. 75 (“GASB 75”).

## General Requirements
The selected consultant shall provide actuarial services necessary to support SHRA’s valuation, accounting, and financial reporting needs for retiree healthcare OPEB. Services shall include review of data, development of assumptions and methods, preparation of valuation and GASB 75 reports, consultation with Agency staff, and coordination with the Agency’s auditor as needed.
All work shall be prepared by qualified actuarial professionals with demonstrated experience in public-sector OPEB valuations and GASB 75 reporting.

## Actuarial Valuation Services
The consultant shall prepare new Actuarial Valuation Reports for SHRA for retiree healthcare as of December 31, 2025,  December 31, 2027, and as of December 31, 2029.
The December 31, 2025 actuarial valuation shall support SHRA’s GASB 75 reporting for the fiscal years ending December 31, 2026 and December 31, 2027. The December 31, 2027 actuarial valuation shall support GASB 75 reporting for the fiscal years ending December 31, 2028 and December 31, 2029. The December 31, 2029 actuarial valuation shall support GASB 75 reporting for the fiscal year ending December 31, 2030.
Each actuarial valuation report shall, at a minimum:
A. Measure SHRA’s retiree healthcare OPEB liabilities as of the applicable valuation date.
B. Reflect applicable plan provisions, eligibility rules, subsidy structures, and current retiree healthcare arrangements.
C. Measure both explicit subsidy liabilities and implicit subsidy liabilities.
D. Use actuarial methods and assumptions that comply with applicable Actuarial Standards of Practice and are appropriate for the stated purpose of the report.
E. Include a description of participant data, actuarial assumptions, methods, and material plan provisions used in the valuation.
F. Provide a reconciliation of results from the prior valuation, including explanation of significant changes in liabilities due to plan changes, demographic experience, healthcare cost changes, investment experience, assumption changes, participation changes, or other material factors.
G. Provide information sufficient to support future GASB 75 reporting.
H. Prepare Actuarially Determined Contributions (ADCs) for SHRA’s OPEB prefunding program. The December 31, 2025 valuation shall include ADCs for fiscal years 2026 through 2028. Subsequent valuations shall include ADCs for the applicable future fiscal years necessary to support SHRA’s OPEB prefunding and budget planning.
I. Calculate ADCs separately for each of SHRA’s four designated fund groups and on a combined Agency-wide basis.
J. Clearly identify the components, assumptions, actuarial cost method, amortization method and period, asset valuation method, and other factors used in the development of the ADCs.

## GASB 75 Financial Reporting Services
The consultant shall provide the actuarial basis for SHRA’s GASB 75 financial reporting for retiree healthcare implicit subsidy and explicit subsidy for the fiscal years ending December 31, 2026, December 31, 2027, December 31, 2028, December 31, 2029, and December 31, 2030.
For purposes of this engagement, the GASB 75 reporting shall be structured as follows:
A. The GASB 75 reports for fiscal years ending December 31, 2026, and December 31, 2027, shall be based on the December 31, 2025 actuarial valuation. 
B. The GASB 75 reports for fiscal years ending December 31, 2028, and December 31, 2029, shall be based on the December 31, 2027 actuarial valuation.
C. The GASB 75 reports for fiscal years ending December 31, 2030, shall be based on the December 31, 2029 actuarial valuation.

Each GASB 75 report shall include the actuarial information needed by SHRA and its auditor to assist in preparing the Agency’s Annual Comprehensive Financial Report.
The work product shall include the actuarial schedules, exhibits, and supporting information necessary for GASB 75 compliance and audit support, including, as applicable:
    A. Total OPEB Liability
    B. Fiduciary Net Position, if applicable
    C. Net OPEB Liability
    D. OPEB expense
    E. Deferred outflows of resources and deferred inflows of resources
    F. Sensitivity disclosures required by GASB 75
    G. Schedules of changes in Net OPEB Liability and related ratios
H. Schedule of contributions, if applicable
I. Actuarially Determined Contribution (ADC) and related contribution schedules, calculated separately for each of the four designated fund groups and in total, as applicable
J. Projected benefit payment schedules
K. Notes regarding actuarial methods and assumptions
L. Supporting exhibits and schedules reasonably required for audit review
The work product shall not include draft Other Post-Employment Benefits (OPEB) footnotes for SHRA’s financial statements.

## Data Review and Validation
The consultant shall:
Provide SHRA with a data request identifying the information needed to perform the valuation and GASB 75 work.
Review census, premium, contribution, trust, and plan data provided by SHRA for reasonableness, consistency, and completeness.
Identify data concerns, anomalies, or missing information and work with SHRA staff to resolve such issues.
Clearly identify the extent of reliance on Agency-provided data and any limitations affecting the results.

## Assumptions, Methods, and Compliance
The consultant shall:
Apply actuarial methods and assumptions appropriate to the assignment and compliant with applicable Actuarial Standards of Practice.
Prepare work products that allow SHRA to report in compliance with GASB 75.
Clearly disclose all actuarial assumptions, methods, and sources of information used.
Identify and explain any changes in assumptions or methods from prior reports and quantify their effect where material.
Maintain work papers and documentation sufficient to support the conclusions presented in the reports.

## Consultation and Agency Support
The consultant shall provide reasonable consultation, presentation, and technical support in connection with the actuarial services throughout the term of the engagement. Such support shall include communication of actuarial results to Agency staff, executive management, the Board, Board committees, and the Agency’s independent auditor, as requested by SHRA.
At a minimum, the consultant shall:
A. Conduct a kickoff discussion with Agency staff regarding project schedule, data needs, assumptions, deliverables, and reporting requirements.
    B. Meet or confer with Agency staff to review draft and final valuation results, GASB 75 reports, and related actuarial findings.
    C. Explain significant findings, changes in liabilities, reporting impacts, and major actuarial assumptions and methods in a clear and understandable manner.
    D. Assist SHRA staff in understanding the distinction between explicit subsidy, implicit subsidy, and combined reporting results, including the financial statement impact of each.
    E. Provide reasonable consultation to Agency staff regarding actuarial calculations, assumptions, report content, and related technical issues.
F. Present the results of actuarial valuation reports, ADCs, and GASB 75 reports to Agency staff, executive management, the governing Board, Board committees, or other designated decision-making bodies, as requested by SHRA.
    G. Be available to answer questions from Agency staff, executive management, Board members, and the Agency’s independent auditor regarding the actuarial reports and GASB 75 reporting.
    H. Provide executive summaries, presentation materials, or Board-ready summaries of actuarial results, if requested by SHRA.
    I. Participate in meetings in person or by videoconference, as requested by SHRA and mutually scheduled.
    J. Respond to Agency questions and requests for clarification in a timely manner throughout the engagement.
The base scope shall include one kickoff meeting, one staff review meeting per cycle, and one presentation associated with each valuation and each annual GASB 75 reporting cycle. Proposers shall separately identify any assumptions or additional fees associated with meetings beyond those included in the base scope.

## Auditor Support
The consultant shall provide reasonable assistance to SHRA and its independent auditor in connection with the actuarial reports and GASB 75 reporting, including:
Responding to auditor questions regarding methods, assumptions, and calculations.
Providing supporting schedules and explanations reasonably required for the audit process.
Assisting in reconciliation of actuarial information presented in the Agency’s Annual Comprehensive Financial Report.

## Deliverables
At a minimum, the consultant shall provide the following deliverables:
A. Valuation Reports
1. Actuarial Valuation Report as of December 31, 2025 
2. Actuarial Valuation Report as of December 31, 2027 
3. Actuarial Valuation Report as of December 31, 2029 
4. ADC schedules associated with each valuation, including calculations by each of SHRA’s four designated fund groups and in total
B. GASB 75 Report
For each applicable Annual Financial Statement reporting year, three GASB 75 reports:
      1. Explicit subsidy only
      2. Implicit subsidy only
    3. Explicit subsidy plus implicit subsidy
Specifically, the engagement shall include GASB 75 actuarial reporting support for:
a. December 31, 2026
b. December 31, 2027
c. December 31, 2028
d. December 31, 2029
e. December 31, 2030
with report basis as follows:
a. FYE 2026 GASB 75 reports based on the December 31, 2025 valuation
b. FYE 2027 GASB 75 reports based on the December 31, 2025 valuation
c. FYE 2028 GASB 75 reports based on the December 31, 2027 valuation
d. FYE 2029 GASB 75 reports based on the December 31, 2027 valuation
e. FYE 2030 GASB 75 reports based on the December 31, 2029 valuation
C. Presentation and Meeting Support
a. Kickoff meeting at the beginning of the engagement.
b. Staff review meeting for each actuarial valuation and annual GASB 75 reporting cycle.
c. Presentation of actuarial valuation, ADC, and/or GASB 75 results to Agency staff, executive management, the governing Board, Board committees, or other designated bodies, as requested by SHRA.
d. Presentation materials, executive summaries, or Board-ready materials, as requested by SHRA.
 
D. Format
All reports shall be provided in electronic PDF format, with key schedules provided in Excel or other editable format if requested by SHRA.

## Optional and Additional Services
Because this Scope of Work is intended as a general guide and not a complete listing of all required services, SHRA reserves the right to request additional related actuarial services under the resulting agreement, including but not limited to:
Special studies or scenario modeling
Alternative funding analyses
Trust sufficiency or depletion projections
Sensitivity analyses beyond standard GASB disclosures
Additional consulting related to OPEB funding strategy, budgeting, or policy evaluation
