Solicitation Text:
## Project Overview
The Sacramento Housing and Redevelopment Agency, on behalf of SHARP, seeks qualified security guard services for the residential portion of Edge Water Apartments. SHARP is also requesting an alternate option that extends the same patrol service to Capital Terrace as a separate service location. The selected firm will provide a visible security presence through regular foot patrols, observe and report suspicious or unauthorized activity, deter loitering and trespassing, and respond appropriately to incidents. The parking garage is a secondary patrol area and is not the primary focus of this assignment.

## Agency Contact
It is recommended that specific questions regarding requirements be submitted via the Question & Answer module of the project page.
All other communications regarding this Solicitation shall be directed to:
SHARP Procurement Services
Address: 801 12th Street, Sacramento CA 95814
Phone: (916) 440-1378
Email: 
psSHARP@shra.org
OpenGov Portal: 
https://procurement.opengov.com/portal/shra
Unauthorized contact with other Agency staff or evaluation committee members regarding this Solicitation may result in disqualification

## Property and Service Information
First property
Edge Water Apartments
Service address
626 I Street, Sacramento, CA 95814
Second property
Capital Terrace
Second service address
1820 Capitol Avenue, Sacramento, CA 95814
Requested start
As soon as practicable following award and notice to proceed
Initial term
One year, with optional additional 4 years
Coverage days
Monday-Sunday, including observed California holidays.
Coverage hours
17:30–07:30 the following day.
Base staffing
Coverage shall be at least one unarmed security guard available per scheduled shift, per site. Relief staff for all mandated breaks, lunches, etc. can be used, as required by law.
Primary areas
Residential buildings, residential floors, entrances, walkways, and other resident-access areas designated by SHARP
Secondary areas
Parking garage, as time and conditions permit
SHARP representative
Jeana Thomas, Regional Manager, or designee

## Basis of Award and Validity Date
The basis of award for this IFQ is cost reasonableness, responsiveness to the requirements of the solicitation
, 
and ability to perform within required timeframe.
The Agency intends to award one (1) Agreement; however, the Agency reserves the right to make multiple awards or to award specific components of the Services, where it determines such action to be in its best interest.
Quotes submitted to the Agency shall remain valid for a period 
of 
180 days
 c
alendar days from the submission deadline, unless otherwise extended by mutual agreement.
Ultimately, the Agency may also make no award if it determines that no Quotations are in its best interest.

## Quotation Submission and Requirements
Quotations for the requested goods and/or services must be submitted by the dates listed in Timeline.
Please submit your responses via the Vendor Questionnaire and submit all requested documentation via the upload questions.

## Clarification and Interviews
The Agency may request clarifications or conduct interviews after the IFQ Submission Deadline. If the Agency elects to conduct interviews, it will be noted in Timeli
General Requirements
ne.
Clarifications or interviews are not scored and are merely to verify or obtain more detail regarding the information provided in the Quotation submission.

## Determination of Responsiveness
The Agency reserves the right to determine whether a Quotation is responsive and to reject any Quotation deemed non-responsive.
The Agency reserves the right to waive minor informalities or irregularities in Quotations that do not materially affect the solicitation process or prejudice other Contractors.

## Reports and Notifications
Complete a Daily Activity Report for every shift. At a minimum, each report shall identify the guard, date and shift hours, patrol times and areas, observations, contacts, actions taken, and any unresolved follow-up item.
Submit the Daily Activity Report to Jeana Thomas or the SHARP designee at the end of each shift, anticipated at 7:00 a.m., for office review. Submit the report by email to 
regionalmanagers@shra.org
. 
Provide an option for a Guard Tour System. 
Prepare a separate detailed incident report for any event involving police, fire, emergency medical services, violence or threats, suspected criminal conduct, significant property damage, resident injury, or other serious occurrence.
For emergencies, call 911 first, then notify the designated SHARP after-hours contact and the primary property contact. Notify SHARP as soon as practicable and no later than one hour after the occurrence unless emergency conditions prevent timely notice.
Immediately notify SHARP of any missed shift, late arrival, early departure, or interruption in coverage. The firm shall provide a qualified replacement without additional delay.

## Guard and Firm Qualifications
Maintain all licenses, permits, registrations, insurance, training, and certifications required for private security services in California throughout the contract term.
Assign guards who are trained in foot patrol procedures, report writing, emergency response, conflict de-escalation, professional communication, and fair and respectful interaction with residents.
Conduct legally required screening and background checks before assignment. Upon request, the firm shall confirm that assigned personnel satisfy all applicable requirements.
Provide a field supervisor who is available during service hours and can respond promptly to staffing, performance, or incident concerns.
Require guards to wear a clean professional uniform with company identification and to carry all required credentials while on duty.
Prohibit sleeping, smoking or vaping outside designated areas, personal visitors, excessive personal phone use, and other conduct that interferes with assigned duties.

## General Compliance
The Contractor shall comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws, regulations, ordinances, rules, codes, and other legal requirements that pertain to the solicitation, award, and performance of the Contract. This includes requirements in effect when the solicitation is issued, as well as any applicable amendments, revisions, or successor requirements that become effective during the contract term. The Contractor is responsible for identifying and maintaining compliance with all legal requirements applicable to its work, including requirements applicable to its employees, subcontractors, licenses, permits, wages, safety, and performance of the Contract.

## Public Records
All Quotations are subject to disclosure pursuant to the California Public Records Act following award of the Agreement.

## Quotation Costs
The Agency is not responsible for any costs incurred in preparation or submission of Quotations.

## Staffing Changes and Site Access
The firm shall notify SHARP at least one hour before a planned staffing change and immediately upon learning of an unplanned change. SHARP may request removal or replacement of assigned personnel for documented performance, conduct, safety, or site-suitability concerns, subject to applicable law and contract terms.
SHARP may provide keys, access credentials, or other property items needed for the work. The firm is responsible for controlling and safeguarding those items. Lost or compromised items must be reported immediately. The firm may be responsible for reasonable replacement, rekeying, or access-restoration costs resulting from its loss or misuse.

## Breaks and Relief Coverage
The firm is solely responsible for compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local wage-and-hour requirements. Pricing shall include any relief staffing necessary to maintain the coverage required by this Scope of Work. A scheduled fixed post shall not be left unattended during meal or rest periods.

## Quotation Submission
Quotations must be submitted by the specified deadline in the Solicitation Timeline. Contractors are responsible for ensuring timely submission and are encouraged to initiate uploads sufficiently in advance of the deadline.
The Agency may accept late submissions, or submissions other than non-electronic submission, only where such acceptance does not compromise fair and open competition and is consistent with applicable procurement requirements.
The Agency reserves all rights permitted under applicable law, including the right to reject any or all Quotations, request additional information, or modify the scope of Services. The Agency may cancel, amend, or reissue this Solicitation at any time and for any reason.
The Agency’s determinations under this Solicitation shall be final to the extent permitted by applicable law.

## Questions and Addenda
All questions must be submitted via OpenGov as indicated in the Solicitation Timeline.
Responses and any addenda will be posted via OpenGov. The Agency is not responsible for oral interpretations. All addenda issued by the Agency are incorporated by reference and become part of the Solicitation, and if issued, the resulting Agreement.

## Agency Coordination and Quality Control
SHARP and the firm shall meet as reasonably needed to exchange information, review performance, update post orders, and address security concerns.
The firm shall maintain supervisory review of patrol performance and reports and shall promptly correct missed patrols, incomplete reports, attendance problems, or unprofessional conduct.
SHARP may adjust patrol priorities within the property based on operational needs, provided the change does not materially expand staffing hours or the overall scope without a written amendment.

## Term and Maximum Compensation of Agreement
The Agency intends to a
ward one (1) Agreement for the Services descri
bed in this Solicitation.
Any extension of the Agreement shall be subject to satisfactory performance and the Agency’s continued need for the Services.
The Contractor may request adjustments to pricing in connection with any renewal period by submitting a written request at least sixty (60) calendar days prior to the expiration of the then-current term. Any such request shall include reasonable supporting documentation. The Agency reserves the right, in its sole discretion, to approve, negotiate, or reject any requested pricing adjustments. Any unilateral adjustment to pricing by the Contractor shall constitute a material breach of the Agreement.
Contractors are advised to review the sample Agreement and all attachments prior to submission of a Quotation. Contractors are responsible for identifying and resolving any internal concerns with the terms of the Agreement prior to submission. The Agency intends to award the Agreement substantially in the form provided and does not anticipate accepting exceptions. The Agency reserves the right, in its sole discretion, to reject any Quotation or deem it non-responsive if it contains exceptions, deviations, or proposed modifications to the Agreement, particularly where such exceptions are material or inconsistent with the Agency’s requirements.

## Acceptance of Services
Services will be accepted based on complete scheduled coverage, performance of required patrols, timely and accurate reporting, compliance with post orders, professional conduct, and prompt correction of deficiencies. SHARP may verify attendance and patrol activity through reports, site observations, available access records, or other reasonable documentation.

## Observed Holidays
For purposes of preparing the Pricing Proposal, holiday dates shall follow the State of California holiday calendar, available at 
https://www.sos.ca.gov/state-holidays
. Holiday hours shall be included in the Pricing Proposal line items corresponding to holiday hourly rates.
Agency staff will observe the Agency’s holiday and closure schedule, available at 
https://www.shra.org/contact-us/
, which may differ from the State of California calendar. Both websites currently list 2026 dates and may be amended over time, including to reflect 2027 holidays and closure dates.
Agency offices are also closed every other Friday and for one full week in December. These closures do not independently qualify as holidays for security guard staffing or pricing purposes; holiday pricing applies only to dates designated under the State of California calendar.

## Scope of Work for Food Service Providers RFSQ
The County of San Mateo is creating a Food Services Directory to connect certified food providers with County staff who need food services for various events and programs. This is not a formal proposal process; it’s a simple process in which your business can be included in our go-to list of food vendors. We encourage all food providers certified by the San Mateo County Environmental Health Services Food Program to apply.
This directory will help ensure staff can quickly and easily find and identify food vendors who meet the diverse needs of their event(s), from casual lunches to formal celebrations.
The directory will remain active for two (2) years from the launch date and used by County staff to source meals for a wide variety of occasions.
How it works: 
When staff need food services, they’ll search the directory and may either select a vendor directly or request quotes from the list. Once services are provided, vendors will invoice the requesting County Department directly. All submitted and approved invoices shall be paid on a 
Net 30
 basis (within 30 days of receiving the invoice).
Please note: 
County staff are not permitted to pay by credit card
, so all transactions must be invoiced.
This is a great opportunity for food providers to get visibility and be considered for future County catering needs. We invite all qualified vendors to submit their information for inclusion in the directory.
1. Specifications and Standards:
The selected Proposers shall be required to adhere to the following specifications and standards as set by the County of San Mateo's Environmental Health Department:
*San Mateo County Environmental Health Services Food Program inspects and permits all food sold in restaurants, markets, schools, mobile facilities, special events, and more. You can find more information on these food programs below. To see inspection results or facility closures, please visit the 
Food Safety page
.
1.1 Licenses and Qualifications.
The Proposer must have a valid business license (business, health and beverage sales/service) in compliance with all applicable County of San Mateo, State of California, and U.S. Government code requirements and regulations (must provide copies of applicable licenses under attachments).
All Proposers must be able to furnish proof of insurance, including general liability and worker's compensation coverage.
All Proposers must comply with the California Food Code and any applicable County specific Health Regulations.
1.2 Menu Offerings.
Proposers shall offer a wide range of menu options, including but not limited to:
Breakfast, lunch, and dinner options
Buffet-style service
Plated meal service
Boxed and pre-packaged meals
Appetizers and snacks
Desserts and beverages
*Please be detailed in your general food category.
Menus must include vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options.
Proposer shall also be required to accommodate food allergies or special dietary requirements upon request. 
1.3 Quality Standards.
All food and beverages must be prepared in sanitary conditions and served at appropriate temperatures to ensure safety and quality.
All products must be fresh and prepared with high-quality ingredients, ideally sourced locally when possible.
Proposers must comply with all food safety standards and have protocols in place for handling food allergens.
1.4 Staffing Requirements.
All staff of each Proposer must be professionally trained and knowledgeable about food safety requirements.
Proposers staff shall wear appropriate uniforms and adhere to professional standards of appearance when on site in any County of San Mateo building or event.
Proposers serving staff shall be available to set up, serve, and clean up at designated events on an as needed basis.
2. Service Requirements:
Selected Proposers must demonstrate the ability to provide services that adhere to the following requirements:
2.1 Event Coordination.
Proposers shall be available for pre-event planning consultations to discuss menu options, dietary restrictions, and logistics.
Proposers shall provide all necessary equipment, including serving utensils, tableware, and linens, unless otherwise specified by the County.
Set-up, execution, and breakdown of service areas should be conducted efficiently to avoid disruption to the event or facility/location.
2.2 Customer Service.
Proposer shall provide a point of contact for the County to facilitate communication regarding orders and service.
Proposers service personnel must be courteous, professional, and responsive to any requests from the County staff during events.
2.3 Payment Method.
Proposers shall meet the required method of payment by the County of San Mateo through invoice, 30-day net.
3. Delivery Requirements:
The successful Proposers will be tasked with meeting specific delivery requirements as follows:
3.1 Delivery Locations
Deliveries will be made to various locations within San Mateo County region, including County offices, community centers, and other event venues.
Proposers must confirm delivery addresses and any special access instructions prior to the event.
3.2 Packaging (in adherence to SB1383)
*As of January 2022, 
state law (SB 1383)
 requires large food generating entities to hold a contract or written agreement with a food recovery organization for the recovery of their surplus food for redistribution to those in need in the community. For more information, visit 
smcsustainability.org/ediblefoodrecovery
.
Proposers shall include in their proposals packages; Compostable Paper Service to include but not limited to the following napkins, tablecloths, plastic knives forks, spoons, serving size forks, spoons, and tongs, and coffee stirrers, etc.
All food must be packaged in a manner that ensures safety, quality, and freshness during transportation.
3.3 Delivery Schedule.
Deliveries must be made within the scheduled timeframe as agreed upon during the planning phase.
In the case of unforeseen circumstances affecting delivery, the Proposer must notify the County contact immediately.

## Ubiquiti Security Camera, Network Equipment, and Supporting Hardware Installation
1. Project Description
 
The Contractor shall provide all labor, tools, equipment, installation materials, and miscellaneous hardware necessary to install, configure, test, and place into service a Ubiquiti security camera and network system at three (3) radio sites located in San Mateo County, California.
 
Each site will receive approximately seven (7) to nine (9) Ubiquiti security cameras, with cameras installed both inside and outside of the site structures. The anticipated total installation is approximately 21–27 cameras.
 
Each site shall also receive the Ubiquiti network, recording, cellular failover, rack, and environmental monitoring equipment identified in Section 3.
 
The Contractor shall provide a complete, professional, operational installation, including equipment mounting, network cabling, conduit and fittings, cable termination, weatherproofing, equipment configuration, labeling, testing, commissioning, and cleanup.
 
2. Camera Installation
 
The Contractor shall:
Install approximately 7–9 Ubiquiti security cameras at each radio site.
Install cameras at locations designated by the Owner or Owner's representative.
Install cameras both inside and outside the applicable structures.
Provide and install all required camera mounting hardware, brackets, anchors, fasteners, and miscellaneous supporting hardware.
Properly secure and align each camera to provide the required field of view.
Route and secure all camera cabling from each camera to the designated network equipment.
Protect exposed cabling from weather, UV exposure, physical damage, and other environmental conditions.
Provide appropriate cable protection and routing for all exterior installations.

each of the three (3) radio sites

4. Rack and Equipment Installation
 
The Contractor shall assemble and install one U-Rack-6U-TL Toolless Mini Rack at each site.
 
The Contractor shall:
Assemble the rack in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions.
Install and secure the rack in the designated location.
Verify that the rack is level and stable.
Secure all network equipment within the rack as appropriate.
Install the UACC-UCG-Industrial-RM 19-inch rack ears on the UCG-Industrial.
Properly arrange and secure all equipment and cabling.
Maintain appropriate airflow and equipment clearances.
Utilize the rack's lockable casters where applicable.
Provide cable management and strain relief as necessary.
The final rack installation shall be neat, accessible, and suitable for ongoing maintenance.

At each site, the Contractor shall install and connect:
 
UCG-Industrial – Cloud Gateway Industrial
The Contractor shall install the UCG-Industrial as the designated site network gateway/core device.

Rack mounting using the specified

Network connections.
WAN connection.
LAN connections.
Connection to the Ubiquiti network infrastructure.
Configuration as directed by the Owner.
Verification of network connectivity.

The Contractor shall install one 
UNVR-Pro Network Video Recorder Pro
 at each site.
 
Installation shall include:
Rack installation.
Network connection.
Connection to the camera network.
Installation of recording/storage drives if provided by the Owner.
Configuration of the recorder as directed by the Owner.
Verification that all installed cameras communicate with the recorder.
Verification of recording functionality.
USW-Pro-8-PoE – Network Switch
The Contractor shall install one 
USW-Pro-8-PoE
 at each site.
 
Installation shall include:
Rack installation.
Network uplink connection.
PoE connections to applicable cameras and other powered devices.
Configuration as directed by the Owner.
Verification of PoE operation.
Verification of network connectivity for all connected devices.
The Contractor shall organize camera connections and switch ports in a logical and documented manner.
 
U5G-Max-Outdoor – Cellular WAN Failover
The Contractor shall install one 
U5G-Max-Outdoor
 cellular WAN failover device at each site.
 
Installation shall include:
Mounting of the outdoor cellular device at an Owner-approved location.
Installation of required network cabling.
Installation of required conduit and fittings for exterior cable routing.
Weatherproofing of all exterior penetrations.
Connection to the site's network gateway.
Configuration of cellular WAN failover as directed by the Owner.
Verification of network connectivity and failover functionality, subject to cellular service availability.
The Owner shall be responsible for providing or activating any required cellular service/account unless otherwise specified.
 
UP-Sense – Temperature/Humidity Sensor

 at each site.
 
The sensor shall be installed at an Owner-approved location within the applicable equipment/radio structure or equipment area.
 
Installation shall include:
Physical mounting.

Configuration and enrollment as directed by the Owner.
Verification of temperature and humidity readings.
Verification that the sensor is reporting to the applicable Ubiquiti management system.
 
6. Network Cabling
 
The Contractor shall furnish and install all network cabling required for the complete installation.
 
The Contractor shall provide:
Weather-rated CAT 6 Ethernet cable
 for exterior and environmentally exposed installations.
CAT 6 cable for interior installations where appropriate.
All required RJ45/network connectors.
Cable terminations at cameras, switches, gateways, recorders, cellular equipment, and other network equipment.
Patch cables and interconnection cables as required.
Cable supports, clips, ties, management hardware, and other miscellaneous installation materials.
 
All network cabling shall be installed in a neat, secure, and professional manner and shall be properly supported throughout the installation.
 
7. Conduit and Fittings
 
The Contractor shall furnish and install all conduit and fittings required to protect and route network cabling.
 
This shall include, as required:
Exterior-rated conduit.
Interior conduit or raceway.
Conduit fittings and connectors.
Weatherproof junction boxes.
Bushings and cable protection.
Clamps, straps, supports, and mounting hardware.
Sleeves and other penetration protection.
 
Conduit shall be installed in a manner that protects the cabling and provides a clean and professional finished installation.
 
8. Weatherproofing and Building Penetrations
 
Weatherproofing of all Contractor-created holes and penetrations is mandatory.
 
The Contractor shall properly seal and weatherproof 
every hole, penetration, opening, or attachment point created during the installation
.
 
This includes, but is not limited to:
Camera mounting holes.
Camera cable penetrations.
Conduit penetrations.
Wall penetrations.
Roof penetrations.
Junction box penetrations.
Cellular equipment mounting penetrations.
Network cable penetrations.
Equipment mounting penetrations.
Any other openings created in the structure.
 
Weatherproofing materials shall be appropriate for the installation surface and environmental conditions and shall be applied in accordance with the manufacturer's recommendations.
 
The Contractor shall be responsible for preventing water intrusion resulting from its installation activities.
 
9. Camera and Network Configuration
 
The Contractor shall perform initial configuration and commissioning of the installed Ubiquiti equipment as directed by the Owner.
 
Configuration shall include, as applicable:
Adoption of Ubiquiti network devices.
Network switch configuration.
PoE configuration.
Gateway configuration.
Camera adoption and configuration.
UNVR-Pro configuration.
Camera recording configuration.
Cellular WAN failover configuration.
UP-Sense sensor enrollment and configuration.
Device naming and identification.
Basic network connectivity verification.
 
The Owner shall provide any required administrative credentials, network addressing information, cloud accounts, cellular service information, and other account information necessary for configuration.
 
10. Testing and Commissioning
 
After installation at each site, the Contractor shall test and commission the system.
 
Testing shall include:
Verification that each camera powers on.
Verification of network connectivity.
Verification of video transmission.
Verification that each camera is properly communicating with the UNVR-Pro.
Verification of camera recording functionality.
Verification of PoE operation.
Verification of network cable terminations.
Verification of UCG-Industrial network connectivity.
Verification of USW-Pro-8-PoE operation.
Verification of U5G-Max-Outdoor connectivity and failover functionality, where cellular service is available.
Verification of UP-Sense temperature/humidity reporting.
Inspection of conduit and cable routing.
Inspection of all exterior penetrations and weatherproofing.
 
The Contractor shall correct any installation-related deficiencies identified during testing.
 
11. Cable and Equipment Labeling
 
The Contractor shall provide permanent and legible identification for installed network cables and equipment.
 
Labels shall identify, as applicable:
Camera identification.
Camera cable.
Network switch.
Switch port.
UNVR-Pro.
UCG-Industrial.
Cellular WAN equipment.
UP-Sense sensor.
Other major network connections.
 
Labeling shall be consistent across all three sites.
 
12. Site Protection and Cleanup
 
The Contractor shall protect existing radio-site equipment and infrastructure during installation.
 
The Contractor shall:
Coordinate site access with the Owner.
Avoid disruption to existing radio and communications equipment.
Protect existing equipment, cabling, structures, and finishes.
Maintain a clean work area.
Remove all construction debris, cable scraps, packaging, and unused installation materials upon completion.
Leave each site in a clean and orderly condition.
 
13. Vendor-Furnished Materials
 
The Vendor shall furnish all materials required to complete the installation, including but not limited to:
Weather-rated CAT 6 cable.
Interior CAT 6 cable where required.
RJ45/network connectors.
Conduit.
Conduit fittings.
Weatherproof junction boxes and fittings.
Cable supports and management hardware.
Camera mounting brackets and hardware.
Anchors and fasteners.
Patch cables.
Weatherproofing/sealing materials.
Miscellaneous hardware, consumables, and installation materials.
 
The Vendor shall not charge additional fees for ordinary incidental materials necessary to complete the installation unless specifically authorized by the Owner.
 
14. Owner-Furnished Equipment
 
The Owner will furnish the Ubiquiti cameras and network equipment identified in Section 3.
 
The Contractor shall be responsible for the proper installation, connection, configuration, testing, and commissioning of Owner-furnished equipment.

## Protest of Non-Responsiveness Determination
Within five (5) working days of the County's issuance of a notice of non-responsiveness, any firm that has submitted a proposal and believes that the County has incorrectly determined that its proposal is non-responsive may submit a written notice of protest.  Such notice of protest must be received by the County on or before the fifth working day following the County's issuance of the notice of non-responsiveness.  The notice of protest must include a written statement specifying in detail each and every one of the grounds asserted for the protest.  The protest must be signed by an individual authorized to represent the proposer, and must cite the law, rule, local ordinance, procedure or RFP provision on which the protest is based.  In addition, the protestor must specify facts and evidence sufficient for the County to determine the validity of the protest.

## Overview
The expected tasks and deliverables for the selected project manager(s) are described below. The project manager will be responsible for:
Managing County project team 
Maintaining and managing the implementation of of systems associated with an assigned project and in accordance with a project plan
Working with vendor’s project team, coordinating and aligning the work, managing the issues and risks, and reviewing deliverables
Ensuring project management, training and communication are effective (and adjusted accordingly if goals are not met)
Reviewing and approving staffing changes of the vendor in consultation with County staff
Serving as consultant to the project sponsor and/or team members as requested
Escalating issues and facilitating decision processes in connection with any assigned project
Managing scope, schedule and budget
Working with County Department subject matter experts to ensure business  and technical requirements are met within the scope of the project.
Completing a post implementation review, including interviews with a few operating departments, key project members, and the vendor.
Reviewing and recommending approval vendor invoices as requested
Providing hands-on assistance with detailed tasks relating to any assigned project as needed
Coordinating work of other project team members for work related to:
Planning
Design
Configuration and Development
Business process documentation
Testing
Data conversion and data validation
Integration testing
Change management and County readiness
Training
In addition to the foregoing, the selected project manager(s) will be expected to execute the tasks and provide the deliverables described below. The specific deliverables described below represent ongoing categories of work to be accomplished over the course of any assigned project.
1. Project Plan updates:
 The selected project manager will be responsible for working with vendor project manager(s), make updates to the project plan as appropriate. Updates include recording current status on a regular basis, providing more specificity of tasks on a 90-day rolling forward basis. The project manager will also maintain executive dashboard status as reflected in the project plan.
2. Manage project scope, schedule, budget
: The selected project manager(s) will be responsible for following standard industry IT project management practices and for carefully managing the project scope, schedule and budget to deliver a quality system and efficient business processes to the County on schedule and in budget. This will require the project manager to carefully manage the relationship with the vendor who is responsible for most of the key deliverables to meet this objective. County project team roles vary depending on the project activity, sometimes the role supports the work, other times the County is responsible for the activity. The project manager will help guide the team while influencing the success of the associated vendor and their ability to deliver.
3. Manage County project team and County assigned project activities:
 The selected project manager will be responsible for providing expert guidance, mentor team members and coordinate the work of County team members for each stage of the project.
4. Effectively Navigate Implementation/Integration Requirements: 
The selected project manager(s) can demonstrate fluency in selected software and associated platforms. The selected project manager shall also engage with the County’s requirement to integrate chosen software systems with other County software systems. Implementation and integration work shall be performed in a manner to ensure accurate and transparent transfer of data between County systems.
5. Coordinate with vendor on project activities (e.g., planning, testing, deployment)
 The selected project manager(s) will be responsible for proactively working to plan the approach, strategies and specific tasks needed to be accomplished for work to be done by both the vendor and/or the County project team. The selected project manager(s) will be responsible for prioritizing and managing to the scope and schedule, maintaining rigor on change request review procedures, setting expectations up front for the format and content of documentation and deliverables and reviewing vendor deliverables.
6. Issue and Risk Management: 
The selected project manager(s) will be responsible for managing the issues log, review and assigning resources for issue resolution; assessing risks, developing risk mitigation strategies; escalating risks and issues to the County Project Sponsor, and following through and facilitating decision process.
7. Working with Stakeholders:
 This project requires the project manager(s) to coordinate numerous interactions with the various County stakeholders to address concerns, manage expectations, facilitate decisions and acceptance of business process and system design.
8. Coordinate with County Departments:
 The project manager(s) will coordinate project activities requiring Department involvement to ensure Department resources are available to perform tasks related to integration testing, data validation, end user testing and training to ultimately get their acceptance prior to Go Live.
9. Manage project quality:
 The project manager(s) is responsible for ensuring project quality. This includes a number of aspects of quality: validating with testing that the system and custom development items work and meet the business requirements, validating that vendor deliverables meet the standards described in their contract scope of work, and other aspects of project quality needed to make this project successful.
10. Provide expert guidance for sub-project work:
 The project manager(s) will be expected to bring a wealth of experience to provide strategy guidance to the team. The project manager will help team members and coordinate the work of team leads and team members for work related to:
•Design
•Testing
•Configuration and Development
•Business process documentation
•Data conversions and data validation
•Integration testing
•Change management and County readiness.
•Training
•Cutover planning, preparation and actual cutover
•Post-production support
11. Status Reporting and Project Documentation: 
The project manager(s) must report status on a regular basis through a number of types of status and project documentation, for example: project plans, dashboard reports, issue statements/decision papers, issue logs, testing results reporting, and risk mitigation plans.

## Role Summary and QA Tester Responsibilities
The County is looking for one or more Quality Assurance (QA) testers. The QA tester is responsible for ensuring the quality, functionality, and reliability of a software platform application and configurations before they are deployed to production environments. They work with County subject matter experts, vendor developers, other QA testers, business/systems analyst, and other stakeholders to ensure that solutions meet business requirements and are free of defects.
QA Tester Responsibilities:
Requirement Analysis:
 Collaborate with County and vendor staff, and stakeholders to understand business requirements, user stories, and technical specifications, translating them into detailed test cases.
Test Planning and Execution
: Design, write, and execute comprehensive test cases for all functionalities, features, and bug fixes related to the platform functionality
Types of Testing
: Perform various types of manual testing, including functional, regression, integration, user acceptance testing (UAT), security, and performance testing.
Defect Management:
 Identify, document, track, and report application defects/bugs using bug tracking system and work closely with vendor QA testers to ensure timely resolution and verification of fixes.
Configuration and Customization Validation
: Validate platform configurations (e.g., custom objects, fields, layouts, flows, validation rules, permission sets) and custom Apex code to ensure they function as expected and align with requirements.
Integration Testing:
 Ensure seamless and accurate data exchange between system platform(s) using APIs (REST) and tools like Postman if appropriate.
Data Validation:
 Verify data integrity and accuracy during data migration or routine operations using tools like Data Loader and database queries (SOQL/SQL).
Collaboration and Communication:
 Provide testing status updates and reports, and support County users during Integration Testing and UAT.

## Key Skills and Qualifications
Technical Proficiency: Strong understanding of various enterprise, SaaS, or complex business-system implementations and other platforms utilized by public agencies, configurations, and customization options.
Testing Expertise: Knowledge of testing methodologies (Agile, Scrum) and experience with test management tools (e.g., Jira, Postman).
Analytical Skills: Strong problem-solving, analytical, and debugging skills with keen attention to detail.
Communication: Excellent verbal and written communication skills to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams and stakeholders.

Description:
Certified public accountancy services are needed to support the Public Administrator and Public Guardian programs with preparation and filing of tax returns for decedents, conserved persons, and other cases under the program’s jurisdiction. Services may include gathering and reviewing financial records, preparing federal and state individual income tax returns, identifying filing requirements and deadlines, coordinating with program staff on documentation, and ensuring compliance with applicable tax laws and reporting obligations.
The San Mateo County Public Guardian program serves older adults and adults with physical or mental disabilities who lack capacity to provide for their needs. The Public Guardian may be appointed for clients without alternative, appropriate conservators. Deputy Public Guardians (DPGs) arrange health care, housing, meals, transportation, personal care, and recreation for conservatees. DPGs also gather and manage client assets, apply for public benefits, and collect and pay bills. There are two types of conservatorships: probate and LPS, discussed below. The Public Guardian serves both probate and LPS conservatees, but the legal standards for the conservatorships and the populations served are different.
The San Mateo County Public Administrator helps families manage the affairs of a loved one who has passed away with dignity, respect, and care. Serving as a neutral third party, the Public Administrator can handle every aspect of estate management, from securing property and paying bills to locating heirs, liquidating assets, and distributing inheritance, without the need to hire an attorney. Services include making burial arrangements, closing accounts, and investigating potential assets, providing peace of mind during a difficult time. The office may be appointed by heirs, named in a will, or assigned by the court when no administrator exists. Fees are based on estate value and subject to court approval.

The County seeks a qualified Certified Public Accountant (CPA) firm to provide tax compliance, tax return preparation, filing support, and related tax consultation services for matters administered by the County’s Public Administrator and Public Guardian Programs.
The Contractor will provide tax-related services for conserved persons, decedents’ estates, trusts, and other persons or entities for which the County holds legal authority or responsibility. Services will be performed only upon County referral or written authorization. The County does not guarantee a minimum number of assignments, tax returns, billable hours, or total compensation under any resulting agreement.
The Contractor shall perform all services in accordance with applicable federal and California tax laws; Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and California Franchise Tax Board (FTB) filing requirements; professional standards applicable to Certified Public Accountants; the County’s confidentiality and information-security requirements; and the terms of the resulting agreement.

## Tax Research, Analysis, and Advisory Services
The Contractor shall provide tax research and advisory services necessary to support Public Administrator and Public Guardian operations, including:
A. Research complex tax circumstances affecting Public Administrator and Public Guardian clientele, including amending prior‑year returns and evaluating historical filing accuracy.
B. Determine tax‑basis values when records are incomplete or unavailable, including developing recommended basis values supported by reasonable assumptions and industry standards.
C. Consult on filing requirements for federal, state, and local returns, including identifying missing information and advising on corrective actions.
D. Consult on fiscal‑year tax returns to maximize benefit to the Estate, including timing considerations and strategic filing recommendations.
E. Provide recommendations on tax consequences of investment sales, including capital gains implications, depreciation recapture, and other relevant tax impacts.
F. Provide estate-related financial analyses, including tax-impact modeling and scenario-based recommendations, to support Public Administrator and Public Guardian fiduciary decision-making in cases involving conservatorships of the estate and decedent estate administrations.
G. Support court‑related requests, including preparing summaries, clarifications, or documentation needed for hearings or judicial review.
H. Support the transition of cases from the Public Guardian to the Public Administrator, maintaining continuity of tax records, filings, and historical documentation.

The Contractor shall assist Public Administrator and Public Guardian clients with transitioning from paper-check tax payments to ACH or other authorized electronic payment methods and provide guidance on applicable IRS and Treasury electronic payment requirements.

## Levine Act Disclosure
The Levine Act (California Government Code Section 84308) imposes certain requirements on parties contracting with the County of San Mateo related to campaign contributions to County “officers,” including elected County officers and candidates seeking elective office, who may participate in making a decision on certain County contracts. Elected County officers in San Mateo County include: the San Mateo County Board of Supervisors, Assessor-County Clerk-Recorder, County Controller, Coroner, District Attorney, Sheriff, and Tax Collector-Treasurer.
Generally, under current County policy, approval by the Board of Supervisors is required for any agreement for services above $200,000, and agreements for services below that threshold may be approved by Department heads.
If your proposal is selected, you will be required to certify compliance with the Levine Act.
As part of this process, you will need to certify and warrant that you have fully complied, and will remain in full compliance, with all applicable requirements of the Levine Act in connection with the Agreement, including making any required disclosures of campaign contributions to County Officers, which includes but may not be limited to elected County Officers. Elected County Officers include members of the San Mateo County Board of Supervisors, as well as the Assessor-County Clerk-Recorder, Controller, Coroner, District Attorney, Sheriff, and Tax Collector-Treasurer.  
Any campaign contribution required to be disclosed under the Levine Act in connection with this Agreement shall be disclosed on the County of San Mateo Levine Act Disclosure Form, a copy of which is available from the County upon request.
Parties are solely responsible for accurate certification and disclosure.  The Levine Act is complex, and this brief description is not legal advice.  For example, certain contributions must be aggregated when determining whether contributions have exceeded the $500 threshold.  If your proposal is selected, you are urged to review the Levine Act and consider consulting an attorney.

The County of San Mateo (“County”) through its Department of Housing (“DOH”) is seeking qualified and experienced developer teams to submit a description of their qualifications together with a conceptual proposal to develop and operate a mix of low-, moderate- and middle-income housing with a preference for employees of public agencies within the County of San Mateo, including County employees, on a County-owned Property of approximately 20,500 square feet in size and located at 710 Hamilton St, Redwood City, CA 94063 (Assessor’s Parcel Number 052 364 110) (“Property”). The parcel is currently improved with a County-operated law library and is intended to be redeveloped for the provision of affordable housing with the foregoing local public employee preference. The Property is within a civic and commercial area in Redwood City (“City”) and located on a corner lot.
This Request for Proposals (“RFP”) seeks submissions from all interested and qualified proposers (“Proposers”). The County seeks by way of this RFP to select a development team that has the qualifications to implement their proposal in a manner that maximizes the quality of development while also maximizing value to the County, and, by extension, the employees of the County. Proposers must be able to show that they and any proposed subcontractors can perform in a highly professional and effective manner. Such evidence includes, but is not limited to, Proposer’s demonstrated competency and experience in delivering affordable, deed-restricted development projects of a similar scope and type and capacity of the Proposer's personnel and financial resources.
 
The County expects to negotiate and sign a long-term ground lease with the selected Developer/Owner to transfer control of the Property at the time the Developer/Owner achieves close of construction financing for a County-approved affordable housing project on the Property (the “Project”). Under the lease, the County will retain ownership of the land, and, unless specifically excepted, the selected Developer/Owner will own and maintain the improvements and manage the Project.
 
To achieve the County’s goals, expedite the development process, and secure a return on County investment, the County is prepared to contribute up to 80% of the total development costs to the project financing. The County expects all County financing to be repaid on a proposed time horizon with a return to the County, though alternate terms and structures for the County contribution will be considered assuming it meets other goals and objectives of this RFP.
 
The County intends that the Project will further the County’s public objective of facilitating the development of affordable housing with a preference for public employees, and that applicable County rights and privileges, including intergovernmental immunities, may apply to the extent permitted by law. Without waiving any such rights or privileges, the County also intends that the selected Proposer will propose a Project that is eligible for ministerial approval under State housing laws, and that will utilize applicable Redwood City entitlement procedures.
 
Note:
 Subject to the approval of the County Board of Supervisors, at the time the County and the selected Developer/Owner enter into an Exclusive Negotiating Agreement (ENA) for development of the Property, DOH intends to make available to the selected Developer/Owner initial predevelopment funding, through a predevelopment loan agreement, in an amount not to exceed

 for early predevelopment tasks related to development of an affordable housing project on the Property.

The area offers a true urban, live-work-play environment with easy access to restaurants, cafés, entertainment venues, and everyday services centered around Broadway, Courthouse Square, and the historic Fox Theatre. Residents can walk to the Caltrain station for convenient service to San Francisco and San Jose, while major corridors including El Camino Real, Highway 101, and Woodside Road provide strong regional connectivity. The neighborhood is served by schools within the Redwood City School District and Sequoia Union High School District, including Sequoia High School, a well-regarded local high school. Nearby parks, library facilities, community events, outdoor concerts, and seasonal festivals contribute to an active community atmosphere, making the area attractive to professionals, commuters, and households seeking a highly walkable downtown setting with strong transit access and abundant neighborhood amenities.

Elected County officers in San Mateo County include: the San Mateo County Board of Supervisors, Assessor-County Clerk-Recorder, County Controller, Coroner, District Attorney, Sheriff, and Tax Collector-Treasurer. 
Generally, under current County policy, approval by the Board of Supervisors is required for any agreement for services above $200,000, and agreements for services below that threshold may be approved by Department heads. 
If your proposal is selected, you will be required to certify compliance with the Levine Act. 
As part of this process, you will need to certify and warrant that you have fully complied, and will remain in full compliance, with all applicable requirements of the Levine Act in connection with the Agreement, including making any required disclosures of campaign contributions to County Officers, which includes but may not be limited to elected County Officers. Elected County Officers include members of the San Mateo County Board of Supervisors, as well as the Assessor-County Clerk-Recorder, Controller, Coroner, District Attorney, Sheriff, and Tax Collector-Treasurer.  
Any campaign contribution required to be disclosed under the Levine Act in connection with this Agreement shall be disclosed on the County of San Mateo Levine Act Disclosure Form, a copy of which is available from the County upon request.Parties are solely responsible for accurate certification and disclosure.  The Levine Act is complex, and this brief description is not legal advice.  For example, certain contributions must be aggregated when determining whether contributions have exceeded the $500 threshold.  If your proposal is selected, you are urged to review the Levine Act and consider consulting an attorney.

Scope of Services
The purpose of this Request for Proposal (RFP) is to solicit certified fire inspection professionals, Fire Plan Examiner, Fire Inspector I and Fire Inspector II with the appropriate credentials, expertise and experience performing plan review, permit processing and inspections. San Mateo County Fire welcomes proposals from Fire Inspection professionals and/or firms with expertise in in fire inspection services.  As efficient customer service is a primary goal for the County, the selected Contractors(s) must be responsive, and all work must be performed within predetermined time schedules.
Fire plan review services
Construction fire inspection services
Planning and development of fire/safety review services
Fire Marshal technical advisory services
Deputy Fire Marshal technical support services
Specialized fire protection engineering and code consulting services

Professional qualifications of the personnel proposed to perform the work.
Prior experience of providing fire inspection services to the County and to other jurisdictions.
Availability of the Contractor to perform necessary services upon demand.

## State Legislative Advocacy Services
State legislative advocate lobbyist services will proactively provide counsel and assistance on multiple County initiatives, including but not limited to the following: Strategy, monitoring and analysis, platform and program development, and meetings with the County Chief Executive Officer, Board of Supervisors, and designated Intergovernmental and Public Affairs (IGPA) team to assist in advancing the County’s legislative priorities.
1. Core Legislative Monitoring and Analysis
Continuously monitor, identify, analyze, and track all introduced, amended, and pending state legislation, budget trailer bills, and administrative/regulatory actions relevant to the agency's adopted legislative platform and policy priorities.
Provide updates on bills and regulations that may have impacts on the County's operations, programs, and services.
Monitor, report, and advise on the activities of the Legislature, the Executive Branch, State departments and agencies, State regulatory bodies, and other officials.
Maintain working knowledge of the state and federal laws and regulatory frameworks most relevant to the County’s operations (e.g., the in-lieu Vehicle License Fees (VLF) shortfall, Educational Revenue Augmentation Funds (ERAF), land-use and housing law, H.R. 1, and other policy areas specific to the County’s adopted policy priorities).
Track and report monthly on emerging issues and opportunities not yet reflected in the agency's adopted legislative platform.
2. Legislative Platform and Program Development
Advise County executive staff on the annual development or update of the County’s state legislative platform and program, including annual meetings with County departments and County Supervisors, as requested by IGPA staff.
Recommend an annual government relations strategy and a list of state funding priorities consistent with the platform.
3. Direct Advocacy and Representation
Serve as the County’s primary advocate before the State Legislature, the Governor's Office, state agencies, and (where applicable) other officials.
Attend and monitor relevant legislative and budget committee hearings, providing oral testimony on high-priority bills as needed.
Draft, coordinate, and submit formal position letters to legislative committees and the Governor's Office, as requested.
For County-sponsored legislative proposals, work with County staff to draft bill language, identify and secure an author/sponsor, and develop and execute a strategy to advance the proposal through the legislative process to the Governor for signature.
Help to negotiate amendments sought by the County; actively work against advancement of opposed measures; and support advancement of measures the County supports.
Provide logistical support to arrange staff appointments and meetings with legislators and state agency staff, including organizing a minimum of two in-person or virtual delegation meetings per legislative session.
4. Relationship Management and Coalition Building
Develop and maintain positive, effective working relationships with the County’s legislative delegation and staff, relevant legislative committees, the Governor's/Executive Branch staff, and key state agency contacts (e.g., HCD, the Department of Finance, and other agencies relevant to the County’s priorities).
Coordinate and cooperate with statewide associations, including the California State Association of Counties, the Urban Counties of California, through regular participation in these associations’ caucus meetings, annual legislative conferences, and key staff meetings to build coalitions that advance the County’s interests.
5. Funding, Grants, and Budget Advocacy
Identify state programs, competitive grants, and earmark/member-request opportunities available to fund County projects, programs, and services.
Advocate for the County’s funding requests through the state budget process, including member/earmark requests, and assist the agency in pursuing niche or specialized funding streams tied to the County’s specific capital or infrastructure needs (e.g., coastal resiliency, water quality infrastructure, transportation, or similar capital priorities).
6. Reporting and Communication
Provide monthly written reports detailing pending state legislation, budget issues, and regulatory developments of concern to the County; actions taken on the County’s behalf; expected future action; and recommended next steps.
Provide weekly email updates on upcoming committee hearings and other relevant developments during active legislative session periods, and high-priority bill/issue alerts within 24–48 hours of a significant development.
Participate in regular (at minimum monthly, or bi-weekly during active session) coordination calls or meetings with the IGPA staff to review the legislative calendar and strategy.
Provide an annual end-of-session report summarizing the completed legislative year, including budget actions, major legislative activity, and results of the agency's legislative requests, along with a forecast of issues expected in the upcoming session.
Present legislative updates, priorities, and strategy to the Board of Supervisors at least twice annually, or as needed/upon request.
Provide training to agency staff, upon request, on the state legislative and budget process.
7. Compliance, Registration, and Administration
Prepare and file all applicable lobbying registration documents and reports with the Secretary of State and/or Fair Political Practices Commission within all statutory deadlines and promptly notify the agency of any changes affecting the engagement.
Comply with all applicable conflict-of-interest disclosure requirements, including Statement of Economic Interests (Form 700) filings, and disclose any political contributions subject to the Levine Act or equivalent local requirements.
Provide an initial list of current clients at the start of the engagement and promptly notify the agency of any changes to that list, including new clients whose interests may conflict with the County’s.
If subcontractors are used to perform any portion of the work, submit the proposed subcontractor(s) for the agency's review and approval in advance, and remain responsible for managing and coordinating their performance.
Notify the County in advance of any changes in the key personnel assigned to the account and maintain back-up staffing arrangements sufficient to ensure continuity of service in the event a primary team member is unavailable.

Levine Act Disclosure 
The Levine Act (California Government Code Section 84308) imposes certain requirements on parties contracting with the County of San Mateo related to campaign contributions to County “officers,” including elected County officers and candidates seeking elective office, who may participate in deciding on certain County contracts. Elected County officers in San Mateo County include: the San Mateo County Board of Supervisors, Assessor-County Clerk-Recorder, County Controller, Coroner, District Attorney, Sheriff, and Tax Collector-Treasurer. 
Generally, under current County policy, approval by the Board of Supervisors is required for any agreement for services above $200,000, and agreements for services below that threshold may be approved by Department heads. 
If your proposal is selected, you will be required to certify compliance with the Levine Act. 
As part of this process, you will need to certify and warrant that you have fully complied, and will remain in full compliance, with all applicable requirements of the Levine Act in connection with the Agreement, including making any required disclosures of campaign contributions to County Officers, which includes but may not be limited to elected County Officers. Parties are solely responsible for accurate certification and disclosure.  The Levine Act is complex, and this brief description is not legal advice.  For example, certain contributions must be aggregated when determining whether contributions have exceeded the $500 threshold.  If your proposal is selected, you are urged to review the Levine Act and consider consulting an attorney.

## Bid Evaluation Criteria
A Scoring Tabulation will be generated to compile the prices and ranking to determine the awarded bidder. Bids will be evaluated based on the Total Bid Price. All responsive and responsible bidders will be ranked from the lowest to the highest price based on the Total Bid Prices.

## COMMENCEMENT OF PERFORMANCE
Written Notice
Until the County provides written authorization to commence deliveries of the goods and services specified, there is no contractual agreement between the County and the selected bidder. No verbal instructions or promises are binding on the County.
Purchase Orders and Task Orders
If the contract anticipates multiple Purchase Orders or Task Orders, the relevant scope of work, payment terms, delivery instructions, period of performance, and any unique contractual terms and conditions may be set forth in the Purchase Orders or Task Orders.
Estimated Quantities
If this solicitation is for an indefinite quantity contract, any estimates of expected use or quantities provided are for bid purposes only. The County does not guarantee any specific number of orders.
Levine Act Disclosure
The Levine Act (California Government Code Section 84308) imposes certain requirements on parties contracting with the County of San Mateo related to campaign contributions to County “officers,” including elected County officers and candidates seeking elective office, who may participate in making a decision on certain County contracts. Elected County officers in San Mateo County include: the San Mateo County Board of Supervisors, Assessor-County Clerk-Recorder, County Controller, Coroner, District Attorney, Sheriff, and Tax Collector-Treasurer.
Generally, under current County policy, approval by the Board of Supervisors is required for any agreement for services above $200,000, and agreements for services below that threshold may be approved by Department heads.
If your proposal is selected, you will be required to certify compliance with the Levine Act.
As part of this process, you will need to certify and warrant that you have fully complied, and will remain in full compliance, with all applicable requirements of the Levine Act in connection with the Agreement, including making any required disclosures of campaign contributions to County Officers, which includes but may not be limited to elected County Officers. Elected County Officers include members of the San Mateo County Board of Supervisors, as well as the Assessor-County Clerk-Recorder, Controller, Coroner, District Attorney, Sheriff, and Tax Collector-Treasurer.  
Any campaign contribution required to be disclosed under the Levine Act in connection with this Agreement shall be disclosed on the County of San Mateo Levine Act Disclosure Form, a copy of which is available from the County upon request.
Parties are solely responsible for accurate certification and disclosure.  The Levine Act is complex, and this brief description is not legal advice.  For example, certain contributions must be aggregated when determining whether contributions have exceeded the $500 threshold.  If your proposal is selected, you are urged to review the Levine Act and consider consulting an attorney.

## Protest of Non-Responsiveness Determination
Within five (5) working days of the County's issuance of a notice of non-responsiveness, any firm that has submitted a proposal and believes that the County has incorrectly determined that its proposal is non-responsive may submit a written notice of protest.  Such notice of protest must be received by the County on or before the fifth working day following the County's issuance of the notice of non-responsiveness.  The notice of protest must include a written statement specifying in detail each and every one of the grounds asserted for the protest.  The protest must be signed by an individual authorized to represent the proposer, and must cite the law, rule, local ordinance, procedure or RFP provision on which the protest is based.  In addition, the protestor must specify facts and evidence sufficient for the County to determine the validity of the protest.

## PAYMENT
Compensation
The County will pay the quoted prices as full consideration for Contractor’s full, complete and faithful performance of the Contractor’s obligations under the contract.
The County does not accept COD shipments. Payment will be by one of the following methods, as indicated in the Contract Documents:
Full payment will be made after the County’s acceptance of goods or services and receipt of a complete invoice, as applicable; or
Partial payments will be made in accordance with the schedule set forth in the Scope of Work; or
Payments will be invoiced monthly by Contractor in arrears, based upon goods or services provided and at the amounts set forth in the payment schedule up to the maximum amount of the contract; or
The County may issue Purchase or Task Orders, which will be paid according to the payment schedule attached to the contract or Purchase or Task Order, or on the County’s receipt and acceptance of the goods and services and receipt and acceptance of a complete invoice; or
As otherwise agreed to by the parties.
Late Payment Charges
The County will not be responsible for late payment charges unless they are stated on the Purchase Order or contract. A payment is late only if payment of an invoice exceeds the time allowed by the payment terms of the Purchase Order or contract.
Credits
Prior to releasing final payment, the County must be reimbursed for any overpayments, advance payments, or other credits due from the Contractor, and the County may deduct these amounts from payments otherwise due Contractor.
Conditions Prerequisite to Payment
The County may withhold payment under any of the following circumstance:
Contractor, with or without knowledge, made a misrepresentation of substantial and material nature with respect to any information furnished to County;
Contractor took any action pertaining to this agreement that required County approval, without having first received County approval;
Contractor was or is in default under any of the terms of this contract;
The County or any other authorized government entity has requested but has not received and approved any reports, data, audits or other information requested from Contractor, including final reports and documentation due at contract termination.
Payment in the event of non-compliance
If the County determines that the quantity or quality of the goods provided or work performed is unacceptable, the County will notify Contractor and may withhold payment until correction has been made to County’s satisfaction. If corrections have not been completed after what the County deems a reasonable time, County may make corrections on its own or through a third party, and deduct the cost of replacement or correction from any sums that may be or become due to Contractor on this or any other agreement. No additional payment will be provided to Contractor for replacements or corrections.

Description:
Planning and Building is seeking qualified community-based organizations, nonprofit organizations, firms, academic partners, and individuals to assist with equitably engaging communities in the County of San Mateo.
The goal of this 
Request for Statement of Qualifications (RFSQ)
 is to make it easier for San Mateo County jurisdictions to find community partners to help conduct community outreach to historically underrepresented groups, to allow more meaningful participation in government decisions.

Community-based organizations play an important role in the communities they serve. They are often the ones who interact with the community every day, speak their language, and understand their lived realities. While many consulting firms bring expertise in community engagement, they often lack the strong local ties and relationships that come with being embedded in the community and are needed to conduct high quality, culturally sensitive outreach. This is especially important for reaching communities that have historically been left out of government decision-making and are often the hardest to reach, such as renters, low-income families, unhoused individuals and families, people with disabilities, seniors, and communities of color. Almost half of San Mateo County residents speak a language other than English at home. Approximately 40% of the population are renters, and many residents struggle to pay the bills. The decisions planning departments make often disproportionately affect these groups, and as a part of our commitment to furthering fair housing, it is important to make sure the people who are most are affected by government decisions are involved in shaping them.
Planning and Building Department will lead this RFSQ process in collaboration with cities in the San Mateo County and compile a list of qualified community partners, also referred to as a “bench.” The list will highlight which populations each organization has experience with. As a Request for Statement of Qualifications, this is 
not
 an invitation to bid, 
but rather a solicitation of qualifications and experience to perform the required services
. While this RFSQ is being issued for the Planning and Building Department, all departments can use the bench. Interested cities will work with their own procurement offices to identify the policies and steps they need to follow to contract with the organizations on their own. When the cities and the County of San Mateo want to conduct outreach, they may reach out to organizations or individuals on the bench to see if they are interested in working on a project as paid consultants. Generally, when the organization or individuals’ services are needed, city/county staff will forward a request for services to relevant potential partners, including a project description and scope of work. Community partners on the bench would then respond with a proposal and cost estimate.
It is also possible that the cities and County of Santa Clara will use the bench.

## Range of Community Outreach Expertise
Selected community-based organizations, nonprofit organizations, academic partners, firms, or individuals may be asked to provide any of the services listed below. The County/cities are seeking a broad range of expertise across these services, and any given consultant or organization may have skills and experience in only one, several, or many of the areas listed. Specific needs will vary by project and jurisdiction and will be defined and mutually agreed upon by the requesting jurisdiction and the consultant or organization within each scope of work. Consultants and/or organizations may respond to all or some of the listed scope of services:
Build community trust and relationships between the cities/County and community, including leveraging existing relationships.
Serve as a trusted liaison between the community and the County/cities, sharing information and feedback both ways
Conduct background/technical research to determine which communities are most impacted or will experience greater impacts.
Create online, social media, radio, video and print public outreach and educational materials accessible to audiences with different language speakers, ages, cultures, abilities and familiarity with the issue requiring engagement.
Identify and implement equity-focused and creative community engagement strategies usings formats that are relevant to the communities where traditional public meeting formats may not be effective, which could include arts, music and other cultural activities.
Tailor community engagement strategies to reach specific hard-to-reach populations, which may include (depending on the project) renters, unhoused individuals and families, seniors/older adults, people with disabilities, immigrant and refugee communities, undocumented residents, non-English/limited-English speakers, low-income households, small businesses, and communities that have historically been excluded from civic processes.
Lead community engagement activities and associated follow-up activities, which may include facilitating and summarizing public meetings, workshops, surveys, polling, and mapping exercises.
Design and lead engagement activities specifically for youth and teens (e.g., participatory mapping, photovoice, storytelling exercises), and partner with schools, school districts, youth-serving organizations, and university youth engagement programs to meet young people where they are.
Coordinate the work of other team members and community ambassadors, including youth ambassadors and culturally/linguistically specific ambassadors.
Assist City or County staff in summarizing findings, attending, and/or facilitating at public forums, commissions, committees, and/or City Council meetings.
Plan and facilitate in-person and virtual events, which may require food, room rentals, childcare, distributing compensation to the community (e.g., stipends, gift cards), translation and interpretation services, and accessibility support.
Provide tracking, documentation and analysis of engagement activities and outcomes, including analysis of the engagement’s success at reaching priority populations (and adapting strategies in response).
Build capacity in their communities to understand how government works and engage successfully with their local jurisdiction(s).
Support jurisdiction staff in “closing the loop” with the community to explain how their feedback was responded to and/or integrated into decisions.
