Group Facilitation & Meeting Management
 
Subject
Scope of Service Description
Examples:
Group Building, Development & Collaboration
Collaborative groups drive innovation, efficient processes, greater success, and improved communication by listening and learning from each other.
"Building Effective Group Relationships.”
Meeting Management
Meeting Management is the process of managing the stages and components of the entire meeting process, including before, during, and after the meeting.
"Leading an Effective Meeting"; "The Art of Making Meetings Work"; "How to Run Effective Meetings"
Retreat facilitation
Retreat facilitation is the process of designing, leading, and guiding a group through a structured meeting. These meetings help participants achieve specific goals, such as group development and cohesive governance.
Services can support the launch of new advisory bodies or help existing groups conduct periodic or needed resets. 
 
Conflict Resolution & Internal Group Communication
 
Subject
Scope of Service Description
Examples:
Conflict Resolution/
Management
Conflict management is the practice of identifying and managing disagreements, conflict, and discord sensibly, fairly, and efficiently through meeting facilitation, resolution discussions, and cooperative goal setting.
"Conflict Resolution"; "Getting to Resolution: Turning Conflict into Sustainable Collaboration"; "Managing Conflict with Emotional Intelligence"
Internal Group
Communication
Communication is the process of exchanging, expressing, or conveying information and ideas through writing and speaking; good communicators listen carefully, speak or write clearly, and respect differing opinions.
"Ask, Listen, and Influence: Develop Inquiry and Listening Skills"; "Effective Communication Skills"; "Emotional Intelligence in the Context of Public Advisory Bodies"
 
Strategic & Organizational Development
 
Subject
Scope of Service Description
Examples:
Strategic Planning
Strategic planning is a structured, long-term process that defines a group’s vision, sets goals, identifies how to achieve them, and aligns resources and teams to execute the plan.
Services can support the development of new advisory bodies or help existing groups conduct periodic or needed resets.
Workplan Development
A workplan is a project plan that works as an organizational tool. It specifies the processes required for a project and sets reasonable completion dates. The plan establishes goals, objectives, tasks, and assigns team members responsible for completing them.
Services can support developing new plans or help existing groups conduct periodic or needed resets. 
Group Adaptation 
Group adaptation is a systematic approach to managing transitions or transformations in a group’s goals, processes, or technologies by implementing strategies to effect, control, and support others in adapting to change.
"Creatively Managing Today's Constant Changes"; "Planning the Next Normal"
 
Community Engagement
 
Subject
Scope of Service Description
Examples:
Community Outreach and Engagement
Community outreach and engagement inform community members about an issue, problem, opportunity, or decision. Public engagement can broaden participation and incorporate community input into decision-making. It is a strategic process for connecting with the public to educate, support, or collaborate on issues affecting a community. The goal is to inform the community about a project or process a local government is developing.
 
The Contractor shall coordinate with the County’s communications and engagement teams throughout the planning and implementation of all outreach and engagement activities. The Contractor shall consider County input when determining the timing, messaging, outreach methods, and platforms, locations and visual identity or branding of each engagement effort and shall ensure these efforts align with existing County outreach and engagement work. 
The scope of community engagement services needed can vary. They can be countywide or district-specific. Examples may include:
Hosting pop-ups or tabling at community events. 
Partnering with community-based organizations to share information through trusted messengers and existing community networks.
Developing Multilingual Outreach content consistent with County branding.
Informing community members about a Commission's work plan or public comment opportunities. 
Community Listening Sessions
A listening session is a facilitated discussion with a group of people to collect information about their experiences. Participants in listening sessions are asked to talk about what they know and think and sometimes answer specific questions about a topic. The goal is to understand the opportunities and challenges surrounding a specific topic in a small community.
 
The Contractor shall design listening sessions in coordination with the County’s communications and engagement teams, including methods, locations, brand identity and messaging. Sessions should be designed so that the input falls within the scope of the Board or Commission’s authority, governance, or project. The Contractor shall plan how community input will be documented, reported back to the Board or Commission, and followed up on with participants. 
The scope of community engagement services needed can vary. They can be countywide or district-specific. Examples may include:
Gathering community input to shape a Commission's annual priorities or work plan.
Facilitating in-language sessions or holding sessions with a specific population such as youth, or residents of an unincorporated area, to inform a commission's recommendations. 
Preparing a summary of themes and findings and reporting back to participants on how their input was used.

Levine Act Disclosure
The Levine Act (California Government Code Section 84308) imposes certain requirements on parties contracting with the County of San Mateo related to campaign contributions to County “officers,” including elected County officers and candidates seeking elective office, who may participate in making a decision on certain County contracts. Elected County officers in San Mateo County include: the San Mateo County Board of Supervisors, Assessor-County Clerk-Recorder, County Controller, Coroner, District Attorney, Sheriff, and Tax Collector-Treasurer.
Generally, under current County policy, approval by the Board of Supervisors is required for any agreement for services above $200,000, and agreements for services below that threshold may be approved by Department heads.
If your proposal is selected, you will be required to certify compliance with the Levine Act.
As part of this process, you will need to certify and warrant that you have fully complied, and will remain in full compliance, with all applicable requirements of the Levine Act in connection with the Agreement, including making any required disclosures of campaign contributions to County Officers, which includes but may not be limited to elected County Officers. Elected County Officers include members of the San Mateo County Board of Supervisors, as well as the Assessor-County Clerk-Recorder, Controller, Coroner, District Attorney, Sheriff, and Tax Collector-Treasurer.  
Any campaign contribution required to be disclosed under the Levine Act in connection with this Agreement shall be disclosed on the County of San Mateo Levine Act Disclosure Form, a copy of which is available from the County upon request.
Parties are solely responsible for accurate certification and disclosure.  The Levine Act is complex, and this brief description is not legal advice.  For example, certain contributions must be aggregated when determining whether contributions have exceeded the $500 threshold.  If your proposal is selected, you are urged to review the Levine Act and consider consulting an attorney.

The County will pay the quoted prices as full consideration for Contractor’s full, complete and faithful performance of the Contractor’s obligations under the contract.
The County does not accept COD shipments. Payment will be by one of the following methods, as indicated in the Contract Documents:
Full payment will be made after the County’s acceptance of goods or services and receipt of a complete invoice, as applicable; or
Partial payments will be made in accordance with the schedule set forth in the Scope of Work; or
Payments will be invoiced monthly by Contractor in arrears, based upon goods or services provided and at the amounts set forth in the payment schedule up to the maximum amount of the contract; or
The County may issue Purchase or Task Orders, which will be paid according to the payment schedule attached to the contract or Purchase or Task Order, or on the County’s receipt and acceptance of the goods and services and receipt and acceptance of a complete invoice; or
As otherwise agreed to by the parties.
Late Payment Charges
The County will not be responsible for late payment charges unless they are stated on the Purchase Order or contract. A payment is late only if payment of an invoice exceeds the time allowed by the payment terms of the Purchase Order or contract.
Credits
Prior to releasing final payment, the County must be reimbursed for any overpayments, advance payments, or other credits due from the Contractor, and the County may deduct these amounts from payments otherwise due Contractor.
Conditions Prerequisite to Payment
The County may withhold payment under any of the following circumstance:
Contractor, with or without knowledge, made a misrepresentation of substantial and material nature with respect to any information furnished to County;
Contractor took any action pertaining to this agreement that required County approval, without having first received County approval;
Contractor was or is in default under any of the terms of this contract;
The County or any other authorized government entity has requested but has not received and approved any reports, data, audits or other information requested from Contractor, including final reports and documentation due at contract termination.
Payment in the event of non-compliance
If the County determines that the quantity or quality of the goods provided or work performed is unacceptable, the County will notify Contractor and may withhold payment until correction has been made to County’s satisfaction. If corrections have not been completed after what the County deems a reasonable time, County may make corrections on its own or through a third party, and deduct the cost of replacement or correction from any sums that may be or become due to Contractor on this or any other agreement. ## San Mateo County Health and Hospital Division As-Needed Bird Abatement and Control Services, Including Specific Mitigation at San Mateo Medical Center Loading Dock
The selected contractor shall provide all necessary labor, materials, equipment, tools, and supervision services to perform bird abatement, control, and humane exclusion services across all San Mateo County Health and Hospital division facilities. The contract includes both on-call, as-needed services and a specific initial installation project at the San Mateo Medical Center (SMMC).
3-yr As-Needed (On-Call) Services (Health and Hospital Facilities)
The contractor shall provide preventative and emergency bird control services on an as-needed basis across all Health and Hospital Division properties:
San Mateo Medical Center (222 W.39th Ave, San Mateo, CA 94403)
San Mateo Medical Center Admin/Link Building (225 W. 27th Ave, San Mateo, CA 94403)
Serenity House (3701 Hacienda Street. San Mateo, CA 94403)
Fair Oaks Clinic (2710 Middlefield Rd. Redwood City, CA 94063)
Cordilleras Mental Health Center (200, 220, 240, 260, 280 Edmonds Rd. Redwood City, CA 94062)
Canyon Oaks Youth Mental Health Center (400 Edmonds Rd. Redwood City, CA 94062)
Coastside Mental Health Clinic (225 S. Cabrillo Hwy Ste 100A. Halfmoon Bay, CA 94019)
South San Francisco Health Clinic (306 Spruce Ave. South San Francisco, CA 94080)
North County Health Clinic-Wellness Center-(1024 Mission Rd. South San Francisco, CA 94080)
Site Assessments & Inspections: Conducting professional evaluations of facilities to identify pest bird pressures (e.g., pigeons, gulls, swallows), roosting habits, and nesting activity.
Humane Exclusion & Deterrent Solutions: Supplying and installing industry-standard deterrents. 
Cleaning, Sanitization, and Debris Removal: Cleaning accumulated bird droppings, nesting materials, and biohazards from affected structures, followed by proper sanitization compliant with OSHA and environmental standards.
Emergency Response: Providing prompt dispatch and response for urgent nuisance or health-hazard situations within 48 hours.
Quote & Approval requirements: For all as-needed tasks, the contractor must provide a detailed cost quote based on the contracted rate sheet. No work shall commence until the quote has been formally reviewed and approved by the designated County representative. 
Defined Project-San Mateo Medical Center-New Loading Dock Ceiling Netting
 
Install 3/4-inch black polyethylene Bird Netting 50'x100' to ceiling to create a physical barrier against pigeons. Netting is installed using a stainless-steel cable framework, 3/4-inch anchors, aluminum fasteners and industrial staples if appropriate. Netting is attached to the cable framework using net rings. Netting is nearly invisible and is the only effective barrier against nesting pigeons. Netting will be positioned above the lights
 .
Remove any existing bird nesting material within work areas if present. Clean and sanitize all areas if present. Clean and sanitize all areas affected by bird activity in compliance with OSHA and environmental standards.
Final inspection and adjustment of the completed installation. 
Pricing, Labor Rates, and Prevailing Wage Requirements 
Proposers must submit pricing structured into two components:
Lum-Sum Project price: Provide a single, all inclusive fixed price for the defined San Mateo Medical Center Loading Dock ceiling netting project.
As needed Hourly labor rates and Markups:
For ongoing on-call services over the 3-year term, vendors must submit a comprehensive rate sheet 
Rate Breakdown: Hourly labor rates must be clearly itemized by Regular/Stright-Time, Overtime (OT), Weekend, and Holiday rates
Material &Equipment Markups: include any applicable percentage markups for wholesale materials, specialized hardware, and equipment (such as scissor lifts or scaffolding) required for maintenance, repairs, or emergency call-outs.
Prevailing Wage Compliance: All labor performed under this contract is subject to California prevailing wage requirements as determined by the Department of Industrial Relations (DIR). Bidders must factor applicable prevailing wage scales into their submitted rates.

The County is seeking proposals from qualified vendors with demonstrated expertise in implementing enterprise-grade Picture Archiving and Communication Systems (PACS) supporting Radiology, Cardiology, and dental imaging within complex healthcare environments. Within five (5) working days of the County's issuance of a notice of intent to award the contract, any firm that has submitted a responsive proposal and believes that the County has incorrectly selected another proposer for award may submit a written notice of protest.  Such notice of protest must be received by the County on or before the fifth working day after the County's issuance of the notice of intent to award.
The notice of protest must include a written statement specifying in detail each and every one of the grounds asserted for the protest.  The protest must be signed by an individual authorized to represent the proposer, and must cite the law, rule, local ordinance, procedure or RFP provision on which the protest is based.  In addition, the protestor must specify facts and evidence sufficient for the County to determine the validity of the protest.

## Background
The County currently utilizes ScImage PACS (Picom application), implemented in 2009 as part of the transition from film-based to digital imaging. This system has supported clinical imaging workflows for many years and remains an important part of ongoing operations.
As imaging technology, interoperability standards, and clinical demands continue to evolve, the County is seeking to modernize its imaging environment to further enhance efficiency, integration, and scalability. This effort is intended to build upon existing capabilities and support a long-term enterprise imaging strategy.
The County performs approximately:
65,000 radiology studies annually 
5,000 cardiology studies annually 
8,000 mammography interpretations annually 
The County utilizes EPIC as its enterprise EHR platform, with mammography workflows supported through a Radiology Information Communication System (RICS) model.

## Protest of Purchase Order/Agreement Award
Within five (5) working days of the County's issuance of a notice of intent to award the PO/agreement, any firm that has submitted a responsive proposal and believes that the County has incorrectly selected another proposer for award may submit a written notice of protest.  Such notice of protest must be received by the County on or before the fifth working day after the County's issuance of the notice of intent to award.

## Registry Contract
Nursing Registry Staffing Services
 
1. Purpose and Objective
The purpose of this Agreement is to secure a qualified, Joint Commission-accredited vendor who can demonstrate that it can function as a single source for temporary staffing services, which may include, but is not limited to, providing comprehensive temporary registry staffing workforce under independent contracts including but not limited to nurses, pharmacists, pharmacy technicians, laboratory technicians, radiologists, physical therapists, perioperative nurse manager, project manager and respiratory therapists. Experience in similar successful engagements and in similar institutions for public hospitals in the State of California is especially important.
This comprehensive management services regarding temporary staff shall include but is not limited to centralized methods of processing, providing staffing (licensed and certified clinical staff), managing temporary staff assignment to the hospital, maintaining placement of and monitoring the qualifications and fitness of all temporary registry personnel scheduled to work at the County on an as needed basis.
All temporary registry staff must have the legal right to practice and work in the United States without any restriction and condition.
2. Nursing Personnel Qualification Standards
Consistent with the Purpose and Objective set forth in Section 1, above, all temporary Registered Nurses (RNs) and other non-RN temporary nursing staff deployed under this contract must satisfy the following baseline experience criteria prior to placement:
Non-Specialty Nursing Roles (e.g., Med-Surg, General Telemetry): Minimum of two (2) years of experience in an acute care setting within the Continental United States (including Alaska and Hawaii).
Specialty Nursing Roles & Management (e.g., ICU, ED, OR, NICU, Perioperative Management): Minimum of four (4) years of experience in an acute care setting within the Continental United States (including Alaska and Hawaii).
3. Scope of Required Services
Consistent with the Purpose and Objective set forth in Section 1, above, the Contractor shall serve as a centralized service provider responsible for managing, processing, scheduling, and monitoring all temporary nursing registry personnel. Key management responsibilities include:
Screening and Pre-Assignment Vetting
Health & Background Vetting: Conduct comprehensive pre-employment health clearances and background checks prior to assignment. Screenings  must include:
Full criminal history background check and drug screening.
General physical examination clearance.
TB screening and/or Chest X-Ray verifying the absence of active disease.
Vaccination history or positive titer proof for Measles, Mumps, Rubella (MMR), Diphtheria, Tetanus, Pertussis (Tdap), Hepatitis B, and COVID-19.
Credentialing & Verification: Verify active, unrestricted California nursing licenses, clinical competencies, certifications (e.g., BLS, ACLS, PALS), and primary education.
Document Management: Maintain, audit, and provide complete copies of all nursing credentialing documentation to the County or regulatory bodies upon request in compliance with Joint Commission standards.
B. Administrative, Reporting, and Operational Support
Operational Availability: Provide dedicated administrative support 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year to manage urgent staffing requests and escalation needs.
Data & Analytics Reporting: Deliver real-time and on-demand reporting detailing registry labor utilization, including timekeeping audit trails, detailed labor costs, fill rates, and historical trending analysis.
Executive Oversight: Report temporary nursing staffing activity and operational performance directly to the County’s Chief Nursing Officer (or designated representative).
Contractual & Legal Compliance: Ensure full compliance with organizational requirements, including HIPAA Business Associate Agreements (BAA) and specified liability insurance coverage before deployment.

.

## Scope of Work
The Contractor shall provide one or more residential living facilities that meet all required physical standards and support a safe, recovery‑focused environment for residents.
Facility Standards
Recovery Residence services under this RFP are non-clinical housing and recovery-support services. The Contractor shall provide safe, stable, substance-free housing within a structured and supportive living environment that promotes sustained recovery and increased independence. Recovery-oriented supports shall help participants maintain stable housing; remain engaged in required substance use disorder and/or mental health treatment; build healthy, recovery-supportive relationships and connections to community resources; develop practical skills needed for independent living; establish routines and responsibilities that support recovery; and plan for successful transition to longer-term stable housing and community-based recovery supports.
Recovery-oriented supports may include peer and social support; linkage to mutual-aid and other community recovery resources; assistance with transportation coordination; development of budgeting, meal planning, household management, employment-readiness, and other independent living skills; encouragement and support with attending treatment, court, medical, and other required appointments; and assistance with transition and housing planning.
The Contractor shall not provide or represent Recovery Residence services as substance use disorder or mental health treatment unless such services are separately licensed, authorized, and expressly included under another agreement. Clinical assessment, diagnosis, treatment planning, clinical treatment, and court-related treatment reporting shall remain the responsibility of the County, Adult Drug Court, and/or designated treatment providers.
The Vendor shall ensure all residential facilities meet the following minimum physical requirements:
Each sleeping room must provide at least 50 square feet per bed.
There must be at least one sink, toilet, and shower for every six residents.
Adequate personal items storage and food storage space must be available for all residents.
Onsite laundry services must be accessible to residents.
Kitchen and dining areas must be sufficiently sized to accommodate all residents for shared meals.
A designated group area must be provided for house meetings, small‑group activities, and social interactions.
Program Requirements
The Contractor shall maintain a structured, recovery‑oriented environment through the following activities:
Conduct onsite random drug screenings no fewer than two times per month.
Facilitate weekly house meetings led by a designated house manager.
Contractor Responsibilities
The Contractor shall:
Maintain all residences in good repair, clean, and well‑kept throughout the contract period.
Ensure all residences remain entirely drug‑and alcohol‑free.
Obtain certification under the National Association of Recovery Residences (NARR) standards through the California Consortium of Addiction Programs and Professionals (CCAPP) no later than December 31, 2027.
Expectations
The Contractor is expected to:
Comply with all facility and operational standards outlined in the Solano County Guidelines for Sober Living Environments.
Cooperate with monitoring activities conducted by Solano County Behavioral Health to verify adherence to all guidelines and requirements.
Consistently provide safe, stable, and recovery‑focused housing that supports resident participation in treatment and aligns with best practices for sober living environments.

The Contractor is expected to:
A. Maintain all residences in clean, safe, sanitary, and good repair throughout the contract term;
B. Obtain or maintain all required licenses, permits, certifications, insurance, and approvals;
C. Ensure residences remain compliant with applicable housing laws, and County requirements;
D. Maintain adequate staffing and supervision;
E. Maintain complete and accurate program and participant records;
F. Protect participant confidentiality;
G. Immediately address conditions that present a health or safety risk;
H. Cooperate with County monitoring and quality-assurance activities; and
I. Notify the County promptly of any material change affecting the Contractor's ability to provide the required services.

## Expected Outcomes 
The recovery housing program is intended to support the following outcomes:
A. Increased housing stability among Prop 36 participants;
B. Increased engagement and retention in court-ordered substance use disorder and/or mental health treatment;
C. Reduced disruptions to treatment resulting from unstable housing;
D. Increased participant compliance with recovery residence requirements;
E. Increased successful transitions to longer-term stable housing and recovery supports; and
F. Support for successful completion of applicable Proposition 36 treatment requirements.
The Contractor shall not be solely responsible for court disposition, treatment completion, or other outcomes controlled by the Court, County, or clinical treatment provider. Contractor performance shall be evaluated based on the housing and recovery-support services within its control.

## Target Population 
Services shall be provided to adults who:
A. Are referred by the Solano County Superior Court – Adult Drug Court, County Behavioral Health or its designated representative;
B. Are eligible to participate in the applicable Proposition 36 treatment-mandated pathway under Health and Safety Code section 11395;
C. Are actively participating in, or are required to participate in, court-ordered substance use disorder and/or mental health treatment; and
D. Require a safe, stable, recovery-oriented living environment to support treatment engagement and compliance with court requirements.
The County anticipates serving a 
minimum of nine (9) unique participants
 during the contract term.
The Contractor shall not independently determine an individual's clinical eligibility for treatment or make court-related determinations. Clinical eligibility and court participation shall remain the responsibility of the appropriate County, court, and/or treatment personnel.

## Referral and Admission Process 
Both the County and the Solano County Superior Court – Adult Drug Court, or its designated representative, shall make referrals to the Contractor.
The Contractor shall:
A. Respond to referrals within 
[one business day]
;
B. Coordinate with the referring County representative regarding admission availability;
C. Conduct an intake and orientation consistent with the Contractor's approved policies and the requirements of this RFP;
D. Review and execute all required participant agreements and house rules;
E. Provide participants with written information regarding program expectations, resident rights, grievance procedures, and consequences for violations;
F. Notify the County promptly of admission, unsuccessful placement, discharge, or other significant changes in participant status; and
G. Coordinate with the County and treatment provider regarding barriers that may affect the participant's ability to maintain housing or participate in required treatment.

## Facility Standards
Each residence shall meet, at minimum, all applicable requirements of the 
Solano County Guidelines for Recovery Residences
, applicable federal, State, and local requirements, and the following minimum physical standards:
A. Each sleeping room shall provide at least 
50 square feet per bed
.
B. There shall be at least 
one sink, toilet, and shower for every six (6) residents
.
C. Adequate and secure storage shall be available for residents' personal belongings and food.
D. Onsite laundry facilities shall be available and accessible to residents.
E. Kitchen and dining areas shall be appropriately sized and equipped to accommodate residents for shared meals and routine household activities.
F. A designated common/group area shall be available for house meetings, recovery activities, and resident interaction.
G. The residence shall comply with all applicable occupancy, fire/life-safety, building, health, zoning, and other applicable requirements.
H. The Contractor shall maintain appropriate documentation demonstrating compliance with applicable facility requirements and shall make such documentation available to the County upon request.

## Staffing and House Management
The Contractor shall designate a qualified 
House Manager/Residence Manager
 for each residence.
The House Manager shall be responsible for day-to-day operation of the residence, including:
A. Enforcing established house rules consistently;
B. Facilitating weekly house meetings;
C. Maintaining a safe and recovery-supportive environment;
D. Monitoring resident compliance with program requirements;
E. Documenting incidents, drug-screening results, admissions, discharges, and other required activities;
F. Communicating significant concerns to the Contractor's program administrator and designated County representative; and
G. Implementing the Contractor's emergency and safety procedures.
The Contractor shall maintain staffing levels sufficient to safely operate each residence and shall identify its staffing and supervision model in its proposal.

## Drug- and Alcohol-Free Environment
The Contractor shall maintain a zero-tolerance environment for the possession, use, distribution, or sale of alcohol or illicit substances within the residence, consistent with applicable law and the approved program rules.
The Contractor shall maintain written procedures addressing:
A. Random and for-cause drug and alcohol testing;
B. Suspected substance use or possession;
C. Relapse response;
D. Contraband;
E. Emergency situations;
F. Participant safety; and
G. Circumstances requiring removal from the residence.
A relapse or failed drug test shall be addressed in accordance with the Contractor's approved policies and the participant's treatment and recovery needs. The Contractor shall coordinate with the County and treatment provider before discharge whenever circumstances permit, except where immediate removal is necessary to protect the participant or others.

## Participant Rights and Grievances
The Contractor shall:
A. Treat all participants with dignity and respect;
B. Maintain written participant rights and responsibilities;
C. Maintain a written grievance and complaint procedure;
D. Ensure that house rules and disciplinary procedures are applied consistently and fairly;
E. Prohibit discrimination and harassment; and
F. Provide participants with information regarding how to report concerns regarding housing conditions, staff conduct, safety, or program operations.

## Coordination with County and Treatment Providers
The Contractor shall coordinate with the Solano County Superior Court – Adult Drug Court, Solano County Behavioral Health, and designated treatment/case-management personnel as appropriate to support participant housing stability and treatment engagement.
The Contractor shall promptly notify the designated County representative of significant events. Significant events include but are not limited to the following:
A. Admission and discharge;
B. Unplanned departure from the residence;
C. Serious rule violations;
D. Positive drug or alcohol tests;
E. Significant behavioral or safety incidents;
F. Emergency medical or behavioral health events;
G. Law enforcement involvement occurring at the residence; and
H. Circumstances that may jeopardize continued housing.
All information sharing shall comply with applicable confidentiality, privacy, and information-sharing requirements.

## Monitoring and Quality Assurance
The County and/or its designated representatives may monitor Contractor’s performance and compliance with the requirements of this RFP throughout the contract term. 
Monitoring activities may include, but are not limited to:
A. Site visits and facility inspections;
B. Review of policies and procedures;
C. Review of participant records and required program documentation;
D. Review of drug and alcohol screening records;
E. Review of incident, grievance, and discharge records;
F. Interviews with Vendor staff and, as appropriate, participants;
G. Verification of Recovery Residence certification status and progress toward certification; and
H. Review of program utilization, performance measures, and required reports.
Contractor shall cooperate with County monitoring activities and provide requested records and documentation within reasonable timeframes established by the County.
When monitoring identifies a material deficiency or area of noncompliance, the County may require the Vendor to submit and implement a Corrective Action Plan (CAP). The CAP shall identify the deficiency, the corrective action to be taken, the responsible party, and the timeframe for completion. The Vendor shall correct identified deficiencies within the timeframe established or approved by the County.
Conditions presenting an immediate health or safety risk shall be addressed promptly and shall not be subject to the standard corrective-action timeframe.

## Goals & Deliverables
Contractor shall work toward the following program goals and shall report performance utilization data. Performance shall be evaluated based on factors within the Contractor’s reasonable control and shall take into consideration participant referrals, individual needs, and other circumstances that may affect utilization and outcomes.
Goal 1 – Maintain Recovery Housing Capacity
Contractor shall maintain contracted Recovery Residence capacity available to meet the housing needs of eligible County-referred participants throughout the contract period.
Performance Measure: Provide up to 4,590 occupied bed-days during the contract period, based on participant referrals, eligibility, and need.
Goal 2 – Serve Eligible Proposition 36 Participants
Contractor shall provide Recovery Residence services to eligible individuals referred through the Solano County Superior Court Adult Drug Court and/or County.
Performance Measure: Serve a minimum of nine (9) unique participants during the contract period.
Goal 3 – Promote Housing Stability and Successful Transitions
Contractor shall support participants in maintaining stable Recovery Residence placement for as long as the placement remains appropriate and, when participants exit, support planned transitions to stable housing or other appropriate recovery-supportive living arrangements.
Performance Measures: The Contractor shall track and report the number and percentage of participants who: (1) remain stably housed in the Recovery Residence; (2) exit through a planned transition to stable housing or another appropriate residential setting; (3) leave through an unplanned exit; and (4) exit to homelessness or an unknown destination. The Contractor shall also report average length of stay and discharge destination for all participants who exit the program.
Goal 4 – Achieve Recovery Residence Certification
Contractor shall obtain certification for all Recovery Residences utilized under this contract in accordance with the National Alliance for Recovery Residences (NARR) standards through the applicable California certifying entity.
Performance Measure: One hundred percent (100%) of Recovery Residences utilized under this contract shall obtain required certification no later than December 31, 2027.

The Contractor shall obtain and maintain certification consistent with National Alliance for Recovery Residences (NARR) standards through the California Consortium of Addiction Programs and Professionals (CCAPP) no later than December 31, 2027, unless otherwise approved in writing by the County. The Contractor shall provide documentation of certification, application status, corrective actions, or other evidence of compliance upon request. Failure to achieve or maintain the required certification may constitute a material contract deficiency and may result in corrective action, withholding of payment, or other remedies available under the agreement

## Agricultural Chemicals (Herbicides)
Scope of Work: Agricultural Chemicals (Herbicides)
1. Scope
Solano County Public Works is seeking a qualified vendor to provide and deliver agricultural chemicals, including herbicides, for use in County vegetation management and maintenance operations.
The County will procure materials through authorized purchase orders. The vendor shall provide the specified products and deliver them to the County's designated facility.
2. Vendor Responsibilities
The vendor shall:
Provide and deliver herbicides and related agricultural chemicals specified by the County.
Coordinate delivery with County staff and ensure products are properly packaged, labeled, and transported.
Provide current Safety Data Sheets (SDS), product labels, and other applicable product information upon request.
Notify the County of product shortages, substitutions, discontinued products, or anticipated delivery delays.
Comply with all applicable federal, state, and local requirements, including California Department of Pesticide Regulation requirements.
Replace products that are damaged, defective, incorrectly supplied, or improperly labeled at no additional cost to the County.
3. Annual Recommendations
The vendor shall provide annual herbicide recommendations for Solano County Public Works based on current regulations, available products, industry practices, and the County's vegetation management needs.
Recommendations may include appropriate products, uses, application timing, rates, methods, and product alternatives.
4. Training
The vendor shall provide annual training for designated Solano County Public Works staff regarding the herbicides supplied under the contract. Training may include product use, handling, storage, safety, label requirements, application practices, and regulatory updates.
5. Ordering and Delivery
The County will procure materials on an as-needed basis. The County will identify specific products, quantities, and delivery requirements through purchase orders or other authorized procurement documents.
The vendor's responsibility under this Scope of Work is limited to providing and delivering the specified materials, annual herbicide recommendations, and training.

In order to address the competitive disadvantage faced by local businesses that seek to enter into contracts with the County because of the higher costs of doing business in the County, and to encourage businesses to locate and remain in the County, the County has implemented a local preference policy.
Definition of Local Business
For purposes of this section, a “local business” means a business enterprise, including but not limited to a sole proprietorship, partnership, or corporation, which has the following:

Should the lowest responsible local business bidder decline to match as set forth above, the purchasing agent shall provide the next lowest responsible local business bidder, should one exist, and its bid is within five percent (5%) of the lowest responsible bidder, with the same notice and opportunity to match the bid of the lowest responsible bidder as above.  This process shall continue as necessary, until an award is made either to a responsible local business bidder within five percent (5%) of the lowest responsible bidder, or the lowest responsible bidder itself.
In instances where a local business and a non-local business submit equivalent, lowest responsible bids, the purchasing agent shall give preference to the local business.
No contract awarded to a local business under this section shall be assigned or subcontracted in any manner that permits more than fifty (50) percent or more of the dollar value of the contract to be performed by an entity that is not a local business.

The County of Solano, Department of 
Sheriff's Office - Office of Emergency Services
, hereinafter referred to as the "County", intends to secure a contract with a qualified Proposer to provide

The proposed project will significantly strengthen the County’s emergency preparedness and operational resilience by enabling rapid, high-volume sandbag production during flood, storm, and other hazard events. By deploying an advanced sandbagging system, the County will enhance its ability to respond quickly to emerging threats, protect critical infrastructure, and support life‑safety operations across multiple jurisdictions. The machine’s high production rate will allow emergency personnel to generate large quantities of sandbags in a short period, ensuring timely protection of vulnerable areas during severe weather or disaster conditions. The system’s ability to accommodate multiple bag sizes and diverse fill materials ensures adaptability across different incident types, supporting dynamic and evolving operational needs during homeland security and disaster response activities. With user-friendly operation and minimal training requirements, the system enables staff and volunteers to produce large volumes of sandbags efficiently. This reduces operational strain, minimizes response delays, and increases overall mission effectiveness. By streamlining sandbag production and reducing labor demands, the equipment will lower emergency response costs and enable more strategic allocation of personnel and resources during critical events. Upon implementation, the project will improve the County’s response times, mitigate damage to public and private property, strengthen community resilience, and enhance the County’s ability to protect lives, infrastructure, and essential services during emergencies. This increased capability aligns directly with Homeland Security grant priorities focused on preparedness, risk reduction, and enhanced operational capacity.

## Scope of Work 
The Supplier shall procure and deliver 
one (1) fully assembled, operational sandbagging machine
 capable of filling and sealing up to 1,200 sandbags per hour with a four-person crew. The equipment shall meet all specified material‑handling, bag‑type, fill‑weight, control, sealing, and construction requirements described in this Scope of Work, ensuring the machine is commercially available, attainable, and ready for operation upon delivery.
Equipment Requirements
Performance & Capacity: Capable of filling and sealing up to 1,200 sandbags per hour, with adjustable fill weights from approximately 1 pound to 5,000 pounds depending on bag and material configuration.
Material & Bag Compatibility: Able to process varied fill materials (wet/dry sand, gravel, soil, mulch, salt, lava rock, wood chips) and compatible with woven polypropylene, polyethylene, canvas, and geotextile bags.
Construction & Mobility: Built with a heavy‑duty welded steel frame, 10‑gauge minimum steel hopper, and forklift pockets for safe relocation.
Integrated System Components:
 To ensure the machine meets measurable functionality and operates reliably in remote conditions, the equipment package shall include:
Generator: Appropriately sized and fully compatible with all electrical and operational components for locations without utility power.
Dual Hopper Agitators: Two (2) integrated agitators supporting consistent material flow, including wet and sticky materials.
Inline Industrial Sewing System: Integrated sewing system capable of sealing filled bags as part of standard operation.
Controls & Production Monitoring
Digital Control Panel: Programmable interface enabling precise runtime, material flow, and fill adjustments.
Production Monitoring: Integrated bag counter and pallet alarm to provide measurable, real‑time production tracking.
Delivery, Testing & Acceptance
The Supplier shall provide a machine that is new, tested, complete, and fully operational upon delivery. 
All required components, including hopper, agitators, control panel, sewing system, frame, mobility features, and generator shall be present and functional at inspection. 
Any deficiencies identified during acceptance shall be corrected by the Supplier in accordance with the purchase agreement to ensure reliability.
Documentation & Warranty
The Supplier shall provide operating manuals, maintenance instructions, specifications, warranty materials, and all standard manufacturer documentation. 
The machine shall be supported by a minimum two‑year or one‑million‑cycle manufacturer’s warranty to ensure long‑term reliability.
Schedule & Final Deliverable
The Supplier shall complete procurement and delivery of the fully assembled sandbagging machine by the mutually agreed-upon delivery date. 
All testing, documentation, warranty information, and required components shall be provided prior to final acceptance, ensuring timely completion of the contract deliverable.

Event Name: Behavioral Health Interim Housing Placement
Description:
The County is seeking proposals for an interim shelter model that provides time-limited stabilization through an interim housing program of approximately 90 to 120 days.
The program must primarily serve adults and older adults (ages 18 and over) with Serious Mental Illness and/or Substance Use Disorders who are experiencing homelessness, are at risk of homelessness, or are transitioning from institutional settings. Proposers may also elect to serve additional populations as a program enhancement, including parents or families with minor children who meet the same eligibility criteria and adult couples seeking to be sheltered together. While not required, the ability to effectively incorporate these populations will be considered a competitive advantage during proposal evaluation. Additionally, the County encourages Proposers to consider incorporating a limited number of immediate-access nightly (e.g., drop-in) beds for individuals requiring urgent shelter placement. Although not a minimum program requirement, this capability will be evaluated as a program enhancement.
Program design should reflect the unique needs of the population served, emphasize cost efficiency, and support the delivery of wrap-around or day services. The County is open to a range of facility configurations, including larger congregate settings, smaller-scale or single-family home–style environments, or other innovative models, provided the design promotes safety, stability, and effective service delivery. The County may fund one or multiple proposals, individually or in combination, to achieve a total capacity of up to 50 beds.

In March 2024, California voters approved Proposition 1, the Behavioral Health Services Act (BHSA), which modernizes the Mental Health Services Act (MHSA) to better respond to current behavioral health system needs. BHSA expands eligible populations to include individuals with Substance Use Disorders (SUD), prioritizes services for individuals with Serious Mental Illness (SMI), and establishes a more structured framework for accountability, outcomes, and service delivery.
BHSA is guided by core principles that include sustained investments in housing interventions, workforce development, prevention and early intervention, and innovative and pilot programs. Beginning in Fiscal Year 2026-2027, counties are required to allocate 30 percent of BHSA funding to housing interventions serving individuals with the most significant behavioral health needs who are experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness. Of this housing allocation, no less than 50 percent must be prioritized for individuals experiencing chronic homelessness. This RFP is intended to support the County’s compliance with these housing requirements while expanding urgently needed interim shelter capacity for high-need populations.
The County conducts a comprehensive Community Program Planning (CPP) process to assess the behavioral health system of care, engage community stakeholders, and identify service gaps and priority needs. Through this process, the County has identified a continued need for interim housing and shelter options that are specifically designed to serve adults with SMI who are experiencing homelessness or transitioning from institutional settings.

## Program Overview
Program Purpose and Model
The County is seeking qualified interim housing provider agencies (Proposers) to enter into a new contract to operate an interim housing program serving the vulnerable populations identified in this solicitation. The program shall provide 
low-barrier, Housing First, recovery-oriented, culturally responsive, trauma-informed, and person-centered services
 designed to promote engagement, stabilization, housing readiness, and transition to longer-term or permanent housing.
The interim housing program is intended to function as more than temporary shelter. It shall provide a safe and stable setting where participants can engage with supportive services, address barriers to housing, coordinate care, and develop a pathway toward permanent housing.
The program model may include 
up to 50 interim housing beds
, with time-limited placements generally ranging from 
90 to 120 days
. The County may fund one or multiple proposals, either individually or in combination, to achieve the total capacity of up to 50 participants at any given time.
The County encourages innovative approaches that reduce barriers to access and strengthen participant engagement. Proposed approaches may include, but are not limited to, co-located services; flexible sleeping arrangements or site configurations; accommodations for adult couples, adults with minor children, and individuals with pets or service animals; personal property storage; and other program or facility features that support trauma-informed and client-centered care.
Target Population
The program shall be designed to serve individuals who may experience one or more of the following:
Homelessness or chronic homelessness;
Transition from institutional or other restrictive settings;
Serious Mental Illness (SMI), persistent mental health conditions, Substance Use Disorders (SUD), or co-occurring disorders;
Complex trauma histories;
Significant barriers related to Social Determinants of Health (SDOH);
Frequent utilization of crisis, emergency, or inpatient services; and
Cross-system involvement or other complex service needs.
Participants may present with challenging symptoms or behaviors, including active substance use or acute psychiatric symptoms. The selected provider shall demonstrate the capacity to safely and effectively serve this population using appropriate engagement, harm-reduction, de-escalation, and behavioral health coordination strategies.

## Prerequisites
Proposer Minimum Qualifications
 
To be considered responsive to this RFP, the Proposer must meet the following minimum qualifications at the time of proposal submission:
 
Organizational Experience
 
Proposer must have at least two (2) years of experience providing housing, shelter, residential, or other closely related services to adults experiencing homelessness or housing instability.
 
Residential Program Experience
 
Proposer must demonstrate experience operating and staffing a residential housing or shelter setting. Experience limited to housing navigation, case management, outreach, or referral services without responsibility for residential program operations does not meet this requirement.
 
Experience Serving Individuals with Complex Needs
 
Proposer must demonstrate experience serving adults with significant and complex needs, which may include serious mental illness, substance use, justice-system involvement, chronic homelessness, physical health conditions, or other barriers to housing stability.
 
24/7 Program Operations
 
Proposer must demonstrate the ability to operate and appropriately staff a 24-hour, seven-day-per-week residential program, including adequate coverage for evenings, overnight hours, weekends, holidays, staff leave, and unexpected absences.
 
Behavioral Health and Crisis Response Capacity
 
Proposer must demonstrate experience supporting individuals experiencing behavioral health symptoms, substance use, behavioral challenges, or crises. The Proposer must have the ability to provide or arrange appropriate crisis response, de-escalation, and coordination with Behavioral Health treatment teams and other service providers.
 
Housing First and Harm Reduction
 
Proposer must demonstrate the ability and willingness to operate the program consistent with Housing First, Harm Reduction, Trauma-Informed Care, and low-barrier service principles, including serving individuals who may continue to experience behavioral health or substance use challenges while enrolled in the program.
 
Housing and Service Coordination
 
Proposer must demonstrate the ability to coordinate participants' access to behavioral health care, physical health care, benefits, housing navigation, permanent housing resources, and other community-based services needed to support housing stability.
 
Administrative and Fiscal Capacity
 
Proposer must demonstrate sufficient administrative, fiscal, staffing, data collection, and quality assurance capacity to successfully manage the proposed program and meet County contracting, reporting, and performance requirements.
 
Future Specialty Mental Health Services (SMHS) Capacity
 
Prior experience providing Medi-Cal Specialty Mental Health Services (SMHS), current SMHS certification, and the ability to provide SMHS at program startup are 
not minimum qualifications
 for this RFP. However, Proposer must demonstrate a willingness and reasonable organizational ability to work with the County toward developing SMHS capacity in the future, which may include becoming a certified SMHS site during a future contract term or renewal.
 
 
Proposers that do not demonstrate that they meet the minimum qualifications above may be determined non-responsive and may not advance to further evaluation.

Maintain an environment that supports participant engagement while appropriately addressing behavioral health, substance use, safety, and other complex needs.

The interim housing program is intended to serve individuals who meet applicable

## Essential Program Components and Care Approach
The selected provider shall operate interim housing services within Solano County for both referred individuals and walk‑ins, maintaining low‑barrier access. Services must be recovery‑oriented and grounded in harm reduction, with a strong focus on client stabilization, wellness, and resilience.
Providers must implement a zero‑exclusion, no‑fail approach. Entry and continued access may not be conditioned on treatment compliance, abstinence, or progress toward preset goals. Clients may not be discharged solely for ongoing substance use, psychiatric symptoms, or limited engagement. Instead, providers must use clinically appropriate strategies to re‑engage participants and adjust services as needs evolve.
Providers must coordinate with Medi-Cal managed care plans to support access to Enhanced Care Management (ECM), Community Supports (CS), and referrals to other levels of care, including mild‑to‑moderate services. 
Services must be person‑centered and aligned with each participant’s preferences, goals, and needs. At a minimum, the program model shall include:
Services Provided Directly by the Contractor:
Symptom monitoring
Medication support (reminders and coordination)
Behavioral redirection, de‑escalation, and crisis prevention
Milieu management and reinforcement of safety and communal living standards
Regular engagement and check‑ins
Motivational support
Relapse prevention and psychoeducation
Peer support and wellness/recovery activities
Substance use engagement and harm‑reduction interventions
Services Provided Directly or Through Coordinated Referral:
Medi-Cal CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM)
Justice system coordination and reentry support, when applicable
Community Supports (CS), including Housing Navigation
For participants who are not eligible for ECM or CS, providers must deliver comparable care coordination, housing navigation, and stabilization services.
All services must promote resilience, wellness, and recovery, with intensity adjusted based on individual needs, acuity, and risk factors.
Proposals must include a detailed Staffing, Training, and Implementation Plan demonstrating the provider’s capacity to operate the interim housing program and deliver required services throughout the contract term. Providers must also identify the expected number of Solano County clients served annually and show how staffing and budget align with that capacity.

## Individualized Housing Support and Stabilization
The provider shall develop an individualized 
Housing Support Plan
 for each participant that:
Identifies housing goals, barriers, strengths, and service needs;
Establishes measurable objectives related to housing stability and transition;
Guides service delivery throughout the participant's interim housing stay; and
Is updated as necessary to reflect changes in housing status, needs, or circumstances.
The Housing Support Plan shall be completed within 
30 calendar days of enrollment
, consistent with applicable DHCS requirements. The provider shall use the participant's interim housing stay to actively advance housing readiness and transition planning rather than treating the placement solely as a shelter arrangement.

## Housing Navigation and CalAIM Coordination
The provider shall ensure that participants are connected to 
Medi-Cal CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) and Community Supports (CS)
, as appropriate and based on eligibility. The provider may:
Provide ECM and/or CS services directly if authorized by the applicable Managed Care Plan; or
Coordinate timely referrals and warm handoffs to qualified ECM and/or CS providers.
For participants receiving services through an external provider, the selected provider shall maintain a defined coordination process that includes:
Referral upon program entry, when appropriate;
Communication protocols between providers;
Ongoing case coordination or case conferencing;
Monitoring of participant engagement; and
Coordination of housing transition activities and outcomes.
Housing Navigation shall be integrated into the participant's overall service and housing transition plan regardless of whether services are provided directly or through a partner organization.
Staff whose primary responsibilities are the delivery of MCP-funded ECM and/or CS services shall 
not be included in the proposed County contract budget
. If the Proposer provides these services directly, applicable services shall be supported through Managed Care Plan reimbursement.
The County recognizes that some participants may not qualify for CalAIM services. The proposed County budget may therefore include a reasonable allocation of staff time for comparable care coordination, housing navigation, and housing stabilization activities provided to participants who are not eligible for ECM and/or CS.

## Tasks, Responsibilities, and Expectations
The County is seeking proposals for an interim shelter model capable of serving up to 50 participants at any given time, supporting for approximately 90 to 120 days. 
Target Population
Required: The proposed program must primarily serve and be designed to meet the needs of the population described below.
Adults and Older Adults (ages 18 and over) with Serious Mental Illness (SMI) who are experiencing homelessness, at risk of homelessness, and/or transitioning from custodial or institutional settings.
Optional Program Enhancement (Preferred, Not Required):
Proposers may also elect to reserve a limited number of beds for immediate-access, nightly shelter. These beds would remain available each night for eligible individuals requiring urgent shelter and would not be assigned to a single participant for an extended stay.
Proposers may also elect to serve one or more of the following additional populations as a program enhancement. While not required, the ability to effectively incorporate these populations will be considered a competitive advantage in proposal evaluation: 
Parents or families with minor children who are chronically homeless or experiencing homelessness and who meet the criteria described in section 1 above; and/or  
Adult couples seeking to be sheltered together who meet the criteria described in section 1 above.
Program Design
The facility type and program design must take into consideration the unique needs of the population(s) served, cost efficiency, and the delivery of wrap-around or day services. Proposers may utilize a range of facility configurations, including but not limited to larger congregate settings, smaller-scale or single-family home style environments, or other innovative models, provided the design supports safety, stability, and effective service delivery for adults with Serious Mental Illness and/or Substance Use Disorders.
Program Scope
The County may fund one or multiple proposals, either individually or in combination, to achieve a minimum total capacity of 50 beds in order to best meet the needs of the populations described above.
While prior experience operating a Medi-Cal Specialty Mental Health Services (SMHS) program is 
not required
, Solano County Behavioral Health's long-term vision is for the selected Contractor to build the capacity to become a certified SMHS provider. Accordingly, proposers are not expected to have existing SMHS certification or begin contract operations as an SMHS billing site. However, the County is interested in partnering with a provider that demonstrates the willingness and organizational capacity to develop this capability over time, with the expectation that SMHS services may be implemented during a future contract term or renewal. This would allow the program to eventually provide services such as targeted case management, crisis intervention, mental health rehabilitation, and collateral services directly within the interim housing program.

## Health, Safety, and Regulatory Compliance
The selected provider shall operate the interim housing program in compliance with all applicable 
federal, state, and local laws, regulations, codes, standards, and County requirements
 governing interim housing, homeless services, behavioral health coordination, health, safety, accessibility, privacy, and participant services.
This includes, but is not limited to, applicable requirements under the 
California Health and Safety Code, including AB 130, Sections 33–36
, governing homeless shelter inspection, reporting, and corrective action requirements.
The provider shall:
Maintain a safe, sanitary, and appropriately staffed residential environment;
Cooperate with County, state, and other authorized inspections and monitoring activities;
Submit required reports and documentation within established deadlines;
Promptly correct deficiencies identified through inspections, monitoring, or other compliance activities; and
Maintain policies, procedures, training, staffing, and documentation necessary to demonstrate ongoing compliance.

## Definitions
Housing First
Housing First is an evidence-based approach that prioritizes rapid access to housing without preconditions, such as mandatory service participation, sobriety, or treatment compliance. Interim housing programs operating under Housing First principles must maintain low-barrier access, ensuring participants are not excluded due to behavioral health symptoms, substance use, or service refusal. Programs may offer supportive services, but participation must remain voluntary and participant self-determination must be upheld at all times. Requirements such as medication compliance, drug testing, or housing readiness assessments are not permitted under Housing First principles.
Harm Reduction
Harm Reduction refers to a set of practical, evidence-based strategies designed to reduce the negative consequences associated with high-risk behaviors, while meeting participants where they are. This approach emphasizes non-judgmental, client-centered services that focus on improving health, safety, and quality of life. High-risk behaviors may include, but are not limited to, active substance use, sharing needles, sex work, or other behaviors that pose health risks. Harm Reduction utilizes education-based, non-abstinence-based approaches delivered in a trauma-informed and culturally responsive manner. Punitive responses, including drug testing or sanctions for such behaviors, are inconsistent with Harm Reduction principles.
Trauma-Informed Care
Trauma-Informed Care is an approach that recognizes the widespread prevalence and impact of trauma and integrates this understanding into all aspects of service delivery. Programs operating under this framework actively seek to avoid re-traumatization, promote physical and emotional safety, build trust, and support empowerment, healing, and participant choice.
Whole Person Care
Whole Person Care is a coordinated, person-centered approach to service delivery that addresses the full range of factors impacting an individual’s stability and wellbeing. This includes, but is not limited to, physical health, behavioral health, housing stability, and social needs. Whole Person Care recognizes that these factors are interconnected and must be addressed collectively to support long-term stabilization and improved health outcomes.
Motivational Interviewing
Motivational Interviewing is a collaborative, person-centered counseling approach that supports individuals in exploring and resolving ambivalence about change. This approach emphasizes autonomy, self-efficacy, and intrinsic motivation by drawing out an individual’s own beliefs, values, strengths, and motivations, rather than directing or prescribing specific actions.
Homelessness
For purposes of this program, eligibility determinations related to homelessness must align with Behavioral Health Services Act (BHSA) requirements and the definitions of homelessness adopted by the DHCS for CalAIM Community Supports. These definitions are consistent with those set forth at 24 CFR Section 91.5, with the following modifications applicable to interim housing populations:
Individuals exiting an institutional or carceral setting shall be considered homeless if they were experiencing homelessness immediately prior to entry into the institutional or carceral stay, or if they become homeless during the stay, regardless of the length of institutionalization or incarceration. 
Individuals or families are not required to have an annual income below 30 percent of the area median income in order to meet homelessness eligibility criteria for this program.

## Background:

## Minimum Requirements:

 The Proposer must have a minimum of five (5) years of experience providing student transportation services similar in scope and complexity to those requested in this RFP. Experience providing transportation services to California K-12 public school districts or other public agencies is preferred.
KNOWLEDGE:
 The Proposer must demonstrate knowledge of applicable federal, state, and local laws, regulations, safety requirements, industry standards, and best practices governing pupil transportation, including the transportation of general education and special education students and students requiring specialized transportation accommodations.

Stockton Unified School District (“District”) is seeking a qualified transportation contractor to provide safe, reliable, compassionate, and highly specialized pupil transportation services for students attending Walton Special Center.
Walton Special Center provides special education services to eligible students with severe disabilities from approximately ages 3 through 22, including preschool, elementary, secondary, young adult, and other specialized programs. Walton also provides early intervention services supporting infants and toddlers with special needs and their families.
Transportation provided under this Scope of Work shall recognize that Walton Special Center serves a student population whose physical, medical, behavioral, developmental, sensory, communication, and mobility needs may be significantly greater than those of students transported on conventional school bus routes.

Student safety;
Dignity and respect;
Individualized service;
Continuity of care;
Appropriate supervision;
Reliable and timely transportation;
Effective communication;
Medical and emergency preparedness; and
Compliance with each student's Individualized Education Program (“IEP”) and transportation accommodations, when applicable.

## Vehicle Requirements:
Vehicles used for Walton Special Center transportation shall be appropriate for the individual needs of the students assigned to the vehicle.
All vehicles shall:
Meet all applicable California laws and regulations governing pupil transportation;
Be maintained in safe and reliable operating condition;
Successfully complete all inspections required by applicable law;
Be properly licensed and insured;
Have functioning heating and air-conditioning systems;
Be maintained in a clean and sanitary condition;
Be free from unsecured equipment or objects;
Provide adequate space for required mobility and medical equipment;
Have appropriate emergency equipment;
Have operable communication equipment; and
Be equipped with all required student restraint and securement systems.
Vehicles transporting students using wheelchairs shall be appropriately equipped with:
ADA-compliant or otherwise legally required wheelchair lifts or ramps;
Wheelchair securement systems;
Occupant restraint systems;
Appropriate lift safety barriers;
Adequate wheelchair positioning space; and
Securement locations appropriate for the student's wheelchair or mobility device.
A wheelchair shall never be transported without being properly secured.

## Air-Conditioning and Climate Control:
Due to the medical and physical vulnerability of students served by Walton Special Center, functioning climate control shall be considered an essential vehicle requirement.
The Contractor shall:
Ensure air-conditioning and heating systems are operational prior to dispatch;
Immediately report a climate-control failure to District Transportation;
Avoid prolonged exposure of students to excessive heat or cold;
Provide a replacement vehicle when continued operation could adversely affect student health or safety; and
Prioritize students with medically documented temperature sensitivities when responding to equipment failures.

## School Bus Drivers:
Drivers assigned to Walton Special Center routes shall possess all licenses, certificates, medical clearances, training, and qualifications required by applicable federal and California law.
In addition to normal school bus driver qualifications, Walton drivers shall receive specialized training addressing the population they will transport.
Training shall include, as applicable:
Transporting students with severe disabilities;
Disability awareness;
Student dignity and respectful interaction;
Wheelchair lift operation;
Wheelchair securement;
Child safety restraint systems;
Safety vest and harness procedures;
Emergency evacuation of students with limited mobility;
Seizure awareness;
Basic recognition of medical emergencies;
Behavioral support and de-escalation;
Autism and sensory awareness;
Communication with nonverbal students;
Confidentiality;
Student-specific transportation plans;
Mandated reporting responsibilities;
Emergency procedures;
First aid and CPR;
Bloodborne pathogen precautions; and
Procedures for contacting District personnel during an emergency.
The District may require additional training when necessary to safely transport a particular student.

## Bus Attendants:
The Contractor shall provide a qualified Bus Attendant when required by the District or a student's IEP.
Bus Attendants shall be trained to support students with severe disabilities and shall assist the driver with student supervision and safety.
Bus Attendant responsibilities may include:
Monitoring students throughout transportation;
Assisting students during boarding and exiting;
Assisting with wheelchair loading;
Monitoring wheelchair securements;
Assisting with child safety restraint systems;
Monitoring student behavior;
Implementing District-approved behavioral support strategies;
Observing students for signs of medical distress;
Supporting emergency evacuation;
Maintaining appropriate seating and positioning;
Monitoring students who cannot independently communicate distress;
Providing reassurance and appropriate sensory support;
Maintaining student confidentiality; and
Immediately communicating safety or medical concerns to the driver.
The primary responsibility of the Bus Attendant shall be student safety and supervision.
Bus Attendants shall not perform duties that distract them from monitoring students while the vehicle is in motion.

## Medical and Health Considerations:
Some Walton students may have significant medical or health-related needs.
The Contractor shall establish procedures for drivers and attendants to respond appropriately to medical emergencies while remaining within the scope of their training and authorization.
The Contractor may be required to accommodate students with:
Seizure disorders;
Respiratory conditions;
Feeding precautions;
Mobility limitations;
Medical devices;
Oxygen or respiratory equipment;
Emergency medication protocols;
Temperature sensitivities;
Significant allergies;
Specialized positioning requirements; or
Other medically related accommodations.
Drivers and attendants shall receive any student-specific health or emergency information determined necessary by the District before transporting the student.
Nothing in this Scope of Work shall require transportation personnel to perform medical procedures for which they are not properly trained or legally authorized.

Communication methods;
Safety precautions; or

## Student Loading and Unloading:
Students shall never be rushed during loading or unloading.
Drivers and attendants shall provide sufficient time for:
Wheelchair lift operation;
Wheelchair positioning;
Securement;
Specialized restraint installation;
Student transfers;
Student communication;
Behavioral transition;
Verification of authorized receiving adults; and
Other student-specific procedures.
A final safety check shall be completed prior to vehicle movement.

## Wheelchair Transportation:
For students utilizing wheelchairs or mobility devices, the Contractor shall ensure:
The wheelchair or mobility device is compatible with safe vehicle transportation.
The wheelchair is secured using an approved securement system.
The student is secured using the required occupant restraint system.
Securements are checked prior to vehicle movement.
Wheelchair brakes are applied as appropriate during loading and securement.
Lift procedures are followed at all times.
Students are never left unattended while positioned on an operating wheelchair lift.
Equipment does not obstruct aisles or emergency exits.
Wheelchairs and mobility devices remain properly positioned during transportation.
Drivers and attendants responsible for wheelchair transportation shall demonstrate proficiency in wheelchair securement procedures.

Conventional car seats;
Safety vests;
Specialized harnesses;
Integrated seats;
Booster-style systems;
Specialized positioning systems; or

## Student Behavior and Supervision:
Drivers and attendants shall manage student behavior using safe, respectful, and District-approved methods.
Transportation personnel shall not:
Use corporal punishment;
Humiliate or ridicule students;
Threaten students;
Use inappropriate physical restraint;
Leave a student unsupervised as punishment;
Remove a student from the vehicle at an unauthorized location; or
Deny transportation without District authorization.
Behavior concerns shall be documented and reported to District Transportation and appropriate school personnel.
The District shall retain responsibility for determining appropriate student disciplinary or behavioral interventions.

## Communication with Non-Verbal and Limited-Verbal Students:
The Contractor shall recognize that some students may have limited ability to communicate discomfort, illness, fear, or distress.
Drivers and attendants shall be trained to observe changes in:
Behavior;
Breathing;
Skin color;
Body positioning;
Facial expression;
Vocalizations;
Movement;
Responsiveness; and
Other indicators of possible distress.
Student communication devices shall remain accessible when required and shall be transported safely.

## Adult Present / Safe Transfer Requirement:
Students identified by the District as requiring adult supervision shall never be left unattended at a residence, bus stop, school, or other location.
When an authorized adult is required to receive the student and no authorized adult is present, the Contractor shall:
Keep the student safely supervised aboard the vehicle.
Attempt to contact the parent, guardian, or authorized responsible adult.
Notify District Transportation.
Follow District instructions regarding additional delivery attempts.
Notify school administration when directed.
Return the student to an approved District location when directed.
The Contractor shall not release a student to an unauthorized individual.
There shall be no driver or contractor discretion to waive this requirement.

## Ride Time:

Avoid unnecessarily lengthy routes;
Limit excessive numbers of stops;
Minimize student transfers;
Avoid unnecessary vehicle changes;
Reduce prolonged waiting aboard vehicles;
Comply with IEP transportation limitations; and
Prioritize student health, safety, and comfort when designing routes.

## Route Continuity:
Consistency is particularly important for students with severe disabilities.
The Contractor shall make reasonable efforts to maintain consistent:
Drivers;
Bus Attendants;
Vehicles;
Pickup times;
Drop-off times;
Seating assignments; and
Transportation routines.
Frequent unnecessary changes in assigned personnel are discouraged.
When substitutions are necessary, substitute personnel shall have access to all information and training necessary to safely perform the assignment.
