## Route Familiarization:
Prior to independently operating a Walton Special Center route, assigned drivers shall become familiar with:
The route;
Pickup and drop-off locations;
School loading areas;
Student-specific loading requirements;
Wheelchair-accessible loading locations;
Known transportation hazards;
Authorized receiving procedures; and
Student-specific transportation accommodations.
The District may require route dry runs or orientation before service begins.

## Absence of Assigned Personnel:
The Contractor shall maintain sufficient substitute drivers and Bus Attendants to ensure uninterrupted service.
The absence of a regularly assigned:
Driver;
Bus Attendant;
Dispatcher; or
Other Contractor employee
shall not relieve the Contractor of its obligation to provide service.
Substitute staff assigned to Walton routes shall meet the same qualification and training requirements applicable to regularly assigned employees.

## Breakdowns and Replacement Vehicles:
The Contractor shall give Walton transportation requests priority when a vehicle becomes disabled due to the vulnerability of the student population.
When a breakdown occurs:
Students shall remain appropriately supervised;
District Transportation shall be notified immediately;
Parents or schools shall be notified as directed by the District;
A suitable replacement vehicle shall be dispatched promptly;
The replacement vehicle shall accommodate all student mobility and restraint needs; and
Required Bus Attendant coverage shall continue.
A standard vehicle shall not be substituted when it cannot accommodate the students assigned to the route.

## Delays:
The Contractor shall immediately notify District Transportation of significant delays.
The Contractor shall provide:
Route number;
Vehicle number;
Reason for delay;
Current location;
Estimated arrival time; and
Any student safety concerns.
When directed by the District, the Contractor shall also provide parent/guardian notifications.

## Emergency and Evacuation Planning:
The Contractor shall maintain emergency procedures specifically addressing students who may be unable to independently evacuate a vehicle.
Procedures shall address:
Wheelchair users;
Nonambulatory students;
Students using specialized restraints;
Students with significant cognitive disabilities;
Students who may resist evacuation;
Students with sensory sensitivities;
Students dependent upon medical or mobility equipment; and
Students requiring continuous adult assistance.
Drivers and attendants shall receive hands-on training regarding emergency evacuation.
Emergency planning shall prioritize life safety while recognizing the unique needs of individual students.

## Accidents and Safety Incidents:
Any accident, injury, medical emergency, student elopement, restraint failure, wheelchair securement failure, unauthorized student release, or other significant safety event shall be reported immediately to District Transportation.
The Contractor shall:
Protect students from additional injury.
Contact emergency services when appropriate.
Notify the District immediately.
Follow all required accident-reporting procedures.
Preserve relevant video and electronic data.
Submit written documentation within the timeframe established by the District.
Cooperate fully with District, law enforcement, CHP, Risk Management, and regulatory investigations.

## Student Left on Vehicle Prevention:
The Contractor shall maintain strict procedures designed to prevent a student from being left unattended aboard a vehicle.
At the conclusion of every route or trip, the driver shall physically inspect:
Every passenger seating area;
Wheelchair positions;
Floor areas;
Areas behind seats; and
The rear of the vehicle.
Any required electronic child-check system shall be properly utilized.
Leaving a student unattended aboard a vehicle shall constitute a serious safety violation and shall be immediately reported to the District.

## Video and Vehicle Safety Technology:
Vehicles shall be equipped with technology capable of supporting student safety and incident review.
Technology shall include:
GPS/AVL tracking;
Interior video;
Exterior video;
Driver tablets;
Electronic route manifests;
Real-time vehicle tracking;
Electronic student ridership systems;
RFID or student identification systems;
Parent notifications mobile application; and
District transportation dashboards.
Video and electronic records shall be preserved upon District request.

## Student Ridership Accountability:
The Contractor shall maintain accurate records identifying which students board and exit each vehicle.
When required by the District, the transportation system shall record:
Student name or identification number;
Vehicle;
Route;
Boarding location;
Boarding time;
Exit location;
Exit time; and
Date of transportation.
Drivers and attendants shall verify that students exit at the correct authorized location.

## Confidentiality: 
Transportation personnel may receive confidential information regarding student disabilities, medical conditions, behavioral needs, and educational accommodations.
Such information shall be used solely for the purpose of safely transporting the student.
The Contractor and its employees shall comply with all applicable student privacy and confidentiality requirements.
Student information shall not be discussed with unauthorized individuals.

## Community-Based Instruction and Off-Campus Transportation:
Walton Special Center provides community-based instruction and other off-campus educational opportunities.
The Contractor may be required to transport students to locations including, but not limited to:
Shopping centers;
Grocery stores;
Parks;
Community facilities;
Work experience locations;
Recreational facilities;
Therapeutic programs;
Field trip destinations; and
Other instructional locations designated by the District.
Vehicles used for these trips shall provide the same specialized accommodations required for the students' regular home-to-school transportation.

## Field Trips:
The Contractor may be asked to provide field trips transportation. The Contractor shall be capable of providing accessible transportation for Walton field trips and other off-campus experiences.
The Contractor shall provide vehicles capable of accommodating:
Wheelchairs;
Mobility devices;
Specialized restraints;
Bus Attendants;
School staff;
Necessary student equipment; and
Other accommodations designated by the District.
No student shall be excluded from a District-approved activity because the Contractor failed to provide an appropriately equipped vehicle.

## Summer Program Services:
Walton Special Center may provide extended school year, summer session, or other summer educational services.
The Contractor shall maintain the ability to provide specialized transportation during summer programs as requested by the District.
Summer transportation shall be subject to the same safety, staffing, equipment, supervision, and individualized accommodation requirements contained within this Scope of Work.

## Staff Professionalism:
Personnel assigned to Walton Special Center transportation shall demonstrate patience, professionalism, compassion, and respect toward students and families.
The District may request removal from a Walton assignment of any Contractor employee whose conduct demonstrates:
Unsafe behavior;
Inappropriate treatment of students;
Lack of patience;
Failure to follow student-specific procedures;
Failure to maintain confidentiality;
Repeated communication problems;
Failure to follow District direction; or
Conduct inconsistent with the safe transportation of students with severe disabilities.

## Parent and Guardian Interaction:
Drivers and attendants shall maintain professional and respectful communication with parents and guardians.
Transportation personnel shall not independently:
Change student transportation arrangements;
Approve alternate stops;
Modify pickup or drop-off times;
Change authorized receiving adults;
Modify student restraints; or
Change IEP-related transportation accommodations.
Requests for changes shall be referred to District Transportation.

## District Training and Observation:
The District reserves the right to:
Provide additional training;
Observe Contractor employees performing transportation duties;
Conduct vehicle inspections;
Observe student loading and unloading;
Review wheelchair securement procedures;
Review restraint installation;
Review driver and attendant qualifications;
Review training records; and
Require corrective action when deficiencies are identified.
The Contractor shall cooperate fully with such activities.

## Contractor Management:
The Contractor shall designate management personnel responsible for Walton Special Center transportation.
At minimum, the Contractor shall provide access to:
An Operations Manager;
Dispatch personnel;
A qualified Driver Trainer/Safety representative;
A Fleet Maintenance representative; and
An emergency contact whenever students are being transported.
Management shall be capable of responding immediately to significant student safety concerns.

## Required Records:
The Contractor shall maintain records relating to Walton transportation, including:
Driver qualifications;
Bus Attendant qualifications;
Training records;
Vehicle inspection records;
Preventive maintenance records;
Route assignments;
Student ridership;
Wheelchair securement training;
Specialized restraint training;
Accident reports;
Incident reports;
Late route reports;
Missed trip reports;
Complaint records; and
Corrective actions.
Records shall be made available to the District upon request.

## Performance Expectations:
The District expects a high level of service reliability for Walton Special Center.
Performance shall be evaluated using factors including:
On-time performance;
Missed trips;
Late pickups;
Student ride times;
Driver continuity;
Bus Attendant continuity;
Vehicle availability;
Breakdown frequency;
Parent complaints;
School complaints;
Safety incidents;
Proper use of specialized restraints;
Wheelchair securement compliance;
Communication effectiveness; and
Compliance with individualized transportation requirements.
Repeated failure to meet established performance standards may result in corrective action, financial penalties where authorized by the contract, removal of personnel, or other contractual remedies.

## Missed Transportation:
A missed trip involving a Walton student shall be treated as a priority service failure.
The Contractor shall immediately:
Notify District Transportation.
Determine the reason transportation was missed.
Dispatch appropriate replacement transportation when directed.
Ensure the replacement vehicle accommodates the student's individual needs.
Document the event.
Submit corrective action when requested.
The Contractor shall never direct a parent or guardian to personally transport a student as a substitute for contracted service unless specifically authorized by the District.

## Service Philosophy:
Transportation of students attending Walton Special Center requires a level of care beyond ordinary transportation services.
Contractor employees shall understand that:
Every student is to be transported with dignity, patience, safety, and respect.
Efficiency shall never take priority over the health or safety of a student.
Employees shall recognize that seemingly minor changes to a transportation routine may significantly affect a student with severe developmental, physical, sensory, behavioral, or medical needs.
The Contractor shall therefore operate Walton transportation using a 
student-centered approach
 that prioritizes consistency, individualized support, and close coordination with the District.

## Compliance:
The Contractor shall comply with all applicable federal, state, and local requirements governing transportation of students with disabilities, including applicable requirements of:
The Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA);
Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act;
The Americans with Disabilities Act;
California Education Code;
California Vehicle Code;
California Department of Education requirements;
California Highway Patrol requirements;
Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards;
Student privacy laws; and
All applicable District policies and procedures.
Where an IEP or student-specific transportation plan establishes a higher level of service than the Contractor's normal operating procedures, the student-specific requirement shall govern unless otherwise directed by the District.

## District Authority:
The District shall retain authority to determine:
Student eligibility for transportation;
Student assignments;
Routes;
Stops;
School arrival and departure requirements;
Vehicle type;
Bus Attendant requirements;
Student transportation accommodations;
Authorized pickup and drop-off locations;
Maximum allowable ride times;
Required specialized restraints;
Wheelchair transportation requirements;
Medical or behavioral transportation precautions; and
Changes necessary to support a student's IEP.
The Contractor shall implement District-approved transportation requirements within the timeframe established by the District.

## Schedule / Term of Services:
Work will commence on the date of the executed contract and all work shall be completed by end of contract date.
The initial term of the Agreement shall be for one (1) year. At the District’s discretion, the Agreement may be renewed for up to four (4) additional one-year terms, for a total potential contract term not to exceed five (5) years.
Renewal is not automatic and shall be subject to satisfactory Contractor performance, continued District need, availability of funding, mutual written agreement of the parties, and all required District approvals.
In determining whether to renew the Agreement, the District may consider the Contractor’s quality of legal services, responsiveness, communication, timeliness, management of legal matters, compliance with Agreement requirements, billing practices, and overall performance.
The District is under no obligation to exercise any renewal option.

## Evaluation criteria
- Firm Qualifications & Experience: 30
- Approach to Services: 25
- Staffing, Vehicles, and Safety: 25
- Cost Proposal: 20
- Understanding of Walton Special Center Transportation Needs : 5
- Operational Approach and Service Continuity: 5
- Student Safety and Specialized Transportation Practices: 5
- Management Team and Organizational Capacity: 5
- Responsiveness and Overall Interview: 5

Description:
The City of Thousand Oaks is seeking proposals from qualified construction management firms to provide construction management services for the City’s Downtown Thousand Oaks Project, from pre-construction and design-phase support through bidding and award assistance, construction management, and project closeout.
 
The selected Consultant will support the City throughout project Phases by providing constructability review, cost and schedule input, and construction-feasibility analysis. Services will also include recommendations for sequencing, staging, and utility coordination; assistance with bidding and award; construction management; project documentation; schedule monitoring; change order management; issue resolution; punch list support; and project closeout assistance. The Consultant will coordinate, as directed by the City, with the developer, design consultant, contractor, utility agencies, regulatory agencies, and other stakeholders.
 
At the City’s sole discretion, the agreement may be amended to include construction management services for future Downtown Project phases, subject to City approval, available funding, successful Consultant performance, and compliance with applicable procurement and contracting requirements.
 
The selected firm shall have demonstrated experience with large developer-funded or developer-coordinated infrastructure projects, municipal public works projects, public right-of-way improvements, utility coordination, and stakeholder coordination.

On July 7, 2026, the Thousand Oaks City Council approved the entitlements of the City’s Downtown Project. The Downtown Project is located at 2100 East Thousand Oaks Boulevard, encompasses approximately 17.6 acres, and includes public and developer-related improvements within the Downtown area. The project is anticipated to be delivered in multiple phases. The approved Downtown Entitlement Plans are included as Attachment B and should be used by Proposers as the current planning-level reference for Phase 1.
 
Phase 1 is expected to include the realignment of the Ventura County Watershed Protection District reinforced concrete box culvert, on-site civil improvements, roadway encroachment improvements, public utility improvements, and partial demolition of existing non-structural elements of the Civic Arts Plaza. Phase 2A is anticipated to primarily include construction of the private mixed-use development on the Westside Parcel. Phase 2B is anticipated to include renovations to Carpenter Park. Phase 2C is anticipated to include the City Hall adaptive reuse, including a public market. Phase 3 is anticipated to include construction of the amphitheater. In addition, the Oakwood Improvement Project (CI5814) is anticipated to provide street improvements along Oakwood Drive as part of the Downtown Project, including curb, gutter, sidewalk, drainage, and roadway-widening improvements.
 
RRM Design Group, Inc. is serving as the design consultant for the Downtown Project with Smith Group and KPFF as lead subconsultants.
 
The City is seeking proposals from qualified construction management firms to provide construction management services for the entire Phase 1 delivery period. The selected Consultant will provide pre-construction and design-phase support, bidding and award assistance, construction management, and project closeout services, including constructability review, coordination, cost and schedule review, phasing, staging, utility coordination, and overall project delivery support.
 
The City may, at its sole discretion, amend the selected Consultant’s agreement to include services for future phases of the Downtown Project, subject to City approval, available funding, successful Consultant performance, and compliance with applicable procurement and contracting requirements.

## Project Background Information and Purpose
As described in the Background section, Phase 1 of the Downtown Project includes public improvements, including the realignment of the Ventura County Watershed Protection District reinforced concrete box culvert, on-site civil improvements, roadway encroachment improvements, and public utility improvements. RRM Design Group, Inc. is serving as the prime design consultant for Phase 1 of the Downtown Project. The approved Downtown Entitlement Plans are included as Attachment B and are incorporated by reference for purposes of describing the Phase 1 improvements.
 
Through this Request for Proposal (RFP), the City is seeking proposals from qualified construction management firms to provide pre-construction support, bidding and award assistance, construction management, coordination with the developer and project stakeholders, construction support services, and project closeout for the entire Phase 1 delivery period.
 
The purpose of this RFP is to retain a qualified construction management consultant to support the City in the successful delivery of Phase 1. The selected consultant will provide construction management expertise, assist with coordination among the City, developer, design consultant, contractor, utility agencies, regulatory agencies, and other stakeholders, monitor construction progress, manage project documentation, support issue resolution, and help ensure the project is delivered in accordance with approved plans, specifications, schedule, budget, and applicable City requirements. The consultant will also coordinate Phase 1 improvements with anticipated Phase 2A development to identify and address potential interface, sequencing, and construction impacts including assisting the City with the Phase 2A developer selection process.
 
The City may, at its sole discretion, amend the selected consultant’s agreement to include construction management services for future phases of the Downtown Project, including Phase 2A, Phase 2B, Phase 2C, Phase 3 and CI5814. Any future amendment(s) shall be subject to City approval, available funding, successful consultant performance, and compliance with applicable procurement and contracting requirements.
 
A draft Professional Services Agreement is included for reference (Attachment A).

## Scope of Work
The selected Consultant shall provide construction management services for Phase 1 of the Downtown Project. Services shall include pre-construction support, bidding and award assistance, construction management, coordination with developers and project stakeholders, construction support services, and project closeout. The Consultant shall provide experienced personnel, systems, and procedures necessary to support the City in delivering Phase 1 in accordance with approved plans, specifications, schedule, budget, applicable regulatory requirements, and City standards. The Consultant shall use the approved Downtown Entitlement Plans (Attachment B), together with subsequent City-issued addenda and permit-ready construction documents, as applicable, when performing the services.

Reviewing project plans, specifications, cost estimates, schedules, bid documents, and related materials. This review shall include the approved Downtown Entitlement Plans (Attachment B) and subsequent City-issued documents, as applicable.
Providing constructability review comments related to completeness, coordination, sequencing, staging, access, utilities, and potential construction issues.
Providing cost, schedule, phasing, staging, sequencing, procurement and risk reduction recommendations.
Assisting with bid package review, bid item review, technical specifications, special provisions, and coordination of bidding documents.
Supporting the bidding process, including pre-bid meetings or site walks, bidder questions, addenda review, bid evaluation, contractor qualification review, and award recommendations.
Participating in Phase 1 design meetings to provide construction-focused input regarding constructability.
Participating in pre-construction meetings and assisting with agendas, meeting notes, and action item tracking.

## Phases/Services
The Downtown Project is anticipated to be delivered in multiple phases. The City is currently advancing Phase 1 from approved entitlement plans toward permit-ready construction documents. Phase 1 includes site preparation work, including roads and utilities, and is expected to include the Ventura County Watershed Protection District reinforced concrete box culvert realignment, on-site civil improvements, roadway encroachment improvements including the construction of West Street and extension of Oakwood Drive, public utility improvements and partial demolition of existing non-structural elements of the Civic Arts Plaza. The approved Downtown Entitlement Plans are included as Attachment B and should be reviewed by Proposers in preparing their approach, staffing, schedule, and fee proposal.
 
Phase 1 design is anticipated to occur from September 2026 through mid-2028. Phase 1 construction is anticipated to begin in late 2028, following completion of permit-ready construction documents, applicable agency and utility approvals, bidding, and City award of a construction contract. These timeframes are preliminary and are provided for proposal-planning purposes only.
 
The selected construction management consultant will be expected to coordinate with the City, Phase 1 design consultant, selected developer, utility agencies, regulatory agencies, and other stakeholders to address interfaces between Phase 1 public infrastructure improvements and future development activity.
 
At this time the base agreement is anticipated to cover Phase 1 as described in Section 4 – Scope of Work.  Additional phases for the selected consultant may be issued as amendments at a later dates.
 
Potential phases shall include  Phase 2A, which includes the private development portion of the project, including the mixed-use buildings and hotel on the Westside Parcel; Phase 2B, consisting of the park and restaurant pad; Phase 2C, consisting of the City Hall adaptive reuse, including a public market; and Phase 3, consisting of construction of the amphitheater. In addition, the Oakwood Improvement Project (CI5814) is anticipated to provide future roadway widening, drainage, and sewer improvements in support of the Downtown Project.  At the City’s sole discretion, the selected consultant’s agreement may be amended to include construction management services for future phases, subject to City approval, available funding, successful consultant performance, and compliance with applicable procurement and contracting requirements.

## Levine Act Compliance
California Government Code section 84308 (Levine Act) prohibits any Thousand Oaks City Council member from participating in any action related to a contract, agreement, or franchise agreement (excluding labor or competitively bid contracts) if the Council member receives a campaign contribution totaling more than $500 (aggregated) from the party to the contract, agreement or franchise agreement, their agents, or any financially interested participant who actively supports or opposes the matter within the previous twelve (12) months. Council members must also disclose any eligible campaign contribution received on the record of the proceeding.
Council members are prohibited from accepting, soliciting, or directing a campaign contribution of more than $500 (aggregated) from a party, their agent/representative, or a financially interested participant during a proceeding and for 12 months following the date a final decision is made. In addition, a party, their agent/representative, or a financially interested participant is prohibited from contributing more than $500 (aggregated) to a Council member during a proceeding and for 12 months following the date a final decision is made.
The Levine Act also requires parties to certain contracts, agreements, or franchise agreements to disclose any campaign contribution over $500 (aggregated) within the preceding twelve (12) months by the party to the agreement, contract, or franchise agreement and their agents. The Levine Act does not apply to competitively bid, labor, or personal employment contracts.
All proposals must include completion of the Levine Act Disclosure Form.

Description:
The County of Tuolumne, through its Health and Human Services Agency, Department of Social Services, hereinafter referred to as the “County”, is requesting proposals from qualified Resource Families (formerly known as Foster Families) interested in providing Quality Parenting and Caregiving Respite Services at the Tuolumne County Resource Family Home (TCRFH), formerly known as the Emergency Children’s Shelter.
The County intends to contract with an unlimited number of qualified applicants paying up to $100 per day. In the event respite services are needed, the qualified individuals on the list will be contacted. If a qualified applicant is not available to provide respite services, the County will continue to contact qualified providers on the list to provide contracted services.
California law and federal law provide specific employment restrictions for retirees and/or current County employees that desire to contract with the County. 
For CalPERS retirees
: if the work you will perform as a contractor is the same or similar to work you performed as an active employee or is work that is performed by active employees, it is most likely subject to the PERS retired annuitant restrictions, meaning the employment is disallowed and the County will not be able to enter into a contract with you. 
For current County employees:
 California and federal law prohibit a current employee from contracting with its employer while being an active employee.  If an employee is interested in becoming an independent contractor, the employee must consider separation from employment with the County, however should the employee retire, he/she may be subject to the CalPERS retired annuitant laws.  Should a current County employee respond to a RFQ while in active employment status, the employee must separate from employment prior to award of the contract. 
No County time is allowed to be used to prepare for or work on a response to a County RFQ.

Child Welfare Services clients are often struggling with substance abuse, mental illness, and interpersonal violence within the co-occurring contexts of poverty, socioeconomic status, and cultural differences. The complex interaction of psychological states and presenting problems require the program have team members who are knowledgeable and committed to this population, and who understand their obstacles of logistical issues, child-related concerns, court mandates, and the negative consequences of Child Welfare Services involvement.
When parents and caregivers cannot care for their children, the Resource Family (formerly known as foster family) must be able to provide the loving, committed, skilled care that the child needs while working effectively with the system to achieve the best permanency option for that child. When successful, the Resource Families work with agency staff and the child’s parents/caregivers as a team to support the child. Tuolumne County Child Welfare Services is seeking a contractor who supports the family, not just the youth, in hopes of reunifying the child with his/her family.
The County of Tuolumne, through its Department of Social Services (DSS) seeks to establish a list of qualified persons (“Qualified Provider List”) interested in providing Quality Parenting and Caregiving Respite Services (formerly known as ECS Management Respite Services) at the Tuolumne County Resource Family Home (formerly known as the Emergency Children’s Shelter). A qualified individual’s placement on the Qualified Provider List does not in any way guarantee being chosen for Respite services when the need arises. The County cannot accept proposals from any individual who is currently employed with the County of Tuolumne (California Government Code §29708).
The responsibility of this position is to provide Quality Parenting and Caregiving Respite Services at the County owned Tuolumne County Resource Family Home when the contracted Quality Parenting and Caregiving individual requires respite as mandated in the Agreement. Contracted Quality Parenting and Caregiving Services providers are provided respite at a rate of four (4) days per month, and four (4) one-week vacations per Agreement per year, for a total of seventy-six (76) days. However, in the event of unforeseen circumstances the need for respite could exceed these allotments.

## Sample Agreement
A sample Agreement is attached to this RFQ, which details all standard terms and conditions required by the County of Tuolumne.

## Project Scope
It is the County’s intent to establish a Qualified Provider List of 3 to 5 providers to provide Quality Parenting and Caregiving Respite Services at the County owned Tuolumne County Resource Family Home. The selected individual(s) will be responsible for working closely with children placed in the home, children's families, County staff, and community partners who work with children placed in the home.

## Minimum Qualifications
Minimum Qualifications:
 The Review Committee will consider all applicants whose qualifications comply with the following criteria:
Must provide certificate of Resource Family Approval.
Other Desired Qualifications
:
Knowledge of Tuolumne County demographics.
Knowledge of child development, including developmental milestones, principles of individual and group behaviors, attachment and placement issues, boundary setting, behavior modification, and trauma informed parenting techniques.
Basic knowledge of the Juvenile Court process.
Valid California Drivers License
Married and/or single Resource Families may not have children or relatives residing in their care during the period providing respite services unless approved in writing by the Health and Human Services Director or her designee.
Must be willing to accept children of all ages, and genders from birth to 17+ years of age, for up to ninety (90) days.

## Submittal of Proposals
Sealed proposals must be received online and will be accepted and reviewed on a rolling basis until the County builds a qualified provider list of three to five (3 to 5) qualified providers or NO LATER THAN  
5:00 pm
, whichever comes first. Providers could be approved to start respite care as soon as May 1, 2026.  
Proposals are to be submitted electronically using the County’s e-Procurement platform, 
https://procurement.opengov.com/portal/tuolumnecountyca
. Proposals will be received only as instructed above, and must be received before 
5:00 pm
 on 
Wednesday, June 30, 2027
. Proposals shall not be submitted via hard copy, (hand delivered or mailed), facsimile, nor via email. It is the sole responsibility of the proposer to properly upload its proposal so that it is received by the time and date required. Any proposal received after said time and/or date or in any other format other than as instructed herein, cannot be considered and will not be accepted. The County’s e-Procurement Platform records the time stamp for every proposal submitted properly in the system. Once a proposal is submitted in the e-procurement platform, the Proposer will receive an email confirmation, and the proposal status will also show as “submitted.”

## Respite Duties
Duties of the Respite Quality Parenting and Caregiving provider will include:
Reside at the home twenty-four (24) hours a day each day of scheduled respite;
Provide care consistent with Resource Family Approval (RFA) written directives set by the California Department of Social Services (CDSS), to ensure a safe and stable environment for the children in care;
Remain in compliance with RFA written directives at all times;
Maintain current RFA certification;
Provide transportation for children to school, visitations, and other appointments;
Provide nutritionally balanced meals and snacks for the children;
Maintain working relationships with County staff and community partners;
Report and document the needs and behaviors of the children placed at the home;
Maintain a safe and sanitary environment at the home, including basic housekeeping duties; and
Attend required meetings and trainings
All Federal, State, County and Agency policies, protocols and standards will be followed.

.

. Any oral responses to questions are not binding on the County.

## Site Preparation Prescription
Masticate/Shred/Chip
Masticate/Shred/Chip:
All shrubs > 12 inches in height including, white thorn, manzanita, deer brush, buckbrush, and bear cover, except as described below:
Shrubs growing within 6 inches of the bole of a residual tree.
Riparian vegetation.
Live hardwoods, except as described below:
Retain all blue and valley oaks trees, as well as bigleaf maple.
Retain the 5 largest oaks per acre that are ≥ 8 feet tall and 0.5-inch DBH.
Conifers smaller than 10 inches DBH to a spacing of 12 feet x 12 feet and all conifers greater than 10 inches DBH to a spacing of 25 feet x 25 feet, as measured from the bole, except for the following:
Retain all healthy sugar pine without evidence of white pine blister rust or bark beetle attack.
Species preference for retention trees: sugar pine, Douglas-fir, giant sequoia, ponderosa pine/Jeffrey pine, incense cedar, and white fir.
Favor cutting incense cedar and white fir.
Retain obligate riparian species - resprouting trees such as alders, big leaf maples, dogwoods, cottonwoods and aspens, and shrubs such as willows. 
Masticate all existing piles and slash to contract specifications, where allowable.
Brush, small dead trees, and slash shall not be pushed into retained trees and left untreated.
Mastication shall occur on slopes up to 45%. On slopes 45%-55%, or if otherwise inoperable by mechanical equipment, cut slash and coarse woody debris ≤ 12 inches in diameter shall be cut and piled by hand (see Piling Specs section below). Contractor shall obtain approval of machine inoperable area designation from project manager. During pre-bid site visits, contractor should assess inoperable areas and factor machine inoperable cost. Project manager approval of an area as inoperable is not equivalent to a change in treatment prescription.
All treated standing material shall be severed from the main stem to no more than 6 inches above the ground when hand felling and 3 inches when masticating on level surfaces.  When cut vegetation occurs near natural obstacles such as rock, downed logs, or leave trees, leave stump no more than 8 inches heights. 
Debris created through mastication shall not exceed 3 feet in length and debris depth shall not exceed 12 inches or shall be piled for burning.
Debris created through chipping shall not exceed 3 feet in length and depth of material shall not exceed 6 inches except when masticating piles. Debris exceeding 6 inches in depth shall be piled for burning.
In areas where fuel densities prohibit the construction of piles, material shall be chipped and evenly dispersed.
Snag and Downed Log Removal and Retention
Masticate, chip, or pile all standing snags and downed woody logs less than 12-inch DBH, except as described below:
Snag specifications within Riparian Conservation Areas (RCAs):
Remove whole dead trees from RCAs, perennial, intermittent, and ephemeral drainages given Exclusion Zone limitations.
Trees that cannot be removed in their entirety shall be lopped off at the start of the Exclusion Zone and that material built into piles.
All remaining parts of trees left in Exclusion Zones shall have branches lopped off at the bole and piled following all specifications on pile construction and placement.
Within Exclusion Zones, hand pile all felled material ≤ 12 inches in diameter and > 6 feet in length, following all specifications on pile construction and placement.
Retain all hardwood snags greater than or equal to 12 inches DBH.
Except for the five largest per acre, fell all standing conifer snags and treat like downed woody logs.
Retained snags shall be at least one tree length from roadways and/or other infrastructure.
Leave the five largest downed woody logs greater than 12-inch DBH at the small end per acre, bucked into 20-ft. length making full contract with the ground.
Limbs and tops less than 12-in. DBH shall be masticated or hand piled if machine operability is a constrain.
Road Barriers
In sections along the road that are relatively flat and preexisting barriers do not exist to discourage breach, vegetation will be utilized to create a barrier. 
Preference for barrier material would be:
Large, downed logs.
Live conifers or hardwoods between 6 to 9 inches DBH spaced 6 feet apart at the bole.
Shrubs (i.e. manzanitea, deer brush, bear clover, etc.) shall be used as a roadside barrier only if large, downed logs, live conifers, or live hardwoods are not present and/or if there is an operational or safety concern that prevents the use of the preferred barrier material.
If live vegetation is used, the remaining material shall be no closer than 15-feet off the road so it will not grow into the road and will consist of a single row wide paralleling the road where the breach is likely to occur.
See attached Roadside Barrier Diagram in Attachment L, Contract_Road Diagram.

## Pile Specifications
Machine Piles
Where mechanical pile construction is preferred, slash, felled trees, snags, live vegetation, and existing down woody material less than 12-in. diameter- unless otherwise treated - shall be piled to the following specifications:
Size and Location
:
Minimum size of 10 feet long x 10 feet wide x 10 feet high.  Larger piles are preferred with a variable maximum size dictated by the proximity to the drip line of residual trees.
All piles shall be made as compact as possible to facilitate burning.
Piles shall be located to minimize damage to, or ignition of, residual trees (at least 25 feet from the dripline) and other retained features (natural regeneration, snags, downed logs) during burning operations.
Piles shall be constructed at least 50 feet from ephemeral, intermittent or perennial stream courses.
Do not build piles under powerlines or within 25 feet of infrastructure.
Pile Material
:
Material shall be bucked into 10-foot lengths to facilitate production of piles that are tight and with minimal airspace.
Material extending 3 feet or more outside the uniform edge of the pile shall be trimmed.
Piles shall be neat, compact, and sufficiently free of dirt (<10% soil). If piles do not meet this requirement, they will need to be re-spread and rebuilt.
Pile Fuel Break and Fire Line
:
An 8-foot-wide fuel break shall be cleared of all but fine material around each pile.
A 24-inch-wide fire line shall be cleared to bare mineral soil around the outer ring of the pile fuel break.
In areas where there is a potential for material to roll, material shall be piled parallel to the slope (perpendicular to the contour) to prevent it from rolling.
In areas where there is potential for burning material to roll, fire lines shall be trenched on the downhill side of each pile to adequately prevent material from crossing fire lines.
Coverings
:
All piles shall be covered on the top with a minimum of a 4 feet x 4 feet piece of durable waterproof (paper or plastic) material and covered with enough slash so that the material does not fly away. The purpose of this is to maintain a dry area in the pile to ease ignition operation in the future.
Hand Piles
Where hand pile construction is preferred, slash, felled trees, snags, live vegetation, and existing down woody material less than 12-in. diameter - unless otherwise treated - shall be piled to the following specifications:
Size and Location
:
Piles shall be a minimum of 10 feet long x 10 feet wide x 5 feet high. Fewer and larger piles are preferred as long as they can be safely consumed.
All piles shall be made as compact as possible to facilitate burning.
Piles shall be placed at least 25 feet away from the dripline of trees OR at such a distance from trees so that burning shall not result in damage to residual trees.
Piles shall be constructed at least 50 feet from ephemeral, intermittent or perennial stream courses.
Do not build piles under powerlines or within 25 feet of infrastructure such as roads.
Pile Material
:
Pile light green fuels on the inside and heavy green fuels on the outside to allow the fuel to dry out so as to not attract bark beetles.
Material extending 3 feet or more outside the uniform edge of the pile shall be trimmed.
Any material greater than 12 inches in diameter is not required to be hand piled.
Pile Fuel Break and Fire Line
:
An 8-foot-wide fuel break shall be cleared of all but fine material around each pile.
An 18-inch-wide fire line shall be cleared down to bare mineral soil around the pile.
In areas where there is a potential for material to roll, material shall be piled parallel to the slope (perpendicular to the contour) to prevent roll-out.
In areas where there is potential for burning material to roll, fire lines shall be trenched on the downhill side of each pile to prevent material from crossing fire lines.
Coverings
:
All piles shall be covered with, at a minimum, a 4-foot x 4-foot piece of durable waterproof (paper or plastic) material and weighted with enough slash so that the material does not fly away. The purpose of this is to maintain a dry area in the pile to ease ignition operation in the future.

## Definitions
Chips
 - The woody residue resulting from the mechanical shredding/chipping activity. Residue size is usually less than 2 inches, but occasionally is up 2 feet in length.
Chip size for mastication:
FINE TREATMENT
75% ≤ 6 inches (15.2 cm) in length
20% > 6 inches (15.2 cm) and < 2 feet (.6 m) in length
5% 2 feet (.6 m) through 3 feet (1.8 m) in length
With accumulations ≤ 12 inches (45.7 cm) in depth
Conifer
 - A cone bearing tree with needles or leaf scales, including, but not limited to: ponderosa pine (
Pinus ponderosa
)
,
 sugar pine (
Pinus lambertiana
), incense cedar (
Calocedrus decurrens
), Douglas fir (
Pseudotsuga menziesii
), giant sequoia (
Sequoiadendron giganteum
), and bull pine ((
Pinus sabiniana
) also known as Gray pine); does not necessarily have cones at any given time.
Controlled Area
 - Area within contract boundaries designated to be protected from all contractor operations, these areas will be flagged on the ground and avoided during all operations.
Diameter at Breast Height (DBH)
 - The diameter of the main trunk of a tree/shrub measured at 4.5 feet above ground level.
Downed Log
 - All or part of the trunk of a felled tree > 10 inches in diameter at the mid-point and ≥ 10 feet in length. This includes logs in all of the various stages of decomposition.
Ephemeral Streams
 – Streams that flow only during or shortly after rainfall or snowmelt.
Exclusion Zones
 - Areas of inoperability near watershed features including regulations around Special Aquatic Features (SAFs), perennial, intermittent, ephemeral waterways.
Hardwood
 - A tree with broad, flat leaves including but not limited to oak, maple, willow, alder, cottonwood or dogwood.
High Ground Pressure Equipment
 – Equipment that exceeds 9 pounds per square inch (psi) on flat ground. Equipment types typically include: wheeled skidders, passenger vehicles and pickups, and fixed-track dozers.
Intermittent Streams
 – Streams that flow during the wet season, but dry by summer or fall.
Limited Operating Period (LOP)
 - A specified period of time during which certain activities are prohibited.
Low Ground Pressure Equipment
 – Equipment that exerts a maximum ground pressure of 9 psi on flat ground. Equipment types typically include: tracked masticators, excavators, skid steers, and feller bunchers.
Mastication
 - The physical process of cutting, shredding and/or chipping vegetation.
Mineral Soil
 - State of soil, generally below where humus and large organic matter is present marked by the absence of combustible material.
Perennial Streams
 – Streams that flow all year round.
Residual Tree or Retention Tree
 – Live tree(s) to be left standing and undamaged that comprise the forest following the contractor’s operations.
Shrubs
 – Live scrub vegetation, though some may be over 20 feet tall or woody plants such as manzanita 
(Arctostaphylos spp.)
, deer brush 
(Ceanothus spp.)
 and various other species. This does not include small conifers.
Slash
 – Debris consisting of portions of brush and /or trees created naturally, by work under this contract or debris created prior to this contract including all brush and cut trees, tops, trunks, branches, and previously made piles. Material > 1 inch in diameter and over 3 feet in length.
Snag
 - Standing dead tree with no green needles or leaves.
Special Aquatic Features (SAFs)
 – Lakes, meadows, bogs, fens, wetlands, vernal pools and springs.
Riparian Conservation Areas (RCAs)
 – Near stream areas with specific management objectives and some limitations on activities.
Perennial streams and SAFs: 300 feet on each side of stream.
Intermittent and ephemeral streams: 150 feet on each side of stream.

## Equipment Operation
Soils
Monitor ground-based operations occurring between October 15 and May 15 to prevent soil compaction. Project manager or delegated representative will assess soil conditions for traffic and operability prior to mechanical equipment off road operations after significant rainfall (> ¼ inch). Ground-based equipment will only operate on relatively dry soils of high soil strength or bearing capacity.
Wet weather recommendations: Equipment may operate when soils are dry to a minimum of 4 inches. Low-ground pressure equipment may operate off designated skid trails when soils are dry to a minimum depth of 4 inches. High-ground pressure equipment may operate off designated skid trails when soils are dry to a depth of 8 inches.
The contractor’s equipment shall not travel over the same tracks, except where designated by the project manager for access and service routes.
Soil displacement shall be minimized by working the equipment in as straight a line as possible, parallel slopes, given the known limitations of residual trees and terrain.
Rutting depth shall not exceed 4 inches over 90% of the unit. Rutting depth is measured from the top of the undisturbed litter/duff layer to the top of the duff in the rut (“duff-to duff”). Soils in the operating area must be dry enough to prevent rutting by a single pass of the equipment.
Erosion work shall be required and kept current with contract work progress for unit or partial unit acceptance. Erosion control work shall include, but is not limited to, draining of puddles on roads or smoothing out berms created by the contractor moving equipment over areas that are too wet.
Limit rubber-tired or fixed-track equipment to slopes < 35%; limit low ground pressure tracked equipment (e.g., traditional masticator or excavator) to < 45%.
Limit dozer piling to slopes < 25% and mulching mastication treatments to < 35% slope.
Safety
The contractor shall provide for public safety when operating equipment within 200 feet of structures and open roadways. The contractor shall be responsible for obtaining and following all safety procedures policies, laws and regulations required by the state, county, and private roadways for the safe operation of equipment necessary to complete the contract.
The contractor shall abide by the Maintenance Operations Signing Standards provided in Attachment G, Appendix G_Guidelines for Operations.
Protection of Improvements and Resources
Exclusion Zones
 - The Exclusion Zone begins at the edge of the channel where slopes rise uniformly or at the edge of the stream bank, whichever is
                                    furthest from the stream.
The Exclusion Zone for perennial/intermittent streams starts at: 
 The edge of the active channel where slopes rise uniformly from the stream, or at the outer edge of the following features, whichever is the furthest from the stream.
The first slope-break adjacent to the stream (e.g., stream bank, inner gorge).
Flat or nearly flat ground adjacent to the channel (e.g., floodplain or terrace). 
Obligate riparian shrub and/or tree communities associated with any of the above. 
The Exclusion Zone for SAFs begins at:
The outer edge of obligate trees, shrubs or herbaceous plants in wet meadows, bogs, fens and springs, or the high-water line of lakes and vernal pools. 
The top of the first slope-break immediately adjacent to the special aquatic feature if further than the obligate vegetation or high-water
line.
Equipment shall be operated such that shredded material stays within the treatment unit and is not distributed on lava caps, streams, roads, structures, private property, protected sites, improvements, telephone lines, established trails, stock driveways, fence lines, established land corners, or other improvements.
Equipment shall be kept free of debris accumulations that may result in fire starts.
Exclude equipment tracks within 50 feet of perennial, intermittent, or ephemeral streams. Follow regulations around SAFs.
Operate mechanical equipment on a straight-in and straight-out pattern and minimize operations and turning within the RCA.
Equipment shall not damage streambanks.
Do not exceed 2 stream crossings per mile along perennial or intermittent streams. Stream crossings must be designated by the project manager after consultation with the Forest Service Aquatic Biologist.
Do not exceed 3 stream crossings per mile along ephemeral streams. Stream crossings must be designated by the project manager after consultation with the Forest Service Aquatic Biologist.
Equipment shall not be walked between units on paved or chip-sealed roads.
The walking of equipment between units shall be worked out with the project manager, to avoid the possibility of Control Area or resource damage.
Exit and entry of units will be confined to within unit boundaries unless otherwise stated by the project manager. Entry and exit points to the unit will be chosen in a manner as to reduce resource damage and soil erosion.
See also Resource Protection Measures in Section 2.14 Project-Specific Requirements and the Best Management Practices (BMP) Checklist in Attachment J, RIM_BMP_Checklist.

## Road Use Specifications
Safety
The contractor shall furnish, install, and maintain all temporary traffic controls that provide the public with adequate warning of hazardous or potentially hazardous conditions associated with operations occurring in the area. A specific traffic control plan for each individual contract work area shall be agreed to by contractor and project manager prior to commencing operations. Devices shall be appropriate to current conditions and shall be covered or removed when not needed. Refer to Attachment G, Appendix G_GuidelinesforOperations: Sign Standards.
Accessibility
All work areas are accessible by standard pickup. Four-wheel drive vehicles may be beneficial in improving the access points of any given treatment unit. It is the contractor's responsibility to reach the work site when it is ready for treatment, including conducting any clearing of National Forest System roads.
The project manager will determine the access routes to be used by vehicles. These routes may not necessarily be the shortest distance between units.
Contractor shall be responsible to coordinate with the County to gain access to roads and/or gates as necessary.
All roads leading into each project area are to be kept open and free of any debris that may occur as a result of the work.
Protection of Roads and Road Features
The contractor shall keep all roads and trails needed for fire protection or other purposes and designated on the Map free of equipment and products, slash, and debris resulting from the contractor’s operations.
The contractor is responsible for mitigating damage to system roads and restoring system roads damaged by the contract operations.
Contractor shall clean ditches and drainage structure inlets as soon as practicable, but not to exceed 48 hours, to keep them functioning while working within the unit. Upon completion of a unit, the contractor shall clean ditches and drainage structures prior to unit acceptance. Prevent unnecessary or excessive vegetation disturbance and removal on features such as swales, ditches, shoulders, and cut and fill slopes.
Maintain road surface drainage by removing berms, unless specifically designated otherwise.
Rehabilitate temporary staging, parking, and refueling/servicing areas immediately following use.
Protection of Streamcourses
If contractor maintains storage facilities for oil or oil products on Project Area, contractor shall take appropriate preventative measures to ensure that any spill of such oil or oil products does not enter any stream or other waters.
Allow temporary refueling and servicing only at approved sites located outside of RCAs.
Install temporary wash sites only in areas where the water and residue can be adequately collected and either filtered on site or conveyed to an appropriate wastewater treatment facility. Temporary wash sites shall be approved by the Project Manager prior to use.
Refer to attached documents - Best Management Practices (BMP) Checklist (Attachment J, RIM_BMP_Checklist and Attachment K, Spill_Prevention_and_Reporting_Procedures).
Dust Abatement
Water shall be applied to unpaved road sections of any Forest Service road used to walk or haul equipment as necessary to control road surface loss, provide for road user safety, minimize damage to adjacent resources, and comply with dust abatement. Also conduct road watering for road maintenance and road surface protection using approved existing water source locations.
Non-System Roads
Existing non-system roads in the project area may be used for access only. These non-system roads are considered temporary and may require rehabilitation/obliteration, including installation of barriers to prevent further access following project activities.

## Project-Specific Requirements
Safety
The Contractor shall remove all trash from the work site.
The Contractor shall provide a Spill Prevention Control and Countermeasures (SPCC) plan on all projects as per the contract. Review and ensure spill plans are up to date. Please see Attachment K, Spill_Prevention_and_Reporting_Procedures. 
The Contractor shall Report spills and initiate appropriate clean-up action in accordance with applicable State and Federal laws, rules, and regulations. The Forest Service hazardous materials coordinator’s name and phone number shall be available to Forest Service personnel who administer or manage activities utilizing petroleum powered equipment. 
Please see Attachment K - 
Spill_Prevention_and_Reporting_Procedures
. 
 
 
The Contractor shall remove contaminated soil and other material from NFS lands and dispose of this material in a manner according to controlling regulations.
Resource Protection Measures
Control Areas
Locations of known areas needing special measures for the protection of plants, animals, cultural resources, and/or cave resources are shown on the Contract Area Map (Table 2: Control Area Restrictions) and/or identified on the ground (Table 1: Flagging Colors).
In addition to any special protection measures noted below, the Contractor has a general duty to protect all known and identified resources referenced in this subsection from damage or removal during the contractor’s operations. Discovery of additional areas, resources, or members of species needing special protection by either party shall be promptly reported to the other party, and operations shall be delayed or interrupted at that location, if project manager determines there is risk of damage to such areas, resources, or species from continued operations.
Wheeled or track-laying equipment shall not be operated in areas identified as needing special measures for the protection of cultural resources, except on roads, landings, tractor roads, or approved skid trails. Unless agreed otherwise, trees will not be felled into such areas. Contractor may be required to backblade skid trails and other ground disturbed by contractor’s operations within such areas in lieu of required cross ditching.
Contractor shall immediately notify the project manager if disturbance occurs to any area identified as needing special protection measures and shall immediately halt operations in the vicinity of the disturbance until the project manager – after consultation with the Forest Service - authorizes the contractor to proceed. The contractor shall bear costs of resource evaluation and restoration to identified sites. Such payment shall not relieve the contractor from civil or criminal remedies otherwise provided by law.
The Forest Service has exercised due diligence and followed established protocols in identifying known areas needing special protection measures. 
Nevertheless, nothing in this provision shall be interpreted as creating any warranty that all locations and special measures for the protection of plants, animals, improvements, streamcourses, cultural resources, and cave resources have been described herein, elsewhere in the contract or designated on the ground.

The Forest Service may unilaterally modify or cancel all or portions of this agreement to protect an area, object of antiquity, artifact, or similar object which is or may be entitled to protection under the American Antiquities Act of 1906 (54 USC 320301-03 ), National Historic Preservation Act of 1966 (54 USC 302101-303903 ), and implementing regulations (36 CFR 800), the American Indian Religious Freedom Act, and the Archaeological Resources Protection Act of 1979 (PL 96-95 and 36 CFR 261.9, 296.1-296.21) regardless of when the area, object or artifact is discovered or identified. Discovery of such areas or objects by either party shall be promptly reported to the other party.
The Contractor shall protect Control Areas 1 and 2 (CA-1 and CA-2) identified on the Map by avoidance unless treatment is otherwise agreed to. Contractor shall protect all known and identified or discovered historic or prehistoric sites, buildings, objects, and properties related to American history, architecture, archaeology and culture against destruction, obliteration, removal, or damage during the Contractor's operations.
The Contractor shall immediately halt operations and notify the County if damage occurs to any CA-1 and CA-2 resources. Operations shall cease in the vicinity of the resource where damage occurred until the County - after consultation with the Forest Service - authorizes the Contractor to proceed.
If damage is caused by the Contractor's operations, the Contractor shall bear costs of investigation and restoration in accordance with 36 CFR 296.14(c), provided that such payment shall not relieve the Contractor from civil or criminal remedies otherwise provided by law.
Forest Service roads that are also CA-2 sites are not fully flagged. Ingress and egress locations shall be approved by the Project Manager after consultation with a Forest Service archaeologist prior to use by Contractor.
Equipment tracks shall be excluded within 20 feet of Forest Service roads that are also CA-2 sites. Equipment working towards Forest Service roads that are also CA-2 sites shall stop no less than 20 feet from the edge of the roadbed and shall utilize a masticator attachment on an articulated arm to treat remaining roadside fuels.
Equipment utilizing Forest Service roads that are also CA-2 sites shall drive down the road centerline to avoid impacts to road morphology. If traffic approaches, only pre-approved pullout locations can be utilized.
Forest Service roads that are also CA-2 sites shall not be widened. If equipment is wider than the roadbed, Contractor shall work with the Project Manager to identify alternative access.
Where flagging is unclear, Contractor shall contact the Project Manager who will consult with a Forest Service archaeologist to fix the flagging.
Lava Caps
 
Lava caps shall be avoided and a physical barrier, such as shrubs, should be retained to protect sensitive lava cap plant species.
 
Any slash or debris resulting from Contractor's operations distributed upon lava cap shall be removed manually by Contractor after consultation with Forest Service.
 
The contractor must avoid tracking machinery on lava caps.
 
Any damage created by the Contractor’s operations on lava caps shall be immediately reported to the Project Manager and restored to condition prior to damage at the Contractor's expense and after consultation with the Project Manager and the Forest Service.
 
Residual Trees
The contractor’s operations shall not unnecessarily damage young growth or other trees to be reserved.
Excessive residual stand damage may result in contract shut down and/or default. No more than four (4) damaged trees per acre will be permitted. If damage is in excess of four (4) trees, the contractor shall be required to alter their operations to prevent the occurrence of such damage. If more than four (4) damaged trees per acre exist, a cost of $50.00 per tree will be charged.
Containment of Noxious Weeds
Noxious weeds are known to exist within the project area.
All shredding equipment, road grading or construction equipment, clothing, particularly footwear, and other equipment, including the transport vehicle should be free of soil, mud (wet or dried), seeds, vegetative matter or other debris that could contain seeds in order to prevent new infestations of invasive weeds in the project area. Dust or very light dirt, which would not contain weed seed, is not a concern.
All equipment and vehicles to be used at the job site shall be cleaned and certified free of noxious weeds and their seeds prior to entrance onto the National Forest
If by agreement, operations occur within a noxious weed area in a treatment unit(s), cleaning of equipment is required immediately afterwards, within a designated cleaning site, prior to working in any area not infested with the same species or in any weed free areas, and prior to transporting equipment out of the project area.
Contractors 
are required to
 prevent the transfer of noxious weeds from Non-National Forest System lands to National Forest System lands and from National Forest System lands to Non-National Forest System lands. 
 
If damage, breach, or incursion into areas to be avoided is caused by the Contractor's operations, the Contractor shall bear costs of investigation and restoration; monitoring and mitigation may be required if determined necessary during evaluation of damage, breach, or incursion.
Land Survey Monuments
The Contractor shall protect all known survey monuments, witness corners, reference monuments and bearing trees against avoidable destruction, obliteration, or damage during the contractor’s operations. If the contractor causes such damage, the contractor shall hire the appropriate registered land surveyor to establish or restore at the same location the monuments, corners, or accessories. Such surveyors shall use procedures in accordance with the “Bureau of Land Management Instructions for the Survey of the Public Lands of the United States” for the General Land Office surveys, land in accordance with the state law for other. Contractor shall record such survey in the appropriate county records.
Streamcourses
Streamcourses that are subject to provisions of this Section are shown on the Map. Unless otherwise agreed, the following measures shall be observed to protect streamcourses:
(a) Contractor’s Operations shall be conducted to prevent debris from entering streamcourses, except as may be authorized under paragraph (d). In event contractor causes debris to enter streamcourses in amounts that may adversely affect the natural flow of the stream, water quality, or fishery resource, contractor shall remove such debris as soon as practicable, but not to exceed 48 hours, and in an agreed manner that will cause the least disturbance to streamcourses.
(b) Culverts or bridges shall be required on Temporary Roads at all points where it is necessary to cross streamcourses. Such facilities shall be of sufficient size and design and installed in a manner to provide unobstructed flow of water and to minimize damage to Streamcourses. Trees or products shall not be otherwise hauled or yarded across Streamcourses unless fully suspended.
(c) Wheeled or track-laying equipment shall not be operated within 50 ft of streamcourses, except at crossings designated by the project manager after consultation with the Forest Service Aquatic Biologist. Project managers will walk each unit with the foreman to identify stream crossings 
(d) Flow in streamcourses may be temporarily diverted only if such diversion is necessary for contractor’s planned construction and Forest Service gives written authorization. Such flow shall be restored to the natural course as soon as practicable and, in any event, prior to a major storm runoff period or runoff season.
(e) Damage to streamcourses caused by contractor’s operations shall be repaired by the contractor in a timely and agreed manner to the extent practical as determined by the Forest Service to restore and prevent further damage.
Fell trees within RCAs directionally away from stream channels and SAFs unless otherwise recommended by a hydrologist or biologist. Fall hazard trees that cannot be removed either parallel to the contour of the slope or into the channel, as recommended by a hydrologist or biologist.
Remove activity-created woody debris to above the high-water line of stream channels.
Locate and design stream crossings to minimize disturbance to the water body. Use structures appropriate to the site conditions and traffic. Favor armored fords for streams where vehicle traffic is seasonal or temporary, and where the design maintains the channel pattern, profile, and dimension.
Prior to conducting a stream crossing, inspect and clean equipment and remove external oil, grease, dirt and mud. Repair leaks prior to unloading at the site. Inspect equipment daily and correct identified problems before entering streams or areas that drain directly to water bodies. Remove all dirt and plant parts to ensure that noxious weeds and aquatic invasive species are not brought to the site.
Soil and Erosion Control
Maintain 60% well-distributed soil cover (unburned duff; needle cast; basal live plant cover; fine woody debris; and downed logs where permitted) on slopes > 25%.
Maintain 50% well-distributed soil cover (unburned duff; needle cast; basal live plant cover; fine woody debris; and downed logs where permitted) on slopes  ≤  to 25%.
Maintain 75% well distributed soil cover within 100 feet of perennial and intermittent streams and SAFs and 50 feet of ephemeral streams. 60% in the rest of the RCA.
See Equipment Operations – see above in section 2.8 - Equipment Operation: Soils .
Improvements
So far as practicable, the contractor shall protect all physical improvements, including, but not limited to, roads, trails, ditches, fences, waterlines, and other improvements, existing in the contract area, determined to have continuing need or use.
All protected improvements shall be protected from damage by the contractor. If any protected improvements are disturbed, the contractor shall immediately contact the project manager and shall be liable for the cost of repairs. The contractor shall make timely restoration of any such improvements damaged by the contractor’s operations and, when directed shall move such improvements if and as specified in consultation with the Forest Service.
The Contractor shall be responsible for contacting all utility companies to determine the location of under and above ground utilities. The contractor shall protect or avoid these utilities during all operations of this contract.
Waterbars in skid trails, fire lines, and roads disturbed by the contractor shall be restored to condition prior to damage at the contractor’s expense.
Identify and protect National Forest System Trails (NFST) during operations. Trails, if damaged, will be restored in kind according to Forest Service standards including the placement of rolling dips.
Close skid trails to motorized travel with earth berms, logs, and/or rocks after operations are complete. Do not use stumps or root wads to close skid trails.
General Cutting
The contractor shall remove all shredded material, trees, or debris resulting from contract operations that is distributed outside of treatment unit or on Control Areas, lava caps, streams, roads, structures, private property, protected sites, improvements, telephone lines, established trails, stock driveways, fence lines, established land corners or other improvements.
Any debris resulting from the contractor’s operations on or into such areas as described in the above specifications shall be removed if possible, and any resulting damage shall be immediately reported to the project manager and restored to condition prior to damage at the contractors’ expense.

##  Inspection and Acceptance
Contractor Inspection Requirements
:
The Contractor is responsible for performing or having performed all inspections and tests necessary to substantiate that the supplies or services furnished under this contract conform to contract requirements, including any applicable technical requirements for specified manufacturers' parts. This clause takes precedence over County inspections and testing required in the contract's specifications, except for specialized inspections or tests specified to be performed solely by County.
 
Specific Inspection Procedures
:
The Contractor shall submit a unit or partial unit to the County for acceptance only when the Contractor's inspections for quality control assure the work specifications have been met. County inspections may be by work observation, measurement by pacing, tape, clinometers, prism, ocular estimation, progress of work over time, or by formal inspection. Formal inspections will cover at least one percent of the work unit on a systematic plot basis, plots will be 1/20th acre radius (26.2 feet) and will address the work specifications.
 
Measurable Performance Standards
:
* Treatment of slash, shrubs, trees
 
* Slash pile fuelbreaks
 
* Amount of soil in piles
 
* Compact and tight piles
 
* Stump height
 
* Area treated
 
* Pile covering presence/placement
 
Acceptance
:
Work on this contract will be deemed acceptable when the above measurable performance standards are met.
 
Quality Assurance Plan
:
The County will conduct inspections of each unit or sub-unit to determine work quality. Initial inspections will consist of a 100 percent visual inspection and will be based on adherence to the specific tasks listed in the contract. The County may also install a series of circular plots. Plots will be randomly located throughout each sub-item to obtain a representative sample of work. Plot size 1/20th of an acre.
 
After inspection of all plots for a unit, the quality shall be calculated as follows:
 
(Total number of acceptable plots)/(Total number of plots) * 100 = Performance Quality Percent
 
Payment will be made in full if inspection results are 95 percent or higher. No payment will be made if inspection results are less than 95 percent.
 
Inspections
:
County inspections are for the purpose of satisfying the County that the services are acceptable and do not relieve the Contractor of the responsibility for maintaining quality control.
 
The County or designated Project Manager will conduct all inspections. The Contractor (or designated representative) is encouraged to be present to observe inspections. Summary results will be made available on request.
 
Compliance Inspections
:
Visual compliance inspections will be made on a periodic basis. Such inspections are not final and do not constitute acceptance.
 
Final Inspections
:
Final (formal) inspections for payment will be made on completed units only. Contractor shall request final inspections in writing. Inspections will be attempted to be completed within fifteen (15) business days after the notice is received. The County will make all reasonable efforts to complete the inspection of work within fifteen (15) business days; however, this timeline is subject to adjustment based on Forest Service availability due to fire assignments, severe weather events, government shutdowns, or other unforeseen circumstances. In the event that the approval period is unreasonably delayed, payment may be issued with a ten percent (10%) retention at the discretion of the County until Forest Service approval is obtained. If the work is not ready for inspection at the time specified by the Contractor, the cost associated with the inspection attempt may be charged to the Contractor. 
 
Disputed Inspection
:
The Contractor may request reinspection without rework if the results are unacceptable. Reinspection must be requested in writing within 48 hours after receiving written notice of the inspection results. Reinspection will be accomplished within five working days after receipt of the Contractor's written request.
 
The same sampling and inspection procedures will be used, but new samples will be taken. The inspection pattern will be shifted so that new samples will not overlap previously inspected samples. Results will be rounded to the nearest whole percent.
 
If reinspection results are within five percentage points of the first inspection, the original inspection result will be used in determining acceptability and payment. If reinspection results are greater than five percentage points above or below the first inspection, the reinspection results will be used.
 
If the reinspection results are within five percentage points of the first inspection, the Contractor shall pay the actual costs of the reinspection.
 
Reinspection after Rework
:
Where rework after a failed inspection may improve the inspection results, the Contractor may rework the area and request (in writing) a second inspection. County will charge to the Contractor the cost of this additional inspection. Reinspection will be accomplished within five working days after the notice is received. The results of the second inspection will be final, and no further rework will be permitted. Areas not ready for reinspection at the time specified by the Contractor will not be reinspected, and the results of the first inspection will be final.

Event Name: Mechanical Site Prep: Cherry West Item 1
Description:
The County of Tuolumne is seeking proposals from qualified individuals to conduct fuels reduction and mechanical site preparation and associated treatments for reforestation as authorized in the Master Stewardship Agreement the County has with the USDA, Forest Service, Stanislaus National Forest on behalf of the Yosemite Stanislaus Solutions (YSS) Collaborative.
The County intends to select Contractors that meet the specifications of this Solicitation based on best value.
The Cherry West Project consists of approximately 535.90 acres of mechanical site preparation, including mastication and piling. Specifications and treatment requirements are detailed in Section 2, Scope of Services. The County intends for site preparation work in the priority units (M014A and M014C) to begin no earlier than June 2027 and be completed no later than October 31, 2027. These units are scheduled for planting in Spring 2028.
All remaining units must be completed no later than October 31, 2028, and are scheduled for planting in Fall 2028.
The project is located at an approximate elevation of 6,000 feet and may be inaccessible during periods of snow cover. The Contractor shall plan and schedule work accordingly to meet the required completion deadlines.

In December 2017, the Tuolumne County Board of Supervisors approved a Master Stewardship Agreement (MSA) with the USDA, Forest Service, Stanislaus National Forest on behalf of the Yosemite Stanislaus Solutions (YSS) Collaborative, giving the County authority over the next 10 years to work with the Forest Service to conduct landscape restoration activities on the Stanislaus National Forest within the boundaries of Tuolumne County. It was executed in January of 2018.
The Supplemental Project Agreements (SPA) developed under the MSA are for the purpose of protecting, enhancing and restoring forest and watershed health and bringing economic opportunities to the local area. The County is using the collaborative group YSS and its sub-partners inside YSS to assist with Forest Health Projects.
It is the County's intent to subcontract out program administration and project management, this will include supervision of Contractors and oversee the work being done on this project.

## Minimum Qualifications
Proposer, their principal, or their staff, including sub-contractors, shall have been regularly engaged in the items contained in Section 2: Scope of Services within forested environments for at least 3 years.
Proposer shall possess all permits, licenses, and professional credentials necessary to perform services as specified under this RFP.

The selected contractor must be authorized to conduct business within the state of California, including by being registered with the Secretary of State, where applicable, with all necessary filings current and up to date.
