## Introduction
The County of Tuolumne is seeking proposals from qualified individuals to conduct fuels reduction and mechanical site preparation and associated treatments for reforestation as authorized in the Master Stewardship Agreement the County has with the USDA, Forest Service, Stanislaus National Forest on behalf of the Yosemite Stanislaus Solutions (YSS) Collaborative.
The County intends to select Contractors that meet the specifications of this Solicitation based on best value.
The Cherry West Project consists of approximately 535.90 acres of mechanical site preparation, including mastication and piling. Specifications and treatment requirements are detailed in Section 2, Scope of Services. The County intends for site preparation work in the priority units (M014A and M014C) to begin no earlier than June 2027 and be completed no later than October 31, 2027. These units are scheduled for planting in Spring 2028.
All remaining units must be completed no later than October 31, 2028, and are scheduled for planting in Fall 2028.
The project is located at an approximate elevation of 6,000 feet and may be inaccessible during periods of snow cover. The Contractor shall plan and schedule work accordingly to meet the required completion deadlines.

## Site Preparation Prescription
Masticate/Shred/Chip
Masticate/Shred/Chip:
All shrubs > 12 inches in height including, white thorn, manzanita, deer brush, buckbrush, and bear cover, except as described below:
Shrubs growing within 6 inches of the bole of a residual tree.
Riparian vegetation.
Live hardwoods, except as described below:
Retain all blue and valley oaks trees, as well as bigleaf maple.
Retain the 5 largest oaks per acre that are ≥ 8 feet tall and 0.5-inch DBH.
Conifers smaller than 10 inches DBH to a spacing of 12 feet x 12 feet and all conifers greater than 10 inches DBH to a spacing of 25 feet x 25 feet, as measured from the bole, except for the following:
Retain all healthy sugar pine without evidence of white pine blister rust or bark beetle attack.
Species preference for retention trees: sugar pine, Douglas-fir, giant sequoia, ponderosa pine/Jeffrey pine, incense cedar, and white fir.
Favor cutting incense cedar and white fir.
Retain obligate riparian species - resprouting trees such as alders, big leaf maples, dogwoods, cottonwoods and aspens, and shrubs such as willows. 
Masticate all existing piles and slash to contract specifications, where allowable.
Brush, small dead trees, and slash shall not be pushed into retained trees and left untreated.
Mastication shall occur on slopes up to 45%. On slopes 45%-55%, or if otherwise inoperable by mechanical equipment, cut slash and coarse woody debris ≤ 12 inches in diameter shall be cut and piled by hand (see Piling Specs section below). Contractor shall obtain approval of machine inoperable area designation from project manager. During pre-bid site visits, contractor should assess inoperable areas and factor machine inoperable cost. Project manager approval of an area as inoperable is not equivalent to a change in treatment prescription.
All treated standing material shall be severed from the main stem to no more than 6 inches above the ground when hand felling and 3 inches when masticating on level surfaces.  When cut vegetation occurs near natural obstacles such as rock, downed logs, or leave trees, leave stump no more than 8 inches heights. 
Debris created through mastication shall not exceed 3 feet in length and debris depth shall not exceed 12 inches or shall be piled for burning.
Debris created through chipping shall not exceed 3 feet in length and depth of material shall not exceed 6 inches except when masticating piles. Debris exceeding 6 inches in depth shall be piled for burning.
In areas where fuel densities prohibit the construction of piles, material shall be chipped and evenly dispersed.
Snag and Downed Log Removal and Retention
Masticate, chip, or pile all standing snags and downed woody logs less than 12-inch DBH, except as described below:
Snag specifications within Riparian Conservation Areas (RCAs):
Remove whole dead trees from RCAs, perennial, intermittent, and ephemeral drainages given Exclusion Zone limitations.
Trees that cannot be removed in their entirety shall be lopped off at the start of the Exclusion Zone and that material built into piles.
All remaining parts of trees left in Exclusion Zones shall have branches lopped off at the bole and piled following all specifications on pile construction and placement.
Within Exclusion Zones, hand pile all felled material ≤ 12 inches in diameter and > 6 feet in length, following all specifications on pile construction and placement.
Retain all hardwood snags greater than or equal to 12 inches DBH.
Except for the five largest per acre, fell all standing conifer snags and treat like downed woody logs.
Retained snags shall be at least one tree length from roadways and/or other infrastructure.
Leave the five largest downed woody logs greater than 12-inch DBH at the small end per acre, bucked into 20-ft. length making full contract with the ground.
Limbs and tops less than 12-in. DBH shall be masticated or hand piled if machine operability is a constrain.
Road Barriers
In sections along the road that are relatively flat and preexisting barriers do not exist to discourage breach, vegetation will be utilized to create a barrier. 
Preference for barrier material would be:
Large, downed logs.
Live conifers or hardwoods between 6 to 9 inches DBH spaced 6 feet apart at the bole.
Shrubs (i.e. manzanitea, deer brush, bear clover, etc.) shall be used as a roadside barrier only if large, downed logs, live conifers, or live hardwoods are not present and/or if there is an operational or safety concern that prevents the use of the preferred barrier material.
If live vegetation is used, the remaining material shall be no closer than 15-feet off the road so it will not grow into the road and will consist of a single row wide paralleling the road where the breach is likely to occur.
See attached Roadside Barrier Diagram in Attachment L, Contract_Road Diagram.

## Pile Specifications
Machine Piles
Where mechanical pile construction is preferred, slash, felled trees, snags, live vegetation, and existing down woody material less than 12-in. diameter- unless otherwise treated - shall be piled to the following specifications:
Size and Location
:
Minimum size of 10 feet long x 10 feet wide x 10 feet high.  Larger piles are preferred with a variable maximum size dictated by the proximity to the drip line of residual trees.
All piles shall be made as compact as possible to facilitate burning.
Piles shall be located to minimize damage to, or ignition of, residual trees (at least 25 feet from the dripline) and other retained features (natural regeneration, snags, downed logs) during burning operations.
Piles shall be constructed at least 50 feet from ephemeral, intermittent or perennial stream courses.
Do not build piles under powerlines or within 25 feet of infrastructure.
Pile Material
:
Material shall be bucked into 10-foot lengths to facilitate production of piles that are tight and with minimal airspace.
Material extending 3 feet or more outside the uniform edge of the pile shall be trimmed.
Piles shall be neat, compact, and sufficiently free of dirt (<10% soil). If piles do not meet this requirement, they will need to be re-spread and rebuilt.
Pile Fuel Break and Fire Line
:
An 8-foot-wide fuel break shall be cleared of all but fine material around each pile.
A 24-inch-wide fire line shall be cleared to bare mineral soil around the outer ring of the pile fuel break.
In areas where there is a potential for material to roll, material shall be piled parallel to the slope (perpendicular to the contour) to prevent it from rolling.
In areas where there is potential for burning material to roll, fire lines shall be trenched on the downhill side of each pile to adequately prevent material from crossing fire lines.
Coverings
:
All piles shall be covered on the top with a minimum of a 4 feet x 4 feet piece of durable waterproof (paper or plastic) material and covered with enough slash so that the material does not fly away. The purpose of this is to maintain a dry area in the pile to ease ignition operation in the future.
Hand Piles
Where hand pile construction is preferred, slash, felled trees, snags, live vegetation, and existing down woody material less than 12-in. diameter - unless otherwise treated - shall be piled to the following specifications:
Size and Location
:
Piles shall be a minimum of 10 feet long x 10 feet wide x 5 feet high. Fewer and larger piles are preferred as long as they can be safely consumed.
All piles shall be made as compact as possible to facilitate burning.
Piles shall be placed at least 25 feet away from the dripline of trees OR at such a distance from trees so that burning shall not result in damage to residual trees.
Piles shall be constructed at least 50 feet from ephemeral, intermittent or perennial stream courses.
Do not build piles under powerlines or within 25 feet of infrastructure such as roads.
Pile Material
:
Pile light green fuels on the inside and heavy green fuels on the outside to allow the fuel to dry out so as to not attract bark beetles.
Material extending 3 feet or more outside the uniform edge of the pile shall be trimmed.
Any material greater than 12 inches in diameter is not required to be hand piled.
Pile Fuel Break and Fire Line
:
An 8-foot-wide fuel break shall be cleared of all but fine material around each pile.
An 18-inch-wide fire line shall be cleared down to bare mineral soil around the pile.
In areas where there is a potential for material to roll, material shall be piled parallel to the slope (perpendicular to the contour) to prevent roll-out.
In areas where there is potential for burning material to roll, fire lines shall be trenched on the downhill side of each pile to prevent material from crossing fire lines.
Coverings
:
All piles shall be covered with, at a minimum, a 4-foot x 4-foot piece of durable waterproof (paper or plastic) material and weighted with enough slash so that the material does not fly away. The purpose of this is to maintain a dry area in the pile to ease ignition operation in the future.

## Definitions
Chips
 - The woody residue resulting from the mechanical shredding/chipping activity. Residue size is usually less than 2 inches, but occasionally is up 2 feet in length.
Chip size for mastication:
FINE TREATMENT
75% ≤ 6 inches (15.2 cm) in length
20% > 6 inches (15.2 cm) and < 2 feet (.6 m) in length
5% 2 feet (.6 m) through 3 feet (1.8 m) in length
With accumulations ≤ 12 inches (45.7 cm) in depth
Conifer
 - A cone bearing tree with needles or leaf scales, including, but not limited to: ponderosa pine (
Pinus ponderosa
)
,
 sugar pine (
Pinus lambertiana
), incense cedar (
Calocedrus decurrens
), Douglas fir (
Pseudotsuga menziesii
), giant sequoia (
Sequoiadendron giganteum
), and bull pine ((
Pinus sabiniana
) also known as Gray pine); does not necessarily have cones at any given time.
Controlled Area
 - Area within contract boundaries designated to be protected from all contractor operations, these areas will be flagged on the ground and avoided during all operations.
Diameter at Breast Height (DBH)
 - The diameter of the main trunk of a tree/shrub measured at 4.5 feet above ground level.
Downed Log
 - All or part of the trunk of a felled tree > 10 inches in diameter at the mid-point and ≥ 10 feet in length. This includes logs in all of the various stages of decomposition.
Ephemeral Streams
 – Streams that flow only during or shortly after rainfall or snowmelt.
Exclusion Zones
 - Areas of inoperability near watershed features including regulations around Special Aquatic Features (SAFs), perennial, intermittent, ephemeral waterways.
Hardwood
 - A tree with broad, flat leaves including but not limited to oak, maple, willow, alder, cottonwood or dogwood.
High Ground Pressure Equipment
 – Equipment that exceeds 9 pounds per square inch (psi) on flat ground. Equipment types typically include: wheeled skidders, passenger vehicles and pickups, and fixed-track dozers.
Intermittent Streams
 – Streams that flow during the wet season, but dry by summer or fall.
Limited Operating Period (LOP)
 - A specified period of time during which certain activities are prohibited.
Low Ground Pressure Equipment
 – Equipment that exerts a maximum ground pressure of 9 psi on flat ground. Equipment types typically include: tracked masticators, excavators, skid steers, and feller bunchers.
Mastication
 - The physical process of cutting, shredding and/or chipping vegetation.
Mineral Soil
 - State of soil, generally below where humus and large organic matter is present marked by the absence of combustible material.
Perennial Streams
 – Streams that flow all year round.
Residual Tree or Retention Tree
 – Live tree(s) to be left standing and undamaged that comprise the forest following the contractor’s operations.
Shrubs
 – Live scrub vegetation, though some may be over 20 feet tall or woody plants such as manzanita 
(Arctostaphylos spp.)
, deer brush 
(Ceanothus spp.)
 and various other species. This does not include small conifers.
Slash
 – Debris consisting of portions of brush and /or trees created naturally, by work under this contract or debris created prior to this contract including all brush and cut trees, tops, trunks, branches, and previously made piles. Material > 1 inch in diameter and over 3 feet in length.
Snag
 - Standing dead tree with no green needles or leaves.
Special Aquatic Features (SAFs)
 – Lakes, meadows, bogs, fens, wetlands, vernal pools and springs.
Riparian Conservation Areas (RCAs)
 – Near stream areas with specific management objectives and some limitations on activities.
Perennial streams and SAFs: 300 feet on each side of stream.
Intermittent and ephemeral streams: 150 feet on each side of stream.

## Performance Requirement Summary
Slash piling
: 95% or more of all slash designated for piling shall be piled.
Slash piles
: Constructed piles shall be 90% or more soil free. 95% or more of all piles constructed shall be compact/ tight piles and shall meet size specifications. 99% or more of all piles constructed shall be covered with the required covering.
Fuel break/fire line
: 95% or more of all piles constructed shall meet fuel break/ fire line requirements.
Dead tree/snag cutting
: 95% or more of all dead standing trees that are designated for cutting shall be cut following the requirements specified above. This shall be counted on an individual stem basis. Each individual stem originating from the ground shall count as a single stem.
Mastication
: 95% or more of all treatable material designated for mastication shall be masticated.

## Equipment Specifications
Prior to award, Tuolumne County reserves the right to inspect the equipment to be furnished. If the equipment is found to be in such condition to indicate the need for frequent repairs and delays in performance, it shall be rejected. The decision of the Project Manager shall be final as to whether equipment is in suitable condition for acceptance.
 
All equipment shall comply with specifications in Attachment G - FINAL_AppendixG_GuidelinesforOperations that provides fire precautions and control. Please see Attachment N, Stanislaus_FireInspectionForm_MSA for items contractors will be inspected on; this form may be updated. 
Specific equipment to be furnished is as follows:
A. All equipment shall be furnished on a fully operational basis, of modern design, and in good operating condition, with a competent, fully qualified operator.
 
B. Prime Power Unit – The proposal must include at least one tracked carrier unit with a boom mounted masticating head capable of masticating dead standing snags up to 20 inches DBH and ten feet tall, and down material up to 20 inches in diameter. While not all equipment needs to meet these specifications, providing additional compliant units is encouraged, as it demonstrates the contractor’s capacity to operate at scale.
Equipment shall be capable of working continuously on 0 to 45 percent slopes, and on pitches up to 50 percent.
Contractor shall have at least one piece of equipment capable of mulching masticated material into the soil up to a depth of 6 inches.
Equipment shall have an independently adjustable, mechanically, or hydraulically powered head and housing that controls the height and angle of mulching head. Must be able to raise/reach a minimum of 3 feet above grade, and 2 feet below grade.
C.  All chainsaws or other motorized equipment shall be equipped with Forest Service approved spark arresters. Spark arresters are not required on equipment powered by exhaust-driven turbo-charged engines or motor vehicles equipped with a maintained muffler as defined in California Public Resources Code, Section 4442 and 4443.
 
D.  Equipment shall have a canopy approved by the State of California, Division of Industrial Safety.
 
E.  The Contractor shall provide all tools and equipment for self and employees.
 
F.  All equipment must be in good running condition with no excessive fluid leaks or overheating.
 
G.  All equipment shall be equipped with the tools and supplies necessary for making emergency and routine repairs and servicing.
 
H.  All equipment and service/transport vehicles shall be equipped with the required fire tools. See Attachment H - Appendix H -Fire Plan for Construction and Service Agreements. 
 
I. Contractor shall adhere to the Forest Service level of industrial precaution each day. 
 
J.  Contractor shall be responsible for all fuel, lubrication, repair, and replacement for equipment.
 
K. Contractor must have the ability to clean all equipment with both air and water
,
 and need to use the appropriate cleaning method during operations in areas that cleaning is required.

## Equipment Operation
Soils
Monitor ground-based operations occurring between October 15 and May 15 to prevent soil compaction. Project manager or delegated representative will assess soil conditions for traffic and operability prior to mechanical equipment off road operations after significant rainfall (> ¼ inch). Ground-based equipment will only operate on relatively dry soils of high soil strength or bearing capacity.
Wet weather recommendations: Equipment may operate when soils are dry to a minimum of 4 inches. Low-ground pressure equipment may operate off designated skid trails when soils are dry to a minimum depth of 4 inches. High-ground pressure equipment may operate off designated skid trails when soils are dry to a depth of 8 inches.
The contractor’s equipment shall not travel over the same tracks, except where designated by the project manager for access and service routes.
Soil displacement shall be minimized by working the equipment in as straight a line as possible, parallel slopes, given the known limitations of residual trees and terrain.
Rutting depth shall not exceed 4 inches over 90% of the unit. Rutting depth is measured from the top of the undisturbed litter/duff layer to the top of the duff in the rut (“duff-to duff”). Soils in the operating area must be dry enough to prevent rutting by a single pass of the equipment.
Erosion work shall be required and kept current with contract work progress for unit or partial unit acceptance. Erosion control work shall include, but is not limited to, draining of puddles on roads or smoothing out berms created by the contractor moving equipment over areas that are too wet.
Limit rubber-tired or fixed-track equipment to slopes < 35%; limit low ground pressure tracked equipment (e.g., traditional masticator or excavator) to < 45%.
Limit dozer piling to slopes < 25% and mulching mastication treatments to < 35% slope.
Safety
The contractor shall provide for public safety when operating equipment within 200 feet of structures and open roadways. The contractor shall be responsible for obtaining and following all safety procedures policies, laws and regulations required by the state, county, and private roadways for the safe operation of equipment necessary to complete the contract.
The contractor shall abide by the Maintenance Operations Signing Standards provided in Attachment G, Appendix G_Guidelines for Operations.
Protection of Improvements and Resources
Exclusion Zones
 - The Exclusion Zone begins at the edge of the channel where slopes rise uniformly or at the edge of the stream bank, whichever is
                                    furthest from the stream.
The Exclusion Zone for perennial/intermittent streams starts at: 
 The edge of the active channel where slopes rise uniformly from the stream, or at the outer edge of the following features, whichever is the furthest from the stream.
The first slope-break adjacent to the stream (e.g., stream bank, inner gorge).
Flat or nearly flat ground adjacent to the channel (e.g., floodplain or terrace). 
Obligate riparian shrub and/or tree communities associated with any of the above. 
The Exclusion Zone for SAFs begins at:
The outer edge of obligate trees, shrubs or herbaceous plants in wet meadows, bogs, fens and springs, or the high-water line of lakes and vernal pools. 
The top of the first slope-break immediately adjacent to the special aquatic feature if further than the obligate vegetation or high-water
line.
Equipment shall be operated such that shredded material stays within the treatment unit and is not distributed on lava caps, streams, roads, structures, private property, protected sites, improvements, telephone lines, established trails, stock driveways, fence lines, established land corners, or other improvements.
Equipment shall be kept free of debris accumulations that may result in fire starts.
Exclude equipment tracks within 50 feet of perennial, intermittent, or ephemeral streams. Follow regulations around SAFs.
Operate mechanical equipment on a straight-in and straight-out pattern and minimize operations and turning within the RCA.
Equipment shall not damage streambanks.
Do not exceed 2 stream crossings per mile along perennial or intermittent streams. Stream crossings must be designated by the project manager after consultation with the Forest Service Aquatic Biologist.
Do not exceed 3 stream crossings per mile along ephemeral streams. Stream crossings must be designated by the project manager after consultation with the Forest Service Aquatic Biologist.
Equipment shall not be walked between units on paved or chip-sealed roads.
The walking of equipment between units shall be worked out with the project manager, to avoid the possibility of Control Area or resource damage.
Exit and entry of units will be confined to within unit boundaries unless otherwise stated by the project manager. Entry and exit points to the unit will be chosen in a manner as to reduce resource damage and soil erosion.
See also Resource Protection Measures in Section 2.14 Project-Specific Requirements and the Best Management Practices (BMP) Checklist in Attachment J, RIM_BMP_Checklist.

## Road Use Specifications
Safety
The contractor shall furnish, install, and maintain all temporary traffic controls that provide the public with adequate warning of hazardous or potentially hazardous conditions associated with operations occurring in the area. A specific traffic control plan for each individual contract work area shall be agreed to by contractor and project manager prior to commencing operations. Devices shall be appropriate to current conditions and shall be covered or removed when not needed. Refer to Attachment G, Appendix G_GuidelinesforOperations: Sign Standards.
Accessibility
All work areas are accessible by standard pickup. Four-wheel drive vehicles may be beneficial in improving the access points of any given treatment unit. It is the contractor's responsibility to reach the work site when it is ready for treatment, including conducting any clearing of National Forest System roads.
The project manager will determine the access routes to be used by vehicles. These routes may not necessarily be the shortest distance between units.
Contractor shall be responsible to coordinate with the County to gain access to roads and/or gates as necessary.
All roads leading into each project area are to be kept open and free of any debris that may occur as a result of the work.

The contractor shall keep all roads and trails needed for fire protection or other purposes and designated on the Map free of equipment and products, slash, and debris resulting from the contractor’s operations.
The contractor is responsible for mitigating damage to system roads and restoring system roads damaged by the contract operations.
Contractor shall clean ditches and drainage structure inlets as soon as practicable, but not to exceed 48 hours, to keep them functioning while working within the unit. Upon completion of a unit, the contractor shall clean ditches and drainage structures prior to unit acceptance. Prevent unnecessary or excessive vegetation disturbance and removal on features such as swales, ditches, shoulders, and cut and fill slopes.
Maintain road surface drainage by removing berms, unless specifically designated otherwise.
Rehabilitate temporary staging, parking, and refueling/servicing areas immediately following use.
Protection of Streamcourses
If contractor maintains storage facilities for oil or oil products on Project Area, contractor shall take appropriate preventative measures to ensure that any spill of such oil or oil products does not enter any stream or other waters.
Allow temporary refueling and servicing only at approved sites located outside of RCAs.
Install temporary wash sites only in areas where the water and residue can be adequately collected and either filtered on site or conveyed to an appropriate wastewater treatment facility. Temporary wash sites shall be approved by the Project Manager prior to use.
Refer to attached documents - Best Management Practices (BMP) Checklist (Attachment J, RIM_BMP_Checklist and Attachment K, Spill_Prevention_and_Reporting_Procedures).

Water shall be applied to unpaved road sections of any Forest Service road used to walk or haul equipment as necessary to control road surface loss, provide for road user safety, minimize damage to adjacent resources, and comply with dust abatement. Also conduct road watering for road maintenance and road surface protection using approved existing water source locations.
Non-System Roads
Existing non-system roads in the project area may be used for access only. These non-system roads are considered temporary and may require rehabilitation/obliteration, including installation of barriers to prevent further access following project activities.

 prevent the transfer of noxious weeds from Non-National Forest System lands to National Forest System lands and from National Forest System lands to Non-National Forest System lands. 
 
If damage, breach, or incursion into areas to be avoided is caused by the Contractor's operations, the Contractor shall bear costs of investigation and restoration; monitoring and mitigation may be required if determined necessary during evaluation of damage, breach, or incursion.
Land Survey Monuments
The Contractor shall protect all known survey monuments, witness corners, reference monuments and bearing trees against avoidable destruction, obliteration, or damage during the contractor’s operations. If the contractor causes such damage, the contractor shall hire the appropriate registered land surveyor to establish or restore at the same location the monuments, corners, or accessories. Such surveyors shall use procedures in accordance with the “Bureau of Land Management Instructions for the Survey of the Public Lands of the United States” for the General Land Office surveys, land in accordance with the state law for other. Contractor shall record such survey in the appropriate county records.
Streamcourses
Streamcourses that are subject to provisions of this Section are shown on the Map. Unless otherwise agreed, the following measures shall be observed to protect streamcourses:
(a) Contractor’s Operations shall be conducted to prevent debris from entering streamcourses, except as may be authorized under paragraph (d). In event contractor causes debris to enter streamcourses in amounts that may adversely affect the natural flow of the stream, water quality, or fishery resource, contractor shall remove such debris as soon as practicable, but not to exceed 48 hours, and in an agreed manner that will cause the least disturbance to streamcourses.
(b) Culverts or bridges shall be required on Temporary Roads at all points where it is necessary to cross streamcourses. Such facilities shall be of sufficient size and design and installed in a manner to provide unobstructed flow of water and to minimize damage to Streamcourses. Trees or products shall not be otherwise hauled or yarded across Streamcourses unless fully suspended.
(c) Wheeled or track-laying equipment shall not be operated within 50 ft of streamcourses, except at crossings designated by the project manager after consultation with the Forest Service Aquatic Biologist. Project managers will walk each unit with the foreman to identify stream crossings 
(d) Flow in streamcourses may be temporarily diverted only if such diversion is necessary for contractor’s planned construction and Forest Service gives written authorization. Such flow shall be restored to the natural course as soon as practicable and, in any event, prior to a major storm runoff period or runoff season.
(e) Damage to streamcourses caused by contractor’s operations shall be repaired by the contractor in a timely and agreed manner to the extent practical as determined by the Forest Service to restore and prevent further damage.
Fell trees within RCAs directionally away from stream channels and SAFs unless otherwise recommended by a hydrologist or biologist. Fall hazard trees that cannot be removed either parallel to the contour of the slope or into the channel, as recommended by a hydrologist or biologist.
Remove activity-created woody debris to above the high-water line of stream channels.
Locate and design stream crossings to minimize disturbance to the water body. Use structures appropriate to the site conditions and traffic. Favor armored fords for streams where vehicle traffic is seasonal or temporary, and where the design maintains the channel pattern, profile, and dimension.
Prior to conducting a stream crossing, inspect and clean equipment and remove external oil, grease, dirt and mud. Repair leaks prior to unloading at the site. Inspect equipment daily and correct identified problems before entering streams or areas that drain directly to water bodies. Remove all dirt and plant parts to ensure that noxious weeds and aquatic invasive species are not brought to the site.
Soil and Erosion Control
Maintain 60% well-distributed soil cover (unburned duff; needle cast; basal live plant cover; fine woody debris; and downed logs where permitted) on slopes > 25%.
Maintain 50% well-distributed soil cover (unburned duff; needle cast; basal live plant cover; fine woody debris; and downed logs where permitted) on slopes  ≤  to 25%.
Maintain 75% well distributed soil cover within 100 feet of perennial and intermittent streams and SAFs and 50 feet of ephemeral streams. 60% in the rest of the RCA.
See Equipment Operations – see above in section 2.8 - Equipment Operation: Soils .
Improvements
So far as practicable, the contractor shall protect all physical improvements, including, but not limited to, roads, trails, ditches, fences, waterlines, and other improvements, existing in the contract area, determined to have continuing need or use.
All protected improvements shall be protected from damage by the contractor. If any protected improvements are disturbed, the contractor shall immediately contact the project manager and shall be liable for the cost of repairs. The contractor shall make timely restoration of any such improvements damaged by the contractor’s operations and, when directed shall move such improvements if and as specified in consultation with the Forest Service.
The Contractor shall be responsible for contacting all utility companies to determine the location of under and above ground utilities. The contractor shall protect or avoid these utilities during all operations of this contract.
Waterbars in skid trails, fire lines, and roads disturbed by the contractor shall be restored to condition prior to damage at the contractor’s expense.
Identify and protect National Forest System Trails (NFST) during operations. Trails, if damaged, will be restored in kind according to Forest Service standards including the placement of rolling dips.
Close skid trails to motorized travel with earth berms, logs, and/or rocks after operations are complete. Do not use stumps or root wads to close skid trails.
General Cutting
The contractor shall remove all shredded material, trees, or debris resulting from contract operations that is distributed outside of treatment unit or on Control Areas, lava caps, streams, roads, structures, private property, protected sites, improvements, telephone lines, established trails, stock driveways, fence lines, established land corners or other improvements.
Any debris resulting from the contractor’s operations on or into such areas as described in the above specifications shall be removed if possible, and any resulting damage shall be immediately reported to the project manager and restored to condition prior to damage at the contractors’ expense.
Limited Operating Periods (LOPs)
Limited Operating Periods (LOPs) exist within the landscape. Some of these areas will overlap; each LOP boundary must be adhered to. They may be added, lifted or altered at the discretion of the Forest Service. If the LOP is recreational, that may be lifted by the County.

##  Inspection and Acceptance
Contractor Inspection Requirements
:
The Contractor is responsible for performing or having performed all inspections and tests necessary to substantiate that the supplies or services furnished under this contract conform to contract requirements, including any applicable technical requirements for specified manufacturers' parts. This clause takes precedence over County inspections and testing required in the contract's specifications, except for specialized inspections or tests specified to be performed solely by County.
 
Specific Inspection Procedures
:
The Contractor shall submit a unit or partial unit to the County for acceptance only when the Contractor's inspections for quality control assure the work specifications have been met. County inspections may be by work observation, measurement by pacing, tape, clinometers, prism, ocular estimation, progress of work over time, or by formal inspection. Formal inspections will cover at least one percent of the work unit on a systematic plot basis, plots will be 1/20th acre radius (26.2 feet) and will address the work specifications.
 
Measurable Performance Standards
:
* Treatment of slash, shrubs, trees
 
* Slash pile fuelbreaks
 
* Amount of soil in piles
 
* Compact and tight piles
 
* Stump height
 
* Area treated
 
* Pile covering presence/placement
 
Acceptance
:
Work on this contract will be deemed acceptable when the above measurable performance standards are met.
 
Quality Assurance Plan
:
The County will conduct inspections of each unit or sub-unit to determine work quality. Initial inspections will consist of a 100 percent visual inspection and will be based on adherence to the specific tasks listed in the contract. The County may also install a series of circular plots. Plots will be randomly located throughout each sub-item to obtain a representative sample of work. Plot size 1/20th of an acre.
 
After inspection of all plots for a unit, the quality shall be calculated as follows:
 
(Total number of acceptable plots)/(Total number of plots) * 100 = Performance Quality Percent
 
Payment will be made in full if inspection results are 95 percent or higher. No payment will be made if inspection results are less than 95 percent.
 
Inspections
:
County inspections are for the purpose of satisfying the County that the services are acceptable and do not relieve the Contractor of the responsibility for maintaining quality control.
 
The County or designated Project Manager will conduct all inspections. The Contractor (or designated representative) is encouraged to be present to observe inspections. Summary results will be made available on request.
 
Compliance Inspections
:
Visual compliance inspections will be made on a periodic basis. Such inspections are not final and do not constitute acceptance.
 
Final Inspections
:
Final (formal) inspections for payment will be made on completed units only. Contractor shall request final inspections in writing. Inspections will be attempted to be completed within fifteen (15) business days after the notice is received. The County will make all reasonable efforts to complete the inspection of work within fifteen (15) business days; however, this timeline is subject to adjustment based on Forest Service availability due to fire assignments, severe weather events, government shutdowns, or other unforeseen circumstances. In the event that the approval period is unreasonably delayed, payment may be issued with a ten percent (10%) retention at the discretion of the County until Forest Service approval is obtained. If the work is not ready for inspection at the time specified by the Contractor, the cost associated with the inspection attempt may be charged to the Contractor. 
 
Disputed Inspection
:
The Contractor may request reinspection without rework if the results are unacceptable. Reinspection must be requested in writing within 48 hours after receiving written notice of the inspection results. Reinspection will be accomplished within five working days after receipt of the Contractor's written request.
 
The same sampling and inspection procedures will be used, but new samples will be taken. The inspection pattern will be shifted so that new samples will not overlap previously inspected samples. Results will be rounded to the nearest whole percent.
 
If reinspection results are within five percentage points of the first inspection, the original inspection result will be used in determining acceptability and payment. If reinspection results are greater than five percentage points above or below the first inspection, the reinspection results will be used.
 
If the reinspection results are within five percentage points of the first inspection, the Contractor shall pay the actual costs of the reinspection.
 
Reinspection after Rework
:
Where rework after a failed inspection may improve the inspection results, the Contractor may rework the area and request (in writing) a second inspection. County will charge to the Contractor the cost of this additional inspection. Reinspection will be accomplished within five working days after the notice is received. The results of the second inspection will be final, and no further rework will be permitted. Areas not ready for reinspection at the time specified by the Contractor will not be reinspected, and the results of the first inspection will be final.

The request must be made in writing and must be made within 10 calendar days of completing work on the unit in question. If remeasurement indicates a variance of five percent or less from the stated quantity, the Contractor shall pay for the actual cost of remeasurement, and no adjustment will be made in the quantity. If remeasurement indicates a variance more than five percent from the stated quantity, payment will be based on the remeasured quantity, and the Contractor will not be liable for the costs of remeasurement. All remeasurements will be done by the County. Remeasurement of acreage will be done with two people using a hand compass and ground measurement or by means of a Global Positioning System. This clause is not applicable to quantities listed as estimated quantities.
 
Payments and Deductions
:
Payment can be authorized by the Project Manager for full units, sub-units on a case-by-case basis (weather shutdown or other qualifying event). Payment will be contingent on Forest Service acceptance.
Payment will be made in full if inspection results are 95% or higher work complete. No payment will be made if inspection results show less than 95% work complete.
 
Payment will be made for fully acceptable work and for acres treated at the prices listed in the schedule of items.

In accordance with the inspection clause, payment may be made for less than fully acceptable work at a reduced price.
 
If Contractor needs to check out Forest Service keys, Contractor must return all such keys given to the Contractor by the Forest Service at the end of operations, field season, or at the County’s request. Payment will be withheld until keys are returned.

Event Name: Bulk Fuel and Lubricant Delivery Services
Description:
By way of this Request for Proposals (RFP), the County of Tuolumne, through its Public Works Department (“County”), is seeking proposals from qualified vendors (each, a “Contractor”) to provide bulk fuel and lubricant delivery services at designated County facilities throughout Tuolumne County.
The selected Contractor will furnish and deliver regular unleaded gasoline, diesel fuel, lubricants, and related petroleum products on an as-needed basis in accordance with the requirements of this RFP. Contractors should demonstrate the experience, resources, and capacity necessary to meet the County’s routine, rush, emergency, and after-hours delivery requirements throughout the term of the resulting Agreement.

Tuolumne County is located along the western slope of the Sierra Nevada and maintains facilities and operations throughout the County. The Public Works Department administers bulk fuel services used by County departments for the operation of County-owned vehicles and equipment, including those supporting emergency and essential public services.
The County has historically utilized contracted bulk fuel services to efficiently procure and distribute fuel and related petroleum products to multiple County locations. The resulting agreement will establish a consistent source for these products and associated delivery services to meet the County’s ongoing operational needs.
Services May Include:
Bulk Regular Unleaded Gasoline Delivery
Bulk Diesel Fuel Delivery
Motor Oils and Lubricants
Hydraulic Fluids and Related Petroleum Products
Routine, Rush, Emergency, and After-Hours Deliveries
Delivery and Usage Reporting
OPIS Pricing Documentation
The services provided under this RFP are intended to support the continued operation of County vehicles and equipment through reliable, responsive, and cost-effective fuel and lubricant delivery services.

## Sample Agreement
A sample Agreement is attached to this RFP, which details all standard terms and conditions required by the County of Tuolumne.

## Minimum Qualifications
Proposers shall possess all licenses, permits, and regulatory approvals required to furnish, transport, and deliver the specified fuel and petroleum products. Proposers shall demonstrate sufficient experience, personnel, equipment, product supply, and operational capacity to meet the County’s delivery requirements, including routine, rush, emergency, and after-hours service. Proposers shall also be capable of furnishing products that meet the specifications of this RFP, providing required delivery and pricing documentation, and maintaining all required insurance throughout the term of the Agreement.

## Submittal of Proposals
Sealed proposals must be received online, NO LATER THAN 
5:00 pm
 on 
Friday, October 23, 2026
.
Proposals are to be submitted electronically using Tuolumne County’s e-Procurement platform, 
https://procurement.opengov.com/portal/tuolumnecountyca
. Proposals will be received only as instructed above, and must be received before 
5:00 pm
 on 
Friday, October 23, 2026
. Proposals shall not be submitted via hard copy, (hand delivered or mailed), facsimile, nor via email. It is the sole responsibility of the proposer to properly upload its proposal so that it is received by the time and date required. Any proposal received after said time and/or date or in any other format other than as instructed herein, cannot be considered and will not be accepted. The County’s e-Procurement Platform records the time stamp for every proposal submitted properly in the system. Once a proposal is submitted in the e-procurement platform, the Proposer will receive an email confirmation, and the proposal status will also show as “submitted.”

## Bulk Fuel and Lubricant Delivery Services
Contractor shall furnish and deliver bulk fuel, lubricants, and related petroleum products to designated County facilities on an as-needed basis throughout the term of the Agreement. County may purchase products on an as-needed basis through individual purchase or delivery orders. Orders shall be placed by authorized County personnel by telephone, email, or other mutually agreed-upon method and shall identify the product, quantity, and delivery location.
Fuel
Contractor shall provide regular unleaded fuel of not less than Eighty-Seven (87) Octane and No. 2 Red Dyed Diesel Fuel with delivery to be made via “Tank Wagon” type transporter.
Oil and Lubricants
Contractor shall provide motor oils, hydraulic fluids, greases, and other lubricants as specified by County. All oil and lubricants shall meet or exceed the API specifications of the noted Chevron products. The list of products and container sizes to be provided includes, but is not limited to, the following:
Delo 400 15-40 Motor Oil — Bulk, HUD (55 Gallon), Gallon
Delo 400CJ4 15-40 Motor Oil — Bulk, HUD (55 Gallon), Gallon
Tractor Hydraulic Fluid — Bulk, HUD (55 Gallon), 5 Gallon
Synthetic ATF Heavy Duty — HUD (55 Gallon) Only
Delo Gear Lubricant ESI 80-90 — HUD (55 Gallon) Only
Drivetrain Fluid HD SAE 30 — HUD (55 Gallon) Only
Delo 400 SAE 50 — HUD (55 Gallon) Only
Ultra Duty Grease 2 — ¼ Drum, Tube
Contractor shall provide current Safety Data Sheets (SDS) for all products applicable prior to the first delivery and shall provide updated SDS documentation as necessary throughout the term of the Agreement.
Delivery
Contractor agrees to provide routine, rush, emergency, and after-hours delivery of bulk fuel and bulk and single use oil and lubricants ordered by County at all hours of the day and all days of the year, as the need requires.
Deliveries shall be made to designated County facilities, tanks, or receptacles identified by County. Contractor shall maintain sufficient product supply and delivery capacity to serve all County locations and fulfill County orders.
County reserves the right to add or remove delivery locations and modify fuel storage requirements during the term of the Agreement as necessary to meet County operational needs.
Interruptions in Service
Contractor shall provide at least three (3) calendar days' advance notice of any foreseeable interruptions in service (e.g. – product shortages, work stoppages, facility/equipment maintenance, etc.) so that all locations may be refilled, if necessary, prior to the anticipated down time.
Contractor shall provide documentation, as needed, sufficient to validate invoice pricing, including applicable Oil Price Information Service (OPIS) pricing documentation.
For the purpose of reconciliation, Contractor shall provide hard copy receipts at the time of delivery. Delivery receipts shall identify, at a minimum, the product delivered, quantity, delivery date and time, and delivery location. Contractor shall also provide electronic fuel usage and delivery reports upon request by County.

## Term/Termination
The term of the initial contract awarded under this RFP will be for: 
two (2) years
. By mutual agreement, this contract may be extended for 
two (2) additional one-year extensions
, under the following circumstances:
The County receives adequate funding to extend program operations;
The Contractor has achieved demonstrable success by meeting all of the contract’s service requirements;
The County continues to need the services purchased under this RFP;
The Contractor is willing and able to modify the services provided to best meet the needs of the program as determined by the County.
The contract will be subject to termination by either party upon 
30

.

. Any oral responses to questions are not binding on the County.

ENTER TIMEFRAME

## Cost of Developing the Proposal
All costs incurred in the preparation of a proposal are the responsibility of each proposer and will not be reimbursed by the County.

## Proposal Terms and Conditions
It is the responsibility of each proposer to be familiar with all of the specifications, terms and conditions of the RFP. By the submission of a proposal, the proposer certifies that if awarded a contract, proposer will make no claim against the County based upon ignorance of or misunderstanding of the specifications.
Each proposer shall submit its proposal with the understanding that the proposal will become a part of the official file on this matter and shall be subject to disclosure, if requested by a member of the public, following the completion of negotiations.
By submitting a proposal, each proposer certifies that all statements in this proposal are true. This constitutes a warranty, the falsity of which shall include the right, at the County’s option, of declaring any contract made, as a result thereof, null and void. Proposals shall be completed, executed, and submitted in accordance with the instructions of this RFP. If a proposal is not submitted in the format specified in this RFP, it may be rejected, unless the County determines that the nonconformity is either a minor irregularity or that the defect or variation in the proposal is immaterial or inconsequential. The County may give the proposer an opportunity to cure any deficiency resulting from a minor irregularity or an immaterial or inconsequential defect, or County may waive such deficiency, whichever is most advantageous to the County.
The County cannot accept proposals from any individual who is currently employed with the County of Tuolumne (California Government Code §29708).

## Funding Availability 
It is mutually agreed that if the County budget of the current year and/or any subsequent years covered under this Agreement does not appropriate sufficient funds for the program, this Agreement shall be of no further force and effect. In this event, the County shall have no liability to pay any funds whatsoever to Contractor or to furnish any other considerations under this Agreement and Contractor shall not be obligated to perform any provisions of this Agreement. Contractor’s assumption of risk of possible non-appropriation is part of the consideration for this Agreement. County budget decisions are subject to the discretion of the Board of Supervisors.
If funding for any fiscal year is reduced or deleted by the County budget for purposes of this program, the County shall have the option to either cancel this Agreement with no liability occurring to the County, or offer an Agreement amendment to Contractor to reflect the reduced amount.

## General Insurance 
Contractor shall procure and maintain for the duration of the contract insurance against claims for injuries to persons or damages to property which may arise from or in connection with the performance of the work hereunder and the results of that work by the Contractor, his agents, representatives, employees or subcontractors.  Coverage shall be at least as broad as:
i.  
Commercial General Liability (CGL):
 Insurance Services Office Form CG 00 01 covering CGL on an "occurrence" basis, including products and completed operations, property damage, bodily injury, and personal & advertising injury with limits no less than $2,000,000 per occurrence.  If a general aggregate limit applies, either the general aggregate limit shall apply separately to this project/location (ISO CG 25 03 05 09 or 25 04 05 09) or the general aggregate limit shall be twice the required occurrence limit.
ii.  
Automobile Liability:
 ISO Form Number CA 00 01 covering any auto (Code 1), or if Contractor has no owned autos, covering hired, (Code 8) and non-owned autos (Code 9), with limit no less than $1,000,000 per accident for bodily injury and property damage.
iii.  Workers' Compensation:
 as required by the State of California, with Statutory Limits, and Employer's Liability Insurance with limit of no less than $1,000,000 per accident for bodily injury or disease.
iv.  Pollution Liability / Environmental Impairment Liability: 
Coverage for bodily injury, property damage, cleanup costs, and remediation arising out of the escape, spill, seepage, leakage, release, or discharge of Goods, with limits of not less than Two Million Dollars ($2,000,000) per occurrence or claim and Two Million Dollars ($2,000,000) aggregate. If the Contractor maintains broader coverage and/or higher limits than the minimums shown above, the County requires and shall be entitled to the broader coverage and/or the higher limits maintained by the contractor.  Any available insurance proceeds in excess of the specified minimum limits of insurance and coverage shall be available to the County.
Other Insurance Provisions:  The insurance policies are to contain, or be endorsed to contain, the following provisions:

The Victorville Water District (hereinafter referred to as “District”), a subsidiary district of the City of Victorville (hereinafter referred to as “City”), is requesting bids for the Annual Maintenance of Percolation Pond 14. Contractor will be expected to be available for the mobilization to perform work on an as needed basis through the annual contract period. This will also have the option to renew. Contractor needs to be able to perform work within two weeks of requested maintenance.

The purpose of the annual maintenance of Percolation Pond 14 (Pond 14) is to restore and maximize percolation rates by removing accumulated sediment, vegetation, and compacted material from the pond basin and mechanically conditioning the surface. This maintenance is part of the District’s annual pond rotation program. As part of the maintenance, the contractor is expected to remove 1-2 feet of dirt from the bottom of the pond and place spoils on the side of the pond for future removal. After removal of the specified quantity of bottom material, the contractor is to rip the entire pond basin surface from bank to bank at a depth of 6–8 inches to further enhance percolation rates.

## SCOPE OF WORK 
The purpose of the annual maintenance of Percolation Pond 14 (Pond 14) is to restore and maximize percolation rates by removing accumulated sediment, vegetation, and compacted material from the pond basin and mechanically conditioning the surface. This maintenance is part of the District’s annual pond rotation program. As part of the maintenance, the contractor is expected to remove 1-2 feet of dirt from the bottom of the pond and place spoils on the side of the pond for future removal. After removal of the specified quantity of bottom material, the contractor is to rip the entire pond basin surface from bank to bank at a depth of 6–8 inches to further enhance percolation rates. Below is a further breakdown of what is expected.
Coordination
Coordinate project schedule with District staff.
Provide written notification of anticipated start date at least 5 business days prior to mobilization
Provide written notice of completion within 24 hours of finishing work.
Immediately notify the District of any unforeseen site conditions.
Mobilization & Demobilization
Mobilize all necessary equipment to the project site.
Maintain equipment in safe operating condition.
Remove all equipment, tools, and temporary materials immediately upon completion.
The District shall not be responsible for any damage, theft, or loss of Contractor equipment
Excavation & Material Removal
Excavate and remove 1–2 feet of bottom material within the designated pond basin to restore maximum percolation rates.
GPS / Grade Control Requirements
The Contractor shall provide GPS machine-control equipment capable of achieving the design grades and elevations specified in the project plans. GPS data and machine-control models shall be compatible with the Contractor’s equipment and shall be coordinated with the Agency prior to construction.
Removal depth shall not exceed 2 feet.
Contractor shall stockpile material on-site, coordinate with District staff for removal. 
The Contractor is not responsible for relocating stockpiled material beyond the designated stockpile area.
Scrape and remove all vegetation from pond side slopes & bottom basin.
Dispose of vegetation in designated onsite stockpile area unless otherwise directed.
Dust control may be required and responsibility of the contractor.

## ADDITIONAL SCOPE OF WORK
Site Reconnaissance and Survey Control
The Contractor shall visit both pond sites and establish appropriate horizontal and vertical survey control sufficient to complete the work.
The Contractor shall identify and document the coordinate system, horizontal datum, vertical datum, units of measurement, benchmarks, and survey methods used. Survey control shall be established or verified using recognized surveying practices and shall be suitable for the intended engineering and construction applications.
The Contractor shall identify any site access limitations, obstructions, or existing conditions that may affect survey accuracy or completeness.
Topographic Field Survey
The Contractor shall perform a detailed topographic field survey of both percolation ponds, including pond interiors, surrounding berms and embankments, access roads, drainage features, and adjacent ground areas necessary to document existing site conditions.
The survey shall include, at a minimum, the following features:
Existing ground elevations throughout each pond bottom, including low areas, depressions, uneven surfaces, and changes in grade.
Top and bottom of pond side slopes and embankments.
Top of berm elevations, crest widths, and visible changes in berm geometry.
Inlet and outlet structures, overflow structures, spillways, drainage channels, culverts, and associated improvements.
Visible pipes, valves, manholes, access structures, and other relevant facilities.
Existing access roads, gates, fences, and maintenance access areas.
Ground elevations surrounding each pond sufficient to identify drainage patterns and potential overflow pathways.
Significant breaks in terrain, erosion areas, sediment deposits, and other features that may affect pond performance, maintenance, or sediment removal.
Other site features that may affect proposed excavation, grading, access, or future improvements.
The Contractor shall collect sufficient survey points and breaklines to accurately represent existing pond geometry and surrounding terrain. Survey density shall be appropriate to site conditions and sufficient to develop reliable existing surface models, contours, and area-volume calculations. The Contractor shall identify any areas that could not be surveyed and document any assumptions, exclusions, or limitations affecting the survey results.
Sediment Removal and Excavation Planning
The Contractor shall provide existing topographic contours and digital terrain models suitable for developing proposed excavation grades and estimating sediment removal quantities once the District establishes a target pond-bottom elevation or proposed excavation surface. The existing surface models shall be suitable for comparison against future proposed grading surfaces to calculate estimated excavation quantities. The Contractor’s base proposal shall include preparation of existing-condition survey data necessary to support future sediment removal planning. Development of proposed excavation designs, construction staking, and final sediment removal quantity calculations based on a future design surface shall be identified separately as optional services unless expressly included in the base proposal.
GPS Machine-Control Compatibility
Survey deliverables shall be prepared in a consistent coordinate system and elevation datum suitable for use in engineering design and, where applicable, GPS-equipped grading and excavation equipment. The Contractor shall identify the available digital surface formats and any required coordinate transformations, geoid models, localization parameters, or other information necessary to maintain consistency between survey data and machine-control systems.
The Contractor shall provide, at a minimum, a Civil 3D-compatible surface file and identify other machine-control file formats that can be provided upon request. The earthwork contractor shall be responsible for verifying compatibility of the supplied files with its GPS machine-control equipment, confirming coordinate and elevation settings, and independently verifying project control before commencing earthwork.
No change to the established coordinate system or vertical datum shall be made without the District’s prior written approval.
DELIVERABLES
The Contractor shall provide the following deliverables for each pond:
Topographic Survey Map:
 A complete, legible PDF drawing identifying surveyed features, spot elevations, existing contours, survey control, coordinate system, vertical datum, scale, north arrow, legend, and other customary survey information.
Digital Terrain Model:
 An existing ground surface model compatible with Autodesk Civil 3D or an Agency-approved equivalent, including the applicable native project files and surface data.
Electronic Survey Point Files:
 Electronic point files containing point numbers, descriptions, northings, eastings, and elevations in an agreed-upon format.
Final Electronic Package:
 All final deliverables organized by pond and provided electronically in a format approved by the District.
All electronic deliverables shall be complete, internally consistent, and suitable for use by the District and its authorized design and construction consultants.

California Public Contract Code Section 9204.
(a) The Legislature finds and declares that it is in the best interests of the state and its citizens to ensure that all construction business performed on a public works project in the state that is complete and not in dispute is paid in full and in a timely manner.
(b) Notwithstanding any other law, including, but not limited to, Article 7.1 (commencing with Section 10240) of Chapter 1 of Part 2, Chapter 10 (commencing with Section 19100) of Part 2, and Article 1.5 (commencing with Section 20104) of Chapter 1 of Part 3, this section shall apply to any claim by a contractor in connection with a public works project.
(c) For purposes of this section:
(1) “Claim” means a separate demand by a contractor sent by registered mail or certified mail with return receipt requested, for one or more of the following:
(A) A time extension, including, without limitation, for relief from damages or penalties for delay assessed by a public entity under a contract for a public works project.
(B) Payment by the public entity of money or damages arising from work done by, or on behalf of, the contractor pursuant to the contract for a public works project and payment for which is not otherwise expressly provided or to which the claimant is not otherwise entitled.
(C) Payment of an amount that is disputed by the public entity.
(2) “Contractor” means any type of contractor within the meaning of Chapter 9 (commencing with Section 7000) of Division 3 of the Business and Professions Code who has entered into a direct contract with a public entity for a public works project.
(3) (A) “Public entity” means, without limitation, except as provided in subparagraph (B), a state agency, department, office, division, bureau, board, or commission, the California State University, the University of California, a city, including a charter city, county, including a charter county, city and county, including a charter city and county, district, special district, public authority, political subdivision, public corporation, or nonprofit transit corporation wholly owned by a public agency and formed to carry out the purposes of the public agency.
(B) “Public entity” shall not include the following:
(i) The Department of Water Resources as to any project under the jurisdiction of that department.
(ii) The Department of Transportation as to any project under the jurisdiction of that department.
(iii) The Department of Parks and Recreation as to any project under the jurisdiction of that department.
(iv) The Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation with respect to any project under its jurisdiction pursuant to Chapter 11 (commencing with Section 7000) of Title 7 of Part 3 of the Penal Code.
(v) The Military Department as to any project under the jurisdiction of that department.
(vi) The Department of General Services as to all other projects.
(vii) The High-Speed Rail Authority.
(4) “Public works project” means the erection, construction, alteration, repair, or improvement of any public structure, building, road, or other public improvement of any kind.
(5) “Subcontractor” means any type of contractor within the meaning of Chapter 9 (commencing with Section 7000) of Division 3 of the Business and Professions Code who either is in direct contract with a contractor or is a lower tier subcontractor.
(d) (1) (A) Upon receipt of a claim pursuant to this section, the public entity to which the claim applies shall conduct a reasonable review of the claim and, within a period not to exceed 45 days, shall provide the claimant a written statement identifying what portion of the claim is disputed and what portion is undisputed. Upon receipt of a claim, a public entity and a contractor may, by mutual agreement, extend the time period provided in this subdivision.
(B) The claimant shall furnish reasonable documentation to support the claim.
(C) If the public entity needs approval from its governing body to provide the claimant a written statement identifying the disputed portion and the undisputed portion of the claim, and the governing body does not meet within the 45 days or within the mutually agreed to extension of time following receipt of a claim sent by registered mail or certified mail, return receipt requested, the public entity shall have up to three days following the next duly publicly noticed meeting of the governing body after the 45-day period, or extension, expires to provide the claimant a written statement identifying the disputed portion and the undisputed portion.
(D) Any payment due on an undisputed portion of the claim shall be processed and made within 60 days after the public entity issues its written statement. If the public entity fails to issue a written statement, paragraph (3) shall apply.
(2) (A) If the claimant disputes the public entity’s written response, or if the public entity fails to respond to a claim issued pursuant to this section within the time prescribed, the claimant may demand in writing an informal conference to meet and confer for settlement of the issues in dispute. Upon receipt of a demand in writing sent by registered mail or certified mail, return receipt requested, the public entity shall schedule a meet and confer conference within 30 days for settlement of the dispute.
(B) Within 10 business days following the conclusion of the meet and confer conference, if the claim or any portion of the claim remains in dispute, the public entity shall provide the claimant a written statement identifying the portion of the claim that remains in dispute and the portion that is undisputed. Any payment due on an undisputed portion of the claim shall be processed and made within 60 days after the public entity issues its written statement. Any disputed portion of the claim, as identified by the contractor in writing, shall be submitted to nonbinding mediation, with the public entity and the claimant sharing the associated costs equally. The public entity and claimant shall mutually agree to a mediator within 10 business days after the disputed portion of the claim has been identified in writing. If the parties cannot agree upon a mediator, each party shall select a mediator and those mediators shall select a qualified neutral third party to mediate with regard to the disputed portion of the claim. Each party shall bear the fees and costs charged by its respective mediator in connection with the selection of the neutral mediator. If mediation is unsuccessful, the parts of the claim remaining in dispute shall be subject to applicable procedures outside this section.
(C) For purposes of this section, mediation includes any nonbinding process, including, but not limited to, neutral evaluation or a dispute review board, in which an independent third party or board assists the parties in dispute resolution through negotiation or by issuance of an evaluation. Any mediation utilized shall conform to the timeframes in this section.
(D) Unless otherwise agreed to by the public entity and the contractor in writing, the mediation conducted pursuant to this section shall excuse any further obligation under Section 20104.4 to mediate after litigation has been commenced.
(E) This section does not preclude a public entity from requiring arbitration of disputes under private arbitration or the Public Works Contract Arbitration Program, if mediation under this section does not resolve the parties’ dispute.
(3) Failure by the public entity to respond to a claim from a contractor within the time periods described in this subdivision or to otherwise meet the time requirements of this section shall result in the claim being deemed rejected in its entirety. A claim that is denied by reason of the public entity’s failure to have responded to a claim, or its failure to otherwise meet the time requirements of this section, shall not constitute an adverse finding with regard to the merits of the claim or the responsibility or qualifications of the claimant.
(4) Amounts not paid in a timely manner as required by this section shall bear interest at 7 percent per annum.
(5) If a subcontractor or a lower tier subcontractor lacks legal standing to assert a claim against a public entity because privity of contract does not exist, the contractor may present to the public entity a claim on behalf of a subcontractor or lower tier subcontractor. A subcontractor may request in writing, either on their own behalf or on behalf of a lower tier subcontractor, that the contractor present a claim for work which was performed by the subcontractor or by a lower tier subcontractor on behalf of the subcontractor. The subcontractor requesting that the claim be presented to the public entity shall furnish reasonable documentation to support the claim. Within 45 days of receipt of this written request, the contractor shall notify the subcontractor in writing as to whether the contractor presented the claim to the public entity and, if the original contractor did not present the claim, provide the subcontractor with a statement of the reasons for not having done so.
(e) The text of this section or a summary of it shall be set forth in the plans or specifications for any public works project that may give rise to a claim under this section.
(f) A waiver of the rights granted by this section is void and contrary to public policy, provided, however, that (1) upon receipt of a claim, the parties may mutually agree to waive, in writing, mediation and proceed directly to the commencement of a civil action or binding arbitration, as applicable; and (2) a public entity may prescribe reasonable change order, claim, and dispute resolution procedures and requirements in addition to the provisions of this section, so long as the contractual provisions do not conflict with or otherwise impair the timeframes and procedures set forth in this section.
(g) This section applies to contracts entered into on or after January 1, 2017.
(h) Nothing in this section shall impose liability upon a public entity that makes loans or grants available through a competitive application process, for the failure of an awardee to meet its contractual obligations.
(i) This section shall remain in effect only until January 1, 2027, and as of that date is repealed, unless a later enacted statute that is enacted before January 1, 2027, deletes or extends that date.

## RECYCLING, SALVAGE, AND LANDFILL DIVERSION:
The 
District 
 encourages innovative approaches to recycling, reuse, or salvage.  The City is mandated by the State of California to implement programs to reduce the amount of waste sent to landfill by 50% by the year 2000 and beyond.  In addition, the Victorville Municipal Code (Title 6—Health and Sanitation, Chapters 6.36 and 6.37 require the separation of designated materials for recycling.  Contractors performing work for the 
District 
will be required to comply with all waste recycling and diversion laws.
Construction and Demolition Material Recycling
: 
The 2019 California Green Building Standards Code (CalGreen) Sections 4.408 and 5.408 and the City Development Code (Title 16, Chapter 5, Article 11) and subsequent updates require all building permit applicants to develop and submit a Construction Waste Management Plan.  Current CalGreen standards currently require that 65% of non-hazardous construction waste be diverted from landfill.  In addition, construction projects that include land clearing activities are required to divert 100% of trees, stumps, rocks, and associated vegetation and soils resulting primarily from land clearing.   
 
In order to comply with this State mandate, the District requires all contractors that are bidding on construction and/or demolition projects which require permits to fill out the attached “Construction/Demolition Waste Recycling Plan”.  The plan outlines how the contractor will divert 65% of waste material from the landfill in order to achieve the State goal.  At a minimum, contractors must divert scrap metal, concrete, asphalt, green waste/vegetation materials, non-hazardous wood waste, and soil.
 
The successful contractor will also be required to complete and submit the attached “Summary Waste Disposal and Diversion Report” (SWDDR) at the end of the project.  Weight slips documenting actual amounts disposed and diverted must accompany the SWDDR.  The SWDDR must be completed at the conclusion of the project and must be submitted to the contract administrator before final payment will be made.
 
Recycling and Organic Waste Material Diversion Requirements
:  CA State Law SB 1383 and Victorville Municipal Code Title 6 (Health and Sanitation), Chapters 6.36 and 6.37 mandate the diversion of organic materials and other designated recyclable materials from landfill.  Organic materials include vegetation (tree trimmings, leaves, grass clippings, weeds, brush, etc.) as well as non-hazardous wood waste.  Contractors are required to comply with waste diversion/recycling mandates and must implement procedures to properly separate all waste materials and participate in City waste diversion programs.  Contractors who need information on local scrap metal recyclers, asphalt and concrete recyclers, or organic material (vegetation/wood) recyclers should contact the City Environmental Programs Division at (760) 955-8615.
