Solicitation Text:
## INTRODUCTION:
The City of Victorville (City) is inviting Statements of Qualifications (SOQs) from qualified civil engineering consulting firms to provide On-Call Civil Engineering Design Services to supplement the City's in-house Engineering Department and support the City's Capital Improvement Program (CIP).
The City intends to establish agreements with up to three (3) qualified civil engineering consulting firms to provide professional engineering services on an as-needed, task-order basis. Assignments will be made based on project needs, consultant qualifications, availability, expertise, and the specific requirements of each task order.

## COVER SHEET:
The cover sheet shall present the project title, RFQ number, proposing firm's name, and date of submission. The cover sheet may include the firm's logo and branding.

## SUBMITTAL INCLUSIONS:
All documents required by the RFQ shall be returned in their entirety, with ALL applicable portions fully completed by the Consultant. Each Consultant is encouraged to review and confirm that its Submittal includes and specifically addresses ALL of the requirements of this RFQ solicitation prior to submitting a response.

## GENERAL PROVISIONS:
The City will assume no responsibility for any understandings or representations concerning conditions made by any of its officers or employees prior to execution of a final agreement unless they are included in this Request for Qualifications.
Any reasonable inquiry to determine the responsibility of a prospective Consultant(s) may be conducted. The submission of Qualifications shall constitute permission by the prospective Consultant(s) for the City to verify all information contained therein. If the City deems it necessary, additional information may be requested from the prospective Consultant(s) for further consideration.
A prospective Consultant(s) may withdraw their Qualifications at any time prior to the date and time which is set forth herein as the deadline for acceptance of Qualifications.
The City reserves the right to request additional information from any or all prospective entities as deemed necessary by the City in order to evaluate the Qualifications. This process may not be used as an opportunity to submit missing documentation or to make substantive revisions to the original Qualifications.
The City reserves the right to reject any or all Qualifications and, in the event the Consultant selected, it may attempt to negotiate an agreement with the Consultant that, in the sole judgment of the City, is the best qualified to provide the services requested.
The City shall not enter into an agreement with any prospective Consultant(s) that has previously had an agreement with the City terminated, or that has previously been found to have violated any provision of the Victorville City Code, or related resolutions or ordinances, or any provision of federal law, state, or other local law.
The City reserves the right to enter into an agreement with a Consultant(s) at any time, deviate from this Request, reject any or all SOQs, continue to advertise for new Qualifications, negotiate with multiple entities simultaneously, waive any defects in Qualifications, or to proceed otherwise. The Request and the selection process will in no way be deemed to create a binding contract or agreement of any kind between the City and any prospective Consultant(s). The submission of Qualifications does not in any way commit the City to enter into an agreement with any prospective Consultant(s).
This Request for Qualifications shall be governed in accordance with the laws of the State of California and the jurisdiction of any disputes hereunder shall be had in San Bernardino County.

## TABLE OF CONTENTS: 
The table of contents shall provide a clear and organized outline of the SOQ, including all sections and corresponding page numbers. The table of contents shall facilitate ease of review and navigation by the City’s evaluation committee. All major sections and appendices shall be accurately referenced.

## BACKGROUND:
The Engineering Department is responsible for a broad range of functions, including traffic, surveying, development review, and inspection. The Department also manages the Capital Improvement Program (CIP) — its primary program for delivering public infrastructure improvements, including water, sewer, airport, streets, drainage, and traffic-related projects.
Engineering staff design most CIP projects in-house, occasionally engaging outside consultants for large or complex projects requiring specialized expertise. The Department has maintained a modest capital program, with the CIP budget totaling approximately $18 million in 
FY 2025/26
 and $12 million in 
FY 2026/27
.
The volume, complexity, and variety of CIP projects — combined with the Department's other ongoing responsibilities — has created a need for additional civil engineering design support to supplement projects managed in-house.
The purpose of this solicitation is to establish on-call agreements with qualified civil engineering consulting firms to provide professional services on an as-needed, task-order basis. This arrangement will allow the City to secure supplemental engineering resources for individual projects or assignments without the need to conduct a separate procurement process for each engagement.

## WITHDRAWAL OF SUBMITTAL BEFORE CLOSING:
Any Consultant may request the withdrawal of its submittal by written request, at any time prior to the scheduled closing date and time. Upon receiving the written request to withdraw any proposal, the City will consider the Consultant's submittal null and void. Withdrawal of the Consultant's submittal will not prejudice Consultant's resubmittal for this or any future solicitations.

## SCOPE OF SERVICES:
Given the breadth of the CIP and the Engineering Department's responsibility for managing multiple projects concurrently, the City requires supplemental civil engineering design resources to assist with project development and design. The proposed on-call civil engineering services will provide the CIP team with access to additional engineering expertise and design capacity on an as-needed basis, allowing the City to efficiently advance projects while retaining overall project management and direction in-house.
To support the timely advancement of capital improvement projects, the City intends to retain up to three (3) qualified civil engineering consulting firms on an on-call basis.
Consultant services are intended to supplement, rather than replace, the City's in-house engineering capabilities by providing special studies, plans, or technical support as needed. The City will continue to establish project priorities, manage the CIP, direct project development, and determine when consultant assistance is necessary. Individual assignments will be authorized by the City through task orders issued in accordance with the resulting agreement.
Services may include, but are not limited to, the following"
Roadway widening, rehabilitation, and reconstruction
Sidewalk, curb, gutter, and ADA improvements
Drainage and storm drain improvements
Civil designers/drafters under the direction of City Staff
Sewer and water improvements
Traffic signal and street lighting improvements
Signing and striping
Bikeways and pedestrian facilities
Grading and earthwork
Retaining walls and other civil structures
Utility relocation and coordination
Hydrologic studies and analysis
Hydraulic modeling
Storm drain sizing and design
Floodplain analysis
Detention and retention analysis
Culvert analysis and design
Channel analysis and design
Low-impact development (LID) and stormwater design
Preparation of drainage and hydrology/hydraulics reports
Structural engineering
Electrical engineering
Street lighting
Constructability reviews of CIPs
Cost estimating

## COVER LETTER (MAXIMUM 1 PAGE FRONT/BACK)
The Cover Letter shall present a summary of the Consultant's Statement of Qualifications, highlighting the firm's key strengths and qualifications, along with primary contact information and identification of the proposed team. The Cover Letter shall be clear and concise.

## CONTRACT TERM AND COMPENSATION: 
The City intends to award on-call professional services agreements with an initial term of 
one (1) year
. The City may, at its sole discretion, extend each agreement for up to 
three (3) additional one-year terms
, for a maximum contract term of 
four (4) years
.
 
The anticipated compensation shall not exceed 
$125,000 per year per Consultant
, subject to the City's authorization of individual task orders and the availability of appropriated funds. If all three optional one-year extensions are exercised, the maximum potential compensation under each agreement shall not exceed 
$500,000 over the four-year contract term
.
 
The City does not guarantee any minimum amount of work or compensation during the initial term or any extension term. Individual assignments will be authorized by the City on an as-needed basis through task orders or other written authorizations in accordance with the resulting agreement.

## ORGANIZATIONAL CHART AND RESUME FOR KEY PERSONNEL: 
The Consultant shall identify the team lead responsible for each major area of expertise proposed to support the City’s on-call civil engineering services. The Consultant may include subconsultants, as applicable.
The Consultant shall provide a team organizational chart or table identifying, at a minimum:
Prime Consultant;
Subconsultants, if applicable;
Team lead for each area of expertise;
Primary role and area of responsibility for each team lead; and
Key personnel supporting each area, as applicable.
The areas of expertise should correspond to the potential services identified in this RFQ.  Consultants are encouraged to identify personnel who can serve as the primary technical lead and point of contact for each area, allowing the City to readily determine the appropriate resource for individual task orders.
Resumes are not required for all proposed team members. The Consultant shall provide resumes only for the Principal-in-Charge, Project Manager, and designated discipline/team leads, limited to one (1) double-sided page per individual, highlighting relevant qualifications and experience.

## RELEVANT PROJECT EXPERIENCE:
Provide up to five (5) similar projects demonstrating the firm's experience providing civil engineering design services for public agencies, including state- and federally funded projects. Include a brief description of the services provided, the funding source, the firm's role on each project, and the name, title, phone number, and email address of a contact person for the agency or organization.

## TASK ORDER AND REQUEST FOR QUOTE PROCESS: 
The specific scope of services, deliverables, schedule, and compensation for each assignment shall be established by the City through individual task orders or work authorizations. The Consultant shall provide the requested services in accordance with the requirements, schedule, and authorized fee established for each task order or work authorization.
 
The City will issue a Request for Quote (RFQ) for individual assignments under this Agreement. The Consultant shall submit a fee proposal in response to each RFQ based on the specific scope of services, deliverables, and schedule identified by the City. Upon acceptance of the Consultant's fee proposal, the City will issue a task order authorizing the Consultant to proceed with the requested services. Each task order shall establish the specific scope of services, deliverables, schedule, and authorized compensation for the assignment. The Consultant shall perform the services in accordance with the requirements and schedule set forth in the applicable RFQ and authorized task order.

## MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:
Consultants must have a minimum of five (5) years of experience providing professional civil engineering services to support capital improvement projects for public agencies in California.

## CONTRACT EXECUTION EXCEPTIONS:
Qualified Consultant must be prepared to enter into and comply with the terms and provisions of the City's standard Consultant/Professional Services Provider Agreement, a sample of which is provided as Attachment "A", Sample Agreement, in Section 6 of the Project Documents. In Submitting a response to this RFQ, Consultant is certifying that it takes no exceptions to the provisions of this RFQ, including but not limited to, the Sample Agreement. If any exceptions are taken. such exceptions must be specifically noted on the documents returned in the Consultant's Required Documents Uploads in Section 7, of the Consultant Submittals. Hereof Consultants are directed to carefully review the Sample Agreement, including the insurance and indemnification provisions therein. Submission of requests for exceptions by Consultant shall in no way be considered or construed as binding upon the City or an acceptance of any such request for exception. Consultant that take exception to the provisions of this RFQ and/or the City's standard Agreement also do so at the risk that their submittal may be declared to be nonresponsive and not considered for contract award.

## CAPACITY AND AVAILABILITY:
The Consultant shall provide a Staffing Capacity Table identifying, at a minimum, the number of available staff by discipline/area of expertise and office location(s) proposed to support this contract. In addition, the Consultant shall provide a brief narrative (not to exceed one page) describing the firm's current workload, approach to managing multiple concurrent task order assignments, and ability to respond to time-sensitive requests.

## COMPLIANCE WITH LAWS:
The Consultant shall be required to comply with all federal, state, and local laws and ordinances, and all federal state and local rules or regulations applicable to the services to be provided.

## CITY RIGHTS AND DISCRETIONS DURING CONTRACT TERM:
The City reserves the right to negotiate the scope of services, level of effort, staffing approach, and fee proposal prior to issuing a task order to ensure cost reasonableness and alignment with project objectives and available funding.  All task orders are contingent upon the availability of appropriated and authorized funds. In the event funding is reduced, delayed, suspended, or withdrawn, the City reserves the right to suspend, modify, or terminate any task order, in whole or in part, upon written notice to the Consultant. In such cases, the Consultant shall be compensated only for services expressly authorized and satisfactorily performed up to the effective date of suspension, modification, or termination. The City makes no guarantee regarding the quantity or volume of work to be assigned under this agreement.

## FEE SCHEDULE: 
The proposer shall complete and submit the On-Call Civil Engineering Fee Schedule, identifying fully burdened hourly rates for all proposed staff classifications, including subconsultants, if applicable. Rates shall include all direct labor, fringe benefits, overhead, administrative costs, and profit.
The fee schedule shall include hourly rates for Year 1, proposed escalation rates and corresponding rates for optional extension years, proposed subconsultant firm names and hourly rates, and any proposed markup applied to subconsultant services.
The proposer shall identify any reimbursable or other direct costs, specialty services, or project-related charges, and indicate whether such costs are included in the proposed hourly rates. For any costs billed separately, the proposer shall identify the billing methodology and basis for reimbursement.
The proposer shall also identify any assumptions used in developing the proposed rates, including assumptions related to staffing, travel, field work, remote work, subconsultant usage, escalation, or other cost considerations.
An authorized representative of the firm shall include a signed certification statement confirming that the submitted rates are fully burdened, and that no additional overhead, administrative fees, or indirect costs will be applied beyond the submitted rates and approved subconsultant markup.

##  ADDITIONAL SERVICES AND AUTHORIZATION:
The City reserves the right to modify the scope of any task order, including the removal of tasks or reduction in level of effort, if certain services are determined to be unnecessary, duplicative, not required by applicable regulatory agencies, or no longer aligned with project objectives. The Consultant shall be compensated only for services actually performed and authorized by the City.
Tasks identified in a task order budget but not performed shall not be eligible for payment. Inclusion of a task or budgeted amount within a task order shall not be construed as a guarantee that such services will be required or authorized. 
The Consultant shall perform only those services expressly authorized under an approved task order. If the Consultant believes that additional services are required due to regulatory requirements, agency direction, or changes in project scope, the Consultant shall notify the City in writing and obtain written authorization prior to performing such services. 
The Consultant shall not be entitled to compensation for services performed outside the approved task order scope unless expressly authorized in writing by the City. Determinations regarding regulatory requirements, federal or State agency directives, and scope modifications shall be subject to review and confirmation by the City.

## SAFETY, SANITARY, AND MEDICAL REQUIREMENTS:
The Consultant, Consultant's employees, shall promptly and fully carry out the existing safety, sanitary, and medical requirements as prescribed by the Division of Industrial Safety and by County or State Health Departments to the end that proper work shall be done, and the safety and health of the employees and of the community may be conserved and safeguarded.  In case such regulations and orders are not observed by the Consultant, they may be enforced by the City Engineer at the Consultant’s expense.

## NON MANDATORY PRE-PROPOSAL MEETING:
All prospective Consultants are invited and strongly encouraged to attend a Non-Mandatory Pre-Submittal Meeting at 9:0
0 a.m. PST on October 7, 2026, located at 14343 Civic Dr., Victorville, CA 92392 or
 virtually via Zoom, 
https://victorvilleca-gov.zoom.us/j/84208191101
. Prospective Consultants are encouraged to ask questions, address problems, and other issues regarding this project during this meeting. All questions, other than those asked at the Pre-Submittal Meeting must be submitted via the City's eProcurement Portal.

## NON-DISCRIMINATION AND NON-PREFERENTIAL TREATMENT:
The successful Consultant shall not discriminate, in any way, against any person on the basis of race, sex, color, age, religion, sexual orientation, actual or perceived gender identity, disability, ethnicity, or national origin, in connection with or related to the performance of City of Victorville contracts.

## GROUNDS FOR DISQUALIFICATION:
All prospective entities are expected to conduct themselves with the utmost integrity and responsibility throughout the Request process. Any prospective Consultant(s) that violates these expectations, as determined in the sole discretion of the City, will be subject to disqualification. Generally, the grounds for disqualification include but are not limited to:
Contact regarding this procurement with any City official or employee, other than the contact person designated in this Request, from the time of issuance of this Request until the consideration and approval of a professional services agreement.
Evidence of collusion, directly or indirectly, among prospective entities in regard to the amount, or the terms and conditions of this Request and the prospective agreement.
Influencing, or attempting to influence, any City staff member or official throughout the solicitation process, including the development of specifications beyond those included here, if any.
Evidence of submitting incorrect or inaccurate information in response to this Request or misrepresentation or failing to disclose facts during the evaluation or negotiation process.
Existence of any lawsuit, claim, or dispute between the prospective Consultant(s) and the City.
Evidence of the prospective Consultant(s)’s inability to successfully complete the responsibilities and obligations of the Request process.
The prospective Consultant(s)’s default under any City agreement or termination of a previous agreement.

## QUESTIONS:
All prospective Consultants desiring an explanation or interpretation of the RFQ or specifications must be entered via the City's e-Procurement Portal, OpenGov, in the Question and Answer section of the project. All questions must be submitted on or before
 October 14, 2026, at 2:00 p.m. PST
 to allow a reply to reach the prospective Consultant before the proposal submission date. In order to receive such information, Consultant must submit a request via OpenGov at, 
https://procurement.opengov.com/portal/victorvilleca
. All answers to inquiries will be posted on the OpenGov portal promptly either directly or as an amendment to the solicitation. As a registered consultant, you will receive notifications to your email by clicking "Follow" on this project.

Staff will review qualifications and select the consultant(s) most qualified to provide the requested services.  Staff may contact the consultant(s) for additional information or clarification. General work description:
The Santa Clara Valley Transportation Authority (VTA) will be soliciting an Invitation for Bids (IFB) for "Guadalupe Light Rail Vehicle Wash Improvements" (Project).
Notice is hereby given that VTA is now soliciting Statements of Qualifications (SOQ) from bidders (Bidders) with construction expertise to furnish all labor, materials, tools, equipment, services, supervision, and incidentals necessary to remove and replace existing LRV Wash System located at Building F of the Guadalupe Division with a hybrid drive-through and gantry wash system.

This Request for Pre-Qualification of Bidders is intended to solicit information in the form of a qualification questionnaire and qualification statements. All Bidders that intend to submit a Bid for the Project must fully complete the Pre-Qualification Questionnaire, provide all materials requested herein, and be approved by VTA in order to be included on the final qualified Bidders list.  No bid will be accepted from a Bidder that has failed to comply with these requirements.  If two or more firms submitted a SOQ as part of a Joint Venture, or expect to submit a SOQ as part of a Joint Venture, each entity within the Joint Venture must be separately pre-qualified.
